- kind: summary
  text: Housekeeping requirements under Clause 17 mandate that the contractor keep the work environment clear of
    unnecessary waste as a first-line defence against accidents, establishing a special housekeeping personnel group
    under General Instruction BMRC/SHE/CEO/001, daily cleaning routines, segregated waste containers, full-height
    barricades, and clear passageways.
  evidence_ids:
  - J6cb3b0a3b5e68f12
  relation_type: none
  explicitness: not_a_relation
  from_id: ''
  to_id: ''
  id: C51d4b5d3472f5bc1

    heading: Clause 17.0 — Housekeeping
    source_document: Vol3DLNP1.pdf
    source_sha256: 1ee3fc8dfd12f659f34446b0a6db74e1e1cdd4d593ca91b2a48d59bf1ef97d52

    - 31
    - 32

    json_sha256: 0042f3256acc51ca4ebb327c3cee57a308fa5f47e1a4ccc7f4994fe898fa11ef
    json_pointer: /clauses/0

    quote: "{\n  \"clause_id\": \"17.0\",\n  \"fragments\": [\n    {\n      \"pdf_page\": 31,\n      \"text\": \"\
      17.0     Housekeeping\\n\\n\\n          17.1     Housekeeping is the act of keeping the working environment\
      \ cleared of all unnecessary\\n                   waste, thereby providing a first-line of defence against\
      \ accidents and injuries.\\n\\n\\n          17.2      Contractor shall understand and accept that improper\
      \ housekeeping is the primary\\n                  hazard in any construction site and ensure that a high degree\
      \ of housekeeping is\\n                  always maintained. Indeed “Cleanliness is indeed next to Godliness”\\\
      n\\n\\n          17.3     Housekeeping  is  the  responsibility  of  all  site  personnel, and  line management\\\
      n                 commitment shall be demonstrated by the continued efforts of supervising staff towards\\\
      n                        this activity.\\n\\n\\n          17.4     General Housekeeping shall be carried out\
      \ by the contractor and ensured at all times at\\n                Work Site, Construction Depot, Batching\
      \ Plant, Labour Camp, Stores, Offices and\\n                        toilets/urinals. Towards  this  the  Contractor\
      \  shall  constitute a  special  group  of\\n                  housekeeping personnel as per General Instruction\
      \ BMRC/SHE/CEO/001. This group\\n                      shall ensure daily cleaning at work sites and surrounding\
      \ areas and maintain a register\\n                 as per the approved format by the Employer.\\n\\n\\n  \
      \        17.5     Adequate time shall be assigned to ensure that good housekeeping is maintained.\\n     \
      \         Team of housekeeping squad shall carry out this.\\n\\n\\n          17.6    The contractor shall\
      \ be responsible to provide segregated containers for disposal of\\n                    debris at required\
      \ places and regular cleaning of the same.\\n\\n\\n          17.7      Full height fence, barriers, barricades\
      \ etc. shall be erected around the site in order to\\n                   prevent the surrounding area from\
      \ excavated  soil, rubbish etc, which may cause\\n                   inconvenience to and endanger the public.\
      \ The barricade especially those exposed to\\n                     public shall be aesthetically maintained\
      \ by regular cleaning and painting as directed by\\n                    the Employer. These shall be maintained\
      \ in one line and level.\\n\\n\\n          17.8    The structure dimension of the barricade, material and\
      \ composition, its colour scheme,\\n            BMRC logo and other details shall be in accordance with specifications\
      \ laid down in\\n                   tender document.\\n\\n\\n          17.9       All stairways, passageways\
      \ and gangways shall be maintained without any blockages\\n                     or obstructions. All emergency\
      \ exits passageways, exits fire doors, break-glass alarm\\n                      points, firefighting equipment,\
      \ first aid stations, and other emergency stations shall be\\n                   kept clean, unobstructed\
      \ and in good working order.\\n\\n\\n         17.10    Lumber with protruding nails shall be bent or removed\
      \ and properly stacked.\\n\\n\\n         17.11     All surplus earth and debris are removed/disposed  off\
      \ from the working areas to\\n                          officially designated dumpsites. Trucks  carrying\
      \ sand,  earth and any  pulverized\\n                    materials etc. in order to avoid dust or odour impact\
      \ shall be covered while moving.\\n\\n               The tyres of the trucks leaving the site shall be cleaned\
      \ with water, wherever the\\n                    possibility of spillage on carriageways meant for regular\
      \ road traffic exists.\\n\\n\\n         17.12  No parking of trucks/trolleys, cranes and trailers etc. shall\
      \ be allowed on roads, which\\n              may obstruct the traffic movement.\\n\\n\\n         17.13   Roads\
      \ shall be kept clear and materials like: pipes, steel, sand boulders, concrete,\\n                   chips\
      \ and brick etc. shall not be allowed on the roads to obstruct free movement of\\n                 road traffic.\"\
      \n    },\n    {\n      \"pdf_page\": 32,\n      \"text\": \"17.14   Water logging or bentonite spillage on\
      \ roads shall not be allowed.  If bentonite\\n          spillage is observed on road endangering the safety\
      \ of road users, the contractor\\n          shall be penalised as per relevant clause.\\n\\n\\n17.15   Proper\
      \ and safe stacking of material are of paramount importance at yards, stores\\n       and such locations where\
      \ material would be unloaded for future use. The storage\\n        area shall be well laid out with easy access\
      \ and material stored  / stacked in an\\n         orderly and safe manner.\\n\\n\\n17.16   Flammable chemicals\
      \ / compressed gas cylinders shall be safely stored.\\n\\n\\n17.17   Unused/surplus cables, steel items and\
      \ steel scrap lying scattered at different\\n        places within the working areas shall be removed to identified\
      \ locations(s).\\n\\n\\n17.18    All wooden scrap, empty wooden cable drums and other combustible packing\\\
      n         materials, shall be removed from work place to identified location(s).\\n\\n\\n17.19   Empty cement\
      \ bags and other packaging material shall be properly stacked and\\n        removed.\\n\\n\\n17.20   The \
      \ Contractor  shall  ensure  that  all  his  sub-contractors  maintain  the  site\\n        reasonably clean\
      \ through provisions related to house keeping\"\n    }\n  ],\n  \"heading_line\": \"          17.0     Housekeeping\"\

      \n    },\n    {\n      \"pdf_page\": 32,\n      \"source_line_number\": 6,\n      \"text\": \"\"\n    },\n\

- kind: summary
  text: Working at height regulations under Clause 18 define organizational planning, supervision, weather restrictions,
    worker competence, collective safeguards, scaffolding standards, working platform inspections, and personal
    fall protection systems.

    quote: "{\n  \"pdf_page\": 32,\n  \"text\": \"18.0    Working at Height\\n\\n\\n18.1     Definitions\\n\\n\\\
      n18.1.1   “access” and “egress” include ascent and descent.\\n\\n\\n18.1.2   “fragile surface” means a surface,\
      \ which would be able to fail  if any reasonably\\n         foreseeable loading were to be applied to it.\\\
      n\\n\\n18.1.3   “line” includes rope, chain or webbing\\n\\n\\n18.1.4   “personal fall protection” means -\\\
      n\\n          a)   a  fall prevention, work  restraint, work positioning,  fall arrest or rescue\\n      \
      \         system,   other than a system in which the only safeguards are collective\\n               safeguards;\
      \ or\\n          b)    rope access and positioning techniques;\\n\\n\\n18.1.5    \\\"work at height\\\" means\
      \ -\\n           a)   work in any place, including a place at or below ground level;\\n           b)    obtaining\
      \ access to or egress from such place while at work, except by a\\n                staircase in a permanent\
      \ workplace,\\n              where,  if protective measures were not taken, a person could fall a distance\\\
      n                   liable to cause personal injury;\\n\\n\\n18.1.6    \\\"work equipment\\\" means any machinery,\
      \ appliance, apparatus, tool or installation for\\n        use at work (whether exclusively or not) and includes\\\
      n          a)   a guard-rail, toe-board, barrier or similar collective means of protection\\n          b)\
      \   a working platform\\n           c)   a net, airbag or other collective safe guard for arresting falls.\\\
      n          d)    personal fall protection system\\n          e)    ladders\\n\\n18.1.7    “working platform”\\\
      n          a)   means any platform used as a place of work or as a means of access to or\\n              egress\
      \ from a place of work;\"\n}"

    okf_path: OKF_bundle/Technical/Vol3/vol3_part2.md

    json_path: parsed_json/vol3/part_2_safety/safety_clauses.json

    json_pointer: /clauses/1/fragments/1
    json_record_id: null
    source_review_status: pending_manual_review
    quote: "{\n  \"pdf_page\": 33,\n  \"text\": \"b)    includes any scaffold, suspended scaffold, cradle, mobile\
      \ platforms,  trestle,\\n                      gangway, gantry and stairway which is so used.\\n\\n\\n   \
      \       18.2     Organisation and planning\\n\\n                The contractor shall ensure that work at height\
      \ is\\n\\n                                 i)     properly planned for any emergencies and rescue\\n\\n  \
      \                                  ii)    appropriately supervised; and\\n\\n                            \
      \         iii)    carried out in a manner, which is reasonably practicable safe.\\n\\n\\n          18.3  \
      \  The contractor shall ensure that work at height is carried out only when the weather\\n               \
      \     conditions do not jeopardise the health or safety of persons involved in the work.\\n\\n\\n        \
      \  18.4     Competence\\n\\n                The  contractor  shall ensure  that no person engages  in any\
      \  activity,  including\\n                     organization, planning and supervision, in relation to work\
      \ at height or work equipment\\n                       for use in such work unless he is competent to do so\
      \ or,  if being trained, is being\\n                   supervised by a competent person.\\n\\n\\n        \
      \  18.5     Avoidance of risks from work at height\\n\\n                The contractor shall ensure that work\
      \ is not carried out at height where it is reasonably\\n                     practicable to carry out the\
      \ work safely otherwise than at height.\\n\\n\\n          18.6    Where work is carried out at height, the\
      \ contractor shall take suitable and sufficient\\n                 measures as given below to prevent, so\
      \ far as is reasonably practicable, any person\\n                      falling a distance liable to cause\
      \ personal injury.\\n\\n\\n                     a)    his ensuring that the work is carried out\\n\\n    \
      \                                       i)    from an existing place of work; or\\n\\n                   \
      \                           ii)     (in the case of obtaining access or egress) using an existing means,\\\
      n                             complying to the requirements as given in clause 18.15 .\\n\\n             \
      \         where  it is reasonably practicable to carry  it out safely and under appropriate\\n           \
      \            ergonomic conditions; and\\n\\n\\n                     b)   where  it is not reasonably practicable\
      \ for the work to be carried out in\\n                       accordance with sub-paragraph (a), his providing\
      \ sufficient work equipment\\n                              for preventing, so far as is reasonably practicable,\
      \ a fall occurring.\\n\\n\\n          18.7    Where the measures taken under clause 18.6 do not eliminate\
      \ the risk of a fall\\n                     occurring, every contractor shall\\n\\n                     a)\
      \   so far as is reasonably practicable, provide sufficient work equipment to\\n                        minimise\
      \ -\\n\\n                                           i)     the distance and consequences; or\\n\\n       \
      \                                       ii)    where  it is not reasonably practicable to minimise the distance,\
      \ the\\n                            consequences, of a fall; and\\n\\n                     b)    Without prejudice\
      \ to the generality of clause 18.4 provide such additional\\n                             training and  instruction\
      \ or take other  additional suitable and  sufficient\\n                     measures to prevent, so far as\
      \ is reasonably practicable, any person falling\\n                     a distance liable to cause personal\
      \ injury.\\n\\n\\n          18.8      Selection of ‘work equipment’ for work at height\\n\\n\\n          \
      \           1)    the contractor, in selecting work equipment for use in work at height, shall\\n\\n     \
      \                      a)    give collective protection measures priority over personal protection\\n    \
      \                        measures; and\\n\\n                           b)    take account of\"\n}"

    okf_path: OKF_bundle/Technical/Vol3/vol3_part2.md
    okf_sha256: ee80a88bd673202495b104f1e039fd2b85ddf8e2f3b2cbbf98523266c0f35b6c
    heading: Clause 18.0 — Working at Height
    source_document: Vol3DLNP1.pdf

    sheet_cells: ''

    json_sha256: 0042f3256acc51ca4ebb327c3cee57a308fa5f47e1a4ccc7f4994fe898fa11ef
    json_pointer: /clauses/1/fragments/2
    json_record_id: null
    source_review_status: pending_manual_review
    quote: "{\n  \"pdf_page\": 34,\n  \"text\": \"i)     the working conditions and the risks to the safety of persons\
      \ at\\n                           the place where the work equipment is to be used;\\n\\n                \
      \                       ii)     in the case of work equipment for access and egress, the\\n              \
      \             distance to be negotiated;\\n\\n                                        iii)    the distance\
      \ and consequences of a potential fall;\\n\\n                             iv)    the duration and frequency\
      \ of use;\\n\\n                        v)    the need  for easy and timely evacuation and rescue in an\\n\
      \                        emergency; and\\n\\n                             vi)   any additional risk posed\
      \ by the use, installation or removal of\\n                              that work equipment or by evacuation\
      \ and rescue from it;\\n\\n\\n          2)   The contractor shall select work equipment for work at height\
      \ which:\\n\\n\\n                a)   has characteristics including dimensions which:\\n\\n              \
      \                      i)    are appropriate to the nature of the work to be performed and\\n            \
      \               the foreseeable loadings; and\\n\\n                                       ii)    allow passage\
      \ without risk; and\\n\\n                b)     is in other respects the most suitable work equipment, having\
      \ regard\\n                          in particular to the purposes specified in 18.5 and 18.6 .\\n\\n\\n18.9\
      \      Fragile surfaces\\n\\n\\n18.9.1   The contractor shall ensure that no person at work passes across\
      \ or near, or\\n         working on, from or near, a fragile surface where  it is reasonably practicable to\\\
      n          carry out work safely and under appropriate ergonomic conditions without his\\n         doing so.\\\
      n\\n\\n18.9.2   Where   it  is not reasonably practicable  to carry out work  safely and under\\n        \
      \  appropriate ergonomic conditions without passing across or near, or working on,\\n         from or near,\
      \ a fragile surface, every contractor shall,\\n\\n\\n          a)    ensure, so far as  is reasonably practicable,\
      \ that suitable and sufficient\\n                platforms, coverings, guard rails or similar means of support\
      \ or protection\\n               are provided and used so that any foreseeable loading is supported by such\\\
      n               supports or borne by such protection;\\n\\n\\n          b)   where a risk of a person at work\
      \ falling remains despite the measures taken\\n              under the preceding provisions of this regulation,\
      \ take suitable and sufficient\\n             measures to minimise the distances and consequences of his fall.\\\
      n\\n\\n18.9.3   Where any person at work may pass across or near, or work on, from or near, a\\n         \
      \   fragile surface, every contractor shall ensure that\\n\\n          a)    prominent warning notices are\
      \ so far as is reasonably practicable affixed at\\n                the approach to the place where the fragile\
      \ surface is situated; or\\n\\n          b)   where that is not reasonably practicable, such persons are made\
      \ aware of it\\n              by other means.\\n\\n\\n18.10     Falling objects\\n\\n\\n18.10.1  The contractor\
      \  shall, where necessary to prevent injury to any person, take\\n          suitable and sufficient steps\
      \ to prevent, so far as is reasonably practicable, the fall\\n           of any material or object.\\n\\n\\\
      n18.10.2  Where  it is not reasonably practicable to comply with the requirements of 18.9,\\n         every\
      \ contractor shall take suitable and sufficient steps to prevent any person\\n         being struck by any\
      \ falling material or object which is liable to cause personal\\n            injury.\"\n}"

    okf_path: OKF_bundle/Technical/Vol3/vol3_part2.md

    heading: Clause 18.0 — Working at Height
    source_document: Vol3DLNP1.pdf
    source_sha256: 1ee3fc8dfd12f659f34446b0a6db74e1e1cdd4d593ca91b2a48d59bf1ef97d52
    pdf_pages:
    - 35
    sheet_cells: ''
    json_path: parsed_json/vol3/part_2_safety/safety_clauses.json
    json_sha256: 0042f3256acc51ca4ebb327c3cee57a308fa5f47e1a4ccc7f4994fe898fa11ef
    json_pointer: /clauses/1/fragments/3
    json_record_id: null
    source_review_status: pending_manual_review
    quote: "{\n  \"pdf_page\": 35,\n  \"text\": \"18.10.3  The contractor shall ensure that no material or object\
      \ is thrown or tipped from\\n                    height in circumstances where it is liable to cause injury\
      \ to any person.\\n\\n\\n          18.10.4  Every employer shall ensure that materials and objects are stored\
      \ in such a way\\n                 as  to prevent  risk  to any person  arising from the  collapse, overturning\
      \ or\\n                  unintended movement of such materials or objects.\\n\\n\\n         18.11    Danger\
      \ areas\\n\\n\\n          18.11.1  Without prejudice to the preceding requirements of these Regulations, every\\\
      n                     contractor shall ensure that\\n\\n                     a)   where a workplace contains\
      \ an area in which, owing to the nature of the\\n                         work, there is a risk of any person\
      \ at work\\n\\n                                           i)      falling a distance; or\\n\\n           \
      \                                   ii)    being struck by a falling object,\\n\\n                       which\
      \  is liable to cause personal  injury, the workplace  is so far as  is\\n                        reasonably\
      \  practicable equipped  with devices  preventing unauthorised\\n                       persons from entering\
      \ such area; and\\n\\n                     b)   such area is clearly indicated.\\n\\n\\n         18.12   \
      \ Inspection of work equipment\\n\\n\\n          18.12.1  The contractor shall ensure that, where the safety\
      \ of work equipment depends on\\n               how it is installed or assembled, it is not used after installation\
      \ or assembly in any\\n                     position unless it has been inspected in that position.\\n\\n\\\
      n          18.12.2  The contractor shall ensure that work equipment exposed to conditions causing\\n     \
      \                deterioration which is liable to result in dangerous situations is inspected\\n\\n      \
      \               a)    at suitable intervals; and\\n\\n                     b)   each time that exceptional\
      \ circumstances which are liable to jeopardise the\\n                          safety of the work equipment\
      \ have occurred,\\n\\n                      to ensure  that  health and  safety  conditions  are maintained\
      \ and  that any\\n                     deterioration can be detected and remedied in good time.\\n\\n\\n \
      \         18.12.3  Without prejudice to paragraph 18.12.1, the contractor shall ensure that a working\\n \
      \                   platform\\n\\n                     a)   used for construction work; and\\n\\n        \
      \             b)    from which a person could fall 2 metres or more,\\n\\n                         is not\
      \ used in any position unless it has been inspected in that position or, in the\\n                 case of\
      \ a mobile working platform, inspected on the site, within the previous 7\\n                   days.\\n\\\
      n\\n          18.12.4  The contractor  shall ensure  that the reports  of  all inspections are properly\\\
      n                   maintained and shown to the Employer as and when required.\\n\\n\\n          18.12.5 \
      \  In this clause \\\"inspection\\\",\\n\\n                     a)   means such visual or more rigorous inspection\
      \ by a competent person as is\\n                          appropriate for safety purposes;\\n\\n         \
      \            b)    includes any testing appropriate for those purposes,\\n\\n\\n         18.13    Inspection\
      \ of places of work at height\\n\\n\\n          18.13.1  The contractor shall so far as is reasonably practicable\
      \ ensure that the surface\\n                and every parapet, permanent rail or other such fall protection\
      \ measure of every\\n                   place of work at height are checked on each occasion before the place\
      \ is used.\"\n}"

    source_document: Vol3DLNP1.pdf

    pdf_pages:

    sheet_cells: ''
    json_path: parsed_json/vol3/part_2_safety/safety_clauses.json
    json_sha256: 0042f3256acc51ca4ebb327c3cee57a308fa5f47e1a4ccc7f4994fe898fa11ef
    json_pointer: /clauses/1/fragments/4
    json_record_id: null
    source_review_status: pending_manual_review
    quote: "{\n  \"pdf_page\": 36,\n  \"text\": \"18.14    Duties of persons at work\\n\\n\\n18.14.1  Any workmen\
      \ employed by the contractor shall report to the supervisor about any\\n          defect relating to work\
      \ at height which he knows is likely to endanger the safety of\\n          himself or another person.\\n\\\
      n\\n18.14.2  Every workmen shall use any work equipment or safety device provided to him for\\n         work\
      \ at height by the contractor, in accordance with\\n\\n\\n          a)   any training in the use of the work\
      \ equipment or device concerned which\\n             have been received by him; and\\n\\n          b)    the\
      \ instructions respecting that use which have been provided to him by the\\n                contractor as\
      \ per the requirements of the Employer\\n\\n\\n18.15    Requirements for existing places of work and means\
      \ of access or egress at height\\n         Every existing place of work or means of access or egress at height\
      \ shall\\n\\n\\n          a)   be stable and of sufficient strength and rigidity for the purpose for which\
      \ it is\\n               intended to be or is being used;\\n\\n          b)   where applicable, rest on a\
      \ stable, sufficiently strong surface;\\n\\n           c)   be of sufficient dimensions to permit the safe\
      \ passage of persons and the\\n               safe use of any plant or materials required to be used and to\
      \ provide a safe\\n               working area having regard to the work to be carried out there;\\n\\n  \
      \        d)   possess suitable and sufficient means for preventing a fall;\\n\\n          e)   possess a surface\
      \ which has no gap\\n\\n                          i)    through which a person could fall;\\n\\n         \
      \                   ii)    through which any material or object could fall and injure a person; or\\n\\n \
      \                            iii)    giving rise to other risk of injury to any person, unless measures have\\\
      n                  been taken to protect persons against such risk;\\n\\n               f)    be so constructed\
      \ and used, and maintained  in such condition, as to\\n                prevent, so far as is reasonably practicable\
      \ -\\n\\n                          i)     the risk of slipping or tripping; or\\n\\n                     \
      \       ii)    any person being caught between it and any adjacent structure;\\n\\n          g)   where  \
      \ it has moving parts, be prevented by appropriate devices from\\n             moving inadvertently during\
      \ work at height.\\n\\n\\n18.16    Requirements for guardrails, toe-boards, barriers and similar collective\
      \ means of\\n          protection\\n\\n\\n                i)    Unless the context otherwise requires, any\
      \ reference in this section to\\n            means of protection is to a guardrail, toe-board, barrier or\
      \ similar collective\\n            means of protection.\\n\\n                  ii)   Means of protection shall\\\
      n\\n                a)   be of sufficient dimensions, of sufficient strength and rigidity for the\\n     \
      \              purposes for which they are being used, and otherwise suitable;\\n\\n                b)   be\
      \ so placed, secured and used as to ensure, so far as is reasonably\\n                       practicable,\
      \ that they do not become accidentally displaced; and\\n\\n                 c)   be so placed as to prevent,\
      \ so far as is practicable, the fall of any\\n                     person, or of any material or object, from\
      \ any place of work.\\n\\n                  iii)    In relation to work at height involved in construction\
      \ work\\n\\n                a)    the top guard-rail or other similar means of protection shall be at least\\\
      n                  950 millimetres above the edge from which any person is liable to fall;\\n\\n         \
      \       b)    toe-boards shall be suitable and sufficient to prevent the fall of any\\n                  \
      \   person, or any material or object, from any place of work; and\"\n}"

    json_pointer: /clauses/1/fragments/5
    json_record_id: null
    source_review_status: pending_manual_review
    quote: "{\n  \"pdf_page\": 37,\n  \"text\": \"c)   any intermediate guardrail or similar means of protection\
      \ shall be\\n                                positioned so that any gap between  it and other means of protection\\\
      n                           does not exceed 470 millimetres.\\n\\n                          iv)   Any structure\
      \ or part of a structure which supports means of protection or to\\n                       which means of\
      \ protection are attached shall be of sufficient strength and\\n                           suitable for the\
      \ purpose of such support or attachment.\\n\\n\\n         18.17    Requirements for all Working Platforms\\\
      n\\n\\n                                 i)    Every working platforms requires a supporting structure for\
      \ holding it\\n\\n                                    ii)   Any surface upon which any supporting structure\
      \ rests shall be stable, of\\n                              sufficient  strength and  of  suitable  composition\
      \  safely  to  support  the\\n                         supporting structure, the working platform and any\
      \ loading intended to be\\n                        placed on the working platform.\\n\\n                 \
      \                   iii).    Stability of supporting structure\\n\\n                    Any supporting structure\
      \ shall\\n\\n                           a)   be suitable and of sufficient strength and rigidity for the purpose\
      \ for\\n                            which it is being used;\\n\\n                           b)     in the\
      \ case of a wheeled structure, be prevented by appropriate\\n                              devices from moving\
      \ inadvertently during work at height;\\n\\n                            c)     in other cases, be prevented\
      \ from slipping by secure attachment to\\n                               the bearing surface or to another\
      \ structure, provision of an effective\\n                                      anti-slip device or by other\
      \ means of equivalent effectiveness;\\n\\n                           d)   be stable while being erected, used\
      \ and dismantled; and\\n\\n                           e)   when altered or modified, be so altered or modified\
      \ as to ensure that it\\n                             remains stable.\\n\\n                              \
      \        f)    Have suitable base plates and properly footed thereby.\\n\\n\\n                           \
      \ iv).    Stability of working platforms\\n\\n                  A working platform shall\\n\\n           \
      \                a)   be suitable and of sufficient strength and rigidity for the purpose or\\n          \
      \                  purposes for which it is intended to be used or is being used;\\n\\n                  \
      \         b)   be so erected and used as to ensure that  its components do not\\n                        become\
      \ accidentally displaced so as to endanger any person;\\n\\n                            c)   when altered\
      \ or modified, be so altered or modified as to ensure that it\\n                             remains stable;\
      \ and\\n\\n                           d)   be dismantled in such a way as to prevent accidental displacement.\\\
      n\\n\\n                      v)    Safety on working platforms\\n\\n                  A working platform shall\\\
      n\\n                           a)   be of sufficient dimensions to permit the safe passage of persons and\\\
      n                               the safe use of any plant or materials required to be used and to\\n     \
      \                          provide a safe working area having regard to the work being carried\\n        \
      \                       out there;\\n\\n                           b)   possess a suitable surface and, in\
      \ particular, be so constructed that\\n                               the surface of the working platform\
      \ has no gap\\n\\n                                                     i)      through which a person could\
      \ fall;\\n\\n                                                         ii)      through which any material\
      \ or object could fall and injure a\\n                                      person; or\\n\\n             \
      \                                             iii)      giving  rise  to other  risk  of  injury  to any person,\
      \ unless\\n                                 measures have been taken to protect persons against such\\n  \
      \                                               risk; and\\n\\n                            c)   be so erected\
      \ and used, and maintained in such condition, as to\\n                                prevent, so far as is\
      \ reasonably practicable\\n\\n                                                     i)       the risk of slipping\
      \ or tripping; or\\n\\n                                                         ii)     any person being caught\
      \ between the working platform and\\n                                  any adjacent structure.\"\n}"

    json_pointer: /clauses/1/fragments/6
    json_record_id: null
    source_review_status: pending_manual_review
    quote: "{\n  \"pdf_page\": 38,\n  \"text\": \"vi)   Loading\\n\\n           A working platform and any supporting\
      \ structure shall not be loaded so as to\\n                give rise to a risk of collapse or to any deformation,\
      \ which could affect its\\n               safe use.\\n\\n\\n              vii)   Additional requirements for\
      \ scaffolding\\n\\n               Strength and stability calculations for scaffolding shall be carried out\
      \ unless\\n\\n                a)   a note  of the  calculations, covering the  structural arrangements\\n\
      \                     contemplated, is available; or\\n\\n                b)       it is assembled in conformity\
      \ with a generally recognised standard\\n                       configuration.\\n\\n\\n               viii)\
      \  Depending on the complexity of the scaffolding selected, a competent\\n              person shall draw\
      \ up an assembly, use and dismantling plan. This may be\\n                   in the form of a standard plan,\
      \ supplemented by items relating to specific\\n                  details of the scaffolding in question.\\\
      n\\n\\n             ix)  A copy of the plan, including any instructions  it may contain, shall be kept\\n\
      \                available  for  the use  of  persons  concerned  in  the  assembly,  use,\\n            \
      \    dismantling or alteration of scaffolding until it has been dismantled.\\n\\n\\n           x)   The dimensions\
      \ form and layout of scaffolding decks shall be appropriate to\\n                the nature of the work to\
      \ be performed and suitable for the loads to be\\n                 carried and permit work and passage in\
      \ safety.\\n\\n\\n             xi)   While a scaffold  is not available for use, including during  its assembly,\\\
      n                dismantling or alteration,  it shall be marked with general warning signs in\\n         \
      \     accordance with and be suitably delineated by physical means preventing\\n              access to the\
      \ danger zone.\\n\\n\\n              xii)   Scaffolding may be assembled, dismantled or  significantly altered\
      \ only\\n              under the supervision of a competent person and by persons who have\\n            \
      \   received appropriate and specific training in the operations envisaged which\\n              addresses\
      \ specific risks which the operations may entail and precautions to\\n             be taken, and more particularly\
      \ in\\n\\n                a)    understanding of the plan for the assembly, dismantling or alteration\\n \
      \                       of the scaffolding concerned;\\n\\n                b)    safety during the assembly,\
      \ dismantling or alteration of the scaffolding\\n                    concerned;\\n\\n                 c) \
      \  measures to prevent the risk of persons, materials or objects falling;\\n\\n                d)    safety\
      \ measures in the event of changing weather conditions which\\n                     could adversely affect\
      \ the safety of the scaffolding concerned;\\n\\n                e)    permissible loadings;\\n\\n        \
      \               f)    any other risks which the assembly, dismantling or alteration of the\\n            \
      \           scaffolding may entail.\\n\\n\\n18.18    Requirements for collective safeguards for arresting\
      \ falls\\n\\n\\n                i)     Collective safeguard are a safety net, airbag or other collective safeguard\\\
      n                  for arresting falls\\n\\n\\n                  ii)   A safeguard shall be used only if\\\
      n\\n                a)   a risk assessment has demonstrated that the work activity can so far\\n         \
      \          as is reasonably practicable be performed safely while using  it and\\n                      without\
      \ affecting its effectiveness;\"\n}"

    quote: "{\n  \"pdf_page\": 39,\n  \"text\": \"b)    the use of other, safer work equipment is not reasonably\
      \ practicable;\\n                          and\\n\\n                            c)   a sufficient number of\
      \ available persons have received adequate\\n                                    training specific to the\
      \ safeguard, including rescue procedures.\\n\\n\\n                                     iii)   A safeguard\
      \ shall be suitable and of sufficient strength to arrest safely the\\n                                   \
      \  fall of any person who is liable to fall.\\n\\n\\n                          iv)   A safeguard shall\\n\\\
      n                           a)     in the case of a safeguard which  is designed to be attached, be\\n   \
      \                            securely attached to all the required anchors, and the anchors and the\\n   \
      \                     means  of attachment  thereto  shall be  suitable and  of  sufficient\\n           \
      \                     strength and  stability  for  the purpose  of  safely  supporting  the\\n          \
      \                     foreseeable loading in arresting any fall and during any subsequent\\n             \
      \                  rescue;\\n\\n                           b)     in the case of an airbag, landing mat or\
      \ similar safeguard, be stable;\\n                          and\\n\\n                            c)     in\
      \ the case of a safeguard, which distorts in arresting a fall, afford\\n                                 \
      \    sufficient clearance.\\n\\n\\n                                          iv)      Suitable and sufficient\
      \ steps shall be taken to ensure, so far\\n                                  as practicable, that in the event\
      \ of a fall by any person the\\n                                     safeguard does not itself cause injury\
      \ to that person.\\n\\n\\n         18.19    Requirements for personal fall protection systems\\n\\n      \
      \                           i)   A personal fall protection system shall be used only if\\n\\n           \
      \                a)   a risk assessment has demonstrated that\\n\\n                                      \
      \               i)     the work can so far as is reasonably practicable be performed\\n                  \
      \                     safely while using that system; and\\n\\n                                          \
      \               ii)    the use  of  other  safer work equipment  is  not reasonably\\n                   \
      \                     practicable; and\\n\\n                           b)    the user and a sufficient number\
      \ of available persons have received\\n                            adequate  training  specific  to the operations\
      \ envisaged,  including\\n                             rescue procedures.\\n\\n\\n                       \
      \             ii)   A personal fall protection system shall\\n\\n                           a)   be suitable\
      \ and of sufficient strength for the purposes for which  it is\\n                              being used\
      \ having regard to the work being carried out and any\\n                               foreseeable loading;\\\
      n\\n                           b)   where necessary, fit the user;\\n\\n                            c)   be\
      \ correctly fitted;\\n\\n                           d)   be designed to minimise injury to the user and, where\
      \ necessary, be\\n                               adjusted to prevent the user falling or slipping from  it,\
      \ should a fall\\n                                occur; and\\n\\n                           e)   be so designed,\
      \  installed and used as to prevent unplanned or\\n                                uncontrolled movement of\
      \ the user.\\n\\n\\n                                     iii)   A personal fall protection system designed\
      \ for use with an anchor shall be\\n                         securely attached to at least one anchor, and\
      \ each anchor and the means of\\n                        attachment thereto shall be suitable and of sufficient\
      \ strength and stability\\n                              for the purpose of supporting any foreseeable loading.\\\
      n\\n\\n                          iv)    Suitable and sufficient steps shall be taken to prevent any person\
      \ falling or\\n                            slipping from a personal fall protection system.\"\n}"

    in the case of mobile working platforms, on site within the previous 7 days.

    json_record_id: null
    source_review_status: pending_manual_review
    quote: "{\n  \"pdf_page\": 35,\n  \"text\": \"18.10.3  The contractor shall ensure that no material or object\
      \ is thrown or tipped from\\n                    height in circumstances where it is liable to cause injury\
      \ to any person.\\n\\n\\n          18.10.4  Every employer shall ensure that materials and objects are stored\
      \ in such a way\\n                 as  to prevent  risk  to any person  arising from the  collapse, overturning\
      \ or\\n                  unintended movement of such materials or objects.\\n\\n\\n         18.11    Danger\
      \ areas\\n\\n\\n          18.11.1  Without prejudice to the preceding requirements of these Regulations, every\\\
      n                     contractor shall ensure that\\n\\n                     a)   where a workplace contains\
      \ an area in which, owing to the nature of the\\n                         work, there is a risk of any person\
      \ at work\\n\\n                                           i)      falling a distance; or\\n\\n           \
      \                                   ii)    being struck by a falling object,\\n\\n                       which\
      \  is liable to cause personal  injury, the workplace  is so far as  is\\n                        reasonably\
      \  practicable equipped  with devices  preventing unauthorised\\n                       persons from entering\
      \ such area; and\\n\\n                     b)   such area is clearly indicated.\\n\\n\\n         18.12   \
      \ Inspection of work equipment\\n\\n\\n          18.12.1  The contractor shall ensure that, where the safety\
      \ of work equipment depends on\\n               how it is installed or assembled, it is not used after installation\
      \ or assembly in any\\n                     position unless it has been inspected in that position.\\n\\n\\\
      n          18.12.2  The contractor shall ensure that work equipment exposed to conditions causing\\n     \
      \                deterioration which is liable to result in dangerous situations is inspected\\n\\n      \
      \               a)    at suitable intervals; and\\n\\n                     b)   each time that exceptional\
      \ circumstances which are liable to jeopardise the\\n                          safety of the work equipment\
      \ have occurred,\\n\\n                      to ensure  that  health and  safety  conditions  are maintained\
      \ and  that any\\n                     deterioration can be detected and remedied in good time.\\n\\n\\n \
      \         18.12.3  Without prejudice to paragraph 18.12.1, the contractor shall ensure that a working\\n \
      \                   platform\\n\\n                     a)   used for construction work; and\\n\\n        \
      \             b)    from which a person could fall 2 metres or more,\\n\\n                         is not\
      \ used in any position unless it has been inspected in that position or, in the\\n                 case of\
      \ a mobile working platform, inspected on the site, within the previous 7\\n                   days.\\n\\\
      n\\n          18.12.4  The contractor  shall ensure  that the reports  of  all inspections are properly\\\
      n                   maintained and shown to the Employer as and when required.\\n\\n\\n          18.12.5 \
      \  In this clause \\\"inspection\\\",\\n\\n                     a)   means such visual or more rigorous inspection\
      \ by a competent person as is\\n                          appropriate for safety purposes;\\n\\n         \
      \            b)    includes any testing appropriate for those purposes,\\n\\n\\n         18.13    Inspection\
      \ of places of work at height\\n\\n\\n          18.13.1  The contractor shall so far as is reasonably practicable\
      \ ensure that the surface\\n                and every parapet, permanent rail or other such fall protection\
      \ measure of every\\n                   place of work at height are checked on each occasion before the place\
      \ is used.\"\n}"

  text: The top guard-rail or other similar collective means of protection for work at height in construction must
    be positioned at least 950 millimetres above the edge from which any person is liable to fall, with intermediate
    gaps not exceeding 470 millimetres.

    quote: "{\n  \"pdf_page\": 36,\n  \"text\": \"18.14    Duties of persons at work\\n\\n\\n18.14.1  Any workmen\
      \ employed by the contractor shall report to the supervisor about any\\n          defect relating to work\
      \ at height which he knows is likely to endanger the safety of\\n          himself or another person.\\n\\\
      n\\n18.14.2  Every workmen shall use any work equipment or safety device provided to him for\\n         work\
      \ at height by the contractor, in accordance with\\n\\n\\n          a)   any training in the use of the work\
      \ equipment or device concerned which\\n             have been received by him; and\\n\\n          b)    the\
      \ instructions respecting that use which have been provided to him by the\\n                contractor as\
      \ per the requirements of the Employer\\n\\n\\n18.15    Requirements for existing places of work and means\
      \ of access or egress at height\\n         Every existing place of work or means of access or egress at height\
      \ shall\\n\\n\\n          a)   be stable and of sufficient strength and rigidity for the purpose for which\
      \ it is\\n               intended to be or is being used;\\n\\n          b)   where applicable, rest on a\
      \ stable, sufficiently strong surface;\\n\\n           c)   be of sufficient dimensions to permit the safe\
      \ passage of persons and the\\n               safe use of any plant or materials required to be used and to\
      \ provide a safe\\n               working area having regard to the work to be carried out there;\\n\\n  \
      \        d)   possess suitable and sufficient means for preventing a fall;\\n\\n          e)   possess a surface\
      \ which has no gap\\n\\n                          i)    through which a person could fall;\\n\\n         \
      \                   ii)    through which any material or object could fall and injure a person; or\\n\\n \
      \                            iii)    giving rise to other risk of injury to any person, unless measures have\\\
      n                  been taken to protect persons against such risk;\\n\\n               f)    be so constructed\
      \ and used, and maintained  in such condition, as to\\n                prevent, so far as is reasonably practicable\
      \ -\\n\\n                          i)     the risk of slipping or tripping; or\\n\\n                     \
      \       ii)    any person being caught between it and any adjacent structure;\\n\\n          g)   where  \
      \ it has moving parts, be prevented by appropriate devices from\\n             moving inadvertently during\
      \ work at height.\\n\\n\\n18.16    Requirements for guardrails, toe-boards, barriers and similar collective\
      \ means of\\n          protection\\n\\n\\n                i)    Unless the context otherwise requires, any\
      \ reference in this section to\\n            means of protection is to a guardrail, toe-board, barrier or\
      \ similar collective\\n            means of protection.\\n\\n                  ii)   Means of protection shall\\\
      n\\n                a)   be of sufficient dimensions, of sufficient strength and rigidity for the\\n     \
      \              purposes for which they are being used, and otherwise suitable;\\n\\n                b)   be\
      \ so placed, secured and used as to ensure, so far as is reasonably\\n                       practicable,\
      \ that they do not become accidentally displaced; and\\n\\n                 c)   be so placed as to prevent,\
      \ so far as is practicable, the fall of any\\n                     person, or of any material or object, from\
      \ any place of work.\\n\\n                  iii)    In relation to work at height involved in construction\
      \ work\\n\\n                a)    the top guard-rail or other similar means of protection shall be at least\\\
      n                  950 millimetres above the edge from which any person is liable to fall;\\n\\n         \
      \       b)    toe-boards shall be suitable and sufficient to prevent the fall of any\\n                  \
      \   person, or any material or object, from any place of work; and\"\n}"

    quote: "{\n  \"pdf_page\": 37,\n  \"text\": \"c)   any intermediate guardrail or similar means of protection\
      \ shall be\\n                                positioned so that any gap between  it and other means of protection\\\
      n                           does not exceed 470 millimetres.\\n\\n                          iv)   Any structure\
      \ or part of a structure which supports means of protection or to\\n                       which means of\
      \ protection are attached shall be of sufficient strength and\\n                           suitable for the\
      \ purpose of such support or attachment.\\n\\n\\n         18.17    Requirements for all Working Platforms\\\
      n\\n\\n                                 i)    Every working platforms requires a supporting structure for\
      \ holding it\\n\\n                                    ii)   Any surface upon which any supporting structure\
      \ rests shall be stable, of\\n                              sufficient  strength and  of  suitable  composition\
      \  safely  to  support  the\\n                         supporting structure, the working platform and any\
      \ loading intended to be\\n                        placed on the working platform.\\n\\n                 \
      \                   iii).    Stability of supporting structure\\n\\n                    Any supporting structure\
      \ shall\\n\\n                           a)   be suitable and of sufficient strength and rigidity for the purpose\
      \ for\\n                            which it is being used;\\n\\n                           b)     in the\
      \ case of a wheeled structure, be prevented by appropriate\\n                              devices from moving\
      \ inadvertently during work at height;\\n\\n                            c)     in other cases, be prevented\
      \ from slipping by secure attachment to\\n                               the bearing surface or to another\
      \ structure, provision of an effective\\n                                      anti-slip device or by other\
      \ means of equivalent effectiveness;\\n\\n                           d)   be stable while being erected, used\
      \ and dismantled; and\\n\\n                           e)   when altered or modified, be so altered or modified\
      \ as to ensure that it\\n                             remains stable.\\n\\n                              \
      \        f)    Have suitable base plates and properly footed thereby.\\n\\n\\n                           \
      \ iv).    Stability of working platforms\\n\\n                  A working platform shall\\n\\n           \
      \                a)   be suitable and of sufficient strength and rigidity for the purpose or\\n          \
      \                  purposes for which it is intended to be used or is being used;\\n\\n                  \
      \         b)   be so erected and used as to ensure that  its components do not\\n                        become\
      \ accidentally displaced so as to endanger any person;\\n\\n                            c)   when altered\
      \ or modified, be so altered or modified as to ensure that it\\n                             remains stable;\
      \ and\\n\\n                           d)   be dismantled in such a way as to prevent accidental displacement.\\\
      n\\n\\n                      v)    Safety on working platforms\\n\\n                  A working platform shall\\\
      n\\n                           a)   be of sufficient dimensions to permit the safe passage of persons and\\\
      n                               the safe use of any plant or materials required to be used and to\\n     \
      \                          provide a safe working area having regard to the work being carried\\n        \
      \                       out there;\\n\\n                           b)   possess a suitable surface and, in\
      \ particular, be so constructed that\\n                               the surface of the working platform\
      \ has no gap\\n\\n                                                     i)      through which a person could\
      \ fall;\\n\\n                                                         ii)      through which any material\
      \ or object could fall and injure a\\n                                      person; or\\n\\n             \
      \                                             iii)      giving  rise  to other  risk  of  injury  to any person,\
      \ unless\\n                                 measures have been taken to protect persons against such\\n  \
      \                                               risk; and\\n\\n                            c)   be so erected\
      \ and used, and maintained in such condition, as to\\n                                prevent, so far as is\
      \ reasonably practicable\\n\\n                                                     i)       the risk of slipping\
      \ or tripping; or\\n\\n                                                         ii)     any person being caught\
      \ between the working platform and\\n                                  any adjacent structure.\"\n}"

    quote: "{\n  \"clause_id\": \"19.0\",\n  \"fragments\": [\n    {\n      \"pdf_page\": 40,\n      \"text\": \"\
      19.0    Overhead protection\\n\\n\\n            All contractors shall provide overhead protections as per\
      \ Rule 41 of BOCWR\\n\\n                i)    Overhead protection should be erected along the periphery of\
      \ every building\\n              which is under construction and the building height shall be 15m or above\\\
      n                  after construction.\\n\\n                  ii)    Overhead protection shall be minimum\
      \ 2m wide and the outer edge shall be\\n           150mm higher than the inner edge and an angle not more\
      \ than 200 to its\\n                 horizontal sloping into the building.\\n\\n                  iii)   Overhead\
      \ protection shall not be erected more than a height of 5m from the\\n             base of the building.\\\
      n\\n             iv)   Areas of inadvertent hazard of  falling of material  shall be guarded or\\n       \
      \        barricaded or roped-off thereby by the contractor.\"\n    }\n  ],\n  \"heading_line\": \"19.0   \

    source_document: Vol3DLNP1.pdf
    source_sha256: 1ee3fc8dfd12f659f34446b0a6db74e1e1cdd4d593ca91b2a48d59bf1ef97d52
    pdf_pages:

    json_sha256: 0042f3256acc51ca4ebb327c3cee57a308fa5f47e1a4ccc7f4994fe898fa11ef
    json_pointer: /clauses/5
    json_record_id: null
    source_review_status: pending_manual_review
    quote: "{\n  \"clause_id\": \"22.0\",\n  \"fragments\": [\n    {\n      \"pdf_page\": 44,\n      \"text\": \"\
      22.0     Launching Operation\\n\\n22.1    As launching operation  is one of the  riskiest job, the contractor\
      \ shall take utmost\\n          precaution  at  all stages  like; planning, establishing casing yard, casting\
      \ segments,\\n          transporting segments,  fabrication and  erection  of launching  girders, launching\
      \  of\\n         segments, pre-stressing, auto launching of girders and dismantling of launching girders.\\\
      n\\n\\n22.2    The contractor shall prepare a comprehensive Method Statement  for the launching\\n       \
      \   operation, adhering to the SHE conditions laid down in conditions of contract on SHE and\\n          project\
      \ SHE manual. Particular reference shall be made to the provisions on working at\\n           height. As the\
      \ entire process of launching has to be undertaken at an elevated level, the\\n          safety of workers\
      \ and the girder is paramount important. The following general guidelines\\n           shall be adhered throughout\
      \ the launching operation.\\n\\n\\n                i)    Necessary ‘working platforms’ and fall protection\
      \ anchorage arrangement shall be\\n               provided in the launching girder itself.\\n\\n         \
      \         ii)    Provisions for mounting light fittings shall also be made available in the launching\\n \
      \                 girder.\\n\\n                  iii)   The casting yard shall be established ensuring the\
      \ provision given in clause 38.0\\n\\n             iv)   The workmen engaged in fabrication of reinforcement,\
      \ concreting the segment\\n                  shall be provided with necessary PPEs including compulsory hand\
      \ protection\\n                gloves.\\n\\n           v)    Casting and curing of segment shall be undertaken\
      \ under the direct supervision of\\n                the responsible engineer of the contractor.\\n\\n    \
      \         vi)   Trucks  with  valid  registration,  licence, safe worthiness  certificate, Employer’s\\n \
      \              approval certificate, and pollution under check certificate shall only be used for\\n     \
      \           transport of segments\\n\\n              vii)   Drivers engaged for driving these trucks, shall\
      \ be trained once in 6 months at\\n                specified locations as directed by the employer on defensive\

- kind: parameter
  text: Overhead protection along the periphery of buildings under construction (height 15m or above) must be at
    least 2m wide, sloping into the building at an angle not exceeding 20 degrees with the outer edge 150mm higher,
    and erected at a height not exceeding 5m from the base.

    quote: "{\n  \"clause_id\": \"19.0\",\n  \"fragments\": [\n    {\n      \"pdf_page\": 40,\n      \"text\": \"\
      19.0    Overhead protection\\n\\n\\n            All contractors shall provide overhead protections as per\
      \ Rule 41 of BOCWR\\n\\n                i)    Overhead protection should be erected along the periphery of\
      \ every building\\n              which is under construction and the building height shall be 15m or above\\\
      n                  after construction.\\n\\n                  ii)    Overhead protection shall be minimum\
      \ 2m wide and the outer edge shall be\\n           150mm higher than the inner edge and an angle not more\
      \ than 200 to its\\n                 horizontal sloping into the building.\\n\\n                  iii)   Overhead\
      \ protection shall not be erected more than a height of 5m from the\\n             base of the building.\\\
      n\\n             iv)   Areas of inadvertent hazard of  falling of material  shall be guarded or\\n       \
      \        barricaded or roped-off thereby by the contractor.\"\n    }\n  ],\n  \"heading_line\": \"19.0   \

  text: Lifting appliances and loose gears must be thoroughly tested and examined by a competent person (approved
    by the Chief Inspector of Factories with Employer permission) at least once every six months, and clearly marked
    with their safe working load and identification.

    quote: "{\n  \"pdf_page\": 42,\n  \"text\": \"21.6    The contractor shall also maintain a register containing\
      \ a system of identification\\n           of all tools and tackles, its date of purchase, safe working load,\
      \ competent person\\n         date of examination etc.\\n\\n\\n21.7     Test and periodical examination of\
      \ lifting appliances and gears\\n\\n\\n21.7.1     All  lifting appliances including  all parts and gears \
      \ thereof, whether  fixed or\\n        movable shall be thoroughly tested and examined by a competent person\
      \ once at\\n           least in every six months or after it has undergone any alterations or repairs liable\\\
      n           to affect its strength or stability. Within the validity,  if the lifting appliances are\\n  \
      \         shifted to a new site, re-examination by the same competent person for ensuring\\n             \
      \ its safety shall also be done.\\n\\n21.7.2    Contractors can  utilise the services of any competent person\
      \ as defined  in\\n          Factories Act, 1948 and approved by Chief Inspector  of Factories with the\\\
      n         permission of the Employer.\\n\\n\\n21.7.3     All alarms and signals  like automatic safe load\
      \ indicators (SLI), boom angle\\n           indicators, boom extension indicators, over lift boom alarm, swing\
      \ alarm, hydraulic\\n          safety valves, mechanical radius indicators, load moment indicators etc. shall\
      \ be\\n           periodically examined and maintained always in working condition\\n\\n\\n21.8     Automatic\
      \ safe load indicators\\n\\n\\n21.8.1   As stipulated in Rule 78 of BOCWKR 2006, no lifting appliances gear\
      \ or any\\n         other material handling appliance is used, if:\\n\\n                i)     the  Inspector\
      \  having  jurisdiction  is  not  satisfied  with  reference  to a\\n                   certification of test\
      \ or examination or to an authenticated record maintain as\\n               provided under these rules; and\\\
      n\\n                  ii)     in the view of such Inspector, the lifting appliance, lifting gear or any other\\\
      n                material  handling  appliance  is  not  safe  for use  in  building  or  other\\n       \
      \         construction work; and\\n\\n                  iii)   no pulley block is used in building or other\
      \ construction work unless the safe\\n               working load and its identification are clearly marked\
      \ on such block.\\n\\n\\n21.9      Qualification of operator of lifting appliances and of signaller etc\\\
      n\\n\\n21.9.1   The contractor shall not employ any person to drive or operate a lifting machine\\n      \
      \      like crane, hydra etc whether driven by mechanical power or otherwise or to give\\n          signals\
      \ to work as a operator of a rigger or derricks unless he\\n\\n                i)      is above twenty-one\
      \ years of age and possesses a valid heavy transport\\n                vehicle driving licence as per Motor\
      \ Vehicle Act and Rules.\\n\\n                  ii)     is absolutely competent and reliable\\n\\n       \
      \           iii)   possesses the knowledge of the inherent risks involved in the operation of\\n         \
      \             lifting appliances by undergoing a formal  training  at any  institution  of\\n            \
      \    national importance acceptable to Employer\\n\\n             iv)     is medically examined periodically\
      \ as specified in schedule VII of BOCW\\n               Rules.\\n\\n\\n21.10    General requirements of appliances\\\
      n\\n\\n21.10.1   Out-of level\\n\\n\\n21.10.1.1 One of the most severe effects of being out-of fit level is\
      \ that side loads develop in\\n          the boom. Because of side loads all mobile cranes lose capacity rapidly\
      \ as the\\n         degree of out-of-level increases and therefore\"\n}"

    json_pointer: /clauses/4/fragments/0

    quote: "{\n  \"pdf_page\": 41,\n  \"text\": \"21.0      Lifting Appliances and Gear\\n\\n\\n          21.1 \
      \      Lifting appliances means a crane, hoist machinery, derrick, winch, gin pole, sheer\\n             \
      \         legs, jack, hoist drum, slewing machinery, slewing bearing fasteners,  loffing\\n              \
      \    machinery sheaves, pulley blocks, hooks or other equipment used  for  lifting\\n                    \
      \ materials, objects or building workers and lifting gears means ropes, chain slings,\\n                 \
      \   shackles, hooks, lifting lugs, wire ropes, lifting eyebolts and eyenuts and other\\n                 \
      \  accessories of a lifting appliance.\\n\\n\\n          21.2    No machine shall be selected to do any lifting\
      \ on a specific job until its size and\\n                     characteristics are considered against:\\n\\\
      n\\n                                 i)     the weights, dimensions and lift radii of the heaviest and largest\
      \ loads\\n\\n                                    ii)    the maximum lift height, the maximum lift radius and\
      \ the weight of the loads\\n                            that must be handled at each\\n\\n               \
      \                      iii)    the number and frequency of lifts to be made\\n\\n                        \
      \  iv)   how long the crane will be required on site\\n\\n                      v)    the type of lifting\
      \ to be done (for example, is precision placement of loads\\n                          important?)\\n\\n \
      \                         vi)    the type of carrier required (this depends on ground conditions and machine\\\
      n                          capacity In its operating quadrants) capacity is normally greatest over the\\n\
      \                             rear, less over the side, and non-existent over the front\\n\\n            \
      \                 vii)   whether loads will have to be walked or carried\\n\\n                           \
      \    viii)  whether loads will have to be suspended for lengthy periods\\n\\n                          ix)\
      \    the site conditions, including the ground where the machine will be set up,\\n                      \
      \ access roads and ramps it must travel, space for erection and any obstacles\\n                         \
      \   that might impede access or operation\\n\\n\\n          21.3    The contractor shall ensure that a valid\
      \ certificate of fitness issued as per clause\\n                   21.5  is available for all lifting appliances\
      \ including synchronised mobile jacks, pre-\\n                    stressing hydraulic jacks, jacks fitted\
      \ with launching girders etc. and Employers\\n                   approval before inducting to the site. Only\
      \ after obtaining the approval from the\\n                Employer any lifting appliances and gear shall be\
      \ used.\\n\\n\\n          21.4    The laminated photocopies  of  fitness  certificate issued by competent\\\
      n                  person, the Employers’ approval letter, the operators’ photo, manufacturer’s\\n       \
      \           load chart and competency certificate shall always be either kept in the\\n                  operator\
      \ cabin or pasted on the visible surface of the lifting appliances.\\n\\n\\n          21.5      All lifting\
      \ appliances and loose gears shall be clearly marked for its safe\\n                 working load and identification\
      \ by stamping or other suitable means.\"\n}"

- kind: parameter
  text: Launching operations require comprehensive method statements, mandatory working platforms and fall protection
    anchorage on launching girders, daily monitoring of vertical deflection, maintenance of an operational register,
    and direct supervision by approved engineers.
  evidence_ids:
  - J885c7e78c6927b04
  relation_type: none
  explicitness: not_a_relation

    heading: Clause 22.0 — Launching Operation
    source_document: Vol3DLNP1.pdf
    source_sha256: 1ee3fc8dfd12f659f34446b0a6db74e1e1cdd4d593ca91b2a48d59bf1ef97d52

    quote: "{\n  \"clause_id\": \"22.0\",\n  \"fragments\": [\n    {\n      \"pdf_page\": 44,\n      \"text\": \"\
      22.0     Launching Operation\\n\\n22.1    As launching operation  is one of the  riskiest job, the contractor\
      \ shall take utmost\\n          precaution  at  all stages  like; planning, establishing casing yard, casting\
      \ segments,\\n          transporting segments,  fabrication and  erection  of launching  girders, launching\
      \  of\\n         segments, pre-stressing, auto launching of girders and dismantling of launching girders.\\\
      n\\n\\n22.2    The contractor shall prepare a comprehensive Method Statement  for the launching\\n       \
      \   operation, adhering to the SHE conditions laid down in conditions of contract on SHE and\\n          project\
      \ SHE manual. Particular reference shall be made to the provisions on working at\\n           height. As the\
      \ entire process of launching has to be undertaken at an elevated level, the\\n          safety of workers\
      \ and the girder is paramount important. The following general guidelines\\n           shall be adhered throughout\
      \ the launching operation.\\n\\n\\n                i)    Necessary ‘working platforms’ and fall protection\
      \ anchorage arrangement shall be\\n               provided in the launching girder itself.\\n\\n         \
      \         ii)    Provisions for mounting light fittings shall also be made available in the launching\\n \
      \                 girder.\\n\\n                  iii)   The casting yard shall be established ensuring the\
      \ provision given in clause 38.0\\n\\n             iv)   The workmen engaged in fabrication of reinforcement,\
      \ concreting the segment\\n                  shall be provided with necessary PPEs including compulsory hand\
      \ protection\\n                gloves.\\n\\n           v)    Casting and curing of segment shall be undertaken\
      \ under the direct supervision of\\n                the responsible engineer of the contractor.\\n\\n    \
      \         vi)   Trucks  with  valid  registration,  licence, safe worthiness  certificate, Employer’s\\n \
      \              approval certificate, and pollution under check certificate shall only be used for\\n     \
      \           transport of segments\\n\\n              vii)   Drivers engaged for driving these trucks, shall\
      \ be trained once in 6 months at\\n                specified locations as directed by the employer on defensive\
      \ driving.\\n\\n               viii)   Drivers shall also have undergone proper medical examination as per\
      \ relevant\\n               clause mentioned under ‘Medical Facilities’.\\n\\n             ix)   The segments\
      \ shall rigidly secured to the truck with necessary wooden wedges\\n             and necessary red indicators/safety\
      \ tapes provided so that the vehicle is clearly\\n             seen by other road users both in day / night\
      \ time.\\n\\n           x)    Every launching girder shall have a responsible engineer on duty all the time.\\\
      n\\n             xi)    All the time from erection to dismantling the area between the two piers\\n      \
      \        wherein launching is in progress shall always be barricaded.\\n\\n              xii)   Unloading\
      \  of  segments  from  trucks,  lifting  of  segments,  shifting  of\\n              segments, gluing shall\
      \ be done under the direct supervision of the approved\\n               engineer of the contractor.\\n\\n\
      \               xiii)  Auto launching shall be done only after approval from the Employer. After\\n      \
      \         every auto launching the stability of launching girder shall be ensured.\\n\\n            xiv) \
      \ The vertical deflection of launching girder shall be monitored at all critical\\n               stages like\
      \ with/without loads and after every auto launching.\\n\\n          xv)  A  register containing  all important\
      \ operational  details from erection  to\\n                dismantling of launching girders shall be maintained\
      \ and made available to\\n              Employer whenever called for.\\n\\n            xvi)  Test  certificate\
      \  for  all  lifting  gears  including  Macalloy  bars  shall be\\n               maintained at a location\
      \ closer to the launching girder itself so that it can be\\n                referred during all inspections.\\\
      n\\n             xvii)  Adequate lighting at all time shall be ensured in the entire area of operation.\"\n\
      \    },\n    {\n      \"pdf_page\": 45,\n      \"text\": \"xviii) Access to drinking water & toilet shall\
      \ be ensured to all workmen engaged\\n                              for launching process.\\n\\n         \
      \              xix)  Proper access ladders/stairways shall be maintained for safe ascending  /\\n        \
      \               descending of workmen / engineers.\\n\\n\\n          22.3     Non-adherence to any of the\
      \ clauses mentioned above shall be viewed\\n                   seriously by the Employer and penalty levied\
      \ as per relevant clause.\"\n    }\n  ],\n  \"heading_line\": \"22.0     Launching Operation\",\n  \"retained_lines\"\

    heading: Clause 26.0 — Site Electricity
    source_document: Vol3DLNP1.pdf
    source_sha256: 1ee3fc8dfd12f659f34446b0a6db74e1e1cdd4d593ca91b2a48d59bf1ef97d52

    json_path: parsed_json/vol3/part_2_safety/safety_clauses.json
    json_sha256: 0042f3256acc51ca4ebb327c3cee57a308fa5f47e1a4ccc7f4994fe898fa11ef
    json_pointer: /clauses/9/fragments/2
    json_record_id: null
    source_review_status: pending_manual_review
    quote: "{\n  \"pdf_page\": 48,\n  \"text\": \"26.7      Electrical protection circuits\\n\\n26.7.1    Precautions\
      \ shall be taken, either by earthing or by other suitable means, to prevent\\n         danger arising when\
      \ any conductor (other than a  circuit conductor) which may\\n         reasonably foreseeable become charged\
      \ as a result of either the use of a system, or a\\n            fault in a system, becomes so charged. A conductor\
      \ shall be regarded as earthed\\n        when conductors of sufficient strength and current-carrying capability\
      \ to discharge\\n           electrical energy to earth connect it to the general mass of earth.\\n\\n    \
      \            If a circuit conductor is connected to earth or to any other reference point, nothing\\n    \
      \     which might reasonably be expected to give rise to danger by breaking the electrical\\n           continuity\
      \ or introducing high impedance shall be placed in that conductor unless\\n          suitable precautions\
      \ are taken to prevent that danger.\\n\\n\\n26.7.2    Appropriate electrical protection shall be provided\
      \ for all circuits, against over load,\\n          short circuit and earth fault current.\\n\\n\\n26.7.3 \
      \  The contractor shall provide sufficient ELCBs (maintain sensitivity 30 mA) / RCCBs for\\n             \
      \ all the equipments (including Potable equipments), electrical switchboards, distribution\\n         panels\
      \ etc. to prevent electrical shocks to the workers.\\n\\n\\n26.7.4     All protection devices shall be capable\
      \ of interrupting the circuit without damage to any\\n         equipments and circuits in case of any fault\
      \ may occur.\\n\\n\\n26.7.5    Rating of fuses and circuit breakers used for the protection of circuits should\
      \ be\\n          coordinate with equipment power ratings.\\n\\n\\n26.7.6    Protection against lightning shall\
      \ be ensured to all equipment kept in open at sites.\\n\\n\\n26.8     Cables:\\n\\n\\n26.8.1   Cables shall\
      \ be selected after full consideration of the condition to which they shall be\\n        exposed and the duties\
      \ for which they are required. Supply cable up to 3.3 kV shall be\\n            in accordance with BS 6346.\\\
      n\\n\\n26.8.2   For supplies to mobile or transportable equipment where operating of the equipment\\n    \
      \      subjects the cable to flexing, the cable shall conform to any of these codes BS 6007 /\\n       BS\
      \ 6500 / BS 7375.\\n\\n\\n26.8.3    Flexible cords with a conductor cross sectional area smaller than 1.5\
      \ mm2 shall not be\\n        used and insulated flexible cable shall conform to BS 6500 and BS 7375.\\n\\\
      n\\n26.8.4   Where low voltage cables are to be used, reference shall be made to BS 7375. The\\n         \
      \ following standards shall also be referred to particularly for under ground cables BS\\n        6346 and\
      \ BS 6708\\n\\n\\n26.8.5   Cables buried directly in the ground shall be of a type incorporating armour or\
      \ metal\\n         sheath or both. Such cables shall be marked by cable covers or a suitable marking\\n  \
      \       tape and be buried at a  sufficient depth to avoid  their being damaged by any\\n          disturbance\
      \ of the ground. Cable routes shall be marked on the plans kept in the site\\n           electrical register.\\\
      n\\n26.8.6    Cabling passing under the walk way and across way  for transport and mobile\\n         equipment\
      \ shall be laid in ducts at a minimum depth of 0.6 meters.\\n\\n26.8.7   Cables that need to cross open areas,\
      \ or where span of 3m or more are involved, a\\n         catenary wire on poles or other supports shall be\
      \ provided for convenient means of\\n         suspension. Minimum height shall be 6 m above ground.\\n\\n\\\
      n26.8.8   Cables carrying a voltage to earth in excess of 65V other than supply for welding\\n         process\
      \ shall have metal armour or sheath, which has been effectively earthed and\\n         monitored by the contractor.\
      \ In case of flexible and trailing cables such earthed metal\"\n}"

      \ sum of total of maximum limits set out for each building\\n         worker separately as mentioned in the\
      \ table above.\"\n    }\n  ],\n  \"heading_line\": \"25.0    Manual lifting and carrying of excessive weight\"\

    source_document: Vol3DLNP1.pdf
    source_sha256: 1ee3fc8dfd12f659f34446b0a6db74e1e1cdd4d593ca91b2a48d59bf1ef97d52

    json_pointer: /clauses/6
    json_record_id: null
