    quote: "{\n  \"clause_id\": \"23.0\",\n  \"fragments\": [\n    {\n      \"pdf_page\": 45,\n      \"text\": \"\
      23.0     Construction machinery\\n\\n\\n          23.1     Construction machineries may include dumpers and\
      \ dump trucks,  lift trucks and\\n                     telescopic handlers piling rigs, vibro hammers, rail\
      \ welding equipments, mobile\\n                    elevating work platforms, cranes, tipper lorries, lorry\
      \ loaders, skip wagons, 360°\\n                    excavators, 180° backhoe loaders, crawler tractors, scrapers,\
      \ graders, loading\\n                    shovels,  trenchers,  side  booms,  pavers,  planers,  chippers,\
      \  road  rollers,\\n                    locomotives, tankers and bowsers, trailers, hydraulic and mechanical\
      \ breakers\\n                       etc.\\n\\n\\n          23.2     Safe worthiness certificate\\n\\n\\n \
      \         23.2.1   Every construction equipment shall be in sound mechanical working condition and\\n    \
      \                   certified by  either competent person under Factories Act  or manufacturers’\\n      \
      \             warranty in case of brand new equipments or authorized persons / firms approved\\n         \
      \        by Employer before induction to any site.\\n\\n\\n          23.2.2   Every such  certificate  shall\
      \ have  the  date  of  purchase, main  overhauling\\n                  undertaken in the past, any accident\
      \ to the equipment, visual examination details,\\n                          critical components safety check,\
      \ list of safety devises and its working condition,\\n                   manufacturer’s maintenance checklist,\
      \ past projects wherein the equipments were\\n                 used etc as its minimum content.\\n\\n\\n \
      \         23.3     Reverse Horns\\n\\n\\n          23.3.1    All Vehicles shall be fitted with audible reverse\
      \ alarms and maintained in\\n               good working condition. Reversing  shall be done only when there\
      \  is\\n                 adequate rear view visibility or under the directions of a banksman\\n\\n\\n    \
      \      23.4     General operating procedures\\n\\n\\n                                 i)     Drivers entering\
      \ site shall be instructed to follow the safe system of work adopted on\\n                               \
      \ site. These shall be verbal instructions or, preferably, written instructions showing\\n               \
      \           the relevant site rules, the site layout, delivery areas, speed limits, etc.\\n\\n           \
      \                         ii)   No passengers shall be carried, unless specific seating has been provided\
      \  in\\n                       accordance with the manufacturers’ recommendations.\\n\\n                 \
      \                    iii)   Working on gradients beyond any equipments capability shall not be allowed.\\\
      n\\n                          iv)   Prevention of dumper and dump truck accidents should be managed by providing\\\
      n                       wheel stops at a sufficient distance from the edges of excavations, spoil heaps, pits,\\\
      n                             etc.\\n\\n                      v)   The manufacturer’s recommended bucket size\
      \ must not be exceeded in excavators.\\n\\n                          vi)      If excavators operating on a\
      \ gradient which cannot be avoided, it must be ensured\\n                            that the working cycle\
      \ is slowed down, that the bucket is not extended too far in the\\n                          downhill direction,\
      \ and that travel  is undertaken with extreme caution. A large\\n                         excavator must never\
      \ be permitted to travel in a confined area, or around people,\\n                          without a banksman\
      \ to guide the driver, who should have the excavator attachment\\n                         close in to the\
      \ machine, with the bucket just clear of the ground. On wheeled\\n                         excavators, it\
      \ is essential that the tyres are in good condition and correctly inflated.\\n                           \
      \                If stabilizing devices are  fitted, they should be employed when the machine  is\\n     \
      \                     excavating.\"\n    },\n    {\n      \"pdf_page\": 46,\n      \"text\": \"vii)  When\
      \ the front shovel of the 1800 backhoe loaders is being employed, the backhoe\\n               attachment\
      \ shall be in its “travel” position, with the safety locking device in place.\\n\\n               viii)  When\
      \ operating the backhoe in poor ground conditions, the stabilisers tend to sink\\n                  into the\
      \ surface of the ground, reducing stability. Therefore frequent checks shall be\\n           made for the\
      \ stability of the machine. The loading shovel should always be lowered\\n                 to the ground to\
      \ stabilise the machine when the backhoe is employed.\\n\\n             ix)   The netting operation of the\
      \ skip wagons should be carried out prior to lifting the\\n                skip to reduce the risks of working\
      \ on the rear platform\\n\\n           x)       If a tractor dozer is employed on clearing scrub or felling\
      \ trees, it shall be provided\\n                with adequate driver protection.\\n\\n             xi)   When\
      \ two or more scrapers are working on the same job, a minimum distance of at\\n                 least 25m\
      \ shall be kept between them.\\n\\n              xii)   Incase of hydraulic breakers, hydraulic rams and hoses\
      \ shall be in good working\\n                condition\\n\\n\\n23.5       All wood working machines shall\
      \ be fitted with suitable guards and devices such as top\\n          guard, riving knife, push stick, guards\
      \ for drive belts and chains, and emergency stop\\n          switch easily accessible by the operator.\\n\\\
      n\\n23.6     Penalty\\n\\n\\n23.6.1      If any of the above clauses are not adhered, penalty shall be imposed\
      \ as per\\n         relevant clause depending upon the gravity of the unsafe act and or condition.\"\n   \
      \ }\n  ],\n  \"heading_line\": \"          23.0     Construction machinery\",\n  \"retained_lines\": [\n \

      \    {\n      \"pdf_page\": 45,\n      \"source_line_number\": 52,\n      \"text\": \"\"\n    },\n    {\n\
      \      \"pdf_page\": 45,\n      \"source_line_number\": 53,\n      \"text\": \"                          \
      \       i)     Drivers entering site shall be instructed to follow the safe system of work adopted on\"\n\
      \    },\n    {\n      \"pdf_page\": 45,\n      \"source_line_number\": 54,\n      \"text\": \"           \
      \                     site. These shall be verbal instructions or, preferably, written instructions showing\"\
      \n    },\n    {\n      \"pdf_page\": 45,\n      \"source_line_number\": 55,\n      \"text\": \"          \
      \                the relevant site rules, the site layout, delivery areas, speed limits, etc.\"\n    },\n\
      \    {\n      \"pdf_page\": 45,\n      \"source_line_number\": 56,\n      \"text\": \"\"\n    },\n    {\n\
      \      \"pdf_page\": 45,\n      \"source_line_number\": 57,\n      \"text\": \"                          \
      \          ii)   No passengers shall be carried, unless specific seating has been provided  in\"\n    },\n\
      \    {\n      \"pdf_page\": 45,\n      \"source_line_number\": 58,\n      \"text\": \"                   \
      \    accordance with the manufacturers’ recommendations.\"\n    },\n    {\n      \"pdf_page\": 45,\n     \
      \ \"source_line_number\": 59,\n      \"text\": \"\"\n    },\n    {\n      \"pdf_page\": 45,\n      \"source_line_number\"\
      : 60,\n      \"text\": \"                                     iii)   Working on gradients beyond any equipments\
      \ capability shall not be allowed.\"\n    },\n    {\n      \"pdf_page\": 45,\n      \"source_line_number\"\
      : 61,\n      \"text\": \"\"\n    },\n    {\n      \"pdf_page\": 45,\n      \"source_line_number\": 62,\n \
      \     \"text\": \"                          iv)   Prevention of dumper and dump truck accidents should be\
      \ managed by providing\"\n    },\n    {\n      \"pdf_page\": 45,\n      \"source_line_number\": 63,\n    \
      \  \"text\": \"                       wheel stops at a sufficient distance from the edges of excavations,\
      \ spoil heaps, pits,\"\n    },\n    {\n      \"pdf_page\": 45,\n      \"source_line_number\": 64,\n      \"\
      text\": \"                             etc.\"\n    },\n    {\n      \"pdf_page\": 45,\n      \"source_line_number\"\
      : 65,\n      \"text\": \"\"\n    },\n    {\n      \"pdf_page\": 45,\n      \"source_line_number\": 66,\n \
      \     \"text\": \"                      v)   The manufacturer’s recommended bucket size must not be exceeded\
      \ in excavators.\"\n    },\n    {\n      \"pdf_page\": 45,\n      \"source_line_number\": 67,\n      \"text\"\
      : \"\"\n    },\n    {\n      \"pdf_page\": 45,\n      \"source_line_number\": 68,\n      \"text\": \"    \
      \                      vi)      If excavators operating on a gradient which cannot be avoided, it must be\
      \ ensured\"\n    },\n    {\n      \"pdf_page\": 45,\n      \"source_line_number\": 69,\n      \"text\": \"\
      \                            that the working cycle is slowed down, that the bucket is not extended too far\
      \ in the\"\n    },\n    {\n      \"pdf_page\": 45,\n      \"source_line_number\": 70,\n      \"text\": \"\
      \                          downhill direction, and that travel  is undertaken with extreme caution. A large\"\
      \n    },\n    {\n      \"pdf_page\": 45,\n      \"source_line_number\": 71,\n      \"text\": \"          \
      \               excavator must never be permitted to travel in a confined area, or around people,\"\n    },\n\
      \    {\n      \"pdf_page\": 45,\n      \"source_line_number\": 72,\n      \"text\": \"                   \
      \       without a banksman to guide the driver, who should have the excavator attachment\"\n    },\n    {\n\
      \      \"pdf_page\": 45,\n      \"source_line_number\": 73,\n      \"text\": \"                         close\
      \ in to the machine, with the bucket just clear of the ground. On wheeled\"\n    },\n    {\n      \"pdf_page\"\
      : 45,\n      \"source_line_number\": 74,\n      \"text\": \"                         excavators, it is essential\
      \ that the tyres are in good condition and correctly inflated.\"\n    },\n    {\n      \"pdf_page\": 45,\n\
      \      \"source_line_number\": 75,\n      \"text\": \"                                           If stabilizing\
      \ devices are  fitted, they should be employed when the machine  is\"\n    },\n    {\n      \"pdf_page\":\
      \ 45,\n      \"source_line_number\": 76,\n      \"text\": \"                          excavating.\"\n    },\n\
      \    {\n      \"pdf_page\": 45,\n      \"source_line_number\": 77,\n      \"text\": \"\"\n    },\n    {\n\
      \      \"pdf_page\": 45,\n      \"source_line_number\": 78,\n      \"text\": \"\"\n    },\n    {\n      \"\
      pdf_page\": 45,\n      \"source_line_number\": 79,\n      \"text\": \"\"\n    },\n    {\n      \"pdf_page\"\
      : 45,\n      \"source_line_number\": 80,\n      \"text\": \"\"\n    },\n    {\n      \"pdf_page\": 46,\n \
      \     \"source_line_number\": 3,\n      \"text\": \"              vii)  When the front shovel of the 1800\
      \ backhoe loaders is being employed, the backhoe\"\n    },\n    {\n      \"pdf_page\": 46,\n      \"source_line_number\"\
      : 4,\n      \"text\": \"               attachment shall be in its “travel” position, with the safety locking\
      \ device in place.\"\n    },\n    {\n      \"pdf_page\": 46,\n      \"source_line_number\": 5,\n      \"text\"\
      : \"\"\n    },\n    {\n      \"pdf_page\": 46,\n      \"source_line_number\": 6,\n      \"text\": \"     \
      \          viii)  When operating the backhoe in poor ground conditions, the stabilisers tend to sink\"\n \
      \   },\n    {\n      \"pdf_page\": 46,\n      \"source_line_number\": 7,\n      \"text\": \"             \
      \     into the surface of the ground, reducing stability. Therefore frequent checks shall be\"\n    },\n \
      \   {\n      \"pdf_page\": 46,\n      \"source_line_number\": 8,\n      \"text\": \"           made for the\
      \ stability of the machine. The loading shovel should always be lowered\"\n    },\n    {\n      \"pdf_page\"\
      : 46,\n      \"source_line_number\": 9,\n      \"text\": \"                 to the ground to stabilise the\
      \ machine when the backhoe is employed.\"\n    },\n    {\n      \"pdf_page\": 46,\n      \"source_line_number\"\
      : 10,\n      \"text\": \"\"\n    },\n    {\n      \"pdf_page\": 46,\n      \"source_line_number\": 11,\n \
      \     \"text\": \"             ix)   The netting operation of the skip wagons should be carried out prior\
      \ to lifting the\"\n    },\n    {\n      \"pdf_page\": 46,\n      \"source_line_number\": 12,\n      \"text\"\
      : \"                skip to reduce the risks of working on the rear platform\"\n    },\n    {\n      \"pdf_page\"\
      : 46,\n      \"source_line_number\": 13,\n      \"text\": \"\"\n    },\n    {\n      \"pdf_page\": 46,\n \
      \     \"source_line_number\": 14,\n      \"text\": \"           x)       If a tractor dozer is employed on\
      \ clearing scrub or felling trees, it shall be provided\"\n    },\n    {\n      \"pdf_page\": 46,\n      \"\
      source_line_number\": 15,\n      \"text\": \"                with adequate driver protection.\"\n    },\n\
      \    {\n      \"pdf_page\": 46,\n      \"source_line_number\": 16,\n      \"text\": \"\"\n    },\n    {\n\
      \      \"pdf_page\": 46,\n      \"source_line_number\": 17,\n      \"text\": \"             xi)   When two\
      \ or more scrapers are working on the same job, a minimum distance of at\"\n    },\n    {\n      \"pdf_page\"\
      : 46,\n      \"source_line_number\": 18,\n      \"text\": \"                 least 25m shall be kept between\
      \ them.\"\n    },\n    {\n      \"pdf_page\": 46,\n      \"source_line_number\": 19,\n      \"text\": \"\"\
      \n    },\n    {\n      \"pdf_page\": 46,\n      \"source_line_number\": 20,\n      \"text\": \"          \
      \    xii)   Incase of hydraulic breakers, hydraulic rams and hoses shall be in good working\"\n    },\n  \
      \  {\n      \"pdf_page\": 46,\n      \"source_line_number\": 21,\n      \"text\": \"                condition\"\
      \n    },\n    {\n      \"pdf_page\": 46,\n      \"source_line_number\": 22,\n      \"text\": \"\"\n    },\n\
      \    {\n      \"pdf_page\": 46,\n      \"source_line_number\": 23,\n      \"text\": \"\"\n    },\n    {\n\
      \      \"pdf_page\": 46,\n      \"source_line_number\": 24,\n      \"text\": \"23.5       All wood working\
      \ machines shall be fitted with suitable guards and devices such as top\"\n    },\n    {\n      \"pdf_page\"\
      : 46,\n      \"source_line_number\": 25,\n      \"text\": \"          guard, riving knife, push stick, guards\
      \ for drive belts and chains, and emergency stop\"\n    },\n    {\n      \"pdf_page\": 46,\n      \"source_line_number\"\
      : 26,\n      \"text\": \"          switch easily accessible by the operator.\"\n    },\n    {\n      \"pdf_page\"\
      : 46,\n      \"source_line_number\": 27,\n      \"text\": \"\"\n    },\n    {\n      \"pdf_page\": 46,\n \
      \     \"source_line_number\": 28,\n      \"text\": \"\"\n    },\n    {\n      \"pdf_page\": 46,\n      \"\
      source_line_number\": 29,\n      \"text\": \"23.6     Penalty\"\n    },\n    {\n      \"pdf_page\": 46,\n\
      \      \"source_line_number\": 30,\n      \"text\": \"\"\n    },\n    {\n      \"pdf_page\": 46,\n      \"\
      source_line_number\": 31,\n      \"text\": \"\"\n    },\n    {\n      \"pdf_page\": 46,\n      \"source_line_number\"\
      : 32,\n      \"text\": \"23.6.1      If any of the above clauses are not adhered, penalty shall be imposed\
      \ as per\"\n    },\n    {\n      \"pdf_page\": 46,\n      \"source_line_number\": 33,\n      \"text\": \"\
      \         relevant clause depending upon the gravity of the unsafe act and or condition.\"\n    },\n    {\n\
      \      \"pdf_page\": 46,\n      \"source_line_number\": 34,\n      \"text\": \"\"\n    },\n    {\n      \"\
      pdf_page\": 46,\n      \"source_line_number\": 35,\n      \"text\": \"\"\n    }\n  ],\n  \"review_status\"\
      : \"pending_manual_review\",\n  \"title\": \"Construction machinery\"\n}"

    heading: Clause 26.0 — Site Electricity
    source_document: Vol3DLNP1.pdf
    source_sha256: 1ee3fc8dfd12f659f34446b0a6db74e1e1cdd4d593ca91b2a48d59bf1ef97d52
    pdf_pages:
    - 49
    sheet_cells: ''
    json_path: parsed_json/vol3/part_2_safety/safety_clauses.json
    json_sha256: 0042f3256acc51ca4ebb327c3cee57a308fa5f47e1a4ccc7f4994fe898fa11ef
    json_pointer: /clauses/9/fragments/3
    json_record_id: null
    source_review_status: pending_manual_review
    quote: "{\n  \"pdf_page\": 49,\n  \"text\": \"sheath and/or armour should be in addition to the earth core in\
      \ the cable and shall not\\n                be used as the protective conductor.\\n\\n\\n          26.8.9\
      \   Armoured cables having an over-sheath of polyvinyl chloride (PVC) or an  oil\\n                      resisting\
      \ and flame retardant compound shall be used whenever there is a risk of\\n                  mechanical damage\
      \ occurring\\n\\n\\n          26.9     Plugs, socket-outlets and couplers:\\n\\n\\n          26.9.1   The\
      \ contractor shall ensure plugs, socket-outlets, and couplers available in\\n                  the construction\
      \  site as “splash proof” type. The minimum degree of\\n                  Ingress Protection should be of\
      \ IP44 in accordance with BS EN 60529.\\n\\n\\n          26.9.2   Only plugs and fittings of the weatherproof\
      \ type shall be used and they should be colour\\n                 coded in accordance with the Internationally\
      \ recognised standards for example as detailed\\n                 as follows:\\n\\n                      (a)\
      \   110 volts : Yellow.\\n\\n                      (b)   240 volts : Blue.\\n\\n                       (c)\
      \   415 volts : Red.\\n\\n         26.10    Connections\\n\\n          26.10.1  Every joint and connection\
      \ in a system shall be mechanically and electrically\\n                   suitable  for  use  to  prevent\
      \  danger.  Proper  cable  connectors  as  per\\n                    national/international standards shall\
      \ only be used to connect cables.\\n\\n          26.10.2  No loose connections or tapped joints shall be allowed\
      \ any where in the work\\n                       site, office area, stores and other areas. Penalty as per\
      \ relevant clause shall be\\n                  put in case of observation of any tapped joints.\\n\\n\\n \
      \        26.11    Portable and hand-held equipments:\\n\\n\\n          26.11.1  The contractor shall ensure\
      \ the use of double insulated or all-insulated portable\\n                       electrical hand equipment\
      \ may be used without earthing (i.e. two core cables), but\\n                   they shall still be used only\
      \ on 110V because of the risk of damage to trailing leads.\\n\\n\\n         26.12    Other equipments:\\n\\\
      n\\n          26.12.1   All equipment shall have the provision for major switch/cut-off switch in the equipment\\\
      n                           itself.\\n\\n\\n          26.12.2   All non-current carrying metal parts of electrical\
      \ equipment shall be earthed through\\n                    insulated cable\\n\\n\\n          26.12.3   Isolate\
      \ exposed high-voltage (over 415 Volts) equipment, such as transformer banks,\\n                open switches,\
      \ and similar equipment with exposed energized parts and prevent\\n                   unauthorised access.\\\
      n\\n\\n          26.12.4  Approved perimeter markings shall be used to isolate restricted areas from designated\\\
      n                 work areas and entryways and shall be erected before work begins and maintained for\\n \
      \                     entire duration of work. Approved perimeter marking shall be installed  with either\
      \ red\\n                      barrier tape printed with the words \\\"DANGER—HIGH VOLTAGE\\\" or a barrier\
      \ of yellow\\n                     or orange synthetic rope, approximately 1 to 1.5 meter above the floor\
      \ or work\\n                    surface.\\n\\n\\n         26.13   Work on or near live conductors\"\n}"

    okf_path: OKF_bundle/Technical/Vol3/vol3_part2.md

    heading: Clause 26.0 — Site Electricity
    source_document: Vol3DLNP1.pdf

    pdf_pages:
    - 47
    sheet_cells: ''
    json_path: parsed_json/vol3/part_2_safety/safety_clauses.json
    json_sha256: 0042f3256acc51ca4ebb327c3cee57a308fa5f47e1a4ccc7f4994fe898fa11ef
    json_pointer: /clauses/9/fragments/1
    json_record_id: null
    source_review_status: pending_manual_review
    quote: "{\n  \"pdf_page\": 47,\n  \"text\": \"26.2.1   The contractor shall assess the size and location of\
      \ the electrical loads and the\\n                manner in which they vary with time during the currency of\
      \ the contract.\\n\\n\\n          26.2.2   The contractor shall elaborate as to how the total supply is to\
      \ be obtained  /\\n                   generated. The  details  of  the  source  of  electricity,  earthing\
      \  requirement,\\n                    substation  / panel boards, distribution system shall be prepared and\
      \ necessary\\n                   approval from Employer obtained before proceeding of the execution of the\
      \ job.\\n\\n\\n          26.2.3   The main contractor shall take consideration, the requirements of the sub\
      \ /\\n                   petty contractors’ electric power supply and arrive at the capacity of main\\n  \
      \               source of power supply from diesel generators.\\n\\n\\n          26.2.4   As the sub / petty\
      \ contractors’ small capacity generators create more noise\\n               and safety hazard, no small capacity\
      \ diesel generators shall be allowed for\\n                 whatsoever the type of job to be executed under\
      \ this contract.\\n\\n\\n          26.2.5      If any unsafe noise making small capacity diesel generators\
      \ are found used\\n                by sub / petty contractors the main contractor shall only be penalised.\\\
      n\\n\\n          26.3    Work on site\\n\\n\\n          26.3.1   The contractor shall also submit electrical\
      \ single line diagram, schematic\\n                diagram and the  details of the equipment  for  all temporary\
      \  electrical\\n                     installation and these diagrams together with the temporary  electrical\\\
      n                equipment shall be submitted to the Employer’s for necessary approval.\\n               \
      \    Failure to do so shall invite penalty as per relevant clause.\\n\\n\\n          26.4     Strength and\
      \ capability of electrical equipment\\n\\n\\n          26.4.1   No electrical equipment shall be put into\
      \ use where its strength and capability may\\n                be exceeded in such a way as may give rise to\
      \ danger.\\n\\n\\n          26.5     Adverse or hazardous environments\\n\\n          26.5.1    Electrical\
      \ equipment, which may reasonably foreseably be exposed to-\\n\\n                      (a)   mechanical damage;\\\
      n                      (b)   the effects of the weather, natural hazards, temperature or pressure;\\n    \
      \                   (c)   the effects of wet, dirty, dusty or corrosive conditions; or\\n                \
      \      (d)   any flammable or explosive substance, including dusts, vapours or gases,\\n                 \
      \            shall be of such construction or as necessary protected as to prevent, so far\\n            \
      \          as is reasonably practicable, danger arising from such exposure.\\n\\n\\n\\n          26.6    \
      \  Distribution system:\\n\\n\\n          26.6.1   The contractor shall provide distribution system for control\
      \ and distribution of\\n                        electricity from a main AC supply of 50Hz for typical appliances,\\\
      n\\n\\n                                 i)    Fixed plant – 400V 3 phase\\n\\n                           \
      \         ii)    Movable plant fed via trailing cable over 3.75 kW – 400 3 phase\\n\\n                   \
      \                  iii)    Installation in site buildings – 230V single phase\\n\\n                      \
      \    iv)   Fixed flood lighting – 230V single phase\\n\\n                      v)    Portable and hand tools\
      \ – 115V single phase\\n\\n                          vi)    Site lighting  - 115V single phase\\n\\n     \
      \                        vii)   Portable hand lamps – 115V single phase\"\n}"

    quote: "{\n  \"pdf_page\": 50,\n  \"text\": \"26.13.1  No person shall be engaged in any work activity on or\
      \ so near any live conductor\\n          (other than one suitably covered with insulating material so as to\
      \ prevent danger) that\\n         danger may arise unless-\\n\\n          a)       it is unreasonable in all\
      \ the circumstances for it to be dead; and\\n          b)       it is reasonable in all the circumstances\
      \ for him to be at work on or near it while\\n                             it is live; and\\n           c)\
      \    suitable  precautions  (including where necessary  the  provision  of  suitable\\n                 protective\
      \ equipment) are taken to prevent injury.\\n\\n\\n26.14    Inspection and Maintenance\\n\\n\\n26.14.1   All\
      \ electrical equipment should be permanently numbered and a record kept of the\\n         date of issue, date\
      \ of last inspection and recommended inspection period.\\n\\n\\n26.14.2  Fixed installations shall be inspected\
      \ at least at three monthly intervals; routine\\n         maintenance  being  carried  out  in  accordance\
      \  with  equipment  manufactures\\n         recommendations.\"\n}"

- kind: parameter
  text: Temporary electrical distribution systems require ELCBs or RCCBs with a sensitivity of 30 mA for all equipment,
    portable equipment, and distribution panels.
  evidence_ids:
  - J026fff02246527c2
  relation_type: none
  explicitness: not_a_relation
  from_id: ''
  to_id: ''
  id: Cd27df608bb6233e5
  citations:
  - id: J026fff02246527c2
    okf_path: OKF_bundle/Technical/Vol3/vol3_part2.md
    okf_sha256: ee80a88bd673202495b104f1e039fd2b85ddf8e2f3b2cbbf98523266c0f35b6c
    heading: Clause 26.0 — Site Electricity
    source_document: Vol3DLNP1.pdf
    source_sha256: 1ee3fc8dfd12f659f34446b0a6db74e1e1cdd4d593ca91b2a48d59bf1ef97d52
    pdf_pages:
    - 48
    sheet_cells: ''
    json_path: parsed_json/vol3/part_2_safety/safety_clauses.json
    json_sha256: 0042f3256acc51ca4ebb327c3cee57a308fa5f47e1a4ccc7f4994fe898fa11ef
    json_pointer: /clauses/9/fragments/2
    json_record_id: null
    source_review_status: pending_manual_review
    quote: "{\n  \"pdf_page\": 48,\n  \"text\": \"26.7      Electrical protection circuits\\n\\n26.7.1    Precautions\
      \ shall be taken, either by earthing or by other suitable means, to prevent\\n         danger arising when\
      \ any conductor (other than a  circuit conductor) which may\\n         reasonably foreseeable become charged\
      \ as a result of either the use of a system, or a\\n            fault in a system, becomes so charged. A conductor\
      \ shall be regarded as earthed\\n        when conductors of sufficient strength and current-carrying capability\
      \ to discharge\\n           electrical energy to earth connect it to the general mass of earth.\\n\\n    \
      \            If a circuit conductor is connected to earth or to any other reference point, nothing\\n    \
      \     which might reasonably be expected to give rise to danger by breaking the electrical\\n           continuity\
      \ or introducing high impedance shall be placed in that conductor unless\\n          suitable precautions\
      \ are taken to prevent that danger.\\n\\n\\n26.7.2    Appropriate electrical protection shall be provided\
      \ for all circuits, against over load,\\n          short circuit and earth fault current.\\n\\n\\n26.7.3 \
      \  The contractor shall provide sufficient ELCBs (maintain sensitivity 30 mA) / RCCBs for\\n             \
      \ all the equipments (including Potable equipments), electrical switchboards, distribution\\n         panels\
      \ etc. to prevent electrical shocks to the workers.\\n\\n\\n26.7.4     All protection devices shall be capable\
      \ of interrupting the circuit without damage to any\\n         equipments and circuits in case of any fault\
      \ may occur.\\n\\n\\n26.7.5    Rating of fuses and circuit breakers used for the protection of circuits should\
      \ be\\n          coordinate with equipment power ratings.\\n\\n\\n26.7.6    Protection against lightning shall\
      \ be ensured to all equipment kept in open at sites.\\n\\n\\n26.8     Cables:\\n\\n\\n26.8.1   Cables shall\
      \ be selected after full consideration of the condition to which they shall be\\n        exposed and the duties\
      \ for which they are required. Supply cable up to 3.3 kV shall be\\n            in accordance with BS 6346.\\\
      n\\n\\n26.8.2   For supplies to mobile or transportable equipment where operating of the equipment\\n    \
      \      subjects the cable to flexing, the cable shall conform to any of these codes BS 6007 /\\n       BS\
      \ 6500 / BS 7375.\\n\\n\\n26.8.3    Flexible cords with a conductor cross sectional area smaller than 1.5\
      \ mm2 shall not be\\n        used and insulated flexible cable shall conform to BS 6500 and BS 7375.\\n\\\
      n\\n26.8.4   Where low voltage cables are to be used, reference shall be made to BS 7375. The\\n         \
      \ following standards shall also be referred to particularly for under ground cables BS\\n        6346 and\
      \ BS 6708\\n\\n\\n26.8.5   Cables buried directly in the ground shall be of a type incorporating armour or\
      \ metal\\n         sheath or both. Such cables shall be marked by cable covers or a suitable marking\\n  \
      \       tape and be buried at a  sufficient depth to avoid  their being damaged by any\\n          disturbance\
      \ of the ground. Cable routes shall be marked on the plans kept in the site\\n           electrical register.\\\
      n\\n26.8.6    Cabling passing under the walk way and across way  for transport and mobile\\n         equipment\
      \ shall be laid in ducts at a minimum depth of 0.6 meters.\\n\\n26.8.7   Cables that need to cross open areas,\
      \ or where span of 3m or more are involved, a\\n         catenary wire on poles or other supports shall be\
      \ provided for convenient means of\\n         suspension. Minimum height shall be 6 m above ground.\\n\\n\\\
      n26.8.8   Cables carrying a voltage to earth in excess of 65V other than supply for welding\\n         process\
      \ shall have metal armour or sheath, which has been effectively earthed and\\n         monitored by the contractor.\
      \ In case of flexible and trailing cables such earthed metal\"\n}"

    quote: "{\n  \"pdf_page\": 49,\n  \"text\": \"sheath and/or armour should be in addition to the earth core in\
      \ the cable and shall not\\n                be used as the protective conductor.\\n\\n\\n          26.8.9\
      \   Armoured cables having an over-sheath of polyvinyl chloride (PVC) or an  oil\\n                      resisting\
      \ and flame retardant compound shall be used whenever there is a risk of\\n                  mechanical damage\
      \ occurring\\n\\n\\n          26.9     Plugs, socket-outlets and couplers:\\n\\n\\n          26.9.1   The\
      \ contractor shall ensure plugs, socket-outlets, and couplers available in\\n                  the construction\
      \  site as “splash proof” type. The minimum degree of\\n                  Ingress Protection should be of\
      \ IP44 in accordance with BS EN 60529.\\n\\n\\n          26.9.2   Only plugs and fittings of the weatherproof\
      \ type shall be used and they should be colour\\n                 coded in accordance with the Internationally\
      \ recognised standards for example as detailed\\n                 as follows:\\n\\n                      (a)\
      \   110 volts : Yellow.\\n\\n                      (b)   240 volts : Blue.\\n\\n                       (c)\
      \   415 volts : Red.\\n\\n         26.10    Connections\\n\\n          26.10.1  Every joint and connection\
      \ in a system shall be mechanically and electrically\\n                   suitable  for  use  to  prevent\
      \  danger.  Proper  cable  connectors  as  per\\n                    national/international standards shall\
      \ only be used to connect cables.\\n\\n          26.10.2  No loose connections or tapped joints shall be allowed\
      \ any where in the work\\n                       site, office area, stores and other areas. Penalty as per\
      \ relevant clause shall be\\n                  put in case of observation of any tapped joints.\\n\\n\\n \
      \        26.11    Portable and hand-held equipments:\\n\\n\\n          26.11.1  The contractor shall ensure\
      \ the use of double insulated or all-insulated portable\\n                       electrical hand equipment\
      \ may be used without earthing (i.e. two core cables), but\\n                   they shall still be used only\
      \ on 110V because of the risk of damage to trailing leads.\\n\\n\\n         26.12    Other equipments:\\n\\\
      n\\n          26.12.1   All equipment shall have the provision for major switch/cut-off switch in the equipment\\\
      n                           itself.\\n\\n\\n          26.12.2   All non-current carrying metal parts of electrical\
      \ equipment shall be earthed through\\n                    insulated cable\\n\\n\\n          26.12.3   Isolate\
      \ exposed high-voltage (over 415 Volts) equipment, such as transformer banks,\\n                open switches,\
      \ and similar equipment with exposed energized parts and prevent\\n                   unauthorised access.\\\
      n\\n\\n          26.12.4  Approved perimeter markings shall be used to isolate restricted areas from designated\\\
      n                 work areas and entryways and shall be erected before work begins and maintained for\\n \
      \                     entire duration of work. Approved perimeter marking shall be installed  with either\
      \ red\\n                      barrier tape printed with the words \\\"DANGER—HIGH VOLTAGE\\\" or a barrier\
      \ of yellow\\n                     or orange synthetic rope, approximately 1 to 1.5 meter above the floor\
      \ or work\\n                    surface.\\n\\n\\n         26.13   Work on or near live conductors\"\n}"

- kind: parameter
  text: Small capacity diesel generators used by sub or petty contractors are strictly prohibited due to noise and
    safety hazards, and penalties apply tovironment the main contractor if such generators are observed.

    quote: "{\n  \"pdf_page\": 47,\n  \"text\": \"26.2.1   The contractor shall assess the size and location of\
      \ the electrical loads and the\\n                manner in which they vary with time during the currency of\
      \ the contract.\\n\\n\\n          26.2.2   The contractor shall elaborate as to how the total supply is to\
      \ be obtained  /\\n                   generated. The  details  of  the  source  of  electricity,  earthing\
      \  requirement,\\n                    substation  / panel boards, distribution system shall be prepared and\
      \ necessary\\n                   approval from Employer obtained before proceeding of the execution of the\
      \ job.\\n\\n\\n          26.2.3   The main contractor shall take consideration, the requirements of the sub\
      \ /\\n                   petty contractors’ electric power supply and arrive at the capacity of main\\n  \
      \               source of power supply from diesel generators.\\n\\n\\n          26.2.4   As the sub / petty\
      \ contractors’ small capacity generators create more noise\\n               and safety hazard, no small capacity\
      \ diesel generators shall be allowed for\\n                 whatsoever the type of job to be executed under\
      \ this contract.\\n\\n\\n          26.2.5      If any unsafe noise making small capacity diesel generators\
      \ are found used\\n                by sub / petty contractors the main contractor shall only be penalised.\\\
      n\\n\\n          26.3    Work on site\\n\\n\\n          26.3.1   The contractor shall also submit electrical\
      \ single line diagram, schematic\\n                diagram and the  details of the equipment  for  all temporary\
      \  electrical\\n                     installation and these diagrams together with the temporary  electrical\\\
      n                equipment shall be submitted to the Employer’s for necessary approval.\\n               \
      \    Failure to do so shall invite penalty as per relevant clause.\\n\\n\\n          26.4     Strength and\
      \ capability of electrical equipment\\n\\n\\n          26.4.1   No electrical equipment shall be put into\
      \ use where its strength and capability may\\n                be exceeded in such a way as may give rise to\
      \ danger.\\n\\n\\n          26.5     Adverse or hazardous environments\\n\\n          26.5.1    Electrical\
      \ equipment, which may reasonably foreseably be exposed to-\\n\\n                      (a)   mechanical damage;\\\
      n                      (b)   the effects of the weather, natural hazards, temperature or pressure;\\n    \
      \                   (c)   the effects of wet, dirty, dusty or corrosive conditions; or\\n                \
      \      (d)   any flammable or explosive substance, including dusts, vapours or gases,\\n                 \
      \            shall be of such construction or as necessary protected as to prevent, so far\\n            \
      \          as is reasonably practicable, danger arising from such exposure.\\n\\n\\n\\n          26.6    \
      \  Distribution system:\\n\\n\\n          26.6.1   The contractor shall provide distribution system for control\
      \ and distribution of\\n                        electricity from a main AC supply of 50Hz for typical appliances,\\\
      n\\n\\n                                 i)    Fixed plant – 400V 3 phase\\n\\n                           \
      \         ii)    Movable plant fed via trailing cable over 3.75 kW – 400 3 phase\\n\\n                   \
      \                  iii)    Installation in site buildings – 230V single phase\\n\\n                      \
      \    iv)   Fixed flood lighting – 230V single phase\\n\\n                      v)    Portable and hand tools\
      \ – 115V single phase\\n\\n                          vi)    Site lighting  - 115V single phase\\n\\n     \
      \                        vii)   Portable hand lamps – 115V single phase\"\n}"

    quote: "{\n  \"clause_id\": \"28.0\",\n  \"fragments\": [\n    {\n      \"pdf_page\": 51,\n      \"text\": \"\
      28.0    Hand Tools and Power Tools\\n\\n\\n          28.1     General\\n\\n\\n          28.1.1   The contractor\
      \ is wholly responsible for the safe condition of tools and equipment\\n                 used by his employees\
      \ and that of his sub-contractors.\\n\\n\\n          28.1.2   Use of short / damaged hand tools shall be avoided\
      \ and the contractor shall ensure all\\n                      his hand tools used at his worksite are safe\
      \ to work with or stored and shall also train\\n                      his employees (including his sub-contractors)\
      \ for proper use thereby.\\n\\n\\n          28.1.3     All hand tools and power tools shall be duly inspected\
      \ before use for safe operation.\\n\\n\\n          28.1.4     All hand tools and power tools shall have sufficient\
      \ grip and the design specification\\n                on par with national/international standards on anthropometrics.\\\
      n\\n\\n          28.2    Hand tools\\n\\n\\n          28.2.1   Hand tools shall include saws, chisels, axes\
      \ and hatches, hammers, hand planes,\\n                 screw drivers, crow bars, nail pullers.\\n\\n\\n \
      \         28.2.2   The contractor shall ensure that,\\n\\n\\n                                 i)    For crosscutting\
      \ of hardwood, saws with larger teeth points (no. of points per\\n                           inch) shall be\
      \ preferred to avoid the saw jumping out of the job.\\n\\n                                    ii)   Mushroom\
      \ headed  chisels  shall  not be used  in  the  worksite where  the\\n                        fragments of\
      \ the head may cause injury.\\n\\n                                     iii)   Unless hatchet has a striking\
      \ face, it shall be used as a hammer.\\n\\n                          iv)   Only knives of retractable blades\
      \ shall be used in the worksite.\\n\\n                      v)   No screwdrivers shall be used for scraping,\
      \ chiselling or punching holes.\\n\\n                          vi)   A pilot hole shall always be driven before\
      \ driving a screw.\\n\\n                             vii)   Wherever necessary, usage of proper PPEs shall\
      \ be used by his employees.\\n\\n\\n          28.3     Power tools\\n\\n\\n          28.3.1   Power tools\
      \ include drills, planes, routers, saws, jackhammers, grinders, sprayers,\\n                    chipping hammers,\
      \ air nozzles and drills.\\n\\n\\n          28.3.2   The contractor shall ensure that\\n\\n              \
      \                   i)     Electric tools are properly grounded or / and double insulated.\"\n    },\n   \
      \ {\n      \"pdf_page\": 52,\n      \"text\": \"ii)    GFCIs/ RCCBs shall be used with all portable electric\
      \ tool operated especially\\n               outdoors or in wet condition.\\n\\n                  iii)   Before\
      \ making any adjustments or changing attachments, his workers shall\\n               disconnect the tool from\
      \ the power source.\\n\\n             iv)   When operating in confined spaces or for prolonged periods, hearing\
      \ protection\\n                  shall be required. The same shall also apply to working with equipments,\
      \ which\\n                gives out more noise as mentioned in clause 43.0 of this contract document.\\n\\\
      n           v)    Tool is held firmly and the material is properly secured before turning on the\\n      \
      \             tool.\\n\\n             vi)    All  drills shall have suitable attachments respective of the\
      \ operations and\\n               powerful for ease of operation.\\n\\n              vii)  When any work \
      \ / operation need to be performed repeatedly or continuously,\\n                 tools specifically designed\
      \ for that work shall be used. The same is applicable to\\n               detachable tool bit also.\\n\\n\
      \               viii)   Size of the drill shall be determined by the maximum opening of the chuck n\\n   \
      \           case of drill bit.\\n\\n             ix)   Attachments such as speed reducing screwdrivers and\
      \ buffers shall be provided\\n                 to prevent fatigue and undue muscle strain to his workers.\\\
      n\\n           x)    Stock should be clamped or otherwise secured firmly to prevent it from moving.\\n\\n\
      \             xi)   Workers shall never stand on the top of the ladder to  drill holes in walls  /\\n    \
      \              ceilings, which can be hazardous, instead standing on the fourth or fifth rung\\n         \
      \         shall be recommended.\\n\\n              xii)    Electric plane shall not be operated with loose\
      \ clothing or long scarf or open\\n                 jacket.\\n\\n               xiii)   Safety guards used\
      \ on right angle head or vertical portable grinders must cover\\n             a minimum of 1800 of the wheel\
      \ and the spindle / wheel specifications shall be\\n              checked.\\n\\n            xiv)   All power\
      \ tools / hand tools shall have guards at their nip points.\\n\\n          xv)  Low profile safety chain shall\
      \ be used in case of wood working machines and\\n                the saw shall run at high rpm when cutting\
      \ and also correct chain tension shall\\n             be ensured to avoid “kickback”.\\n\\n            xvi)\
      \  Leather aprons and gloves shall be used as an additional personal protection\\n                  auxiliary\
      \ to withstand kickback.\\n\\n             xvii)  Push sticks shall be provided and properly used to hold\
      \ the job down on the\\n                 table while the heels moves the stock forward and thus preventing\
      \ kickbacks.\\n\\n              xviii)  Air pressure is set at a suitable level for air actuated tool or equipment\
      \ being\\n               used. Before changing or adjusting pneumatic tools, air pressure shall be turned\\\
      n                     off.\\n\\n            xix)  Only trained employees shall use explosive actuated tools\
      \ and the tool shall\\n                also be unloaded when not in use.\\n\\n          xx)  Usage of such\
      \ explosive actuated tools shall be avoided in case of places\\n             where explosive/flammable vapours\
      \ or gases may be present.\\n\\n            xxi)  Explosive actuated tools and their explosives shall be stored\
      \ separately and be\\n               taken out and loaded only before the time of immediate use.\\n\\n   \
      \          xxii)  Misfired cartridges of explosive actuated tools must be placed in a container of\\n    \
      \           water and be removed safely from the project.\\n\\n              xxiii) No worker shall point\
      \ any power operated  / hand tool to any other person\\n                especially during loading / unloading.\"\
      \n    }\n  ],\n  \"heading_line\": \"          28.0    Hand Tools and Power Tools\",\n  \"retained_lines\"\

      : 81,\n      \"text\": \"\"\n    },\n    {\n      \"pdf_page\": 51,\n      \"source_line_number\": 82,\n \
      \     \"text\": \"\"\n    },\n    {\n      \"pdf_page\": 51,\n      \"source_line_number\": 83,\n      \"\
      text\": \"\"\n    },\n    {\n      \"pdf_page\": 51,\n      \"source_line_number\": 84,\n      \"text\": \"\
      \"\n    },\n    {\n      \"pdf_page\": 52,\n      \"source_line_number\": 3,\n      \"text\": \"         \
      \         ii)    GFCIs/ RCCBs shall be used with all portable electric tool operated especially\"\n    },\n\

      \ or in wet condition.\"\n    },\n    {\n      \"pdf_page\": 52,\n      \"source_line_number\": 5,\n     \
      \ \"text\": \"\"\n    },\n    {\n      \"pdf_page\": 52,\n      \"source_line_number\": 6,\n      \"text\"\
      : \"                  iii)   Before making any adjustments or changing attachments, his workers shall\"\n\
      \    },\n    {\n      \"pdf_page\": 52,\n      \"source_line_number\": 7,\n      \"text\": \"            \
      \   disconnect the tool from the power source.\"\n    },\n    {\n      \"pdf_page\": 52,\n      \"source_line_number\"\
      : 8,\n      \"text\": \"\"\n    },\n    {\n      \"pdf_page\": 52,\n      \"source_line_number\": 9,\n   \
      \   \"text\": \"             iv)   When operating in confined spaces or for prolonged periods, hearing protection\"\
      \n    },\n    {\n      \"pdf_page\": 52,\n      \"source_line_number\": 10,\n      \"text\": \"          \
      \        shall be required. The same shall also apply to working with equipments, which\"\n    },\n    {\n\
      \      \"pdf_page\": 52,\n      \"source_line_number\": 11,\n      \"text\": \"                gives out more\
      \ noise as mentioned in clause 43.0 of this contract document.\"\n    },\n    {\n      \"pdf_page\": 52,\n\
      \      \"source_line_number\": 12,\n      \"text\": \"\"\n    },\n    {\n      \"pdf_page\": 52,\n      \"\
      source_line_number\": 13,\n      \"text\": \"           v)    Tool is held firmly and the material is properly\
      \ secured before turning on the\"\n    },\n    {\n      \"pdf_page\": 52,\n      \"source_line_number\": 14,\n\
      \      \"text\": \"                   tool.\"\n    },\n    {\n      \"pdf_page\": 52,\n      \"source_line_number\"\
      : 15,\n      \"text\": \"\"\n    },\n    {\n      \"pdf_page\": 52,\n      \"source_line_number\": 16,\n \
      \     \"text\": \"             vi)    All  drills shall have suitable attachments respective of the operations\
      \ and\"\n    },\n    {\n      \"pdf_page\": 52,\n      \"source_line_number\": 17,\n      \"text\": \"   \
      \            powerful for ease of operation.\"\n    },\n    {\n      \"pdf_page\": 52,\n      \"source_line_number\"\
      : 18,\n      \"text\": \"\"\n    },\n    {\n      \"pdf_page\": 52,\n      \"source_line_number\": 19,\n \
      \     \"text\": \"              vii)  When any work  / operation need to be performed repeatedly or continuously,\"\
      \n    },\n    {\n      \"pdf_page\": 52,\n      \"source_line_number\": 20,\n      \"text\": \"          \
      \       tools specifically designed for that work shall be used. The same is applicable to\"\n    },\n   \
      \ {\n      \"pdf_page\": 52,\n      \"source_line_number\": 21,\n      \"text\": \"               detachable\
      \ tool bit also.\"\n    },\n    {\n      \"pdf_page\": 52,\n      \"source_line_number\": 22,\n      \"text\"\
      : \"\"\n    },\n    {\n      \"pdf_page\": 52,\n      \"source_line_number\": 23,\n      \"text\": \"    \
      \           viii)   Size of the drill shall be determined by the maximum opening of the chuck n\"\n    },\n\
      \    {\n      \"pdf_page\": 52,\n      \"source_line_number\": 24,\n      \"text\": \"              case of\
      \ drill bit.\"\n    },\n    {\n      \"pdf_page\": 52,\n      \"source_line_number\": 25,\n      \"text\"\
      : \"\"\n    },\n    {\n      \"pdf_page\": 52,\n      \"source_line_number\": 26,\n      \"text\": \"    \
      \         ix)   Attachments such as speed reducing screwdrivers and buffers shall be provided\"\n    },\n\
      \    {\n      \"pdf_page\": 52,\n      \"source_line_number\": 27,\n      \"text\": \"                 to\
      \ prevent fatigue and undue muscle strain to his workers.\"\n    },\n    {\n      \"pdf_page\": 52,\n    \
      \  \"source_line_number\": 28,\n      \"text\": \"\"\n    },\n    {\n      \"pdf_page\": 52,\n      \"source_line_number\"\
      : 29,\n      \"text\": \"           x)    Stock should be clamped or otherwise secured firmly to prevent it\
      \ from moving.\"\n    },\n    {\n      \"pdf_page\": 52,\n      \"source_line_number\": 30,\n      \"text\"\
      : \"\"\n    },\n    {\n      \"pdf_page\": 52,\n      \"source_line_number\": 31,\n      \"text\": \"    \
      \         xi)   Workers shall never stand on the top of the ladder to  drill holes in walls  /\"\n    },\n\
      \    {\n      \"pdf_page\": 52,\n      \"source_line_number\": 32,\n      \"text\": \"                  ceilings,\
      \ which can be hazardous, instead standing on the fourth or fifth rung\"\n    },\n    {\n      \"pdf_page\"\
      : 52,\n      \"source_line_number\": 33,\n      \"text\": \"                  shall be recommended.\"\n  \
      \  },\n    {\n      \"pdf_page\": 52,\n      \"source_line_number\": 34,\n      \"text\": \"\"\n    },\n \
      \   {\n      \"pdf_page\": 52,\n      \"source_line_number\": 35,\n      \"text\": \"              xii)  \
      \  Electric plane shall not be operated with loose clothing or long scarf or open\"\n    },\n    {\n     \
      \ \"pdf_page\": 52,\n      \"source_line_number\": 36,\n      \"text\": \"                 jacket.\"\n   \
      \ },\n    {\n      \"pdf_page\": 52,\n      \"source_line_number\": 37,\n      \"text\": \"\"\n    },\n  \
      \  {\n      \"pdf_page\": 52,\n      \"source_line_number\": 38,\n      \"text\": \"               xiii) \
      \  Safety guards used on right angle head or vertical portable grinders must cover\"\n    },\n    {\n    \
      \  \"pdf_page\": 52,\n      \"source_line_number\": 39,\n      \"text\": \"             a minimum of 1800\
      \ of the wheel and the spindle / wheel specifications shall be\"\n    },\n    {\n      \"pdf_page\": 52,\n\
      \      \"source_line_number\": 40,\n      \"text\": \"              checked.\"\n    },\n    {\n      \"pdf_page\"\
      : 52,\n      \"source_line_number\": 41,\n      \"text\": \"\"\n    },\n    {\n      \"pdf_page\": 52,\n \
      \     \"source_line_number\": 42,\n      \"text\": \"            xiv)   All power tools / hand tools shall\
      \ have guards at their nip points.\"\n    },\n    {\n      \"pdf_page\": 52,\n      \"source_line_number\"\
      : 43,\n      \"text\": \"\"\n    },\n    {\n      \"pdf_page\": 52,\n      \"source_line_number\": 44,\n \
      \     \"text\": \"          xv)  Low profile safety chain shall be used in case of wood working machines and\"\
      \n    },\n    {\n      \"pdf_page\": 52,\n      \"source_line_number\": 45,\n      \"text\": \"          \
      \      the saw shall run at high rpm when cutting and also correct chain tension shall\"\n    },\n    {\n\
      \      \"pdf_page\": 52,\n      \"source_line_number\": 46,\n      \"text\": \"             be ensured to\
      \ avoid “kickback”.\"\n    },\n    {\n      \"pdf_page\": 52,\n      \"source_line_number\": 47,\n      \"\

      \            xvi)  Leather aprons and gloves shall be used as an additional personal protection\"\n    },\n\
      \    {\n      \"pdf_page\": 52,\n      \"source_line_number\": 49,\n      \"text\": \"                  auxiliary\
      \ to withstand kickback.\"\n    },\n    {\n      \"pdf_page\": 52,\n      \"source_line_number\": 50,\n  \
      \    \"text\": \"\"\n    },\n    {\n      \"pdf_page\": 52,\n      \"source_line_number\": 51,\n      \"text\"\
      : \"             xvii)  Push sticks shall be provided and properly used to hold the job down on the\"\n  \
      \  },\n    {\n      \"pdf_page\": 52,\n      \"source_line_number\": 52,\n      \"text\": \"             \
      \    table while the heels moves the stock forward and thus preventing kickbacks.\"\n    },\n    {\n     \

      : 52,\n      \"source_line_number\": 54,\n      \"text\": \"              xviii)  Air pressure is set at a\

      \  \"source_line_number\": 55,\n      \"text\": \"               used. Before changing or adjusting pneumatic\
      \ tools, air pressure shall be turned\"\n    },\n    {\n      \"pdf_page\": 52,\n      \"source_line_number\"\
      : 56,\n      \"text\": \"                     off.\"\n    },\n    {\n      \"pdf_page\": 52,\n      \"source_line_number\"\
      : 57,\n      \"text\": \"\"\n    },\n    {\n      \"pdf_page\": 52,\n      \"source_line_number\": 58,\n \
      \     \"text\": \"            xix)  Only trained employees shall use explosive actuated tools and the tool\
      \ shall\"\n    },\n    {\n      \"pdf_page\": 52,\n      \"source_line_number\": 59,\n      \"text\": \" \
      \               also be unloaded when not in use.\"\n    },\n    {\n      \"pdf_page\": 52,\n      \"source_line_number\"\
      : 60,\n      \"text\": \"\"\n    },\n    {\n      \"pdf_page\": 52,\n      \"source_line_number\": 61,\n \
      \     \"text\": \"          xx)  Usage of such explosive actuated tools shall be avoided in case of places\"\
      \n    },\n    {\n      \"pdf_page\": 52,\n      \"source_line_number\": 62,\n      \"text\": \"          \
      \   where explosive/flammable vapours or gases may be present.\"\n    },\n    {\n      \"pdf_page\": 52,\n\
      \      \"source_line_number\": 63,\n      \"text\": \"\"\n    },\n    {\n      \"pdf_page\": 52,\n      \"\
      source_line_number\": 64,\n      \"text\": \"            xxi)  Explosive actuated tools and their explosives\

      \  },\n    {\n      \"pdf_page\": 52,\n      \"source_line_number\": 66,\n      \"text\": \"\"\n    },\n \
      \   {\n      \"pdf_page\": 52,\n      \"source_line_number\": 67,\n      \"text\": \"             xxii)  Misfired\

      : \"\"\n    },\n    {\n      \"pdf_page\": 52,\n      \"source_line_number\": 70,\n      \"text\": \"    \

    quote: "{\n  \"clause_id\": \"29.0\",\n  \"fragments\": [\n    {\n      \"pdf_page\": 52,\n      \"text\": \"\
      29.0     Welding, Gouging and Cutting\\n\\n\\n29.1    Gas cylinders in use shall be kept upright on a custom-built\
      \ stand or trolley fitted\\n          with a bracket to accommodate the hoses and equipment or otherwise secured.\\\
      n        The metal cap shall be kept in place to protect the valve when the cylinder is not\\n         connected\
      \ for use.\\n\\n\\n29.2    Hose clamp or clip shall be used to connect hoses firmly in both sides of cylinders\\\
      n        and torches.\"\n    },\n    {\n      \"pdf_page\": 53,\n      \"text\": \"29.3       All gas cylinders\
      \ shall be fixed with pressure regulator and dial gauges\\n\\n\\n          29.4     Non-return valve and Flashback\
      \ arrester shall be fixed at both end of cylinder and\\n                      torch.\\n\\n\\n          29.5\
      \     Domestic LPG cylinders shall not be used for Gas welding and Cutting purpose.\\n\\n\\n          29.6\
      \    DCP or CO2 type Fire Extinguisher not less than 5 kg shall be fixed at or near to\\n                \
      \   welding process zone  in an easily accessible  location. Fire Extinguisher should\\n                 \
      \   confirm to IS 2190: 1992.\\n\\n\\n          29.7    Use firewatchers if there is a possibility of ignition\
      \ unobserved by the operator (e.g. on\\n                    the other side of bulkheads).\\n\\n\\n       \
      \   29.8    Oxygen cylinders and flammable gas cylinders shall be stored separately, at least 6.6\\n     \
      \             meters (20 feet) apart or separated by a fire proof, 1.5 meters (5 feet) high partition.\\n\
      \                 Flammable substances shall not be stored within 15 meters of cylinder storage areas.\\n\\\
      n\\n          29.9     Transformer used for electrical arc welding shall be fixed with Ammeter and Voltmeter\\\
      n                and also fixed with separate main power switch.\\n\\n\\n         29.10    Welding grounds\
      \ and returns should be securely attached to the work by cable lugs,\\n                 by clamps in the case\
      \ of stranded conductors, or by bolts for strip conductors. The\\n                  ground cable will not\
      \ be attached to equipment or existing installations or apparatus.\\n\\n\\n         29.11   Use a low voltage\
      \ open circuit relay device  if welding with alternating current in\\n                     constricted or\
      \ damp places.\\n\\n         29.12    Take precautions against the risk of increased fume hazards when welding\
      \ with\\n                chrome containing fluxed consumables or high current metal  inert gas (MIG) or\\\
      n                   tungsten inert gas (TIG) processes.\\n\\n         29.13    Avoid being in contact with\
      \ water or wet floors when welding. Use duckboards or\\n                   rubber protection.\\n\\n\\n   \
      \      29.14     All electrical installations shall meet the IS: 5571: 1997 and NFPA 70 for gas cylinder\\\
      n                   storage area and other hazardous areas.\\n\\n\\n         29.15   The current for Electric\
      \ arc welding shall not exceed 300 A on a hand welding\\n                    operation.\"\n    }\n  ],\n \

      31.0      Fire prevention, protection and fighting system\\n\\n\\n31.1    The  contractor  shall ensure  that\
      \  construction  site  is provided  with  fire\\n         extinguishing  equipment  sufficient  to  extinguish\
      \  any  probable   fire  at\\n         construction site. An adequate water supply is provided at ample pressure\
      \ as\\n         per national standard.\\n\\n\\n31.2     Recharging of fire extinguishers and their proper\
      \ maintenance should be ensured and\\n         as a minimum should meet Indian National Standards\\n\\n\\\
      n31.3       All drivers  of vehicles, foreman, supervisors and managers  shall be trained on\\n          operating\
      \ the fire extinguishers and fire fighting equipment.\\n\\n31.4    The contractor shall also give consideration\
      \ to the provision of adequate fire fighting\\n         arrangements within the underground and tunnelling\
      \ operations including the provision\\n           of Fire Service compatible hose connections and emergency\
      \ lighting\\n\\n\\n31.5    As per the BOCWK Rules 2006, Rule 79(a)(vii), all lifting appliances’ driver cabin\\\
      n         should be provided with a suitable portable fire extinguisher.\\n\\n\\n31.6     Combustible scrap\
      \ and other construction debris should be disposed off site on a\\n          regular basis. If scrap is to\
      \ be burnt on site, the burning site should be specified and\\n          located at a distance no less than\
      \ 12 metres from any construction work or any other\\n         combustible material.\\n\\n\\n31.7     Every\
      \ fire, including those extinguished by contractor personnel, shall be reported to\\n          the Employer\
      \ representatives.\\n\\n\\n31.8     Emergency plans and Fire Evacuation plans shall be prepared and issued.\
      \ Mock drills\\n         should be held on a regular basis to ensure the effectiveness of the arrangements\
      \ and\\n         as a part of the programme, the Telephone Number of the local fire brigade should be\\n \
      \         prominently displayed near each telephone on site.\"\n    }\n  ],\n  \"heading_line\": \"31.0  \

    quote: "{\n  \"clause_id\": \"32.0\",\n  \"fragments\": [\n    {\n      \"pdf_page\": 54,\n      \"text\": \"\
      32.0     Corrosive substances\\n\\n\\n32.1    As per BOCWR Rule 44, corrosive substances including alkalis\
      \ and acids shall be\\n          stored and used by a person dealing with such substances at a building /\
      \ construction\\n            site in a manner that it does not endanger the building worker and suitable PPE\
      \ shall\\n        be provided by the contractor to the worker during such handling and work. In case of\\\
      n           spillage of such substances on building worker, the contractor shall take immediate\\n       \
      \  remedial measures.\"\n    }\n  ],\n  \"heading_line\": \"32.0     Corrosive substances\",\n  \"retained_lines\"\

- kind: parameter
  text: Hand and power tools must be inspected before use, equipped with proper guards at nip points, and electrical
    tools must be grounded or double insulated with GFCIs/RCCBs used outdoors or in wet conditions.
  evidence_ids:

  relation_type: none

  citations:
  - id: J5aabcd6a60a03057
    okf_path: OKF_bundle/Technical/Vol3/vol3_part2.md
    okf_sha256: ee80a88bd673202495b104f1e039fd2b85ddf8e2f3b2cbbf98523266c0f35b6c
    heading: Clause 28.0 — Hand Tools and Power Tools
    source_document: Vol3DLNP1.pdf
    source_sha256: 1ee3fc8dfd12f659f34446b0a6db74e1e1cdd4d593ca91b2a48d59bf1ef97d52
    pdf_pages:
    - 51
    - 52
    sheet_cells: ''
    json_path: parsed_json/vol3/part_2_safety/safety_clauses.json
    json_sha256: 0042f3256acc51ca4ebb327c3cee57a308fa5f47e1a4ccc7f4994fe898fa11ef
    json_pointer: /clauses/11
    json_record_id: null
    source_review_status: pending_manual_review
    quote: "{\n  \"clause_id\": \"28.0\",\n  \"fragments\": [\n    {\n      \"pdf_page\": 51,\n      \"text\": \"\
      28.0    Hand Tools and Power Tools\\n\\n\\n          28.1     General\\n\\n\\n          28.1.1   The contractor\
      \ is wholly responsible for the safe condition of tools and equipment\\n                 used by his employees\
      \ and that of his sub-contractors.\\n\\n\\n          28.1.2   Use of short / damaged hand tools shall be avoided\
      \ and the contractor shall ensure all\\n                      his hand tools used at his worksite are safe\
      \ to work with or stored and shall also train\\n                      his employees (including his sub-contractors)\
      \ for proper use thereby.\\n\\n\\n          28.1.3     All hand tools and power tools shall be duly inspected\
      \ before use for safe operation.\\n\\n\\n          28.1.4     All hand tools and power tools shall have sufficient\
      \ grip and the design specification\\n                on par with national/international standards on anthropometrics.\\\
      n\\n\\n          28.2    Hand tools\\n\\n\\n          28.2.1   Hand tools shall include saws, chisels, axes\
      \ and hatches, hammers, hand planes,\\n                 screw drivers, crow bars, nail pullers.\\n\\n\\n \
      \         28.2.2   The contractor shall ensure that,\\n\\n\\n                                 i)    For crosscutting\
      \ of hardwood, saws with larger teeth points (no. of points per\\n                           inch) shall be\
      \ preferred to avoid the saw jumping out of the job.\\n\\n                                    ii)   Mushroom\
      \ headed  chisels  shall  not be used  in  the  worksite where  the\\n                        fragments of\
      \ the head may cause injury.\\n\\n                                     iii)   Unless hatchet has a striking\
      \ face, it shall be used as a hammer.\\n\\n                          iv)   Only knives of retractable blades\
      \ shall be used in the worksite.\\n\\n                      v)   No screwdrivers shall be used for scraping,\
      \ chiselling or punching holes.\\n\\n                          vi)   A pilot hole shall always be driven before\
      \ driving a screw.\\n\\n                             vii)   Wherever necessary, usage of proper PPEs shall\
      \ be used by his employees.\\n\\n\\n          28.3     Power tools\\n\\n\\n          28.3.1   Power tools\
      \ include drills, planes, routers, saws, jackhammers, grinders, sprayers,\\n                    chipping hammers,\
      \ air nozzles and drills.\\n\\n\\n          28.3.2   The contractor shall ensure that\\n\\n              \
      \                   i)     Electric tools are properly grounded or / and double insulated.\"\n    },\n   \
      \ {\n      \"pdf_page\": 52,\n      \"text\": \"ii)    GFCIs/ RCCBs shall be used with all portable electric\
      \ tool operated especially\\n               outdoors or in wet condition.\\n\\n                  iii)   Before\
      \ making any adjustments or changing attachments, his workers shall\\n               disconnect the tool from\
      \ the power source.\\n\\n             iv)   When operating in confined spaces or for prolonged periods, hearing\
      \ protection\\n                  shall be required. The same shall also apply to working with equipments,\
      \ which\\n                gives out more noise as mentioned in clause 43.0 of this contract document.\\n\\\
      n           v)    Tool is held firmly and the material is properly secured before turning on the\\n      \
      \             tool.\\n\\n             vi)    All  drills shall have suitable attachments respective of the\
      \ operations and\\n               powerful for ease of operation.\\n\\n              vii)  When any work \
      \ / operation need to be performed repeatedly or continuously,\\n                 tools specifically designed\
      \ for that work shall be used. The same is applicable to\\n               detachable tool bit also.\\n\\n\
      \               viii)   Size of the drill shall be determined by the maximum opening of the chuck n\\n   \
      \           case of drill bit.\\n\\n             ix)   Attachments such as speed reducing screwdrivers and\
      \ buffers shall be provided\\n                 to prevent fatigue and undue muscle strain to his workers.\\\
      n\\n           x)    Stock should be clamped or otherwise secured firmly to prevent it from moving.\\n\\n\
      \             xi)   Workers shall never stand on the top of the ladder to  drill holes in walls  /\\n    \
      \              ceilings, which can be hazardous, instead standing on the fourth or fifth rung\\n         \
      \         shall be recommended.\\n\\n              xii)    Electric plane shall not be operated with loose\
      \ clothing or long scarf or open\\n                 jacket.\\n\\n               xiii)   Safety guards used\
      \ on right angle head or vertical portable grinders must cover\\n             a minimum of 1800 of the wheel\

- kind: parameter
  text: 'Welding, gouging, and cutting operations require oxygen and flammable gas cylinders to be stored at least
    6.6 meters apart or separated by a 1.5-meter high fireproof partition, with non-return valves, flashback arresters,
    pressure regulators, and at least 5 kg DCP or CO2 fire extinguishers conforming to IS 2190: 1992.'

    quote: "{\n  \"clause_id\": \"29.0\",\n  \"fragments\": [\n    {\n      \"pdf_page\": 52,\n      \"text\": \"\
      29.0     Welding, Gouging and Cutting\\n\\n\\n29.1    Gas cylinders in use shall be kept upright on a custom-built\
      \ stand or trolley fitted\\n          with a bracket to accommodate the hoses and equipment or otherwise secured.\\\
      n        The metal cap shall be kept in place to protect the valve when the cylinder is not\\n         connected\
      \ for use.\\n\\n\\n29.2    Hose clamp or clip shall be used to connect hoses firmly in both sides of cylinders\\\
      n        and torches.\"\n    },\n    {\n      \"pdf_page\": 53,\n      \"text\": \"29.3       All gas cylinders\
      \ shall be fixed with pressure regulator and dial gauges\\n\\n\\n          29.4     Non-return valve and Flashback\
      \ arrester shall be fixed at both end of cylinder and\\n                      torch.\\n\\n\\n          29.5\
      \     Domestic LPG cylinders shall not be used for Gas welding and Cutting purpose.\\n\\n\\n          29.6\
      \    DCP or CO2 type Fire Extinguisher not less than 5 kg shall be fixed at or near to\\n                \
      \   welding process zone  in an easily accessible  location. Fire Extinguisher should\\n                 \
      \   confirm to IS 2190: 1992.\\n\\n\\n          29.7    Use firewatchers if there is a possibility of ignition\
      \ unobserved by the operator (e.g. on\\n                    the other side of bulkheads).\\n\\n\\n       \

- kind: parameter
  text: Dangerous and harmful environments such as confined spaces or excavations using internal combustion engines
    require ventilation to keep carbon monoxide below 50 ppm, and worker entry is prohibited unless certified safe
    by a responsible person as per BOCWR Rule 40.

    quote: "{\n  \"clause_id\": \"30.0\",\n  \"fragments\": [\n    {\n      \"pdf_page\": 53,\n      \"text\": \"\
      30.0    Dangerous and harmful environment\\n\\n\\n                As per BOCWR Rule 40,\\n\\n            \
      \                     i)   When internal combustion engines are to be used into a confined space or\\n   \
      \                      excavation or tunnel or any other workplace where neither natural or artificial\\n\
      \                             ventilation system  is inadequate  to keep carbon monoxide below 50ppm,\\n \
      \                      exposure of building workers shall be avoided unless suitable measures are\\n     \
      \                   taken and provided by the contractor.\\n\\n\\n                                    ii)\
      \   No worker shall be allowed into any confined space or tank or trench or\\n                         excavation\
      \ wherein there  is given  off any dust, fumes  / vapours or other\\n                            impurities\
      \ which is likely to be injurious or offensive, explosive or poisonous or\\n                        noxious\
      \ or gaseous material or other harmful articles unless steps are carried\\n                          out by\
      \ the contractor and certified by the responsible person to be safe.\"\n    }\n  ],\n  \"heading_line\": \"\

- kind: parameter
  text: Fire prevention and protection systems require construction sites to have sufficient fire extinguishing
    equipment and water supply, driver cabins of lifting appliances to have portable extinguishers under BOCWK Rules
    2006 Rule 79(a)(vii), and on-site scrap burning locations placed at least 12 meters away from construction work.
  evidence_ids:

  explicitness: not_a_relation

    quote: "{\n  \"clause_id\": \"31.0\",\n  \"fragments\": [\n    {\n      \"pdf_page\": 54,\n      \"text\": \"\
      31.0      Fire prevention, protection and fighting system\\n\\n\\n31.1    The  contractor  shall ensure  that\
      \  construction  site  is provided  with  fire\\n         extinguishing  equipment  sufficient  to  extinguish\
      \  any  probable   fire  at\\n         construction site. An adequate water supply is provided at ample pressure\
      \ as\\n         per national standard.\\n\\n\\n31.2     Recharging of fire extinguishers and their proper\
      \ maintenance should be ensured and\\n         as a minimum should meet Indian National Standards\\n\\n\\\
      n31.3       All drivers  of vehicles, foreman, supervisors and managers  shall be trained on\\n          operating\
      \ the fire extinguishers and fire fighting equipment.\\n\\n31.4    The contractor shall also give consideration\
      \ to the provision of adequate fire fighting\\n         arrangements within the underground and tunnelling\
      \ operations including the provision\\n           of Fire Service compatible hose connections and emergency\
      \ lighting\\n\\n\\n31.5    As per the BOCWK Rules 2006, Rule 79(a)(vii), all lifting appliances’ driver cabin\\\
      n         should be provided with a suitable portable fire extinguisher.\\n\\n\\n31.6     Combustible scrap\
      \ and other construction debris should be disposed off site on a\\n          regular basis. If scrap is to\
      \ be burnt on site, the burning site should be specified and\\n          located at a distance no less than\
      \ 12 metres from any construction work or any other\\n         combustible material.\\n\\n\\n31.7     Every\
      \ fire, including those extinguished by contractor personnel, shall be reported to\\n          the Employer\
      \ representatives.\\n\\n\\n31.8     Emergency plans and Fire Evacuation plans shall be prepared and issued.\
      \ Mock drills\\n         should be held on a regular basis to ensure the effectiveness of the arrangements\
      \ and\\n         as a part of the programme, the Telephone Number of the local fire brigade should be\\n \
      \         prominently displayed near each telephone on site.\"\n    }\n  ],\n  \"heading_line\": \"31.0  \

      35.0    Work Permit system\\n\\n\\n35.1    The Contractor shall develop a Work Permit system, which is a formal\
      \ written system\\n        used to control certain types of work that are potentially hazardous. A work permit\
      \ is a\\n         document, which specifies the work to be done, and the precautions to be taken. Work\\n\
      \         Permits form an essential part of safe systems of work for many construction activities.\\n    \
      \    They allow work to start only after safe procedures have been defined and they\\n          provide a\
      \ clear record that all foreseeable hazards have been considered. Permits to\\n        Work are usually required\
      \ in high-risk areas as identified by the Risk Assessments.\\n\\n\\n35.2    A permit  is needed when construction\
      \ work can only be carried out   if normal\\n         safeguards are dropped or when new hazards are introduced\
      \ by the work. Examples\\n           of high-risk activities include but are not limited to:\\n\\n\\n    \
      \             i)     Entry into confined spaces\\n                  ii)   Work in close proximity to overhead\
      \ power lines and telecommunication cables.\\n                  iii)   Hot work.\\n             iv)   To dig—where\
      \ underground services may be located.\\n           v)   Work with heavy moving machinery.\"\n    },\n   \
      \ {\n      \"pdf_page\": 57,\n      \"text\": \"vi)   Working on electrical equipment\\n                 \
      \            vii)  Work with radioactive isotopes.\\n                               viii)  Heavy lifting operations\
      \ and lifting operations closer to live power line\\n\\n\\n          35.3    The permit-to-work system should\
      \ be fully documented, laying down:\\n\\n\\n                                 i)   How the system works;\\\
      n                                    ii)   The jobs it is to be used for;\\n                             \
      \        iii)   The responsibilities and training of those involved; and\\n                          iv) \
      \ How to check its operation;\\n\\n\\n          35.4    A Work Permit authorisation form shall be completed\
      \ with the maximum duration\\n                    period not exceeding 12 hours.\\n\\n\\n          35.5  \
      \  A copy of each Permit To Work shall be displayed, during its validity, in a conspicuous\\n            \
      \         location in close proximity to the actual works location to which it applies.\"\n    }\n  ],\n \

    source_document: Vol3DLNP1.pdf

    json_sha256: 0042f3256acc51ca4ebb327c3cee57a308fa5f47e1a4ccc7f4994fe898fa11ef
