    quote: "{\n  \"clause_id\": \"34.0\",\n  \"fragments\": [\n    {\n      \"pdf_page\": 55,\n      \"text\": \"\
      34.0     Excavation and Tunnelling:\\n\\n\\n          34.1     Excavation\\n\\n\\n          34.1.1   The contractor\
      \ shall ensure\\n\\n\\n                                 i)    where any construction building worker engaged\
      \ in excavation is exposed to\\n                       hazard of falling or sliding material or article from\
      \ any bank or side of such\\n                         excavation which is more than one 1.5 m above his footing,\
      \ such worker is\\n                          protected by adequate piling and bracing against such bank or\
      \ side.\\n\\n\\n                                    ii)    where banks of an excavation are undercut, adequate\
      \ shoring is provided to\\n                         support the material or article overhanging such bank.\\\
      n\\n\\n                                     iii)   excavated material is not stored at least 0.65 m from the\
      \ edge of an open\\n                         excavation or trench and banks of such excavation or trench are\
      \ stripped of\\n                         loose rocks and the banks of such excavation or trench are stripped\
      \ of loose\\n                         rocks and other materials which may slide,  roll or  fall upon a construction\\\
      n                           building worker working below such bank\\n\\n\\n                          iv)\
      \   metal ladders and staircases or ramps are provided, as the case may be, for\\n                       \
      \  safe access to and egress from excavation where, the depth of such excavation\\n                      exceeds\
      \ 1.5 m and such ladders, staircases or ramps comply with the IS 3696\\n                          Part 1&2\
      \ and other relevant national standards.\\n\\n\\n                      v)    trench and excavation  is protected\
      \ against  falling of a person by suitable\\n                     measures  if the depth of such trench or\
      \ excavation exceeds 1.5 m and such\\n                           protection is an improved protection in accordance\
      \ with the design and drawing\\n                            of a professional engineer, where such depth exceeds\
      \ 4m.\\n\\n\\n          34.2      Tunnelling\\n\\n\\n          34.2.1   The contractor shall inform in writing\
      \ to the Director General within 30 days, prior to\\n                    the commencement of any tunnelling\
      \ work.\\n\\n\\n          34.2.2   The contractor shall appoint a responsible person for safe operation for\
      \ tunnelling\\n                 work as per Rule 121 & 125 of BOCWR.\\n\\n\\n          34.2.3   The contractor\
      \ shall ensure\"\n    },\n    {\n      \"pdf_page\": 56,\n      \"text\": \"i)    every compressed air system\
      \ in a tunnel is provided with emergency power\\n               supply for maintained continued supply of\
      \ compressed air as per Rule 155 of\\n         BOCWR\\n\\n                  ii)    watertight bulkhead doors\
      \ are installed at the entrance of a tunnel to prevent\\n                 flooding.\\n\\n                \
      \  iii)    reliable and effective means of communication such as telephone or walkie-\\n                 \
      \  talkie are provided and maintained for arranging better effective communication\\n                 at an\
      \ excavation or tunnelling work as per Rule 136 of BOCWR.\\n\\n             iv)     all portable electrical\
      \ hand tools and inspection lamp used in under ground and\\n               confined space at an excavation\
      \ or tunnelling work is operated at a voltage not\\n              exceeding 24V.\\n\\n           v)    only\
      \ flame proof equipment of appropriate type as per IS:5571:2000 and or\\n                other relevant national\
      \ standard is used inside the tunnel\\n\\n             vi)    petrol or LPG of any other flammable substances\
      \ are not used, stored inside the\\n                tunnel except with prior approval from Employer, and also\
      \ no oxy-acetylene gas\\n                    is used in a compressed air environment in excavation or tunnelling\\\
      n\\n              vii)   adequate number of water outlets provided for fire fighting purpose, an audible\\\
      n                     fire alarm and adequate number and types of fire extinguishers are provided\\n     \
      \        and maintained.\\n\\n               viii)  temperature in any working chamber in an excavation or\
      \ tunnelling work where\\n              workers employed does not exceed 29C as per Rule 165 of BOCWR.\\\
      n\\n             ix)     all working areas in a free air tunnel are provided with ventilation system as\\\
      n              approved by the Director General and the fresh air supplied in such tunnel is not\\n      \
      \          less than 6 m3/ min for each worker employed in tunnel as per Rule 153 of\\n          BOCWR.\\\
      n\\n\\n34.3     Warning signs and notices:\\n\\n\\n34.3.1   The contractor shall ensure that\\n\\n       \
      \         i)     suitable warning signs or notices, required for the safety of building workers\\n       \
      \         carrying out the work of an excavation or tunnelling, shall be displayed or\\n               erected\
      \ at conspicuous  places in Hindi and in a language understood by\\n                majority of such building\
      \ workers at such building such excavation or tunnelling\\n              work\\n\\n                  ii) \
      \   such warning signs and notices with regard to compressed air working shall\\n                include\\\
      n\\n                a)    the danger involved in such compressed air work\\n\\n                b)     fire\
      \ and explosion hazard\\n\\n                 c)    the emergency procedures for rescue from such danger or\
      \ hazards.\"\n    }\n  ],\n  \"heading_line\": \"          34.0     Excavation and Tunnelling:\",\n  \"retained_lines\"\
      : [\n    {\n      \"pdf_page\": 55,\n      \"source_line_number\": 21,\n      \"text\": \"          34.0 \

- kind: parameter
  text: Demolition work under Safety Clause 33 must be conducted in a controlled manner under experienced supervision,
    requiring prior notification to local authorities/media, utility shutoffs, protective capping of supply lines,

    quote: "{\n  \"clause_id\": \"33.0\",\n  \"fragments\": [\n    {\n      \"pdf_page\": 54,\n      \"text\": \"\
      33.0     Demolition\\n\\n33.1    The Contractor shall ensure that\\n\\n                i)       all  demolition\
      \  works be  carried  out  in a  controlled manner  under  the\\n            management of experienced and\
      \ competent supervision.\\n\\n                  ii)    the concerned department of the Government or local\
      \ authority be informed and\\n               permission obtained wherever required. Media shall also be informed\
      \ regarding\\n                   this concern.\\n\\n\\n                  iii)     all glass or similar materials\
      \ or articles in exterior openings are removed\\n              before commencing any demolition work and all\
      \ water, steam, electric,\\n             gas and other similar supply lines are put-off and such lines so\
      \ located or\\n            capped with substantial coverings so as to protect it from damage and to\\n   \
      \            afford safety to the building workers and public..\"\n    },\n    {\n      \"pdf_page\": 55,\n\
      \      \"text\": \"iv)   examine the walls of all structures adjacent to the structure to be demolished to\\\

      \                    unless and until remedial measures life sheet piling, shoring, bracing or similar\\n\
      \                    means be ensured for safety and stability for adjacent structure from collapsing.\\n\\\

- kind: parameter
  text: Excavation safety under Clause 34 mandates adequate piling/bracing for excavations deeper than 1.5 m, safe
    access ramps conforming to IS 3696, proper spoil storage clearances of at least 0.65 m, and professional engineering
    designs for trenches exceeding 4 m depth.

    quote: "{\n  \"clause_id\": \"34.0\",\n  \"fragments\": [\n    {\n      \"pdf_page\": 55,\n      \"text\": \"\
      34.0     Excavation and Tunnelling:\\n\\n\\n          34.1     Excavation\\n\\n\\n          34.1.1   The contractor\
      \ shall ensure\\n\\n\\n                                 i)    where any construction building worker engaged\
      \ in excavation is exposed to\\n                       hazard of falling or sliding material or article from\
      \ any bank or side of such\\n                         excavation which is more than one 1.5 m above his footing,\
      \ such worker is\\n                          protected by adequate piling and bracing against such bank or\
      \ side.\\n\\n\\n                                    ii)    where banks of an excavation are undercut, adequate\
      \ shoring is provided to\\n                         support the material or article overhanging such bank.\\\
      n\\n\\n                                     iii)   excavated material is not stored at least 0.65 m from the\
      \ edge of an open\\n                         excavation or trench and banks of such excavation or trench are\
      \ stripped of\\n                         loose rocks and the banks of such excavation or trench are stripped\
      \ of loose\\n                         rocks and other materials which may slide,  roll or  fall upon a construction\\\
      n                           building worker working below such bank\\n\\n\\n                          iv)\
      \   metal ladders and staircases or ramps are provided, as the case may be, for\\n                       \
      \  safe access to and egress from excavation where, the depth of such excavation\\n                      exceeds\
      \ 1.5 m and such ladders, staircases or ramps comply with the IS 3696\\n                          Part 1&2\
      \ and other relevant national standards.\\n\\n\\n                      v)    trench and excavation  is protected\
      \ against  falling of a person by suitable\\n                     measures  if the depth of such trench or\
      \ excavation exceeds 1.5 m and such\\n                           protection is an improved protection in accordance\
      \ with the design and drawing\\n                            of a professional engineer, where such depth exceeds\
      \ 4m.\\n\\n\\n          34.2      Tunnelling\\n\\n\\n          34.2.1   The contractor shall inform in writing\
      \ to the Director General within 30 days, prior to\\n                    the commencement of any tunnelling\
      \ work.\\n\\n\\n          34.2.2   The contractor shall appoint a responsible person for safe operation for\
      \ tunnelling\\n                 work as per Rule 121 & 125 of BOCWR.\\n\\n\\n          34.2.3   The contractor\
      \ shall ensure\"\n    },\n    {\n      \"pdf_page\": 56,\n      \"text\": \"i)    every compressed air system\
      \ in a tunnel is provided with emergency power\\n               supply for maintained continued supply of\
      \ compressed air as per Rule 155 of\\n         BOCWR\\n\\n                  ii)    watertight bulkhead doors\
      \ are installed at the entrance of a tunnel to prevent\\n                 flooding.\\n\\n                \
      \  iii)    reliable and effective means of communication such as telephone or walkie-\\n                 \
      \  talkie are provided and maintained for arranging better effective communication\\n                 at an\
      \ excavation or tunnelling work as per Rule 136 of BOCWR.\\n\\n             iv)     all portable electrical\
      \ hand tools and inspection lamp used in under ground and\\n               confined space at an excavation\
      \ or tunnelling work is operated at a voltage not\\n              exceeding 24V.\\n\\n           v)    only\
      \ flame proof equipment of appropriate type as per IS:5571:2000 and or\\n                other relevant national\
      \ standard is used inside the tunnel\\n\\n             vi)    petrol or LPG of any other flammable substances\
      \ are not used, stored inside the\\n                tunnel except with prior approval from Employer, and also\
      \ no oxy-acetylene gas\\n                    is used in a compressed air environment in excavation or tunnelling\\\
      n\\n              vii)   adequate number of water outlets provided for fire fighting purpose, an audible\\\
      n                     fire alarm and adequate number and types of fire extinguishers are provided\\n     \
      \        and maintained.\\n\\n               viii)  temperature in any working chamber in an excavation or\
      \ tunnelling work where\\n              workers employed does not exceed 29C as per Rule 165 of BOCWR.\\\
      n\\n             ix)     all working areas in a free air tunnel are provided with ventilation system as\\\
      n              approved by the Director General and the fresh air supplied in such tunnel is not\\n      \
      \          less than 6 m3/ min for each worker employed in tunnel as per Rule 153 of\\n          BOCWR.\\\
      n\\n\\n34.3     Warning signs and notices:\\n\\n\\n34.3.1   The contractor shall ensure that\\n\\n       \
      \         i)     suitable warning signs or notices, required for the safety of building workers\\n       \
      \         carrying out the work of an excavation or tunnelling, shall be displayed or\\n               erected\
      \ at conspicuous  places in Hindi and in a language understood by\\n                majority of such building\
      \ workers at such building such excavation or tunnelling\\n              work\\n\\n                  ii) \
      \   such warning signs and notices with regard to compressed air working shall\\n                include\\\
      n\\n                a)    the danger involved in such compressed air work\\n\\n                b)     fire\
      \ and explosion hazard\\n\\n                 c)    the emergency procedures for rescue from such danger or\
      \ hazards.\"\n    }\n  ],\n  \"heading_line\": \"          34.0     Excavation and Tunnelling:\",\n  \"retained_lines\"\

- kind: parameter
  text: Tunnelling provisions under Clause 34 require 30 days prior written notice to the Director General before
    commencement, appointment of a responsible person under BOCWR rules, emergency power supply for compressed air
    systems, watertight bulkhead doors, and 24V voltage limits for portable tools in underground and confined spaces.

    quote: "{\n  \"clause_id\": \"34.0\",\n  \"fragments\": [\n    {\n      \"pdf_page\": 55,\n      \"text\": \"\
      34.0     Excavation and Tunnelling:\\n\\n\\n          34.1     Excavation\\n\\n\\n          34.1.1   The contractor\
      \ shall ensure\\n\\n\\n                                 i)    where any construction building worker engaged\
      \ in excavation is exposed to\\n                       hazard of falling or sliding material or article from\
      \ any bank or side of such\\n                         excavation which is more than one 1.5 m above his footing,\
      \ such worker is\\n                          protected by adequate piling and bracing against such bank or\
      \ side.\\n\\n\\n                                    ii)    where banks of an excavation are undercut, adequate\
      \ shoring is provided to\\n                         support the material or article overhanging such bank.\\\
      n\\n\\n                                     iii)   excavated material is not stored at least 0.65 m from the\
      \ edge of an open\\n                         excavation or trench and banks of such excavation or trench are\
      \ stripped of\\n                         loose rocks and the banks of such excavation or trench are stripped\
      \ of loose\\n                         rocks and other materials which may slide,  roll or  fall upon a construction\\\
      n                           building worker working below such bank\\n\\n\\n                          iv)\
      \   metal ladders and staircases or ramps are provided, as the case may be, for\\n                       \
      \  safe access to and egress from excavation where, the depth of such excavation\\n                      exceeds\
      \ 1.5 m and such ladders, staircases or ramps comply with the IS 3696\\n                          Part 1&2\
      \ and other relevant national standards.\\n\\n\\n                      v)    trench and excavation  is protected\
      \ against  falling of a person by suitable\\n                     measures  if the depth of such trench or\
      \ excavation exceeds 1.5 m and such\\n                           protection is an improved protection in accordance\
      \ with the design and drawing\\n                            of a professional engineer, where such depth exceeds\
      \ 4m.\\n\\n\\n          34.2      Tunnelling\\n\\n\\n          34.2.1   The contractor shall inform in writing\
      \ to the Director General within 30 days, prior to\\n                    the commencement of any tunnelling\
      \ work.\\n\\n\\n          34.2.2   The contractor shall appoint a responsible person for safe operation for\
      \ tunnelling\\n                 work as per Rule 121 & 125 of BOCWR.\\n\\n\\n          34.2.3   The contractor\
      \ shall ensure\"\n    },\n    {\n      \"pdf_page\": 56,\n      \"text\": \"i)    every compressed air system\
      \ in a tunnel is provided with emergency power\\n               supply for maintained continued supply of\
      \ compressed air as per Rule 155 of\\n         BOCWR\\n\\n                  ii)    watertight bulkhead doors\
      \ are installed at the entrance of a tunnel to prevent\\n                 flooding.\\n\\n                \
      \  iii)    reliable and effective means of communication such as telephone or walkie-\\n                 \
      \  talkie are provided and maintained for arranging better effective communication\\n                 at an\
      \ excavation or tunnelling work as per Rule 136 of BOCWR.\\n\\n             iv)     all portable electrical\
      \ hand tools and inspection lamp used in under ground and\\n               confined space at an excavation\
      \ or tunnelling work is operated at a voltage not\\n              exceeding 24V.\\n\\n           v)    only\
      \ flame proof equipment of appropriate type as per IS:5571:2000 and or\\n                other relevant national\
      \ standard is used inside the tunnel\\n\\n             vi)    petrol or LPG of any other flammable substances\
      \ are not used, stored inside the\\n                tunnel except with prior approval from Employer, and also\
      \ no oxy-acetylene gas\\n                    is used in a compressed air environment in excavation or tunnelling\\\
      n\\n              vii)   adequate number of water outlets provided for fire fighting purpose, an audible\\\
      n                     fire alarm and adequate number and types of fire extinguishers are provided\\n     \
      \        and maintained.\\n\\n               viii)  temperature in any working chamber in an excavation or\
      \ tunnelling work where\\n              workers employed does not exceed 29C as per Rule 165 of BOCWR.\\\
      n\\n             ix)     all working areas in a free air tunnel are provided with ventilation system as\\\
      n              approved by the Director General and the fresh air supplied in such tunnel is not\\n      \
      \          less than 6 m3/ min for each worker employed in tunnel as per Rule 153 of\\n          BOCWR.\\\
      n\\n\\n34.3     Warning signs and notices:\\n\\n\\n34.3.1   The contractor shall ensure that\\n\\n       \
      \         i)     suitable warning signs or notices, required for the safety of building workers\\n       \
      \         carrying out the work of an excavation or tunnelling, shall be displayed or\\n               erected\
      \ at conspicuous  places in Hindi and in a language understood by\\n                majority of such building\
      \ workers at such building such excavation or tunnelling\\n              work\\n\\n                  ii) \
      \   such warning signs and notices with regard to compressed air working shall\\n                include\\\
      n\\n                a)    the danger involved in such compressed air work\\n\\n                b)     fire\
      \ and explosion hazard\\n\\n                 c)    the emergency procedures for rescue from such danger or\
      \ hazards.\"\n    }\n  ],\n  \"heading_line\": \"          34.0     Excavation and Tunnelling:\",\n  \"retained_lines\"\

- kind: parameter
  text: The Work Permit system under Clause 35 mandates a formal written system for high-risk activities such as
    confined space entry, overhead power line proximity work, hot work, excavation, heavy machinery work, and electrical
    equipment maintenance, with a maximum permit duration of 12 hours.

    quote: "{\n  \"clause_id\": \"35.0\",\n  \"fragments\": [\n    {\n      \"pdf_page\": 56,\n      \"text\": \"\
      35.0    Work Permit system\\n\\n\\n35.1    The Contractor shall develop a Work Permit system, which is a formal\
      \ written system\\n        used to control certain types of work that are potentially hazardous. A work permit\
      \ is a\\n         document, which specifies the work to be done, and the precautions to be taken. Work\\n\
      \         Permits form an essential part of safe systems of work for many construction activities.\\n    \
      \    They allow work to start only after safe procedures have been defined and they\\n          provide a\
      \ clear record that all foreseeable hazards have been considered. Permits to\\n        Work are usually required\
      \ in high-risk areas as identified by the Risk Assessments.\\n\\n\\n35.2    A permit  is needed when construction\
      \ work can only be carried out   if normal\\n         safeguards are dropped or when new hazards are introduced\
      \ by the work. Examples\\n           of high-risk activities include but are not limited to:\\n\\n\\n    \
      \             i)     Entry into confined spaces\\n                  ii)   Work in close proximity to overhead\
      \ power lines and telecommunication cables.\\n                  iii)   Hot work.\\n             iv)   To dig—where\
      \ underground services may be located.\\n           v)   Work with heavy moving machinery.\"\n    },\n   \
      \ {\n      \"pdf_page\": 57,\n      \"text\": \"vi)   Working on electrical equipment\\n                 \
      \            vii)  Work with radioactive isotopes.\\n                               viii)  Heavy lifting operations\
      \ and lifting operations closer to live power line\\n\\n\\n          35.3    The permit-to-work system should\
      \ be fully documented, laying down:\\n\\n\\n                                 i)   How the system works;\\\
      n                                    ii)   The jobs it is to be used for;\\n                             \
      \        iii)   The responsibilities and training of those involved; and\\n                          iv) \
      \ How to check its operation;\\n\\n\\n          35.4    A Work Permit authorisation form shall be completed\
      \ with the maximum duration\\n                    period not exceeding 12 hours.\\n\\n\\n          35.5  \
      \  A copy of each Permit To Work shall be displayed, during its validity, in a conspicuous\\n            \
      \         location in close proximity to the actual works location to which it applies.\"\n    }\n  ],\n \

    formal work permit system for high-risk activities.

    quote: "{\n  \"clause_id\": \"38.0\",\n  \"fragments\": [\n    {\n      \"pdf_page\": 59,\n      \"text\": \"\
      38.0     Batching Plant and Casting Yard layout\\n\\n\\n                                 i)    The batching\
      \ plant / casting yard shall be effectively planned for smooth flow of\\n                         unloading\
      \ and stacking the aggregates reinforcements and cement, batching\\n                             plant, transport\
      \ of concrete, casting the segment, stacking the segment and\\n                          loading the segments\
      \ to the trucks. As far as possible the conflicts should be\\n                         avoided.\\n\\n    \
      \                                ii)   The batching plant / casting yard shall be barricaded and made as a\
      \ compulsory\\n                  PPE zone\\n\\n                                     iii)      If in case of\
      \ material unloading area is not maintainable as PPE zone, the same\\n                             shall be\
      \ segregated properly and made as a non-PPE zone with appropriate\\n                            barrications.\\\
      n\\n                          iv)    Electrical system  shall also be suitably planned so that location  of\
      \ diesel\\n                          generator,  if any, location of DBs, routing of cables and positioning\
      \ of area\\n                              lighting poles/masts does not infringe on any other utility and\
      \ pose danger.\"\n    },\n    {\n      \"pdf_page\": 60,\n      \"text\": \"v)    Drainage shall be effectively\
      \ provided and waste water shall be disposed after\\n               proper treatment\\n\\n             vi)\
      \   Time office, canteen, drinking water,  toilet and rest place shall be suitably\\n                located\
      \  for the easy access to workers.  All the  facilities shall be properly\\n              cleaned and maintained\
      \ during the entire period of operation.\\n\\n              vii)   Manual handling of cement shall be avoided\
      \ to a larger extent. Whenever  it is\\n                absolutely necessary the workmen shall be given  full\
      \ body protection, hand\\n                protection and respiratory protection as a basic measure of ensuring\
      \ better\\n                 health.\\n\\n               viii)  The PPEs provided to cement handling workmen\
      \ shall conform to international\\n               standards.\\n\\n             ix)   Access roads and internal\
      \ circulation roads shall be well laid and maintained\\n                properly at all time.\\n\\n      \
      \     x)    Non-adherence to any of the above provision shall be penalised as per relevant\\n            \

      \ and maintained during the entire period of operation.\"\n    },\n    {\n      \"pdf_page\": 60,\n      \"\
      source_line_number\": 9,\n      \"text\": \"\"\n    },\n    {\n      \"pdf_page\": 60,\n      \"source_line_number\"\
      : 10,\n      \"text\": \"              vii)   Manual handling of cement shall be avoided to a larger extent.\
      \ Whenever  it is\"\n    },\n    {\n      \"pdf_page\": 60,\n      \"source_line_number\": 11,\n      \"text\"\
      : \"                absolutely necessary the workmen shall be given  full body protection, hand\"\n    },\n\
      \    {\n      \"pdf_page\": 60,\n      \"source_line_number\": 12,\n      \"text\": \"                protection\
      \ and respiratory protection as a basic measure of ensuring better\"\n    },\n    {\n      \"pdf_page\": 60,\n\
      \      \"source_line_number\": 13,\n      \"text\": \"                 health.\"\n    },\n    {\n      \"\
      pdf_page\": 60,\n      \"source_line_number\": 14,\n      \"text\": \"\"\n    },\n    {\n      \"pdf_page\"\
      : 60,\n      \"source_line_number\": 15,\n      \"text\": \"               viii)  The PPEs provided to cement\
      \ handling workmen shall conform to international\"\n    },\n    {\n      \"pdf_page\": 60,\n      \"source_line_number\"\
      : 16,\n      \"text\": \"               standards.\"\n    },\n    {\n      \"pdf_page\": 60,\n      \"source_line_number\"\
      : 17,\n      \"text\": \"\"\n    },\n    {\n      \"pdf_page\": 60,\n      \"source_line_number\": 18,\n \
      \     \"text\": \"             ix)   Access roads and internal circulation roads shall be well laid and maintained\"\
      \n    },\n    {\n      \"pdf_page\": 60,\n      \"source_line_number\": 19,\n      \"text\": \"          \
      \      properly at all time.\"\n    },\n    {\n      \"pdf_page\": 60,\n      \"source_line_number\": 20,\n\
      \      \"text\": \"\"\n    },\n    {\n      \"pdf_page\": 60,\n      \"source_line_number\": 21,\n      \"\

      37.0    Work to adjacent railways\\n\\n          37.1     Whenever work is to be conducted in close proximity\
      \ to the live railways then the\\n                     following measures shall need to be addressed:\\n\\\
      n                      (a)  The rules provided for in the Railway’s manual should be followed.\\n\\n     \
      \                 (b)  No persons are allowed to encroach onto the railway unless the owner has\\n       \
      \                  given specific authority.\\n\\n                       (c)   Adequate protection in accordance\
      \ with the railway owner’s requirements shall\\n                     be followed. (Provision of Block Inspectors,\
      \ Flagmen and Lookouts)\\n\\n                      (d)    All persons shall wear high visibility clothing\
      \ at all times.\\n\\n                      (e)  Any induction training requirements of the railways shall\
      \ be strictly observed\"\n    }\n  ],\n  \"heading_line\": \"          37.0    Work to adjacent railways\"\

    source_document: Vol3DLNP1.pdf
    source_sha256: 1ee3fc8dfd12f659f34446b0a6db74e1e1cdd4d593ca91b2a48d59bf1ef97d52

    json_path: parsed_json/vol3/part_2_safety/safety_clauses.json
    json_sha256: 0042f3256acc51ca4ebb327c3cee57a308fa5f47e1a4ccc7f4994fe898fa11ef

    quote: "{\n  \"clause_id\": \"36.0\",\n  \"fragments\": [\n    {\n      \"pdf_page\": 57,\n      \"text\": \"\
      36.0      Traffic Management\\n\\n\\n          36.1    The basic objective of the following guidelines  is\
      \ to lay down procedures to be\\n                  adopted by contractor to ensure the safe and efficient\
      \ movement of traffic and also to\\n                  ensure the safety of workmen at construction sites.\\\
      n\\n\\n          36.2       All construction workers should be provided with high visibility jackets with\
      \ reflective\\n                   tapes as most of viaduct /tunnelling/station and depot works or either above\
      \ or under\\n                      right-of-way. The conspicuity of workmen at  all times shall be increased\
      \ so as to\\n                     protect from speeding vehicular traffic.\\n\\n\\n          36.3    The guiding\
      \ principles to be adopted for safety in construction zone are to\\n\\n\\n                               \
      \  i)    Warn the road user clearly and sufficiently in advance.\\n\\n                                   \
      \ ii)    Provide safe and clearly marked lanes for guiding road users.\\n\\n                             \
      \        iii)    Provide safe and clearly marked buffer and work zones\\n\\n                          iv)\
      \   Provide adequate measures that control driver behaviour through construction\\n                      \
      \  zones.\\n\\n\\n          36.4     Legal permission\\n\\n\\n          36.4.1    In  all cases, the contractor\
      \ shall employ proper precautions. Wherever operations\\n                  undertaken are likely to interfere\
      \ with public traffic, specific traffic management plans\\n                      shall be drawn up and implemented\
      \ by the contractor in consultation with the approval\\n                      of local police authorities\
      \ and/or the concerned metropolitan/civil authorities as the\\n                 case may be.\\n\\n\\n    \
      \      36.4.2   Such  traffic management plans  shall  include  provision  for  traffic  diversion and\\n\
      \                     selection of alternative routes for transport of equipment.  If necessary, the contractor\\\
      n                      shall carry out road widening before commencement of works to accommodate the\\n  \
      \                  extra load\\n\\n\\n          36.5    The primary traffic control devices used in work zones\
      \ shall include signs, delineators,\\n                    barricades, cones, pylons, pavement markings and\
      \ flashing lights.\\n\\n\\n          36.6    The road construction and maintenance signs which fall into the\
      \ same three major\\n                    categories as do other traffic signs, that are Regulatory Signs,\
      \ Warning Signs and\\n                     Direction (or guidelines) Signs shall only be used. The IRC: 67\
      \ (Code of Practice for\\n               Road Signs) provide a list of traffic signs. The size, colours and\
      \ placement of sign\\n                      shall confirm to IRC: 67.\"\n    },\n    {\n      \"pdf_page\"\
      : 58,\n      \"text\": \"36.7     Regulatory signs\\n\\n\\n36.7.1    Regulatory signs impose legal restriction\
      \ on all traffic.  It is essential, therefore, that\\n         they are used only after consulting the local\
      \ police and traffic authorities.\\n\\n\\n36.8     Warning signs\\n\\n\\n36.8.1   Warning signs in the traffic\
      \ control zone shall be utilised to warn the drivers of specific\\n         hazards that may be encountered.\\\
      n\\n\\n36.8.2   The contractor shall place detour signage at strategic locations and install appropriate\\\
      n         warning signs.  In order to minimize disruption of access to residences and business,\\n       \
      \   the contractor shall maintain at least one entrance to a property where multiple\\n         entrances\
      \ exist.\\n\\n\\n36.8.3   A warning sign as given in general instruction BMRC/SHE/CEO/012 shall be installed\\\
      n        an at all secondary road which merges with the primary road where the construction\\n         work\
      \ is in progress at sufficient distance before it merges with the primary road so as\\n           to alert\
      \ the road users regarding the ‘Metro Work in Progress’.\\n\\n\\n36.8.4    Materials hanging over / protruded\
      \ from the chassis / body of any vehicle especially\\n          during material handling shall be indicated\
      \ by red indicator (red light/flag) to indicate\\n          the caution to the road users.\\n\\n\\n36.9  \
      \    Delineators\\n\\n        The delineators are the elements of a total system of traffic control and have\
      \ two\\n            distinct purposes:\\n\\n                i)    To delineate and guide the driver to and\
      \ along a safe path\\n\\n                  ii)   As a taper to move traffic from one lane to another.\\n\\\
      n\\n36.9.1   These channelizing devices such as cones, traffic cylinders, tapes and drums shall be\\n    \
      \     placed in or adjacent to the roadway to control the flow of  traffic. These should\\n          normally\
      \ be retro-reflectors complying to IRC: 79 - Recommended Practice for Road\\n          Delineators.\\n\\n\\\
      n36.9.2    Traffic cones and cylinders\\n\\n\\n36.9.2.1  Traffic cones of 500mm, 750mm and 1000mm high and\
      \ 300mm to 500mm in diameter\\n          or in square shape at base and are often made of plastic or rubber\
      \ and normally have\\n           retro-reflectorised red and white band shall be used wherever required.\\\
      n\\n36.9.3   Drums\\n\\n36.9.3.1  Drums about 800mm to 1000mm high and 300mm in diameter can be used either\
      \ as\\n          channelising or warning devices. These are highly visible, give the appearance of\\n    \
      \     being formidable objects and therefore command the respect of drivers.\\n\\n\\n36.9.4    Barricades\\\
      n\\n\\n36.9.4.1  Full height fence, barriers, barricades etc. shall be erected around the site in order to\\\
      n         prevent the working area from  the  risk  of  accidents due  to speedy  vehicular\\n        movement.\
      \ Same the way barricades protect the road users from the danger due to\\n          construction equipment\
      \ and other temporary structures.\\n\\n\\n36.9.4.2  The structure dimension of the barricade, material and\
      \ composition, its colour scheme,\\n      BMRC logo and other details shall be in accordance with specifications\
      \ laid down in\\n          tender document.\"\n    },\n    {\n      \"pdf_page\": 59,\n      \"text\": \"\
      36.9.4.3  All barricades shall be erected as per the design requirements of the Employer,\\n             \
      \    numbered, painted and maintained in good condition and also Barricade in-charge\\n                  \
      \ maintains a barricade register in site.\\n\\n\\n          36.9.4.4  All barricades shall be conspicuously\
      \ seen in the dark/night time by the road\\n                 users so that no vehicle hits the barricade.\
      \ Conspicuity. shall be ensured by\\n                     affixing retro reflective stripes of required size\
      \ and shape at appropriate angle at\\n                  the bottom and middle portion of the barricade at\
      \ a minimum gap of 1000mm. In\\n                   addition minimum one red light or red light blinker should\
      \ be placed at the top\\n                   of each barricade.\\n\\n\\n          36.9.5   The contractor shall\
      \ ensure that all his construction vehicles plying on public roads\\n                         (like dump trucks,\
      \ trailers, etc.) have proper license to ply on public roads from the\\n                    State Transport\
      \ Authority. Drivers holding proper valid license as per the requirements\\n                      of Motor\
      \ Vehicles Act shall drive these vehicles\\n\\n\\n          36.9.6   The contractor shall not undertake loading\
      \ and unloading at carriageways obstructing\\n                    the free flow of vehicular traffic and encroachment\
      \ of existing roads by the contractor\\n                    applying the excuse of work execution.\\n\\n\\\
      n          36.9.7   Tow away vehicle\\n\\n\\n          36.9.7.1  The contractor shall make arrangements keeping\
      \ tow away van / manpower to\\n                tow away any breakdown vehicle in the traffic flow without\
      \ loosing any time at\\n                   his cost.\\n\\n          36.9.8   Cleaning of roads\\n\\n\\n  \
      \        36.9.8.1  The contractor shall ensure the cleanliness of roads and footpaths by deploying\\n    \
      \             proper manpower for the same. The contractor shall have to ensure proper\\n                \
      \ brooming, cleaning washing of roads and footpaths on all the time throughout\\n                  the entire\
      \ stretch till the currency of the contract including disposal of seepage.\"\n    }\n  ],\n  \"heading_line\"\

    quote: "{\n  \"clause_id\": \"35.0\",\n  \"fragments\": [\n    {\n      \"pdf_page\": 56,\n      \"text\": \"\
      35.0    Work Permit system\\n\\n\\n35.1    The Contractor shall develop a Work Permit system, which is a formal\
      \ written system\\n        used to control certain types of work that are potentially hazardous. A work permit\
      \ is a\\n         document, which specifies the work to be done, and the precautions to be taken. Work\\n\
      \         Permits form an essential part of safe systems of work for many construction activities.\\n    \
      \    They allow work to start only after safe procedures have been defined and they\\n          provide a\
      \ clear record that all foreseeable hazards have been considered. Permits to\\n        Work are usually required\
      \ in high-risk areas as identified by the Risk Assessments.\\n\\n\\n35.2    A permit  is needed when construction\
      \ work can only be carried out   if normal\\n         safeguards are dropped or when new hazards are introduced\
      \ by the work. Examples\\n           of high-risk activities include but are not limited to:\\n\\n\\n    \
      \             i)     Entry into confined spaces\\n                  ii)   Work in close proximity to overhead\
      \ power lines and telecommunication cables.\\n                  iii)   Hot work.\\n             iv)   To dig—where\
      \ underground services may be located.\\n           v)   Work with heavy moving machinery.\"\n    },\n   \
      \ {\n      \"pdf_page\": 57,\n      \"text\": \"vi)   Working on electrical equipment\\n                 \
      \            vii)  Work with radioactive isotopes.\\n                               viii)  Heavy lifting operations\
      \ and lifting operations closer to live power line\\n\\n\\n          35.3    The permit-to-work system should\
      \ be fully documented, laying down:\\n\\n\\n                                 i)   How the system works;\\\
      n                                    ii)   The jobs it is to be used for;\\n                             \
      \        iii)   The responsibilities and training of those involved; and\\n                          iv) \
      \ How to check its operation;\\n\\n\\n          35.4    A Work Permit authorisation form shall be completed\
      \ with the maximum duration\\n                    period not exceeding 12 hours.\\n\\n\\n          35.5  \
      \  A copy of each Permit To Work shall be displayed, during its validity, in a conspicuous\\n            \
      \         location in close proximity to the actual works location to which it applies.\"\n    }\n  ],\n \

    quote: "{\n  \"clause_id\": \"36.0\",\n  \"fragments\": [\n    {\n      \"pdf_page\": 57,\n      \"text\": \"\
      36.0      Traffic Management\\n\\n\\n          36.1    The basic objective of the following guidelines  is\
      \ to lay down procedures to be\\n                  adopted by contractor to ensure the safe and efficient\
      \ movement of traffic and also to\\n                  ensure the safety of workmen at construction sites.\\\
      n\\n\\n          36.2       All construction workers should be provided with high visibility jackets with\
      \ reflective\\n                   tapes as most of viaduct /tunnelling/station and depot works or either above\
      \ or under\\n                      right-of-way. The conspicuity of workmen at  all times shall be increased\
      \ so as to\\n                     protect from speeding vehicular traffic.\\n\\n\\n          36.3    The guiding\
      \ principles to be adopted for safety in construction zone are to\\n\\n\\n                               \
      \  i)    Warn the road user clearly and sufficiently in advance.\\n\\n                                   \
      \ ii)    Provide safe and clearly marked lanes for guiding road users.\\n\\n                             \
      \        iii)    Provide safe and clearly marked buffer and work zones\\n\\n                          iv)\
      \   Provide adequate measures that control driver behaviour through construction\\n                      \
      \  zones.\\n\\n\\n          36.4     Legal permission\\n\\n\\n          36.4.1    In  all cases, the contractor\
      \ shall employ proper precautions. Wherever operations\\n                  undertaken are likely to interfere\
      \ with public traffic, specific traffic management plans\\n                      shall be drawn up and implemented\
      \ by the contractor in consultation with the approval\\n                      of local police authorities\
      \ and/or the concerned metropolitan/civil authorities as the\\n                 case may be.\\n\\n\\n    \
      \      36.4.2   Such  traffic management plans  shall  include  provision  for  traffic  diversion and\\n\
      \                     selection of alternative routes for transport of equipment.  If necessary, the contractor\\\
      n                      shall carry out road widening before commencement of works to accommodate the\\n  \
      \                  extra load\\n\\n\\n          36.5    The primary traffic control devices used in work zones\
      \ shall include signs, delineators,\\n                    barricades, cones, pylons, pavement markings and\
      \ flashing lights.\\n\\n\\n          36.6    The road construction and maintenance signs which fall into the\
      \ same three major\\n                    categories as do other traffic signs, that are Regulatory Signs,\
      \ Warning Signs and\\n                     Direction (or guidelines) Signs shall only be used. The IRC: 67\
      \ (Code of Practice for\\n               Road Signs) provide a list of traffic signs. The size, colours and\
      \ placement of sign\\n                      shall confirm to IRC: 67.\"\n    },\n    {\n      \"pdf_page\"\
      : 58,\n      \"text\": \"36.7     Regulatory signs\\n\\n\\n36.7.1    Regulatory signs impose legal restriction\
      \ on all traffic.  It is essential, therefore, that\\n         they are used only after consulting the local\
      \ police and traffic authorities.\\n\\n\\n36.8     Warning signs\\n\\n\\n36.8.1   Warning signs in the traffic\
      \ control zone shall be utilised to warn the drivers of specific\\n         hazards that may be encountered.\\\
      n\\n\\n36.8.2   The contractor shall place detour signage at strategic locations and install appropriate\\\
      n         warning signs.  In order to minimize disruption of access to residences and business,\\n       \
      \   the contractor shall maintain at least one entrance to a property where multiple\\n         entrances\
      \ exist.\\n\\n\\n36.8.3   A warning sign as given in general instruction BMRC/SHE/CEO/012 shall be installed\\\
      n        an at all secondary road which merges with the primary road where the construction\\n         work\
      \ is in progress at sufficient distance before it merges with the primary road so as\\n           to alert\
      \ the road users regarding the ‘Metro Work in Progress’.\\n\\n\\n36.8.4    Materials hanging over / protruded\
      \ from the chassis / body of any vehicle especially\\n          during material handling shall be indicated\
      \ by red indicator (red light/flag) to indicate\\n          the caution to the road users.\\n\\n\\n36.9  \
      \    Delineators\\n\\n        The delineators are the elements of a total system of traffic control and have\
      \ two\\n            distinct purposes:\\n\\n                i)    To delineate and guide the driver to and\
      \ along a safe path\\n\\n                  ii)   As a taper to move traffic from one lane to another.\\n\\\
      n\\n36.9.1   These channelizing devices such as cones, traffic cylinders, tapes and drums shall be\\n    \
      \     placed in or adjacent to the roadway to control the flow of  traffic. These should\\n          normally\
      \ be retro-reflectors complying to IRC: 79 - Recommended Practice for Road\\n          Delineators.\\n\\n\\\
      n36.9.2    Traffic cones and cylinders\\n\\n\\n36.9.2.1  Traffic cones of 500mm, 750mm and 1000mm high and\
      \ 300mm to 500mm in diameter\\n          or in square shape at base and are often made of plastic or rubber\
      \ and normally have\\n           retro-reflectorised red and white band shall be used wherever required.\\\
      n\\n36.9.3   Drums\\n\\n36.9.3.1  Drums about 800mm to 1000mm high and 300mm in diameter can be used either\
      \ as\\n          channelising or warning devices. These are highly visible, give the appearance of\\n    \
      \     being formidable objects and therefore command the respect of drivers.\\n\\n\\n36.9.4    Barricades\\\
      n\\n\\n36.9.4.1  Full height fence, barriers, barricades etc. shall be erected around the site in order to\\\
      n         prevent the working area from  the  risk  of  accidents due  to speedy  vehicular\\n        movement.\
      \ Same the way barricades protect the road users from the danger due to\\n          construction equipment\
      \ and other temporary structures.\\n\\n\\n36.9.4.2  The structure dimension of the barricade, material and\
      \ composition, its colour scheme,\\n      BMRC logo and other details shall be in accordance with specifications\
      \ laid down in\\n          tender document.\"\n    },\n    {\n      \"pdf_page\": 59,\n      \"text\": \"\
      36.9.4.3  All barricades shall be erected as per the design requirements of the Employer,\\n             \
      \    numbered, painted and maintained in good condition and also Barricade in-charge\\n                  \
      \ maintains a barricade register in site.\\n\\n\\n          36.9.4.4  All barricades shall be conspicuously\
      \ seen in the dark/night time by the road\\n                 users so that no vehicle hits the barricade.\
      \ Conspicuity. shall be ensured by\\n                     affixing retro reflective stripes of required size\
      \ and shape at appropriate angle at\\n                  the bottom and middle portion of the barricade at\
      \ a minimum gap of 1000mm. In\\n                   addition minimum one red light or red light blinker should\
      \ be placed at the top\\n                   of each barricade.\\n\\n\\n          36.9.5   The contractor shall\
      \ ensure that all his construction vehicles plying on public roads\\n                         (like dump trucks,\
      \ trailers, etc.) have proper license to ply on public roads from the\\n                    State Transport\
      \ Authority. Drivers holding proper valid license as per the requirements\\n                      of Motor\
      \ Vehicles Act shall drive these vehicles\\n\\n\\n          36.9.6   The contractor shall not undertake loading\
      \ and unloading at carriageways obstructing\\n                    the free flow of vehicular traffic and encroachment\
      \ of existing roads by the contractor\\n                    applying the excuse of work execution.\\n\\n\\\
      n          36.9.7   Tow away vehicle\\n\\n\\n          36.9.7.1  The contractor shall make arrangements keeping\
      \ tow away van / manpower to\\n                tow away any breakdown vehicle in the traffic flow without\
      \ loosing any time at\\n                   his cost.\\n\\n          36.9.8   Cleaning of roads\\n\\n\\n  \
      \        36.9.8.1  The contractor shall ensure the cleanliness of roads and footpaths by deploying\\n    \
      \             proper manpower for the same. The contractor shall have to ensure proper\\n                \
      \ brooming, cleaning washing of roads and footpaths on all the time throughout\\n                  the entire\
      \ stretch till the currency of the contract including disposal of seepage.\"\n    }\n  ],\n  \"heading_line\"\

- kind: parameter
  text: Works conducted in close proximity to live railways must adhere to railway manual rules, prohibit unauthorized
    encroachment, follow railway owner protection requirements including block inspectors, flagmen, and lookouts,
    enforce high-visibility clothing, and observe railway induction training.

      37.0    Work to adjacent railways\\n\\n          37.1     Whenever work is to be conducted in close proximity\
      \ to the live railways then the\\n                     following measures shall need to be addressed:\\n\\\
      n                      (a)  The rules provided for in the Railway’s manual should be followed.\\n\\n     \
      \                 (b)  No persons are allowed to encroach onto the railway unless the owner has\\n       \
      \                  given specific authority.\\n\\n                       (c)   Adequate protection in accordance\
      \ with the railway owner’s requirements shall\\n                     be followed. (Provision of Block Inspectors,\
      \ Flagmen and Lookouts)\\n\\n                      (d)    All persons shall wear high visibility clothing\
      \ at all times.\\n\\n                      (e)  Any induction training requirements of the railways shall\
      \ be strictly observed\"\n    }\n  ],\n  \"heading_line\": \"          37.0    Work to adjacent railways\"\

  text: Batching plants and casting yards must be effectively planned to prevent conflicts, barricaded as compulsory
    PPE zones (or appropriately segregated non-PPE unloading areas), and equipped with proper electrical planning,
    drainage, worker amenities, and well-laid access roads.

      \ plant / casting yard shall be effectively planned for smooth flow of\\n                         unloading\
      \ and stacking the aggregates reinforcements and cement, batching\\n                             plant, transport\
      \ of concrete, casting the segment, stacking the segment and\\n                          loading the segments\
      \ to the trucks. As far as possible the conflicts should be\\n                         avoided.\\n\\n    \
      \                                ii)   The batching plant / casting yard shall be barricaded and made as a\
      \ compulsory\\n                  PPE zone\\n\\n                                     iii)      If in case of\
      \ material unloading area is not maintainable as PPE zone, the same\\n                             shall be\
      \ segregated properly and made as a non-PPE zone with appropriate\\n                            barrications.\\\

      \ diesel\\n                          generator,  if any, location of DBs, routing of cables and positioning\
      \ of area\\n                              lighting poles/masts does not infringe on any other utility and\
      \ pose danger.\"\n    },\n    {\n      \"pdf_page\": 60,\n      \"text\": \"v)    Drainage shall be effectively\

      \   Time office, canteen, drinking water,  toilet and rest place shall be suitably\\n                located\

      \ visibility clothing (waistcoat/jacket), Apron, etc)\\n             iv)   Personal fall protection (Full\
      \ body harness, Rope-grap fall arrester, etc)\\n           v)   Eye Protection (Goggles, Welders glasses,\
      \ etc)\\n             vi)   Hand Protection (Gloves, Finger coats, etc)\\n              vii)   Respiratory\
      \ Protection. (Nose mask, SCBAs, etc)\\n               viii)  Hearing Protection (Ear plugs, Ear muffs, etc)\\\
      n\\n\\n39.2    The PPEs and safety appliances provided by the contractor shall be of the\\n         standard\

    quote: "{\n  \"clause_id\": \"40.0\",\n  \"fragments\": [\n    {\n      \"pdf_page\": 62,\n      \"text\": \"\
      40.0      Visitors to site\\n\\n\\n 40.1    No visitor is allowed to enter the site without the permission\
      \ of the Employer. All\\n          authorised visitors should report at the site office. Contractor shall\
      \ provide visitor’s\\n          helmet (White helmet with visitor sticker) and other PPEs like Safety Shoe,\
      \ reflective\\n            jacket, respiratory protection etc. as per requirement of the site.\\n\\n\\n 40.2\
      \       All Visitors shall be accompanied at all times by a responsible member of the site\\n          personnel.\\\
      n\\n\\n 40.3    The contractor shall be fully responsible for all visitors’ safety and health within the\\\
      n             site.\\n\\n\\n 40.4    As indicated earlier in this Manual, the Engineer shall undertake regular\
      \ audits at\\n           quarterly intervals, of the Contractor’s onsite practices and procedures as a means\
      \ of\\n          assessing the ongoing performance of the Contractor.\\n\\n 40.5    The criteria against which\
      \ the audits will be undertaken shall be derived from the\\n          clauses within the Environment Protection\
      \ Requirements (Appendix III herein above),\\n           contract-specific Site Environmental Plan and previous\
      \ site inspection results.\\n\\n 40.6      In addition to the quarterly audits by the Engineer, site inspection\
      \ shall be undertaken\\n         by the Contractor’s staff to inspect the construction activities in order\
      \ to ensure that\\n           appropriate environmental protection and pollution control measures are properly\\\
      n           followed and implemented.\\n\\n 40.7    The frequency of site inspection shall be at least once\
      \ a week.\\n\\n 40.8    The Contractor shall prepare an ‘Environmental Inspection and Action Reporting\\n\
      \          System’ and submit to the Engineer for approval and make amendments as\\n          suggested. \
      \ It shall contain a contract specific comprehensive Environment Inspection\\n           checklist as requirement\
      \ of Site Environmental Plan.\\n 40.9    The area of inspection shall not be limited to environmental compliance\
      \ within the site\\n           but areas outside the site which are likely to be affected, directly or indirectly\
      \ by\\n             activities at site.\\n\\n 40.10     Results of inspection shall be discussed with Engineer\
      \ and his recommendations on\\n           better environmental protection shall be notified to the Contractor\
      \ for taking immediate\\n           action and rapid resolution of identified non-compliance.\\n40.11    \
      \   If significant environmental problems are identified or if there is an environmental\\n          complaint\
      \ or as a part of investigation work, then the Engineer shall also carry out Ad\\n         hoc site inspection\
      \ which shall be attended by Contractor’s Representative.\\n\\n 40.12   REPORTING SYSTEM\\n\\n 40.12.1   reporting\
      \ under  the Environmental Management System  will  contain  results  of\"\n    },\n    {\n      \"pdf_page\"\
      : 63,\n      \"text\": \"monitoring and inspection programs.\\n\\n          40.12.2   In  Site  Environmental\
      \  Plan,  the  Contractor  shall  prepare and submit monthly\\n                   Environmental Quality Management\
      \ Reports in accordance with Requirements as per\\n                    Contract.\\n\\n          40.12.3  The\
      \ monthly report shall include (but not limited to) the following:\\n                       Executive Summary\\\
      n\\n                       Brief mention of construction activities\\n\\n                       Monitoring\
      \ results under AMCP, and NMCP\\n\\n                       Interpretation of monitoring results, significance\
      \ and influencing factors\\n\\n                       Graphical representation of monitored results over\
      \ past four reporting periods.\\n\\n                      Measures to control spill under SPCP.\\n\\n   \
      \                    Action taken on recommendations under site inspection programme or specific\\n     \
      \                     directions.\\n\\n                      Summary of complaints, results of investigations\
      \ and follow-up action\\n\\n                       Future key issues.\\n\\n         40.13   COMPLAINT RESPONSE\
      \ PROCESS\\n          40.13.1   Inquiries, complaints and requests for information can be expected from a\
      \ wide range\\n                      of  individuals and organizations both private and government.  The majority\
      \ of\\n                   complaints is likely to be received by BMRCL, although the site offices are also\
      \ likely\\n                      to be contacted.\\n\\n          40.13.2  The objective of complaint process\
      \ is to ensure that public and agency complaints are\\n                  addressed and resolved consistently\
      \ and expeditiously.\\n\\n          40.13.3  The Contractor’s Site Manager will be notified immediately on\
      \ receipt of complaint that\\n              may relate to environmental impacts. The Site Manager will immediately\
      \ inform the\\n                  Engineer and through him the BMRCL.\\n\\n          40.13.4   Field investigation\
      \ should determine whether the complaint has merit, and if so action\\n                   should be taken\
      \ to address the impact.\\n          40.13.5  The outcome of the investigation and the action taken shall\
      \ be documented on a\\n                   complaint Performa prepared by the Contractor and approved by the\
      \ Engineer in\\n                 advance of the works.\\n\\n          40.13.6  Where possible, a formal response\
      \ to each complaint received shall be prepared by\\n                    the Contractor within seven days in\
      \ order to notify the concerned person(s) that action\\n                 has been taken.\\n\\n         40.14\
      \   COMPLETION OF THE EQM PROGRAMME\\n          40.14.1  The construction of Bangalore Metro  will be undertaken\
      \ as a series of individual\\n                    construction contracts with necessarily different construction\
      \ program and completion\\n                    dates.\\n\\n          40.14.2  The Engineer shall maintain\
      \ an overview of the ‘impact causing potential’ of each site\\n                     or contract and monitoring\
      \ parameter with a view to maintaining the most cost\\n                      effective use of the environmental\
      \ resources dedicated to the Project.\\n\\n          40.14.3 Termination of EQM should focus on the percentage\
      \ contract completion status and on\\n                  the basis of a history of environmental impact arising\
      \ from the site over a representative\\n                 period of monitoring.\\n\\n         40.13.5    Justifiable\
      \ application for termination of EQM shall be put forward by the\\n                    Contractor  to the\
      \ Engineer, as necessary throughout the  construction\\n                       period.\"\n    }\n  ],\n  \"\

      39.0     Personal Protective Equipments (PPEs)\\n\\n\\n39.1    The contractor shall provide required PPEs\
      \ to workmen to protect against safety and /\\n          or health hazards. Primarily PPEs are required for\
      \ the following protection\\n\\n\\n                i)    Head Protection (Safety helmets)\\n             \
      \     ii)    Foot Protection (Safety footwear, Gumboot, etc)\\n                  iii)   Body Protection (High\
      \ visibility clothing (waistcoat/jacket), Apron, etc)\\n             iv)   Personal fall protection (Full\
      \ body harness, Rope-grap fall arrester, etc)\\n           v)   Eye Protection (Goggles, Welders glasses,\
      \ etc)\\n             vi)   Hand Protection (Gloves, Finger coats, etc)\\n              vii)   Respiratory\
      \ Protection. (Nose mask, SCBAs, etc)\\n               viii)  Hearing Protection (Ear plugs, Ear muffs, etc)\\\
      n\\n\\n39.2    The PPEs and safety appliances provided by the contractor shall be of the\\n         standard\
      \ as prescribed by Bureau of Indian Standards  (BIS).  If materials\\n        conforming to BIS standards\
      \ are not available, the contractor as approved by\\n         the Employer shall procure PPE and safety appliances.\\\
      n\\n\\n39.3      All construction workers should be provided with high visibility jackets with\\n        \
      \  reflective tapes confirming to the requirement specified under BS EN 471: 1994\\n        as most of viaduct\
      \ /tunnelling/station and depot works are executed either\\n        above or under right-of-way. The conspicuity\
      \ of workmen at all times shall be\\n         increased so as to protect them from speeding vehicular traffic.\\\
      n\\n39.4    The contractor shall provide safety helmet, safety shoe and high visibility clothing\\n      \
      \      for all employees including workmen, traffic marshal and other employees who are\\n        engaged\
      \ for any work under this contract as per the following requirement.\"\n    },\n    {\n      \"pdf_page\"\

      39.0     Personal Protective Equipments (PPEs)\\n\\n\\n39.1    The contractor shall provide required PPEs\
      \ to workmen to protect against safety and /\\n          or health hazards. Primarily PPEs are required for\
      \ the following protection\\n\\n\\n                i)    Head Protection (Safety helmets)\\n             \
      \     ii)    Foot Protection (Safety footwear, Gumboot, etc)\\n                  iii)   Body Protection (High\
      \ visibility clothing (waistcoat/jacket), Apron, etc)\\n             iv)   Personal fall protection (Full\

    quote: "{\n  \"clause_id\": \"40.0\",\n  \"fragments\": [\n    {\n      \"pdf_page\": 62,\n      \"text\": \"\
      40.0      Visitors to site\\n\\n\\n 40.1    No visitor is allowed to enter the site without the permission\
      \ of the Employer. All\\n          authorised visitors should report at the site office. Contractor shall\
      \ provide visitor’s\\n          helmet (White helmet with visitor sticker) and other PPEs like Safety Shoe,\
      \ reflective\\n            jacket, respiratory protection etc. as per requirement of the site.\\n\\n\\n 40.2\
      \       All Visitors shall be accompanied at all times by a responsible member of the site\\n          personnel.\\\
      n\\n\\n 40.3    The contractor shall be fully responsible for all visitors’ safety and health within the\\\
      n             site.\\n\\n\\n 40.4    As indicated earlier in this Manual, the Engineer shall undertake regular\
      \ audits at\\n           quarterly intervals, of the Contractor’s onsite practices and procedures as a means\
      \ of\\n          assessing the ongoing performance of the Contractor.\\n\\n 40.5    The criteria against which\
      \ the audits will be undertaken shall be derived from the\\n          clauses within the Environment Protection\
      \ Requirements (Appendix III herein above),\\n           contract-specific Site Environmental Plan and previous\
      \ site inspection results.\\n\\n 40.6      In addition to the quarterly audits by the Engineer, site inspection\
      \ shall be undertaken\\n         by the Contractor’s staff to inspect the construction activities in order\
      \ to ensure that\\n           appropriate environmental protection and pollution control measures are properly\\\
      n           followed and implemented.\\n\\n 40.7    The frequency of site inspection shall be at least once\
      \ a week.\\n\\n 40.8    The Contractor shall prepare an ‘Environmental Inspection and Action Reporting\\n\
      \          System’ and submit to the Engineer for approval and make amendments as\\n          suggested. \
      \ It shall contain a contract specific comprehensive Environment Inspection\\n           checklist as requirement\
      \ of Site Environmental Plan.\\n 40.9    The area of inspection shall not be limited to environmental compliance\
      \ within the site\\n           but areas outside the site which are likely to be affected, directly or indirectly\
      \ by\\n             activities at site.\\n\\n 40.10     Results of inspection shall be discussed with Engineer\
      \ and his recommendations on\\n           better environmental protection shall be notified to the Contractor\
      \ for taking immediate\\n           action and rapid resolution of identified non-compliance.\\n40.11    \
      \   If significant environmental problems are identified or if there is an environmental\\n          complaint\
      \ or as a part of investigation work, then the Engineer shall also carry out Ad\\n         hoc site inspection\
      \ which shall be attended by Contractor’s Representative.\\n\\n 40.12   REPORTING SYSTEM\\n\\n 40.12.1   reporting\
      \ under  the Environmental Management System  will  contain  results  of\"\n    },\n    {\n      \"pdf_page\"\
      : 63,\n      \"text\": \"monitoring and inspection programs.\\n\\n          40.12.2   In  Site  Environmental\
      \  Plan,  the  Contractor  shall  prepare and submit monthly\\n                   Environmental Quality Management\
      \ Reports in accordance with Requirements as per\\n                    Contract.\\n\\n          40.12.3  The\
      \ monthly report shall include (but not limited to) the following:\\n                       Executive Summary\\\
      n\\n                       Brief mention of construction activities\\n\\n                       Monitoring\
      \ results under AMCP, and NMCP\\n\\n                       Interpretation of monitoring results, significance\
      \ and influencing factors\\n\\n                       Graphical representation of monitored results over\
      \ past four reporting periods.\\n\\n                      Measures to control spill under SPCP.\\n\\n   \
      \                    Action taken on recommendations under site inspection programme or specific\\n     \
      \                     directions.\\n\\n                      Summary of complaints, results of investigations\
      \ and follow-up action\\n\\n                       Future key issues.\\n\\n         40.13   COMPLAINT RESPONSE\
      \ PROCESS\\n          40.13.1   Inquiries, complaints and requests for information can be expected from a\
      \ wide range\\n                      of  individuals and organizations both private and government.  The majority\
      \ of\\n                   complaints is likely to be received by BMRCL, although the site offices are also\
      \ likely\\n                      to be contacted.\\n\\n          40.13.2  The objective of complaint process\
      \ is to ensure that public and agency complaints are\\n                  addressed and resolved consistently\
      \ and expeditiously.\\n\\n          40.13.3  The Contractor’s Site Manager will be notified immediately on\
      \ receipt of complaint that\\n              may relate to environmental impacts. The Site Manager will immediately\
      \ inform the\\n                  Engineer and through him the BMRCL.\\n\\n          40.13.4   Field investigation\
      \ should determine whether the complaint has merit, and if so action\\n                   should be taken\
      \ to address the impact.\\n          40.13.5  The outcome of the investigation and the action taken shall\
      \ be documented on a\\n                   complaint Performa prepared by the Contractor and approved by the\
      \ Engineer in\\n                 advance of the works.\\n\\n          40.13.6  Where possible, a formal response\
      \ to each complaint received shall be prepared by\\n                    the Contractor within seven days in\
      \ order to notify the concerned person(s) that action\\n                 has been taken.\\n\\n         40.14\
      \   COMPLETION OF THE EQM PROGRAMME\\n          40.14.1  The construction of Bangalore Metro  will be undertaken\
      \ as a series of individual\\n                    construction contracts with necessarily different construction\
      \ program and completion\\n                    dates.\\n\\n          40.14.2  The Engineer shall maintain\
      \ an overview of the ‘impact causing potential’ of each site\\n                     or contract and monitoring\
      \ parameter with a view to maintaining the most cost\\n                      effective use of the environmental\
      \ resources dedicated to the Project.\\n\\n          40.14.3 Termination of EQM should focus on the percentage\
      \ contract completion status and on\\n                  the basis of a history of environmental impact arising\
      \ from the site over a representative\\n                 period of monitoring.\\n\\n         40.13.5    Justifiable\
      \ application for termination of EQM shall be put forward by the\\n                    Contractor  to the\
      \ Engineer, as necessary throughout the  construction\\n                       period.\"\n    }\n  ],\n  \"\

- kind: summary
  text: Volume 3 Part II (Safety) of the Safety, Health and Environment Manual establishes comprehensive safety
    regulations, operational controls, housekeeping mandates, and detailed requirements for working at height, scaffolding,
    and site safety management for BMRCL Tender Package P1.

      pending_manual_review\",\n  \"rotation\": 0,\n  \"text\": \"Safety Health & Environment (SHE) Manual\\n215\\\
      n                                PART – II : SAFETY\\n\\n          17.0     Housekeeping\\n\\n\\n        \
      \  17.1     Housekeeping is the act of keeping the working environment cleared of all unnecessary\\n     \
      \              waste, thereby providing a first-line of defence against accidents and injuries.\\n\\n\\n \
      \         17.2      Contractor shall understand and accept that improper housekeeping is the primary\\n  \
      \                hazard in any construction site and ensure that a high degree of housekeeping is\\n     \
      \             always maintained. Indeed “Cleanliness is indeed next to Godliness”\\n\\n\\n          17.3 \
      \    Housekeeping  is  the  responsibility  of  all  site  personnel, and  line management\\n            \
      \     commitment shall be demonstrated by the continued efforts of supervising staff towards\\n          \
      \              this activity.\\n\\n\\n          17.4     General Housekeeping shall be carried out by the\
      \ contractor and ensured at all times at\\n                Work Site, Construction Depot, Batching Plant,\
      \ Labour Camp, Stores, Offices and\\n                        toilets/urinals. Towards  this  the  Contractor\
      \  shall  constitute a  special  group  of\\n                  housekeeping personnel as per General Instruction\
      \ BMRC/SHE/CEO/001. This group\\n                      shall ensure daily cleaning at work sites and surrounding\
      \ areas and maintain a register\\n                 as per the approved format by the Employer.\\n\\n\\n  \
      \        17.5     Adequate time shall be assigned to ensure that good housekeeping is maintained.\\n     \
      \         Team of housekeeping squad shall carry out this.\\n\\n\\n          17.6    The contractor shall\
      \ be responsible to provide segregated containers for disposal of\\n                    debris at required\
      \ places and regular cleaning of the same.\\n\\n\\n          17.7      Full height fence, barriers, barricades\
      \ etc. shall be erected around the site in order to\\n                   prevent the surrounding area from\
      \ excavated  soil, rubbish etc, which may cause\\n                   inconvenience to and endanger the public.\
      \ The barricade especially those exposed to\\n                     public shall be aesthetically maintained\
      \ by regular cleaning and painting as directed by\\n                    the Employer. These shall be maintained\
      \ in one line and level.\\n\\n\\n          17.8    The structure dimension of the barricade, material and\
      \ composition, its colour scheme,\\n            BMRC logo and other details shall be in accordance with specifications\
      \ laid down in\\n                   tender document.\\n\\n\\n          17.9       All stairways, passageways\
      \ and gangways shall be maintained without any blockages\\n                     or obstructions. All emergency\
      \ exits passageways, exits fire doors, break-glass alarm\\n                      points, firefighting equipment,\
      \ first aid stations, and other emergency stations shall be\\n                   kept clean, unobstructed\
      \ and in good working order.\\n\\n\\n         17.10    Lumber with protruding nails shall be bent or removed\
      \ and properly stacked.\\n\\n\\n         17.11     All surplus earth and debris are removed/disposed  off\
      \ from the working areas to\\n                          officially designated dumpsites. Trucks  carrying\
      \ sand,  earth and any  pulverized\\n                    materials etc. in order to avoid dust or odour impact\
      \ shall be covered while moving.\\n\\n               The tyres of the trucks leaving the site shall be cleaned\
      \ with water, wherever the\\n                    possibility of spillage on carriageways meant for regular\
      \ road traffic exists.\\n\\n\\n         17.12  No parking of trucks/trolleys, cranes and trailers etc. shall\
      \ be allowed on roads, which\\n              may obstruct the traffic movement.\\n\\n\\n         17.13   Roads\
      \ shall be kept clear and materials like: pipes, steel, sand boulders, concrete,\\n                   chips\
      \ and brick etc. shall not be allowed on the roads to obstruct free movement of\\n                 road traffic.\\\
      n\\n\\n\\n\\n\\n         Bangalore Metro Rail Corporation Ltd.              September 2026     Section Page\
