      n                                PART – II : SAFETY\\n\\n          17.0     Housekeeping\\n\\n\\n        \
      \  17.1     Housekeeping is the act of keeping the working environment cleared of all unnecessary\\n     \
      \              waste, thereby providing a first-line of defence against accidents and injuries.\\n\\n\\n \
      \         17.2      Contractor shall understand and accept that improper housekeeping is the primary\\n  \
      \                hazard in any construction site and ensure that a high degree of housekeeping is\\n     \
      \             always maintained. Indeed “Cleanliness is indeed next to Godliness”\\n\\n\\n          17.3 \
      \    Housekeeping  is  the  responsibility  of  all  site  personnel, and  line management\\n            \
      \     commitment shall be demonstrated by the continued efforts of supervising staff towards\\n          \
      \              this activity.\\n\\n\\n          17.4     General Housekeeping shall be carried out by the\
      \ contractor and ensured at all times at\\n                Work Site, Construction Depot, Batching Plant,\
      \ Labour Camp, Stores, Offices and\\n                        toilets/urinals. Towards  this  the  Contractor\
      \  shall  constitute a  special  group  of\\n                  housekeeping personnel as per General Instruction\
      \ BMRC/SHE/CEO/001. This group\\n                      shall ensure daily cleaning at work sites and surrounding\
      \ areas and maintain a register\\n                 as per the approved format by the Employer.\\n\\n\\n  \
      \        17.5     Adequate time shall be assigned to ensure that good housekeeping is maintained.\\n     \
      \         Team of housekeeping squad shall carry out this.\\n\\n\\n          17.6    The contractor shall\
      \ be responsible to provide segregated containers for disposal of\\n                    debris at required\
      \ places and regular cleaning of the same.\\n\\n\\n          17.7      Full height fence, barriers, barricades\
      \ etc. shall be erected around the site in order to\\n                   prevent the surrounding area from\
      \ excavated  soil, rubbish etc, which may cause\\n                   inconvenience to and endanger the public.\
      \ The barricade especially those exposed to\\n                     public shall be aesthetically maintained\
      \ by regular cleaning and painting as directed by\\n                    the Employer. These shall be maintained\
      \ in one line and level.\\n\\n\\n          17.8    The structure dimension of the barricade, material and\
      \ composition, its colour scheme,\\n            BMRC logo and other details shall be in accordance with specifications\
      \ laid down in\\n                   tender document.\\n\\n\\n          17.9       All stairways, passageways\
      \ and gangways shall be maintained without any blockages\\n                     or obstructions. All emergency\
      \ exits passageways, exits fire doors, break-glass alarm\\n                      points, firefighting equipment,\
      \ first aid stations, and other emergency stations shall be\\n                   kept clean, unobstructed\
      \ and in good working order.\\n\\n\\n         17.10    Lumber with protruding nails shall be bent or removed\
      \ and properly stacked.\\n\\n\\n         17.11     All surplus earth and debris are removed/disposed  off\
      \ from the working areas to\\n                          officially designated dumpsites. Trucks  carrying\
      \ sand,  earth and any  pulverized\\n                    materials etc. in order to avoid dust or odour impact\
      \ shall be covered while moving.\\n\\n               The tyres of the trucks leaving the site shall be cleaned\
      \ with water, wherever the\\n                    possibility of spillage on carriageways meant for regular\
      \ road traffic exists.\\n\\n\\n         17.12  No parking of trucks/trolleys, cranes and trailers etc. shall\
      \ be allowed on roads, which\\n              may obstruct the traffic movement.\\n\\n\\n         17.13   Roads\
      \ shall be kept clear and materials like: pipes, steel, sand boulders, concrete,\\n                   chips\
      \ and brick etc. shall not be allowed on the roads to obstruct free movement of\\n                 road traffic.\\\
      n\\n\\n\\n\\n\\n         Bangalore Metro Rail Corporation Ltd.              September 2026     Section Page\

      n                     b)    includes any scaffold, suspended scaffold, cradle, mobile platforms,  trestle,\\\
      n                      gangway, gantry and stairway which is so used.\\n\\n\\n          18.2     Organisation\
      \ and planning\\n\\n                The contractor shall ensure that work at height is\\n\\n             \
      \                    i)     properly planned for any emergencies and rescue\\n\\n                        \
      \            ii)    appropriately supervised; and\\n\\n                                     iii)    carried\
      \ out in a manner, which is reasonably practicable safe.\\n\\n\\n          18.3    The contractor shall ensure\
      \ that work at height is carried out only when the weather\\n                    conditions do not jeopardise\
      \ the health or safety of persons involved in the work.\\n\\n\\n          18.4     Competence\\n\\n      \
      \          The  contractor  shall ensure  that no person engages  in any  activity,  including\\n        \
      \             organization, planning and supervision, in relation to work at height or work equipment\\n \
      \                      for use in such work unless he is competent to do so or,  if being trained, is being\\\
      n                   supervised by a competent person.\\n\\n\\n          18.5     Avoidance of risks from work\
      \ at height\\n\\n                The contractor shall ensure that work is not carried out at height where\
      \ it is reasonably\\n                     practicable to carry out the work safely otherwise than at height.\\\
      n\\n\\n          18.6    Where work is carried out at height, the contractor shall take suitable and sufficient\\\
      n                 measures as given below to prevent, so far as is reasonably practicable, any person\\n \
      \                     falling a distance liable to cause personal injury.\\n\\n\\n                     a)\
      \    his ensuring that the work is carried out\\n\\n                                           i)    from\
      \ an existing place of work; or\\n\\n                                              ii)     (in the case of\
      \ obtaining access or egress) using an existing means,\\n                             complying to the requirements\
      \ as given in clause 18.15 .\\n\\n                      where  it is reasonably practicable to carry  it out\
      \ safely and under appropriate\\n                       ergonomic conditions; and\\n\\n\\n               \
      \      b)   where  it is not reasonably practicable for the work to be carried out in\\n                 \
      \      accordance with sub-paragraph (a), his providing sufficient work equipment\\n                     \
      \         for preventing, so far as is reasonably practicable, a fall occurring.\\n\\n\\n          18.7  \
      \  Where the measures taken under clause 18.6 do not eliminate the risk of a fall\\n                     occurring,\
      \ every contractor shall\\n\\n                     a)   so far as is reasonably practicable, provide sufficient\
      \ work equipment to\\n                        minimise -\\n\\n                                           i)\
      \     the distance and consequences; or\\n\\n                                              ii)    where  it\
      \ is not reasonably practicable to minimise the distance, the\\n                            consequences,\
      \ of a fall; and\\n\\n                     b)    Without prejudice to the generality of clause 18.4 provide\

      \   The contractor shall select work equipment for work at height which:\\n\\n\\n                a)   has\
      \ characteristics including dimensions which:\\n\\n                                    i)    are appropriate\
      \ to the nature of the work to be performed and\\n                           the foreseeable loadings; and\\\

      \     is in other respects the most suitable work equipment, having regard\\n                          in\
      \ particular to the purposes specified in 18.5 and 18.6 .\\n\\n\\n18.9      Fragile surfaces\\n\\n\\n18.9.1\
      \   The contractor shall ensure that no person at work passes across or near, or\\n         working on, from\
      \ or near, a fragile surface where  it is reasonably practicable to\\n          carry out work safely and\
      \ under appropriate ergonomic conditions without his\\n         doing so.\\n\\n\\n18.9.2   Where   it  is\
      \ not reasonably practicable  to carry out work  safely and under\\n          appropriate ergonomic conditions\
      \ without passing across or near, or working on,\\n         from or near, a fragile surface, every contractor\
      \ shall,\\n\\n\\n          a)    ensure, so far as  is reasonably practicable, that suitable and sufficient\\\
      n                platforms, coverings, guard rails or similar means of support or protection\\n          \
      \     are provided and used so that any foreseeable loading is supported by such\\n               supports\
      \ or borne by such protection;\\n\\n\\n          b)   where a risk of a person at work falling remains despite\
      \ the measures taken\\n              under the preceding provisions of this regulation, take suitable and\
      \ sufficient\\n             measures to minimise the distances and consequences of his fall.\\n\\n\\n18.9.3\
      \   Where any person at work may pass across or near, or work on, from or near, a\\n            fragile surface,\
      \ every contractor shall ensure that\\n\\n          a)    prominent warning notices are so far as is reasonably\
      \ practicable affixed at\\n                the approach to the place where the fragile surface is situated;\
      \ or\\n\\n          b)   where that is not reasonably practicable, such persons are made aware of it\\n  \
      \            by other means.\\n\\n\\n18.10     Falling objects\\n\\n\\n18.10.1  The contractor  shall, where\
      \ necessary to prevent injury to any person, take\\n          suitable and sufficient steps to prevent, so\
      \ far as is reasonably practicable, the fall\\n           of any material or object.\\n\\n\\n18.10.2  Where\
      \  it is not reasonably practicable to comply with the requirements of 18.9,\\n         every contractor shall\
      \ take suitable and sufficient steps to prevent any person\\n         being struck by any falling material\
      \ or object which is liable to cause personal\\n            injury.\\n\\n\\n\\nBangalore Metro Rail Corporation\

  text: Part II of the Safety, Health and Environment (SHE) Manual establishes detailed safety obligations and engineering
    controls for working at height, scaffolding, ladders, overhead protection, lifting appliances, and managing
    slipping, tripping, and falling hazards.

      n\\n\\n          21.0      Lifting Appliances and Gear\\n\\n\\n          21.1       Lifting appliances means\
      \ a crane, hoist machinery, derrick, winch, gin pole, sheer\\n                      legs, jack, hoist drum,\
      \ slewing machinery, slewing bearing fasteners,  loffing\\n                  machinery sheaves, pulley blocks,\
      \ hooks or other equipment used  for  lifting\\n                     materials, objects or building workers\
      \ and lifting gears means ropes, chain slings,\\n                    shackles, hooks, lifting lugs, wire ropes,\
      \ lifting eyebolts and eyenuts and other\\n                   accessories of a lifting appliance.\\n\\n\\\
      n          21.2    No machine shall be selected to do any lifting on a specific job until its size and\\n\
      \                     characteristics are considered against:\\n\\n\\n                                 i)\
      \     the weights, dimensions and lift radii of the heaviest and largest loads\\n\\n                     \
      \               ii)    the maximum lift height, the maximum lift radius and the weight of the loads\\n   \
      \                         that must be handled at each\\n\\n                                     iii)    the\
      \ number and frequency of lifts to be made\\n\\n                          iv)   how long the crane will be\
      \ required on site\\n\\n                      v)    the type of lifting to be done (for example, is precision\
      \ placement of loads\\n                          important?)\\n\\n                          vi)    the type\
      \ of carrier required (this depends on ground conditions and machine\\n                          capacity\
      \ In its operating quadrants) capacity is normally greatest over the\\n                             rear,\
      \ less over the side, and non-existent over the front\\n\\n                             vii)   whether loads\
      \ will have to be walked or carried\\n\\n                               viii)  whether loads will have to\
      \ be suspended for lengthy periods\\n\\n                          ix)    the site conditions, including the\
      \ ground where the machine will be set up,\\n                       access roads and ramps it must travel,\
      \ space for erection and any obstacles\\n                            that might impede access or operation\\\
      n\\n\\n          21.3    The contractor shall ensure that a valid certificate of fitness issued as per clause\\\
      n                   21.5  is available for all lifting appliances including synchronised mobile jacks, pre-\\\
      n                    stressing hydraulic jacks, jacks fitted with launching girders etc. and Employers\\n\
      \                   approval before inducting to the site. Only after obtaining the approval from the\\n \
      \               Employer any lifting appliances and gear shall be used.\\n\\n\\n          21.4    The laminated\
      \ photocopies  of  fitness  certificate issued by competent\\n                  person, the Employers’ approval\
      \ letter, the operators’ photo, manufacturer’s\\n                  load chart and competency certificate shall\
      \ always be either kept in the\\n                  operator cabin or pasted on the visible surface of the\
      \ lifting appliances.\\n\\n\\n          21.5      All lifting appliances and loose gears shall be clearly\
      \ marked for its safe\\n                 working load and identification by stamping or other suitable means.\\\

      pending_manual_review\",\n  \"rotation\": 0,\n  \"text\": \"Safety Health & Environment (SHE) Manual\\n221\\\
      n                            c)   any intermediate guardrail or similar means of protection shall be\\n  \
      \                              positioned so that any gap between  it and other means of protection\\n   \
      \                        does not exceed 470 millimetres.\\n\\n                          iv)   Any structure\
      \ or part of a structure which supports means of protection or to\\n                       which means of\
      \ protection are attached shall be of sufficient strength and\\n                           suitable for the\
      \ purpose of such support or attachment.\\n\\n\\n         18.17    Requirements for all Working Platforms\\\
      n\\n\\n                                 i)    Every working platforms requires a supporting structure for\
      \ holding it\\n\\n                                    ii)   Any surface upon which any supporting structure\
      \ rests shall be stable, of\\n                              sufficient  strength and  of  suitable  composition\
      \  safely  to  support  the\\n                         supporting structure, the working platform and any\
      \ loading intended to be\\n                        placed on the working platform.\\n\\n                 \
      \                   iii).    Stability of supporting structure\\n\\n                    Any supporting structure\
      \ shall\\n\\n                           a)   be suitable and of sufficient strength and rigidity for the purpose\
      \ for\\n                            which it is being used;\\n\\n                           b)     in the\
      \ case of a wheeled structure, be prevented by appropriate\\n                              devices from moving\
      \ inadvertently during work at height;\\n\\n                            c)     in other cases, be prevented\
      \ from slipping by secure attachment to\\n                               the bearing surface or to another\
      \ structure, provision of an effective\\n                                      anti-slip device or by other\
      \ means of equivalent effectiveness;\\n\\n                           d)   be stable while being erected, used\
      \ and dismantled; and\\n\\n                           e)   when altered or modified, be so altered or modified\
      \ as to ensure that it\\n                             remains stable.\\n\\n                              \
      \        f)    Have suitable base plates and properly footed thereby.\\n\\n\\n                           \
      \ iv).    Stability of working platforms\\n\\n                  A working platform shall\\n\\n           \
      \                a)   be suitable and of sufficient strength and rigidity for the purpose or\\n          \
      \                  purposes for which it is intended to be used or is being used;\\n\\n                  \
      \         b)   be so erected and used as to ensure that  its components do not\\n                        become\
      \ accidentally displaced so as to endanger any person;\\n\\n                            c)   when altered\
      \ or modified, be so altered or modified as to ensure that it\\n                             remains stable;\
      \ and\\n\\n                           d)   be dismantled in such a way as to prevent accidental displacement.\\\
      n\\n\\n                      v)    Safety on working platforms\\n\\n                  A working platform shall\\\
      n\\n                           a)   be of sufficient dimensions to permit the safe passage of persons and\\\
      n                               the safe use of any plant or materials required to be used and to\\n     \
      \                          provide a safe working area having regard to the work being carried\\n        \
      \                       out there;\\n\\n                           b)   possess a suitable surface and, in\
      \ particular, be so constructed that\\n                               the surface of the working platform\
      \ has no gap\\n\\n                                                     i)      through which a person could\
      \ fall;\\n\\n                                                         ii)      through which any material\
      \ or object could fall and injure a\\n                                      person; or\\n\\n             \
      \                                             iii)      giving  rise  to other  risk  of  injury  to any person,\
      \ unless\\n                                 measures have been taken to protect persons against such\\n  \
      \                                               risk; and\\n\\n                            c)   be so erected\
      \ and used, and maintained in such condition, as to\\n                                prevent, so far as is\
      \ reasonably practicable\\n\\n                                                     i)       the risk of slipping\
      \ or tripping; or\\n\\n                                                         ii)     any person being caught\
      \ between the working platform and\\n                                  any adjacent structure.\\n\\n\\n\\\
      n         Bangalore Metro Rail Corporation Ltd.              September 2026     Section Page 33 of 114\",\n\
      \  \"text_blocks\": [\n    {\n      \"bbox\": [\n        50.15998077392578,\n        15.768376350402832,\n\
      \        564.21923828125,\n        24.210372924804688\n      ],\n      \"block_number\": 0,\n      \"text\"\
      : \"                                                                                                     \
      \                              Safety Health & Environment (SHE) Manual \\n\"\n    },\n    {\n      \"bbox\"\
      : [\n        85.5599594116211,\n        26.57955551147461,\n        88.32714080810547,\n        35.93199157714844\n\
      \      ],\n      \"block_number\": 1,\n      \"text\": \" \\n\"\n    },\n    {\n      \"bbox\": [\n      \
      \  85.5599594116211,\n        809.042724609375,\n        511.7470703125,\n        830.5714111328125\n    \
      \  ],\n      \"block_number\": 2,\n      \"text\": \"Bangalore Metro Rail Corporation Ltd.               \
      \               September 2026         Section Page 33 of 114 \\n \\n\"\n    },\n    {\n      \"bbox\": [\n\
      \        85.56002044677734,\n        38.09945297241211,\n        497.8877258300781,\n        151.49205017089844\n\
      \      ],\n      \"block_number\": 3,\n      \"text\": \"c) \\nany intermediate guardrail or similar means\
      \ of protection shall be \\npositioned so that any gap between it and other means of protection \\ndoes not\
      \ exceed 470 millimetres. \\niv) \\nAny structure or part of a structure which supports means of protection\
      \ or to \\nwhich means of protection are attached shall be of sufficient strength and \\nsuitable for the\
      \ purpose of such support or attachment. \\n \\n18.17 \\nRequirements for all Working Platforms \\n \\n\"\n\
      \    },\n    {\n      \"bbox\": [\n        130.5593719482422,\n        156.65963745117188,\n        497.8901672363281,\n\
      \        787.4918823242188\n      ],\n      \"block_number\": 4,\n      \"text\": \"i)  \\nEvery working platforms\
      \ requires a supporting structure for holding it \\nii)  \\nAny surface upon which any supporting structure\
      \ rests shall be stable, of \\nsufficient strength and of suitable composition safely to support the \\nsupporting\
      \ structure, the working platform and any loading intended to be \\nplaced on the working platform. \\niii).\
      \  \\nStability of supporting structure  \\nAny supporting structure shall \\na) \\nbe suitable and of sufficient\
      \ strength and rigidity for the purpose for \\nwhich it is being used; \\nb) \\nin the case of a wheeled structure,\
      \ be prevented by appropriate \\ndevices from moving inadvertently during work at height; \\nc) \\nin other\
      \ cases, be prevented from slipping by secure attachment to \\nthe bearing surface or to another structure,\
      \ provision of an effective \\nanti-slip device or by other means of equivalent effectiveness; \\nd) \\nbe\
      \ stable while being erected, used and dismantled; and \\ne) \\nwhen altered or modified, be so altered or\
      \ modified as to ensure that it \\nremains stable. \\nf) \\nHave suitable base plates and properly footed\
      \ thereby. \\n \\niv).  \\nStability of working platforms \\nA working platform shall \\na) \\nbe suitable\
      \ and of sufficient strength and rigidity for the purpose or \\npurposes for which it is intended to be used\
      \ or is being used; \\nb) \\nbe so erected and used as to ensure that its components do not \\nbecome accidentally\
      \ displaced so as to endanger any person; \\nc) \\nwhen altered or modified, be so altered or modified as\
      \ to ensure that it \\nremains stable; and \\nd) \\nbe dismantled in such a way as to prevent accidental displacement.\
      \ \\n \\nv) \\nSafety on working platforms \\nA working platform shall \\na) \\nbe of sufficient dimensions\
      \ to permit the safe passage of persons and \\nthe safe use of any plant or materials required to be used\
      \ and to \\nprovide a safe working area having regard to the work being carried \\nout there; \\nb) \\npossess\
      \ a suitable surface and, in particular, be so constructed that \\nthe surface of the working platform has\
      \ no gap \\ni) \\nthrough which a person could fall; \\nii) \\nthrough which any material or object could\
      \ fall and injure a \\nperson; or \\niii) \\ngiving rise to other risk of injury to any person, unless \\\
      nmeasures have been taken to protect persons against such \\nrisk; and \\nc) \\nbe so erected and used, and\
      \ maintained in such condition, as to \\nprevent, so far as is reasonably practicable \\ni) \\nthe risk of\
      \ slipping or tripping; or \\nii) \\nany person being caught between the working platform and \\nany adjacent\
      \ structure. \\n\"\n    },\n    {\n      \"bbox\": [\n        39.599998474121094,\n        24.479991912841797,\n\
      \        63.57600021362305,\n        41.38799285888672\n      ],\n      \"block_number\": 5,\n      \"text\"\
      : \"221\\n\"\n    }\n  ]\n}"

      \    Requirements for personal fall protection systems\\n\\n                                 i)   A personal\

      \ is reasonably practicable be performed\\n                                       safely while using that\

      \                               occur; and\\n\\n                           e)   be so designed,  installed\

      \    A working platform and any supporting structure shall not be loaded so as to\\n                give rise\
      \ to a risk of collapse or to any deformation, which could affect its\\n               safe use.\\n\\n\\n\
      \              vii)   Additional requirements for scaffolding\\n\\n               Strength and stability calculations\
      \ for scaffolding shall be carried out unless\\n\\n                a)   a note  of the  calculations, covering\
      \ the  structural arrangements\\n                     contemplated, is available; or\\n\\n               \
      \ b)       it is assembled in conformity with a generally recognised standard\\n                       configuration.\\\
      n\\n\\n               viii)  Depending on the complexity of the scaffolding selected, a competent\\n     \
      \         person shall draw up an assembly, use and dismantling plan. This may be\\n                   in\
      \ the form of a standard plan, supplemented by items relating to specific\\n                  details of the\
      \ scaffolding in question.\\n\\n\\n             ix)  A copy of the plan, including any instructions  it may\
      \ contain, shall be kept\\n                available  for  the use  of  persons  concerned  in  the  assembly,\
      \  use,\\n                dismantling or alteration of scaffolding until it has been dismantled.\\n\\n\\n\
      \           x)   The dimensions form and layout of scaffolding decks shall be appropriate to\\n          \
      \      the nature of the work to be performed and suitable for the loads to be\\n                 carried\
      \ and permit work and passage in safety.\\n\\n\\n             xi)   While a scaffold  is not available for\
      \ use, including during  its assembly,\\n                dismantling or alteration,  it shall be marked with\
      \ general warning signs in\\n              accordance with and be suitably delineated by physical means preventing\\\
      n              access to the danger zone.\\n\\n\\n              xii)   Scaffolding may be assembled, dismantled\
      \ or  significantly altered only\\n              under the supervision of a competent person and by persons\
      \ who have\\n               received appropriate and specific training in the operations envisaged which\\\
      n              addresses specific risks which the operations may entail and precautions to\\n            \

      \    safety during the assembly, dismantling or alteration of the scaffolding\\n                    concerned;\\\

    quote: "{\n  \"extraction_method\": \"geometric_sort\",\n  \"has_extracted_text\": true,\n  \"page_rect\": [\n\
      \    0.0,\n    0.0,\n    595.219970703125,\n    842.0\n  ],\n  \"pdf_page\": 40,\n  \"review_status\": \"\
      pending_manual_review\",\n  \"rotation\": 0,\n  \"text\": \"Safety Health & Environment (SHE) Manual\\n  \
      \                                                        224\\n18.20    Requirements for Ladders\\n\\n\\n\
      \          1)    Every contractor shall ensure that a ladder is used for work at height only if\\n       \
      \      a risk assessment has demonstrated that the use of more suitable work\\n              equipment is\
      \ not justified because of the low risk and\\n\\n                          i)    The short duration of use;\
      \ or\\n\\n                            ii)    Existing features on site, which he cannot alter.\\n\\n     \
      \     2)    Only metal ladders shall be allowed. Bamboo ladders are prohibited.\\n\\n          3)   Any surface\
      \ upon which a ladder rests shall be stable, firm, of sufficient\\n                strength and of suitable\
      \ composition safely to support the ladder so that its\\n              rungs or steps remain horizontal, and\
      \ any loading intended to be placed on\\n                            it.\\n\\n          4)   A ladder shall\
      \ be so positioned as to ensure its stability during use\\n\\n          5)   A suspended ladder shall be attached\
      \ in a secure manner and so that, with\\n                the exception of a flexible ladder,  it cannot be\
      \ displaced and swinging is\\n               prevented.\\n\\n          6)   A portable ladder shall be prevented\
      \ from slipping during use by -\\n\\n                          i)     securing the stiles at or near their\
      \ upper or lower ends;\\n\\n                            ii)    an effective anti-slip or other effective stability\
      \ device; or\\n\\n                             iii)   any other arrangement of equivalent effectiveness.\\\
      n\\n          7)   A ladder used for access shall be long enough to protrude sufficiently above\\n       \
      \         the place of landing to which  it provides access, unless other measures\\n             have been\
      \ taken to ensure a firm handhold.\\n\\n          8)   No interlocking or extension ladder shall be used unless\
      \ its sections are\\n               prevented from moving relative to each other while in use.\\n\\n     \
      \     9)   A mobile ladder shall be prevented from moving before it is stepped on.\\n\\n         10)  Where\
      \ a ladder or run of ladders raises a vertical distance of 9 metres or\\n             more above its base,\
      \ there shall, where reasonably practicable, be provided\\n                 at suitable intervals sufficient\
      \ safe landing areas or rest platforms.\\n\\n         11)  Every ladder shall be used in such a way that\\\
      n\\n                a)   a secure handhold and secure support are always available to the\\n             \
      \         user; and\\n\\n                b)    the user can maintain a safe handhold when carrying a load\
      \ unless, in\\n                     the case of a step ladder, the maintenance of a handhold  is not\\n  \
      \                     practicable when a load  is  carried, and a  risk assessment has\\n                \
      \   demonstrated that the use of a stepladder is justified because of\\n\\n                              \
      \      i)     the low risk; and\\n\\n                                       ii)    the short duration of use.\\\
      n\\n\\n19.0    Overhead protection\\n\\n\\n            All contractors shall provide overhead protections\
      \ as per Rule 41 of BOCWR\\n\\n                i)    Overhead protection should be erected along the periphery\
      \ of every building\\n              which is under construction and the building height shall be 15m or above\\\
      n                  after construction.\\n\\n                  ii)    Overhead protection shall be minimum\
      \ 2m wide and the outer edge shall be\\n           150mm higher than the inner edge and an angle not more\
      \ than 200 to its\\n                 horizontal sloping into the building.\\n\\n                  iii)   Overhead\
      \ protection shall not be erected more than a height of 5m from the\\n             base of the building.\\\
      n\\n             iv)   Areas of inadvertent hazard of  falling of material  shall be guarded or\\n       \
      \        barricaded or roped-off thereby by the contractor.\\n\\n\\n20.0     Slipping, Tripping, Cutting,\
      \ Drowning and Falling Hazards\\n\\n        As per Rule 42 of BOCWR,\\n\\n                i)      All places\
      \ should be free from dust, debris or similar materials.\\n\\n\\n\\n\\nBangalore Metro Rail Corporation Ltd.\
      \              September 2026     Section Page 36 of 114\",\n  \"text_blocks\": [\n    {\n      \"bbox\":\

      \ \\nAny surface upon which a ladder rests shall be stable, firm, of sufficient \\nstrength and of suitable\
      \ composition safely to support the ladder so that its \\nrungs or steps remain horizontal, and any loading\
      \ intended to be placed on \\nit. \\n4) \\nA ladder shall be so positioned as to ensure its stability during\
      \ use \\n5) \\nA suspended ladder shall be attached in a secure manner and so that, with \\nthe exception\
      \ of a flexible ladder, it cannot be displaced and swinging is \\nprevented. \\n6) \\nA portable ladder shall\
      \ be prevented from slipping during use by -  \\ni) \\nsecuring the stiles at or near their upper or lower\
      \ ends; \\nii) \\nan effective anti-slip or other effective stability device; or \\niii) \\nany other arrangement\
      \ of equivalent effectiveness. \\n7) \\nA ladder used for access shall be long enough to protrude sufficiently\

      \ a firm handhold. \\n8) \\nNo interlocking or extension ladder shall be used unless its sections are \\nprevented\
      \ from moving relative to each other while in use. \\n9) \\nA mobile ladder shall be prevented from moving\
      \ before it is stepped on. \\n10) \\nWhere a ladder or run of ladders raises a vertical distance of 9 metres\
      \ or \\nmore above its base, there shall, where reasonably practicable, be provided \\nat suitable intervals\
      \ sufficient safe landing areas or rest platforms. \\n11) \\nEvery ladder shall be used in such a way that\

      : 5,\n      \"text\": \"All contractors shall provide overhead protections as per Rule 41 of BOCWR  \\ni)\
      \ \\nOverhead protection should be erected along the periphery of every building \\nwhich is under construction\

      \                                                        226\\n\\n21.6    The contractor shall also maintain\
      \ a register containing a system of identification\\n           of all tools and tackles, its date of purchase,\
      \ safe working load, competent person\\n         date of examination etc.\\n\\n\\n21.7     Test and periodical\
      \ examination of lifting appliances and gears\\n\\n\\n21.7.1     All  lifting appliances including  all parts\
      \ and gears  thereof, whether  fixed or\\n        movable shall be thoroughly tested and examined by a competent\
      \ person once at\\n           least in every six months or after it has undergone any alterations or repairs\
      \ liable\\n           to affect its strength or stability. Within the validity,  if the lifting appliances\
      \ are\\n           shifted to a new site, re-examination by the same competent person for ensuring\\n    \
      \          its safety shall also be done.\\n\\n21.7.2    Contractors can  utilise the services of any competent\
      \ person as defined  in\\n          Factories Act, 1948 and approved by Chief Inspector  of Factories with\
      \ the\\n         permission of the Employer.\\n\\n\\n21.7.3     All alarms and signals  like automatic safe\
      \ load indicators (SLI), boom angle\\n           indicators, boom extension indicators, over lift boom alarm,\
      \ swing alarm, hydraulic\\n          safety valves, mechanical radius indicators, load moment indicators etc.\
      \ shall be\\n           periodically examined and maintained always in working condition\\n\\n\\n21.8    \
      \ Automatic safe load indicators\\n\\n\\n21.8.1   As stipulated in Rule 78 of BOCWKR 2006, no lifting appliances\
      \ gear or any\\n         other material handling appliance is used, if:\\n\\n                i)     the  Inspector\
      \  having  jurisdiction  is  not  satisfied  with  reference  to a\\n                   certification of test\
      \ or examination or to an authenticated record maintain as\\n               provided under these rules; and\\\
      n\\n                  ii)     in the view of such Inspector, the lifting appliance, lifting gear or any other\\\
      n                material  handling  appliance  is  not  safe  for use  in  building  or  other\\n       \
      \         construction work; and\\n\\n                  iii)   no pulley block is used in building or other\
      \ construction work unless the safe\\n               working load and its identification are clearly marked\
      \ on such block.\\n\\n\\n21.9      Qualification of operator of lifting appliances and of signaller etc\\\
      n\\n\\n21.9.1   The contractor shall not employ any person to drive or operate a lifting machine\\n      \
      \      like crane, hydra etc whether driven by mechanical power or otherwise or to give\\n          signals\
      \ to work as a operator of a rigger or derricks unless he\\n\\n                i)      is above twenty-one\
      \ years of age and possesses a valid heavy transport\\n                vehicle driving licence as per Motor\
      \ Vehicle Act and Rules.\\n\\n                  ii)     is absolutely competent and reliable\\n\\n       \
      \           iii)   possesses the knowledge of the inherent risks involved in the operation of\\n         \
      \             lifting appliances by undergoing a formal  training  at any  institution  of\\n            \
      \    national importance acceptable to Employer\\n\\n             iv)     is medically examined periodically\
      \ as specified in schedule VII of BOCW\\n               Rules.\\n\\n\\n21.10    General requirements of appliances\\\
      n\\n\\n21.10.1   Out-of level\\n\\n\\n21.10.1.1 One of the most severe effects of being out-of fit level is\
      \ that side loads develop in\\n          the boom. Because of side loads all mobile cranes lose capacity rapidly\
      \ as the\\n         degree of out-of-level increases and therefore\\n\\n\\n\\n\\n\\nBangalore Metro Rail Corporation\
      \ Ltd.              September 2026     Section Page 38 of 114\",\n  \"text_blocks\": [\n    {\n      \"bbox\"\

      \ \\n \\n21.10 \\nGeneral requirements of appliances \\n \\n21.10.1 \\nOut-of level \\n \\n21.10.1.1 One of\

    quote: "{\n  \"extraction_method\": \"geometric_sort\",\n  \"has_extracted_text\": true,\n  \"page_rect\": [\n\
      \    0.0,\n    0.0,\n    595.219970703125,\n    842.0\n  ],\n  \"pdf_page\": 37,\n  \"review_status\": \"\
      pending_manual_review\",\n  \"rotation\": 0,\n  \"text\": \"Safety Health & Environment (SHE) Manual\\n221\\\
      n                            c)   any intermediate guardrail or similar means of protection shall be\\n  \
      \                              positioned so that any gap between  it and other means of protection\\n   \
      \                        does not exceed 470 millimetres.\\n\\n                          iv)   Any structure\
      \ or part of a structure which supports means of protection or to\\n                       which means of\
      \ protection are attached shall be of sufficient strength and\\n                           suitable for the\
      \ purpose of such support or attachment.\\n\\n\\n         18.17    Requirements for all Working Platforms\\\
      n\\n\\n                                 i)    Every working platforms requires a supporting structure for\
      \ holding it\\n\\n                                    ii)   Any surface upon which any supporting structure\
      \ rests shall be stable, of\\n                              sufficient  strength and  of  suitable  composition\
      \  safely  to  support  the\\n                         supporting structure, the working platform and any\
      \ loading intended to be\\n                        placed on the working platform.\\n\\n                 \
      \                   iii).    Stability of supporting structure\\n\\n                    Any supporting structure\
      \ shall\\n\\n                           a)   be suitable and of sufficient strength and rigidity for the purpose\
      \ for\\n                            which it is being used;\\n\\n                           b)     in the\
      \ case of a wheeled structure, be prevented by appropriate\\n                              devices from moving\
      \ inadvertently during work at height;\\n\\n                            c)     in other cases, be prevented\
      \ from slipping by secure attachment to\\n                               the bearing surface or to another\
      \ structure, provision of an effective\\n                                      anti-slip device or by other\
      \ means of equivalent effectiveness;\\n\\n                           d)   be stable while being erected, used\
      \ and dismantled; and\\n\\n                           e)   when altered or modified, be so altered or modified\
      \ as to ensure that it\\n                             remains stable.\\n\\n                              \
      \        f)    Have suitable base plates and properly footed thereby.\\n\\n\\n                           \
      \ iv).    Stability of working platforms\\n\\n                  A working platform shall\\n\\n           \
      \                a)   be suitable and of sufficient strength and rigidity for the purpose or\\n          \
      \                  purposes for which it is intended to be used or is being used;\\n\\n                  \
      \         b)   be so erected and used as to ensure that  its components do not\\n                        become\
      \ accidentally displaced so as to endanger any person;\\n\\n                            c)   when altered\
      \ or modified, be so altered or modified as to ensure that it\\n                             remains stable;\
      \ and\\n\\n                           d)   be dismantled in such a way as to prevent accidental displacement.\\\
      n\\n\\n                      v)    Safety on working platforms\\n\\n                  A working platform shall\\\
      n\\n                           a)   be of sufficient dimensions to permit the safe passage of persons and\\\
      n                               the safe use of any plant or materials required to be used and to\\n     \
      \                          provide a safe working area having regard to the work being carried\\n        \
      \                       out there;\\n\\n                           b)   possess a suitable surface and, in\
      \ particular, be so constructed that\\n                               the surface of the working platform\
      \ has no gap\\n\\n                                                     i)      through which a person could\
      \ fall;\\n\\n                                                         ii)      through which any material\
      \ or object could fall and injure a\\n                                      person; or\\n\\n             \
      \                                             iii)      giving  rise  to other  risk  of  injury  to any person,\
      \ unless\\n                                 measures have been taken to protect persons against such\\n  \
      \                                               risk; and\\n\\n                            c)   be so erected\
      \ and used, and maintained in such condition, as to\\n                                prevent, so far as is\
      \ reasonably practicable\\n\\n                                                     i)       the risk of slipping\
      \ or tripping; or\\n\\n                                                         ii)     any person being caught\
      \ between the working platform and\\n                                  any adjacent structure.\\n\\n\\n\\\
      n         Bangalore Metro Rail Corporation Ltd.              September 2026     Section Page 33 of 114\",\n\

      \      ],\n      \"block_number\": 3,\n      \"text\": \"c) \\nany intermediate guardrail or similar means\
      \ of protection shall be \\npositioned so that any gap between it and other means of protection \\ndoes not\
      \ exceed 470 millimetres. \\niv) \\nAny structure or part of a structure which supports means of protection\
      \ or to \\nwhich means of protection are attached shall be of sufficient strength and \\nsuitable for the\
      \ purpose of such support or attachment. \\n \\n18.17 \\nRequirements for all Working Platforms \\n \\n\"\n\
      \    },\n    {\n      \"bbox\": [\n        130.5593719482422,\n        156.65963745117188,\n        497.8901672363281,\n\
      \        787.4918823242188\n      ],\n      \"block_number\": 4,\n      \"text\": \"i)  \\nEvery working platforms\
      \ requires a supporting structure for holding it \\nii)  \\nAny surface upon which any supporting structure\
      \ rests shall be stable, of \\nsufficient strength and of suitable composition safely to support the \\nsupporting\
      \ structure, the working platform and any loading intended to be \\nplaced on the working platform. \\niii).\
      \  \\nStability of supporting structure  \\nAny supporting structure shall \\na) \\nbe suitable and of sufficient\
      \ strength and rigidity for the purpose for \\nwhich it is being used; \\nb) \\nin the case of a wheeled structure,\
      \ be prevented by appropriate \\ndevices from moving inadvertently during work at height; \\nc) \\nin other\
      \ cases, be prevented from slipping by secure attachment to \\nthe bearing surface or to another structure,\
      \ provision of an effective \\nanti-slip device or by other means of equivalent effectiveness; \\nd) \\nbe\
      \ stable while being erected, used and dismantled; and \\ne) \\nwhen altered or modified, be so altered or\
      \ modified as to ensure that it \\nremains stable. \\nf) \\nHave suitable base plates and properly footed\
      \ thereby. \\n \\niv).  \\nStability of working platforms \\nA working platform shall \\na) \\nbe suitable\
      \ and of sufficient strength and rigidity for the purpose or \\npurposes for which it is intended to be used\
      \ or is being used; \\nb) \\nbe so erected and used as to ensure that its components do not \\nbecome accidentally\
      \ displaced so as to endanger any person; \\nc) \\nwhen altered or modified, be so altered or modified as\
      \ to ensure that it \\nremains stable; and \\nd) \\nbe dismantled in such a way as to prevent accidental displacement.\
      \ \\n \\nv) \\nSafety on working platforms \\nA working platform shall \\na) \\nbe of sufficient dimensions\
      \ to permit the safe passage of persons and \\nthe safe use of any plant or materials required to be used\
      \ and to \\nprovide a safe working area having regard to the work being carried \\nout there; \\nb) \\npossess\
      \ a suitable surface and, in particular, be so constructed that \\nthe surface of the working platform has\
      \ no gap \\ni) \\nthrough which a person could fall; \\nii) \\nthrough which any material or object could\
      \ fall and injure a \\nperson; or \\niii) \\ngiving rise to other risk of injury to any person, unless \\\
      nmeasures have been taken to protect persons against such \\nrisk; and \\nc) \\nbe so erected and used, and\
      \ maintained in such condition, as to \\nprevent, so far as is reasonably practicable \\ni) \\nthe risk of\
      \ slipping or tripping; or \\nii) \\nany person being caught between the working platform and \\nany adjacent\
      \ structure. \\n\"\n    },\n    {\n      \"bbox\": [\n        39.599998474121094,\n        24.479991912841797,\n\
      \        63.57600021362305,\n        41.38799285888672\n      ],\n      \"block_number\": 5,\n      \"text\"\
      : \"221\\n\"\n    }\n  ]\n}"

  text: Ladders used for work at height must be metal; bamboo ladders are strictly prohibited. Portable and suspended
    ladders must be secured against slipping or swinging.

      pending_manual_review\",\n  \"rotation\": 0,\n  \"text\": \"Safety Health & Environment (SHE) Manual\\n  \
      \                                                        224\\n18.20    Requirements for Ladders\\n\\n\\n\
      \          1)    Every contractor shall ensure that a ladder is used for work at height only if\\n       \
      \      a risk assessment has demonstrated that the use of more suitable work\\n              equipment is\
      \ not justified because of the low risk and\\n\\n                          i)    The short duration of use;\
      \ or\\n\\n                            ii)    Existing features on site, which he cannot alter.\\n\\n     \
      \     2)    Only metal ladders shall be allowed. Bamboo ladders are prohibited.\\n\\n          3)   Any surface\
      \ upon which a ladder rests shall be stable, firm, of sufficient\\n                strength and of suitable\
      \ composition safely to support the ladder so that its\\n              rungs or steps remain horizontal, and\
      \ any loading intended to be placed on\\n                            it.\\n\\n          4)   A ladder shall\
      \ be so positioned as to ensure its stability during use\\n\\n          5)   A suspended ladder shall be attached\
      \ in a secure manner and so that, with\\n                the exception of a flexible ladder,  it cannot be\
      \ displaced and swinging is\\n               prevented.\\n\\n          6)   A portable ladder shall be prevented\
      \ from slipping during use by -\\n\\n                          i)     securing the stiles at or near their\
      \ upper or lower ends;\\n\\n                            ii)    an effective anti-slip or other effective stability\
      \ device; or\\n\\n                             iii)   any other arrangement of equivalent effectiveness.\\\
      n\\n          7)   A ladder used for access shall be long enough to protrude sufficiently above\\n       \
      \         the place of landing to which  it provides access, unless other measures\\n             have been\
      \ taken to ensure a firm handhold.\\n\\n          8)   No interlocking or extension ladder shall be used unless\
      \ its sections are\\n               prevented from moving relative to each other while in use.\\n\\n     \
      \     9)   A mobile ladder shall be prevented from moving before it is stepped on.\\n\\n         10)  Where\
      \ a ladder or run of ladders raises a vertical distance of 9 metres or\\n             more above its base,\
      \ there shall, where reasonably practicable, be provided\\n                 at suitable intervals sufficient\
      \ safe landing areas or rest platforms.\\n\\n         11)  Every ladder shall be used in such a way that\\\
      n\\n                a)   a secure handhold and secure support are always available to the\\n             \
      \         user; and\\n\\n                b)    the user can maintain a safe handhold when carrying a load\
      \ unless, in\\n                     the case of a step ladder, the maintenance of a handhold  is not\\n  \
      \                     practicable when a load  is  carried, and a  risk assessment has\\n                \
      \   demonstrated that the use of a stepladder is justified because of\\n\\n                              \
      \      i)     the low risk; and\\n\\n                                       ii)    the short duration of use.\\\
      n\\n\\n19.0    Overhead protection\\n\\n\\n            All contractors shall provide overhead protections\
      \ as per Rule 41 of BOCWR\\n\\n                i)    Overhead protection should be erected along the periphery\
      \ of every building\\n              which is under construction and the building height shall be 15m or above\\\
      n                  after construction.\\n\\n                  ii)    Overhead protection shall be minimum\
      \ 2m wide and the outer edge shall be\\n           150mm higher than the inner edge and an angle not more\
      \ than 200 to its\\n                 horizontal sloping into the building.\\n\\n                  iii)   Overhead\
      \ protection shall not be erected more than a height of 5m from the\\n             base of the building.\\\
      n\\n             iv)   Areas of inadvertent hazard of  falling of material  shall be guarded or\\n       \
      \        barricaded or roped-off thereby by the contractor.\\n\\n\\n20.0     Slipping, Tripping, Cutting,\
      \ Drowning and Falling Hazards\\n\\n        As per Rule 42 of BOCWR,\\n\\n                i)      All places\
      \ should be free from dust, debris or similar materials.\\n\\n\\n\\n\\nBangalore Metro Rail Corporation Ltd.\
      \              September 2026     Section Page 36 of 114\",\n  \"text_blocks\": [\n    {\n      \"bbox\":\

      : 4,\n      \"text\": \"1) \\nEvery contractor shall ensure that a ladder is used for work at height only\
      \ if \\na risk assessment has demonstrated that the use of more suitable work \\nequipment is not justified\
      \ because of the low risk and \\ni) \\nThe short duration of use; or \\nii) \\nExisting features on site,\
      \ which he cannot alter. \\n2) \\nOnly metal ladders shall be allowed. Bamboo ladders are prohibited. \\n3)\
      \ \\nAny surface upon which a ladder rests shall be stable, firm, of sufficient \\nstrength and of suitable\
      \ composition safely to support the ladder so that its \\nrungs or steps remain horizontal, and any loading\
      \ intended to be placed on \\nit. \\n4) \\nA ladder shall be so positioned as to ensure its stability during\
      \ use \\n5) \\nA suspended ladder shall be attached in a secure manner and so that, with \\nthe exception\

      \ be prevented from slipping during use by -  \\ni) \\nsecuring the stiles at or near their upper or lower\
      \ ends; \\nii) \\nan effective anti-slip or other effective stability device; or \\niii) \\nany other arrangement\
      \ of equivalent effectiveness. \\n7) \\nA ladder used for access shall be long enough to protrude sufficiently\
      \ above \\nthe place of landing to which it provides access, unless other measures \\nhave been taken to ensure\
      \ a firm handhold. \\n8) \\nNo interlocking or extension ladder shall be used unless its sections are \\nprevented\
      \ from moving relative to each other while in use. \\n9) \\nA mobile ladder shall be prevented from moving\
      \ before it is stepped on. \\n10) \\nWhere a ladder or run of ladders raises a vertical distance of 9 metres\
      \ or \\nmore above its base, there shall, where reasonably practicable, be provided \\nat suitable intervals\
      \ sufficient safe landing areas or rest platforms. \\n11) \\nEvery ladder shall be used in such a way that\
      \ \\na) \\na secure handhold and secure support are always available to the \\nuser; and \\nb) \\nthe user\
      \ can maintain a safe handhold when carrying a load unless, in \\nthe case of a step ladder, the maintenance\
      \ of a handhold is not \\npracticable when a load is carried, and a risk assessment has \\ndemonstrated that\
      \ the use of a stepladder is justified because of \\ni) \\nthe low risk; and \\nii) \\nthe short duration\
      \ of use. \\n \\n19.0 \\nOverhead protection \\n \\n\"\n    },\n    {\n      \"bbox\": [\n        82.43868255615234,\n\
      \        584.5794677734375,\n        494.7686462402344,\n        778.9716796875\n      ],\n      \"block_number\"\
      : 5,\n      \"text\": \"All contractors shall provide overhead protections as per Rule 41 of BOCWR  \\ni)\
      \ \\nOverhead protection should be erected along the periphery of every building \\nwhich is under construction\
      \ and the building height shall be 15m or above \\nafter construction. \\nii) \\nOverhead protection shall\
      \ be minimum 2m wide and the outer edge shall be \\n150mm higher than the inner edge and an angle not more\
      \ than 200 to its \\nhorizontal sloping into the building. \\niii) \\nOverhead protection shall not be erected\
      \ more than a height of 5m from the \\nbase of the building. \\niv) \\nAreas of inadvertent hazard of falling\
      \ of material shall be guarded or \\nbarricaded or roped-off thereby by the contractor.  \\n \\n20.0 \\nSlipping,\
      \ Tripping, Cutting, Drowning and Falling Hazards \\nAs per Rule 42 of BOCWR,  \\ni) \\nAll places should\

- kind: parameter
  text: Overhead protection along building peripheries under Rule 41 of BOCWR is required for buildings 15m or above
    after construction, must be minimum 2m wide, slope inward at an angle not exceeding 200 (notational typo in
    source text) to the horizontal with the outer edge 150mm higher, and erected at a height of not more than 5m.

      pending_manual_review\",\n  \"rotation\": 0,\n  \"text\": \"Safety Health & Environment (SHE) Manual\\n  \
      \                                                        224\\n18.20    Requirements for Ladders\\n\\n\\n\
      \          1)    Every contractor shall ensure that a ladder is used for work at height only if\\n       \
      \      a risk assessment has demonstrated that the use of more suitable work\\n              equipment is\
      \ not justified because of the low risk and\\n\\n                          i)    The short duration of use;\
      \ or\\n\\n                            ii)    Existing features on site, which he cannot alter.\\n\\n     \
      \     2)    Only metal ladders shall be allowed. Bamboo ladders are prohibited.\\n\\n          3)   Any surface\
      \ upon which a ladder rests shall be stable, firm, of sufficient\\n                strength and of suitable\
      \ composition safely to support the ladder so that its\\n              rungs or steps remain horizontal, and\
      \ any loading intended to be placed on\\n                            it.\\n\\n          4)   A ladder shall\
      \ be so positioned as to ensure its stability during use\\n\\n          5)   A suspended ladder shall be attached\
      \ in a secure manner and so that, with\\n                the exception of a flexible ladder,  it cannot be\
      \ displaced and swinging is\\n               prevented.\\n\\n          6)   A portable ladder shall be prevented\
      \ from slipping during use by -\\n\\n                          i)     securing the stiles at or near their\
      \ upper or lower ends;\\n\\n                            ii)    an effective anti-slip or other effective stability\
      \ device; or\\n\\n                             iii)   any other arrangement of equivalent effectiveness.\\\
      n\\n          7)   A ladder used for access shall be long enough to protrude sufficiently above\\n       \
      \         the place of landing to which  it provides access, unless other measures\\n             have been\
      \ taken to ensure a firm handhold.\\n\\n          8)   No interlocking or extension ladder shall be used unless\
      \ its sections are\\n               prevented from moving relative to each other while in use.\\n\\n     \
      \     9)   A mobile ladder shall be prevented from moving before it is stepped on.\\n\\n         10)  Where\
      \ a ladder or run of ladders raises a vertical distance of 9 metres or\\n             more above its base,\
      \ there shall, where reasonably practicable, be provided\\n                 at suitable intervals sufficient\
      \ safe landing areas or rest platforms.\\n\\n         11)  Every ladder shall be used in such a way that\\\
      n\\n                a)   a secure handhold and secure support are always available to the\\n             \
      \         user; and\\n\\n                b)    the user can maintain a safe handhold when carrying a load\
      \ unless, in\\n                     the case of a step ladder, the maintenance of a handhold  is not\\n  \
      \                     practicable when a load  is  carried, and a  risk assessment has\\n                \
      \   demonstrated that the use of a stepladder is justified because of\\n\\n                              \
      \      i)     the low risk; and\\n\\n                                       ii)    the short duration of use.\\\
      n\\n\\n19.0    Overhead protection\\n\\n\\n            All contractors shall provide overhead protections\
      \ as per Rule 41 of BOCWR\\n\\n                i)    Overhead protection should be erected along the periphery\
      \ of every building\\n              which is under construction and the building height shall be 15m or above\\\
      n                  after construction.\\n\\n                  ii)    Overhead protection shall be minimum\
      \ 2m wide and the outer edge shall be\\n           150mm higher than the inner edge and an angle not more\
      \ than 200 to its\\n                 horizontal sloping into the building.\\n\\n                  iii)   Overhead\
      \ protection shall not be erected more than a height of 5m from the\\n             base of the building.\\\
      n\\n             iv)   Areas of inadvertent hazard of  falling of material  shall be guarded or\\n       \
      \        barricaded or roped-off thereby by the contractor.\\n\\n\\n20.0     Slipping, Tripping, Cutting,\
      \ Drowning and Falling Hazards\\n\\n        As per Rule 42 of BOCWR,\\n\\n                i)      All places\
      \ should be free from dust, debris or similar materials.\\n\\n\\n\\n\\nBangalore Metro Rail Corporation Ltd.\
      \              September 2026     Section Page 36 of 114\",\n  \"text_blocks\": [\n    {\n      \"bbox\":\

    quote: "{\n  \"extraction_method\": \"geometric_sort\",\n  \"has_extracted_text\": true,\n  \"page_rect\": [\n\

      pending_manual_review\",\n  \"rotation\": 0,\n  \"text\": \"Safety Health & Environment (SHE) Manual\\n229\\\
      n                           xviii) Access to drinking water & toilet shall be ensured to all workmen engaged\\\
      n                              for launching process.\\n\\n                       xix)  Proper access ladders/stairways\
      \ shall be maintained for safe ascending  /\\n                       descending of workmen / engineers.\\\
      n\\n\\n          22.3     Non-adherence to any of the clauses mentioned above shall be viewed\\n         \
      \          seriously by the Employer and penalty levied as per relevant clause.\\n\\n\\n          23.0   \
      \  Construction machinery\\n\\n\\n          23.1     Construction machineries may include dumpers and dump\
      \ trucks,  lift trucks and\\n                     telescopic handlers piling rigs, vibro hammers, rail welding\
      \ equipments, mobile\\n                    elevating work platforms, cranes, tipper lorries, lorry loaders,\
      \ skip wagons, 360°\\n                    excavators, 180° backhoe loaders, crawler tractors, scrapers, graders,\
      \ loading\\n                    shovels,  trenchers,  side  booms,  pavers,  planers,  chippers,  road  rollers,\\\
      n                    locomotives, tankers and bowsers, trailers, hydraulic and mechanical breakers\\n    \
      \                   etc.\\n\\n\\n          23.2     Safe worthiness certificate\\n\\n\\n          23.2.1 \
      \  Every construction equipment shall be in sound mechanical working condition and\\n                    \
      \   certified by  either competent person under Factories Act  or manufacturers’\\n                   warranty\
      \ in case of brand new equipments or authorized persons / firms approved\\n                 by Employer before\
      \ induction to any site.\\n\\n\\n          23.2.2   Every such  certificate  shall have  the  date  of  purchase,\
      \ main  overhauling\\n                  undertaken in the past, any accident to the equipment, visual examination\
      \ details,\\n                          critical components safety check, list of safety devises and its working\
      \ condition,\\n                   manufacturer’s maintenance checklist, past projects wherein the equipments\
      \ were\\n                 used etc as its minimum content.\\n\\n\\n          23.3     Reverse Horns\\n\\n\\\
      n          23.3.1    All Vehicles shall be fitted with audible reverse alarms and maintained in\\n       \
      \        good working condition. Reversing  shall be done only when there  is\\n                 adequate\
      \ rear view visibility or under the directions of a banksman\\n\\n\\n          23.4     General operating\
      \ procedures\\n\\n\\n                                 i)     Drivers entering site shall be instructed to\
      \ follow the safe system of work adopted on\\n                                site. These shall be verbal\
      \ instructions or, preferably, written instructions showing\\n                          the relevant site\
      \ rules, the site layout, delivery areas, speed limits, etc.\\n\\n                                    ii)\
      \   No passengers shall be carried, unless specific seating has been provided  in\\n                     \
      \  accordance with the manufacturers’ recommendations.\\n\\n                                     iii)   Working\
      \ on gradients beyond any equipments capability shall not be allowed.\\n\\n                          iv) \
      \  Prevention of dumper and dump truck accidents should be managed by providing\\n                       wheel\
      \ stops at a sufficient distance from the edges of excavations, spoil heaps, pits,\\n                    \
      \         etc.\\n\\n                      v)   The manufacturer’s recommended bucket size must not be exceeded\
      \ in excavators.\\n\\n                          vi)      If excavators operating on a gradient which cannot\
      \ be avoided, it must be ensured\\n                            that the working cycle is slowed down, that\
      \ the bucket is not extended too far in the\\n                          downhill direction, and that travel\
      \  is undertaken with extreme caution. A large\\n                         excavator must never be permitted\
      \ to travel in a confined area, or around people,\\n                          without a banksman to guide\
      \ the driver, who should have the excavator attachment\\n                         close in to the machine,\
      \ with the bucket just clear of the ground. On wheeled\\n                         excavators, it is essential\
      \ that the tyres are in good condition and correctly inflated.\\n                                        \
      \   If stabilizing devices are  fitted, they should be employed when the machine  is\\n                  \
      \        excavating.\\n\\n\\n\\n\\n         Bangalore Metro Rail Corporation Ltd.              September 2026\
      \     Section Page 41 of 114\",\n  \"text_blocks\": [\n    {\n      \"bbox\": [\n        50.15998077392578,\n\

      \      ],\n      \"block_number\": 4,\n      \"text\": \"for launching process. \\nxix) \\nProper access ladders/stairways\
      \ shall be maintained for safe ascending / \\ndescending of workmen / engineers. \\n \\n22.3 \\nNon-adherence\
      \ to any of the clauses mentioned above shall be viewed \\nseriously by the Employer and penalty levied as\
      \ per relevant clause. \\n \\n23.0  \\nConstruction machinery \\n \\n23.1 \\nConstruction machineries may\
      \ include dumpers and dump trucks, lift trucks and \\ntelescopic handlers piling rigs, vibro hammers, rail\
      \ welding equipments, mobile \\nelevating work platforms, cranes, tipper lorries, lorry loaders, skip wagons,\
      \ 360° \\nexcavators, 180° backhoe loaders, crawler tractors, scrapers, graders, loading \\nshovels, trenchers,\
      \ side booms, pavers, planers, chippers, road rollers, \\nlocomotives, tankers and bowsers, trailers, hydraulic\
      \ and mechanical breakers \\netc. \\n \\n23.2 \\nSafe worthiness certificate \\n \\n23.2.1 \\nEvery construction\
      \ equipment shall be in sound mechanical working condition and \\ncertified by either competent person under\
      \ Factories Act or manufacturers’ \\nwarranty in case of brand new equipments or authorized persons / firms\
      \ approved \\nby Employer before induction to any site. \\n \\n23.2.2 \\nEvery such certificate shall have\
      \ the date of purchase, main overhauling \\nundertaken in the past, any accident to the equipment, visual\
      \ examination details, \\ncritical components safety check, list of safety devises and its working condition,\
      \ \\nmanufacturer’s maintenance checklist, past projects wherein the equipments were \\nused etc as its minimum\
      \ content. \\n \\n23.3 \\nReverse Horns \\n \\n23.3.1 \\nAll Vehicles shall be fitted with audible reverse\
      \ alarms and maintained in \\ngood working condition. Reversing shall be done only when there is \\nadequate\
      \ rear view visibility or under the directions of a banksman \\n \\n23.4 \\nGeneral operating procedures \\\
      n \\n\"\n    },\n    {\n      \"bbox\": [\n        130.5555877685547,\n        549.53955078125,\n        533.884765625,\n\
      \        780.8919677734375\n      ],\n      \"block_number\": 5,\n      \"text\": \"i) \\nDrivers entering\
      \ site shall be instructed to follow the safe system of work adopted on \\nsite. These shall be verbal instructions\
      \ or, preferably, written instructions showing \\nthe relevant site rules, the site layout, delivery areas,\
      \ speed limits, etc.  \\nii) \\nNo passengers shall be carried, unless specific seating has been provided\
      \ in \\naccordance with the manufacturers’ recommendations. \\niii) \\nWorking on gradients beyond any equipments\
      \ capability shall not be allowed.  \\niv) \\nPrevention of dumper and dump truck accidents should be managed\
      \ by providing \\nwheel stops at a sufficient distance from the edges of excavations, spoil heaps, pits, \\\
      netc. \\nv) \\nThe manufacturer’s recommended bucket size must not be exceeded in excavators. \\nvi) \\nIf\
      \ excavators operating on a gradient which cannot be avoided, it must be ensured \\nthat the working cycle\
      \ is slowed down, that the bucket is not extended too far in the \\ndownhill direction, and that travel is\
      \ undertaken with extreme caution. A large \\nexcavator must never be permitted to travel in a confined area,\
      \ or around people, \\nwithout a banksman to guide the driver, who should have the excavator attachment \\\
      nclose in to the machine, with the bucket just clear of the ground. On wheeled \\nexcavators, it is essential\
      \ that the tyres are in good condition and correctly inflated. \\nIf stabilizing devices are fitted, they\
      \ should be employed when the machine is \\nexcavating. \\n\"\n    },\n    {\n      \"bbox\": [\n        39.599998474121094,\n\

      pending_manual_review\",\n  \"rotation\": 0,\n  \"text\": \"Safety Health & Environment (SHE) Manual\\n227\\\
      n          21.10.2  Boom\\n\\n\\n                                 i)    The boom is one of the more critical\
      \ elements of the crane and must be in\\n                           perfect condition at all time. No boom\
      \ section with a bent lattice member\\n                             shall be allowed\\n\\n               \
      \                     ii)     All welds shall be crack and corrosion free\\n\\n                          \
      \           iii)   No member of the boom shall be bent\\n\\n                          iv)    All telescopic\
      \ boom shall be free from cracks, rust, flaking or cracked paint,\\n                          bulges, greases\
      \ or varnishes\\n\\n          21.10.3  The sweep area (work area) of the construction machinery shall be always\
      \ free\\n                  from obstructions.\\n\\n\\n          21.10.4   All hydraulic piping and fittings\
      \ shall be maintained leak proof.\\n\\n\\n          21.10.5  The operator cab shall posses good and safe:\\\
      n\\n\\n                                 i)     structure, windows and windshield wipers\\n\\n            \
      \                        ii)    Drivers chair and foot rest\\n\\n                                     iii)\
      \    Control handles\\n\\n                          iv)   Cab instrumentation\\n\\n                      v)\
      \    Telecommunication\\n\\n                          vi)   Cab out fitting\\n\\n                        \
      \     vii)   wind  indicator  with an  adjustable  set  point  shall be  in a  position\\n               \
      \           representative for the wind on the crane. The indicator shall give continuous\\n             \
      \             information regarding constant speeds and gusts.\\n\\n\\n         21.11    Mandatory rigging\
      \ requirements\\n\\n\\n          21.11.1  Rigging shall be done under experienced and qualified rigger only.\\\
      n\\n\\n          21.11.2  The primary requirement in rigging shall be to assess the weight of load\\n    \
      \              before attempting any lift.\\n\\n\\n          21.11.3   All hooks shall be fitted with Master\
      \ Rings having certificate of fitness from\\n                  the competent person, so that the hooks are\
      \ subjected to balanced vertical\\n                  loading only.\\n\\n\\n          21.11.4  Only four legged\
      \ slings shall be allowed which includes master link (ring),\\n                  intermediate master link\
      \ (ring)  if necessary, chain  / wire rope sling, sling\\n               hook or other terminal fitting.\\\
      n\\n\\n          21.11.5  Hand spliced slings up to 32mm diameter shall not be used at site for any\\n   \
      \                    lifting purpose.\\n\\n\\n          21.11.6  No load shall be slewed over public areas\
      \ without stopping the pedestrians\\n               and road traffic first.\\n\\n\\n          21.11.7  Requirements\
      \ of outriggers\\n\\n                              i)     All outriggers shall be fully extended and at all\
      \ tyres are clear of the ground\\n\\n                                    ii)   Heavy duty blocking having\
      \ large bearing area shall be necessary to prevent\\n                        sinking of floats\\n\\n\\n  \
      \        21.11.8   All loads shall have tag-lines attached in order to ensure that the load can be\\n    \
      \               controlled at all times.\\n\\n\\n\\n\\n\\n         Bangalore Metro Rail Corporation Ltd. \
      \             September 2026     Section Page 39 of 114\",\n  \"text_blocks\": [\n    {\n      \"bbox\": [\n\

      \        88.32714080810547,\n        35.93199157714844\n      ],\n      \"block_number\": 1,\n      \"text\"\
      : \" \\n\"\n    },\n    {\n      \"bbox\": [\n        85.5599594116211,\n        809.042724609375,\n     \
      \   511.7470703125,\n        830.5714111328125\n      ],\n      \"block_number\": 2,\n      \"text\": \"Bangalore\
      \ Metro Rail Corporation Ltd.                              September 2026         Section Page 39 of 114 \\\
      n \\n\"\n    },\n    {\n      \"bbox\": [\n        85.5597915649414,\n        38.09945297241211,\n       \
      \ 529.3277587890625,\n        785.4519653320312\n      ],\n      \"block_number\": 3,\n      \"text\": \"\
      21.10.2 \\nBoom \\n \\ni) \\nThe boom is one of the more critical elements of the crane and must be in \\\
      nperfect condition at all time. No boom section with a bent lattice member \\nshall be allowed \\nii) \\nAll\
      \ welds shall be crack and corrosion free \\niii) \\nNo member of the boom shall be bent \\niv) \\nAll telescopic\
      \ boom shall be free from cracks, rust, flaking or cracked paint, \\nbulges, greases or varnishes \\n21.10.3\
      \  The sweep area (work area) of the construction machinery shall be always free \\nfrom obstructions. \\\
      n \\n21.10.4 \\nAll hydraulic piping and fittings shall be maintained leak proof. \\n \\n21.10.5 \\nThe operator\
      \ cab shall posses good and safe: \\n \\ni) \\nstructure, windows and windshield wipers  \\nii) \\nDrivers\
      \ chair and foot rest \\niii) \\nControl handles \\niv) \\nCab instrumentation \\nv) \\nTelecommunication\
      \ \\nvi) \\nCab out fitting \\nvii) \\nwind indicator with an adjustable set point shall be in a position\
      \ \\nrepresentative for the wind on the crane. The indicator shall give continuous \\ninformation regarding\
      \ constant speeds and gusts. \\n \\n21.11 \\nMandatory rigging requirements \\n \\n21.11.1 \\nRigging shall\
      \ be done under experienced and qualified rigger only. \\n \\n21.11.2 \\nThe primary requirement in rigging\
      \ shall be to assess the weight of load \\nbefore attempting any lift. \\n \\n21.11.3 \\nAll hooks shall be\
      \ fitted with Master Rings having certificate of fitness from \\nthe competent person, so that the hooks are\
      \ subjected to balanced vertical \\nloading only. \\n \\n21.11.4  Only four legged slings shall be allowed\
      \ which includes master link (ring), \\nintermediate master link (ring) if necessary, chain / wire rope sling,\
      \ sling \\nhook or other terminal fitting. \\n \\n21.11.5 \\nHand spliced slings up to 32mm diameter shall\
      \ not be used at site for any \\nlifting purpose. \\n \\n21.11.6 \\nNo load shall be slewed over public areas\
      \ without stopping the pedestrians \\nand road traffic first.  \\n \\n21.11.7  Requirements of outriggers\
      \ \\ni) \\nAll outriggers shall be fully extended and at all tyres are clear of the ground \\nii) \\nHeavy\
      \ duty blocking having large bearing area shall be necessary to prevent \\nsinking of floats \\n \\n21.11.8\
      \ \\nAll loads shall have tag-lines attached in order to ensure that the load can be \\ncontrolled at all\
      \ times. \\n \\n\"\n    },\n    {\n      \"bbox\": [\n        39.599998474121094,\n        24.479991912841797,\n\
      \        63.57600021362305,\n        41.38799285888672\n      ],\n      \"block_number\": 4,\n      \"text\"\
      : \"227\\n\"\n    }\n  ]\n}"
