      pending_manual_review\",\n  \"rotation\": 0,\n  \"text\": \"Safety Health & Environment (SHE) Manual\\n  \
      \                                                        228\\n21.11.9  No close working to any  live overhead\
      \ power  line  is permitted without the\\n         operation of a strict Permit to Work.\\n\\n\\n21.11.10\
      \ Minimum lighting is to be ensured at all lifting operations.\\n\\n\\n21.12    Failure to do any of the above\
      \ shall attract penalty from the Employer as per\\n         relevant clause\\n\\n\\n22.0     Launching Operation\\\
      n\\n22.1    As launching operation  is one of the  riskiest job, the contractor shall take utmost\\n     \
      \     precaution  at  all stages  like; planning, establishing casing yard, casting segments,\\n         \
      \ transporting segments,  fabrication and  erection  of launching  girders, launching  of\\n         segments,\
      \ pre-stressing, auto launching of girders and dismantling of launching girders.\\n\\n\\n22.2    The contractor\
      \ shall prepare a comprehensive Method Statement  for the launching\\n          operation, adhering to the\
      \ SHE conditions laid down in conditions of contract on SHE and\\n          project SHE manual. Particular\
      \ reference shall be made to the provisions on working at\\n           height. As the entire process of launching\
      \ has to be undertaken at an elevated level, the\\n          safety of workers and the girder is paramount\
      \ important. The following general guidelines\\n           shall be adhered throughout the launching operation.\\\
      n\\n\\n                i)    Necessary ‘working platforms’ and fall protection anchorage arrangement shall\
      \ be\\n               provided in the launching girder itself.\\n\\n                  ii)    Provisions for\
      \ mounting light fittings shall also be made available in the launching\\n                  girder.\\n\\n\
      \                  iii)   The casting yard shall be established ensuring the provision given in clause 38.0\\\
      n\\n             iv)   The workmen engaged in fabrication of reinforcement, concreting the segment\\n    \
      \              shall be provided with necessary PPEs including compulsory hand protection\\n             \
      \   gloves.\\n\\n           v)    Casting and curing of segment shall be undertaken under the direct supervision\
      \ of\\n                the responsible engineer of the contractor.\\n\\n             vi)   Trucks  with  valid\
      \  registration,  licence, safe worthiness  certificate, Employer’s\\n               approval certificate,\
      \ and pollution under check certificate shall only be used for\\n                transport of segments\\n\\\
      n              vii)   Drivers engaged for driving these trucks, shall be trained once in 6 months at\\n  \
      \              specified locations as directed by the employer on defensive driving.\\n\\n               viii)\
      \   Drivers shall also have undergone proper medical examination as per relevant\\n               clause mentioned\
      \ under ‘Medical Facilities’.\\n\\n             ix)   The segments shall rigidly secured to the truck with\
      \ necessary wooden wedges\\n             and necessary red indicators/safety tapes provided so that the vehicle\
      \ is clearly\\n             seen by other road users both in day / night time.\\n\\n           x)    Every\
      \ launching girder shall have a responsible engineer on duty all the time.\\n\\n             xi)    All the\
      \ time from erection to dismantling the area between the two piers\\n              wherein launching is in\
      \ progress shall always be barricaded.\\n\\n              xii)   Unloading  of  segments  from  trucks,  lifting\
      \  of  segments,  shifting  of\\n              segments, gluing shall be done under the direct supervision\
      \ of the approved\\n               engineer of the contractor.\\n\\n               xiii)  Auto launching shall\
      \ be done only after approval from the Employer. After\\n               every auto launching the stability\
      \ of launching girder shall be ensured.\\n\\n            xiv)  The vertical deflection of launching girder\
      \ shall be monitored at all critical\\n               stages like with/without loads and after every auto\
      \ launching.\\n\\n          xv)  A  register containing  all important operational  details from erection\
      \  to\\n                dismantling of launching girders shall be maintained and made available to\\n    \
      \          Employer whenever called for.\\n\\n            xvi)  Test  certificate  for  all  lifting  gears\
      \  including  Macalloy  bars  shall be\\n               maintained at a location closer to the launching girder\
      \ itself so that it can be\\n                referred during all inspections.\\n\\n             xvii)  Adequate\
      \ lighting at all time shall be ensured in the entire area of operation.\\n\\n\\n\\nBangalore Metro Rail Corporation\
      \ Ltd.              September 2026     Section Page 40 of 114\",\n  \"text_blocks\": [\n    {\n      \"bbox\"\
      : [\n        47.039981842041016,\n        15.768376350402832,\n        561.0993041992188,\n        24.210372924804688\n\
      \      ],\n      \"block_number\": 0,\n      \"text\": \"                                                \
      \                                                                                   Safety Health & Environment\
      \ (SHE) Manual \\n\"\n    },\n    {\n      \"bbox\": [\n        82.4399642944336,\n        26.57955551147461,\n\
      \        85.20714569091797,\n        35.93199157714844\n      ],\n      \"block_number\": 1,\n      \"text\"\
      : \" \\n\"\n    },\n    {\n      \"bbox\": [\n        82.4399642944336,\n        809.042724609375,\n     \
      \   508.6270751953125,\n        830.5714111328125\n      ],\n      \"block_number\": 2,\n      \"text\": \"\
      Bangalore Metro Rail Corporation Ltd.                              September 2026         Section Page 40\
      \ of 114 \\n \\n\"\n    },\n    {\n      \"bbox\": [\n        82.4399642944336,\n        37.97945785522461,\n\
      \        526.2095947265625,\n        783.8915405273438\n      ],\n      \"block_number\": 3,\n      \"text\"\
      : \"21.11.9 \\nNo close working to any live overhead power line is permitted without the \\noperation of a\
      \ strict Permit to Work. \\n \\n21.11.10 Minimum lighting is to be ensured at all lifting operations. \\n\
      \ \\n21.12 \\nFailure to do any of the above shall attract penalty from the Employer as per \\nrelevant clause\
      \ \\n \\n22.0 \\nLaunching Operation \\n22.1 \\nAs launching operation is one of the riskiest job, the contractor\
      \ shall take utmost \\nprecaution at all stages like; planning, establishing casing yard, casting segments,\
      \ \\ntransporting segments, fabrication and erection of launching girders, launching of \\nsegments, pre-stressing,\
      \ auto launching of girders and dismantling of launching girders. \\n \\n22.2 \\nThe contractor shall prepare\
      \ a comprehensive Method Statement for the launching \\noperation, adhering to the SHE conditions laid down\
      \ in conditions of contract on SHE and \\nproject SHE manual. Particular reference shall be made to the provisions\
      \ on working at \\nheight.  As the entire process of launching has to be undertaken at an elevated level,\
      \ the \\nsafety of workers and the girder is paramount important. The following general guidelines \\nshall\
      \ be adhered throughout the launching operation.  \\n \\ni) \\nNecessary ‘working platforms’ and fall protection\
      \ anchorage arrangement shall be \\nprovided in the launching girder itself. \\nii) \\nProvisions for mounting\
      \ light fittings shall also be made available in the launching \\ngirder. \\niii) \\nThe casting yard shall\
      \ be established ensuring the provision given in clause 38.0   \\niv) \\nThe workmen engaged in fabrication\
      \ of reinforcement, concreting the segment \\nshall be provided with necessary PPEs including compulsory hand\
      \ protection \\ngloves. \\nv) \\nCasting and curing of segment shall be undertaken under the direct supervision\
      \ of \\nthe responsible engineer of the contractor. \\nvi) \\nTrucks with valid registration, licence, safe\
      \ worthiness certificate, Employer’s \\napproval certificate, and pollution under check certificate shall\
      \ only be used for \\ntransport of segments \\nvii) \\nDrivers engaged for driving these trucks, shall be\
      \ trained once in 6 months at \\nspecified locations as directed by the employer on defensive driving.   \\\
      nviii) \\nDrivers shall also have undergone proper medical examination as per relevant \\nclause mentioned\
      \ under ‘Medical Facilities’. \\nix) \\nThe segments shall rigidly secured to the truck with necessary wooden\
      \ wedges \\nand necessary red indicators/safety tapes provided so that the vehicle is clearly \\nseen by other\
      \ road users both in day / night time.  \\nx) \\nEvery launching girder shall have a responsible engineer\
      \ on duty all the time. \\nxi) \\nAll the time from erection to dismantling the area between the two piers\
      \ \\nwherein launching is in progress shall always be barricaded. \\nxii) \\nUnloading of segments from trucks,\
      \ lifting of segments, shifting of \\nsegments, gluing shall be done under the direct supervision of the approved\
      \ \\nengineer of the contractor. \\nxiii) \\nAuto launching shall be done only after approval from the Employer.\
      \ After \\nevery auto launching the stability of launching girder shall be ensured. \\nxiv) \\nThe vertical\
      \ deflection of launching girder shall be monitored at all critical \\nstages like with/without loads and\
      \ after every auto launching.  \\nxv) \\nA register containing all important operational details from erection\
      \ to \\ndismantling of launching girders shall be maintained and made available to \\nEmployer whenever called\
      \ for.  \\nxvi) \\nTest certificate for all lifting gears including Macalloy bars shall be \\nmaintained at\
      \ a location closer to the launching girder itself so that it can be \\nreferred during all inspections. \\\
      nxvii) Adequate lighting at all time shall be ensured in the entire area of operation. \\n\"\n    },\n   \
      \ {\n      \"bbox\": [\n        546.0439453125,\n        24.479991912841797,\n        570.0199584960938,\n\
      \        41.38799285888672\n      ],\n      \"block_number\": 4,\n      \"text\": \"228\\n\"\n    }\n  ]\n\
      }"

    quote: "{\n  \"extraction_method\": \"geometric_sort\",\n  \"has_extracted_text\": true,\n  \"page_rect\": [\n\
      \    0.0,\n    0.0,\n    595.219970703125,\n    842.0\n  ],\n  \"pdf_page\": 48,\n  \"review_status\": \"\
      pending_manual_review\",\n  \"rotation\": 0,\n  \"text\": \"Safety Health & Environment (SHE) Manual\\n  \
      \                                                        232\\n26.7      Electrical protection circuits\\\
      n\\n26.7.1    Precautions shall be taken, either by earthing or by other suitable means, to prevent\\n   \
      \      danger arising when any conductor (other than a  circuit conductor) which may\\n         reasonably\
      \ foreseeable become charged as a result of either the use of a system, or a\\n            fault in a system,\
      \ becomes so charged. A conductor shall be regarded as earthed\\n        when conductors of sufficient strength\
      \ and current-carrying capability to discharge\\n           electrical energy to earth connect it to the general\
      \ mass of earth.\\n\\n                If a circuit conductor is connected to earth or to any other reference\
      \ point, nothing\\n         which might reasonably be expected to give rise to danger by breaking the electrical\\\
      n           continuity or introducing high impedance shall be placed in that conductor unless\\n         \
      \ suitable precautions are taken to prevent that danger.\\n\\n\\n26.7.2    Appropriate electrical protection\
      \ shall be provided for all circuits, against over load,\\n          short circuit and earth fault current.\\\
      n\\n\\n26.7.3   The contractor shall provide sufficient ELCBs (maintain sensitivity 30 mA) / RCCBs for\\n\
      \              all the equipments (including Potable equipments), electrical switchboards, distribution\\\
      n         panels etc. to prevent electrical shocks to the workers.\\n\\n\\n26.7.4     All protection devices\
      \ shall be capable of interrupting the circuit without damage to any\\n         equipments and circuits in\
      \ case of any fault may occur.\\n\\n\\n26.7.5    Rating of fuses and circuit breakers used for the protection\
      \ of circuits should be\\n          coordinate with equipment power ratings.\\n\\n\\n26.7.6    Protection\
      \ against lightning shall be ensured to all equipment kept in open at sites.\\n\\n\\n26.8     Cables:\\n\\\
      n\\n26.8.1   Cables shall be selected after full consideration of the condition to which they shall be\\n\
      \        exposed and the duties for which they are required. Supply cable up to 3.3 kV shall be\\n       \
      \     in accordance with BS 6346.\\n\\n\\n26.8.2   For supplies to mobile or transportable equipment where\
      \ operating of the equipment\\n          subjects the cable to flexing, the cable shall conform to any of\
      \ these codes BS 6007 /\\n       BS 6500 / BS 7375.\\n\\n\\n26.8.3    Flexible cords with a conductor cross\
      \ sectional area smaller than 1.5 mm2 shall not be\\n        used and insulated flexible cable shall conform\
      \ to BS 6500 and BS 7375.\\n\\n\\n26.8.4   Where low voltage cables are to be used, reference shall be made\
      \ to BS 7375. The\\n          following standards shall also be referred to particularly for under ground\
      \ cables BS\\n        6346 and BS 6708\\n\\n\\n26.8.5   Cables buried directly in the ground shall be of a\
      \ type incorporating armour or metal\\n         sheath or both. Such cables shall be marked by cable covers\
      \ or a suitable marking\\n         tape and be buried at a  sufficient depth to avoid  their being damaged\
      \ by any\\n          disturbance of the ground. Cable routes shall be marked on the plans kept in the site\\\
      n           electrical register.\\n\\n26.8.6    Cabling passing under the walk way and across way  for transport\
      \ and mobile\\n         equipment shall be laid in ducts at a minimum depth of 0.6 meters.\\n\\n26.8.7   Cables\
      \ that need to cross open areas, or where span of 3m or more are involved, a\\n         catenary wire on poles\
      \ or other supports shall be provided for convenient means of\\n         suspension. Minimum height shall\
      \ be 6 m above ground.\\n\\n\\n26.8.8   Cables carrying a voltage to earth in excess of 65V other than supply\
      \ for welding\\n         process shall have metal armour or sheath, which has been effectively earthed and\\\
      n         monitored by the contractor. In case of flexible and trailing cables such earthed metal\\n\\n\\\
      n\\nBangalore Metro Rail Corporation Ltd.              September 2026     Section Page 44 of 114\",\n  \"\
      text_blocks\": [\n    {\n      \"bbox\": [\n        47.039981842041016,\n        15.768376350402832,\n   \

      : \"                                                                                                     \

      : [\n        82.43990325927734,\n        38.09945297241211,\n        512.7694702148438,\n        786.8916625976562\n\
      \      ],\n      \"block_number\": 3,\n      \"text\": \"26.7 \\nElectrical protection circuits \\n26.7.1\
      \ \\nPrecautions shall be taken, either by earthing or by other suitable means, to prevent \\ndanger arising\
      \ when any conductor (other than a circuit conductor) which may \\nreasonably foreseeable become charged as\
      \ a result of either the use of a system, or a \\nfault in a system, becomes so charged. A conductor shall\

      \ \\nelectrical energy to earth connect it to the general mass of earth.  \\nIf a circuit conductor is connected\
      \ to earth or to any other reference point, nothing \\nwhich might reasonably be expected to give rise to\
      \ danger by breaking the electrical \\ncontinuity or introducing high impedance shall be placed in that conductor\
      \ unless \\nsuitable precautions are taken to prevent that danger.  \\n \\n26.7.2 \\nAppropriate electrical\
      \ protection shall be provided for all circuits, against over load, \\nshort circuit and earth fault current.\
      \  \\n \\n26.7.3 \\nThe contractor shall provide sufficient ELCBs (maintain sensitivity 30 mA) / RCCBs for\
      \ \\nall the equipments (including Potable equipments), electrical switchboards, distribution \\npanels etc.\
      \ to prevent electrical shocks to the workers. \\n \\n26.7.4 \\nAll protection devices shall be capable of\
      \ interrupting the circuit without damage to any \\nequipments and circuits in case of any fault may occur.\
      \ \\n \\n26.7.5 \\nRating of fuses and circuit breakers used for the protection of circuits should be \\ncoordinate\
      \ with equipment power ratings. \\n \\n26.7.6 \\nProtection against lightning shall be ensured to all equipment\
      \ kept in open at sites. \\n \\n26.8 \\nCables: \\n \\n26.8.1 \\nCables shall be selected after full consideration\
      \ of the condition to which they shall be \\nexposed and the duties for which they are required. Supply cable\
      \ up to 3.3 kV shall be \\nin accordance with BS 6346. \\n \\n26.8.2 \\nFor supplies to mobile or transportable\
      \ equipment where operating of the equipment \\nsubjects the cable to flexing, the cable shall conform to\
      \ any of these codes BS 6007 / \\nBS 6500 / BS 7375. \\n \\n26.8.3 \\nFlexible cords with a conductor cross\
      \ sectional area smaller than 1.5 mm2 shall not be \\nused and insulated flexible cable shall conform to BS\
      \ 6500 and BS 7375. \\n \\n26.8.4 \\nWhere low voltage cables are to be used, reference shall be made to BS\
      \ 7375. The \\nfollowing standards shall also be referred to particularly for under ground cables BS \\n6346\
      \ and BS 6708  \\n \\n26.8.5 \\nCables buried directly in the ground shall be of a type incorporating armour\
      \ or metal \\nsheath or both. Such cables shall be marked by cable covers or a suitable marking \\ntape and\
      \ be buried at a sufficient depth to avoid their being damaged by any \\ndisturbance of the ground. Cable\
      \ routes shall be marked on the plans kept in the site \\nelectrical register. \\n26.8.6 \\nCabling passing\
      \ under the walk way and across way for transport and mobile \\nequipment shall be laid in ducts at a minimum\
      \ depth of 0.6 meters. \\n26.8.7 \\nCables that need to cross open areas, or where span of 3m or more are\
      \ involved, a \\ncatenary wire on poles or other supports shall be provided for convenient means of \\nsuspension.\
      \ Minimum height shall be 6 m above ground.   \\n \\n26.8.8 \\nCables carrying a voltage to earth in excess\
      \ of 65V other than supply for welding \\nprocess shall have metal armour or sheath, which has been effectively\
      \ earthed and \\nmonitored by the contractor. In case of flexible and trailing cables such earthed metal \\\
      n\"\n    },\n    {\n      \"bbox\": [\n        546.0439453125,\n        24.479991912841797,\n        570.0199584960938,\n\

      pending_manual_review\",\n  \"rotation\": 0,\n  \"text\": \"Safety Health & Environment (SHE) Manual\\n  \
      \                                                        230\\n              vii)  When the front shovel of\
      \ the 1800 backhoe loaders is being employed, the backhoe\\n               attachment shall be in its “travel”\
      \ position, with the safety locking device in place.\\n\\n               viii)  When operating the backhoe\
      \ in poor ground conditions, the stabilisers tend to sink\\n                  into the surface of the ground,\
      \ reducing stability. Therefore frequent checks shall be\\n           made for the stability of the machine.\
      \ The loading shovel should always be lowered\\n                 to the ground to stabilise the machine when\
      \ the backhoe is employed.\\n\\n             ix)   The netting operation of the skip wagons should be carried\
      \ out prior to lifting the\\n                skip to reduce the risks of working on the rear platform\\n\\\
      n           x)       If a tractor dozer is employed on clearing scrub or felling trees, it shall be provided\\\
      n                with adequate driver protection.\\n\\n             xi)   When two or more scrapers are working\
      \ on the same job, a minimum distance of at\\n                 least 25m shall be kept between them.\\n\\\
      n              xii)   Incase of hydraulic breakers, hydraulic rams and hoses shall be in good working\\n \
      \               condition\\n\\n\\n23.5       All wood working machines shall be fitted with suitable guards\
      \ and devices such as top\\n          guard, riving knife, push stick, guards for drive belts and chains,\
      \ and emergency stop\\n          switch easily accessible by the operator.\\n\\n\\n23.6     Penalty\\n\\n\\\
      n23.6.1      If any of the above clauses are not adhered, penalty shall be imposed as per\\n         relevant\
      \ clause depending upon the gravity of the unsafe act and or condition.\\n\\n\\n24.0    Machine and general\
      \ area guarding\\n\\n\\n24.1    The contractor shall ensure at the construction site all motors, cogwheels,\
      \ chains and\\n            friction gearing,  flywheels,  shafting, dangerous and moving parts  of machinery\
      \ are\\n          securely fenced or legged. The fencing of dangerous part of machinery is not removed\\n\
      \          while such machinery is in motion or in use.\\n\\n\\n25.0    Manual lifting and carrying of excessive\
      \ weight\\n\\n\\n25.1    The  contractor  shall ensure  at  his  construction  site  of a  building  or other\\\
      n          construction work that no building worker lifts by hand or carries overhead or over\\n        \
      \   his back or shoulders any material, article, tool or appliances exceeding in weight\\n         as said\
      \ below as per Rule 38 of BOCWR, Unless aided by another building worker\\n          or device.\\n\\n    \
      \                  Person      Maximum weight in\\n                                                 kg.\\\
      n\\n                          Adult man             55\\n\\n                          Adult              \
      \   30\\n                  woman\\n\\n\\n25.2    No building worker aided by other building worker shall lift\
      \ or carry weight higher\\n         than or exceeding the sum of total of maximum limits set out for each\
      \ building\\n         worker separately as mentioned in the table above.\\n\\n\\n26.0      Site Electricity\\\
      n\\n26.1     Competency of Electrical personnel:\\n\\n26.1.1   The contractor shall employ qualified and competent\
      \ electrical personnel as\\n         specified in general instruction BMRC/SHE/CEO/001.\\n\\n\\n26.2     Assessment\
      \ of power\\n\\n\\n\\n\\n\\nBangalore Metro Rail Corporation Ltd.              September 2026     Section\

      \ shovel of the 1800 backhoe loaders is being employed, the backhoe \\nattachment shall be in its “travel”\

      pending_manual_review\",\n  \"rotation\": 0,\n  \"text\": \"Safety Health & Environment (SHE) Manual\\n  \
      \                                                        232\\n26.7      Electrical protection circuits\\\
      n\\n26.7.1    Precautions shall be taken, either by earthing or by other suitable means, to prevent\\n   \
      \      danger arising when any conductor (other than a  circuit conductor) which may\\n         reasonably\
      \ foreseeable become charged as a result of either the use of a system, or a\\n            fault in a system,\
      \ becomes so charged. A conductor shall be regarded as earthed\\n        when conductors of sufficient strength\
      \ and current-carrying capability to discharge\\n           electrical energy to earth connect it to the general\
      \ mass of earth.\\n\\n                If a circuit conductor is connected to earth or to any other reference\
      \ point, nothing\\n         which might reasonably be expected to give rise to danger by breaking the electrical\\\
      n           continuity or introducing high impedance shall be placed in that conductor unless\\n         \
      \ suitable precautions are taken to prevent that danger.\\n\\n\\n26.7.2    Appropriate electrical protection\
      \ shall be provided for all circuits, against over load,\\n          short circuit and earth fault current.\\\
      n\\n\\n26.7.3   The contractor shall provide sufficient ELCBs (maintain sensitivity 30 mA) / RCCBs for\\n\
      \              all the equipments (including Potable equipments), electrical switchboards, distribution\\\
      n         panels etc. to prevent electrical shocks to the workers.\\n\\n\\n26.7.4     All protection devices\
      \ shall be capable of interrupting the circuit without damage to any\\n         equipments and circuits in\
      \ case of any fault may occur.\\n\\n\\n26.7.5    Rating of fuses and circuit breakers used for the protection\
      \ of circuits should be\\n          coordinate with equipment power ratings.\\n\\n\\n26.7.6    Protection\
      \ against lightning shall be ensured to all equipment kept in open at sites.\\n\\n\\n26.8     Cables:\\n\\\
      n\\n26.8.1   Cables shall be selected after full consideration of the condition to which they shall be\\n\
      \        exposed and the duties for which they are required. Supply cable up to 3.3 kV shall be\\n       \
      \     in accordance with BS 6346.\\n\\n\\n26.8.2   For supplies to mobile or transportable equipment where\
      \ operating of the equipment\\n          subjects the cable to flexing, the cable shall conform to any of\
      \ these codes BS 6007 /\\n       BS 6500 / BS 7375.\\n\\n\\n26.8.3    Flexible cords with a conductor cross\
      \ sectional area smaller than 1.5 mm2 shall not be\\n        used and insulated flexible cable shall conform\
      \ to BS 6500 and BS 7375.\\n\\n\\n26.8.4   Where low voltage cables are to be used, reference shall be made\
      \ to BS 7375. The\\n          following standards shall also be referred to particularly for under ground\
      \ cables BS\\n        6346 and BS 6708\\n\\n\\n26.8.5   Cables buried directly in the ground shall be of a\
      \ type incorporating armour or metal\\n         sheath or both. Such cables shall be marked by cable covers\
      \ or a suitable marking\\n         tape and be buried at a  sufficient depth to avoid  their being damaged\
      \ by any\\n          disturbance of the ground. Cable routes shall be marked on the plans kept in the site\\\
      n           electrical register.\\n\\n26.8.6    Cabling passing under the walk way and across way  for transport\
      \ and mobile\\n         equipment shall be laid in ducts at a minimum depth of 0.6 meters.\\n\\n26.8.7   Cables\
      \ that need to cross open areas, or where span of 3m or more are involved, a\\n         catenary wire on poles\
      \ or other supports shall be provided for convenient means of\\n         suspension. Minimum height shall\
      \ be 6 m above ground.\\n\\n\\n26.8.8   Cables carrying a voltage to earth in excess of 65V other than supply\
      \ for welding\\n         process shall have metal armour or sheath, which has been effectively earthed and\\\
      n         monitored by the contractor. In case of flexible and trailing cables such earthed metal\\n\\n\\\
      n\\nBangalore Metro Rail Corporation Ltd.              September 2026     Section Page 44 of 114\",\n  \"\

      \ Minimum height shall be 6 m above ground.   \\n \\n26.8.8 \\nCables carrying a voltage to earth in excess\

      n\\n          26.9     Plugs, socket-outlets and couplers:\\n\\n\\n          26.9.1   The contractor shall\
      \ ensure plugs, socket-outlets, and couplers available in\\n                  the construction  site as “splash\
      \ proof” type. The minimum degree of\\n                  Ingress Protection should be of IP44 in accordance\
      \ with BS EN 60529.\\n\\n\\n          26.9.2   Only plugs and fittings of the weatherproof type shall be used\
      \ and they should be colour\\n                 coded in accordance with the Internationally recognised standards\
      \ for example as detailed\\n                 as follows:\\n\\n                      (a)   110 volts : Yellow.\\\
      n\\n                      (b)   240 volts : Blue.\\n\\n                       (c)   415 volts : Red.\\n\\\
      n         26.10    Connections\\n\\n          26.10.1  Every joint and connection in a system shall be mechanically\
      \ and electrically\\n                   suitable  for  use  to  prevent  danger.  Proper  cable  connectors\
      \  as  per\\n                    national/international standards shall only be used to connect cables.\\\
      n\\n          26.10.2  No loose connections or tapped joints shall be allowed any where in the work\\n   \
      \                    site, office area, stores and other areas. Penalty as per relevant clause shall be\\\
      n                  put in case of observation of any tapped joints.\\n\\n\\n         26.11    Portable and\
      \ hand-held equipments:\\n\\n\\n          26.11.1  The contractor shall ensure the use of double insulated\
      \ or all-insulated portable\\n                       electrical hand equipment may be used without earthing\
      \ (i.e. two core cables), but\\n                   they shall still be used only on 110V because of the risk\
      \ of damage to trailing leads.\\n\\n\\n         26.12    Other equipments:\\n\\n\\n          26.12.1   All\
      \ equipment shall have the provision for major switch/cut-off switch in the equipment\\n                 \
      \          itself.\\n\\n\\n          26.12.2   All non-current carrying metal parts of electrical equipment\
      \ shall be earthed through\\n                    insulated cable\\n\\n\\n          26.12.3   Isolate exposed\
      \ high-voltage (over 415 Volts) equipment, such as transformer banks,\\n                open switches, and\
      \ similar equipment with exposed energized parts and prevent\\n                   unauthorised access.\\n\\\
      n\\n          26.12.4  Approved perimeter markings shall be used to isolate restricted areas from designated\\\
      n                 work areas and entryways and shall be erected before work begins and maintained for\\n \
      \                     entire duration of work. Approved perimeter marking shall be installed  with either\
      \ red\\n                      barrier tape printed with the words \\\"DANGER—HIGH VOLTAGE\\\" or a barrier\
      \ of yellow\\n                     or orange synthetic rope, approximately 1 to 1.5 meter above the floor\
      \ or work\\n                    surface.\\n\\n\\n         26.13   Work on or near live conductors\\n\\n\\\

      \ type shall be used and they should be colour \\ncoded in accordance with the Internationally recognised\

      \ \\n(c) \\n415 volts : Red. \\n \\n26.10 \\nConnections \\n \\n26.10.1 \\nEvery joint and connection in a\

      n\\n          29.3       All gas cylinders shall be fixed with pressure regulator and dial gauges\\n\\n\\\
      n          29.4     Non-return valve and Flashback arrester shall be fixed at both end of cylinder and\\n\
      \                      torch.\\n\\n\\n          29.5     Domestic LPG cylinders shall not be used for Gas\
      \ welding and Cutting purpose.\\n\\n\\n          29.6    DCP or CO2 type Fire Extinguisher not less than 5\
      \ kg shall be fixed at or near to\\n                   welding process zone  in an easily accessible  location.\
      \ Fire Extinguisher should\\n                    confirm to IS 2190: 1992.\\n\\n\\n          29.7    Use firewatchers\
      \ if there is a possibility of ignition unobserved by the operator (e.g. on\\n                    the other\
      \ side of bulkheads).\\n\\n\\n          29.8    Oxygen cylinders and flammable gas cylinders shall be stored\
      \ separately, at least 6.6\\n                  meters (20 feet) apart or separated by a fire proof, 1.5 meters\
      \ (5 feet) high partition.\\n                 Flammable substances shall not be stored within 15 meters of\
      \ cylinder storage areas.\\n\\n\\n          29.9     Transformer used for electrical arc welding shall be\
      \ fixed with Ammeter and Voltmeter\\n                and also fixed with separate main power switch.\\n\\\
      n\\n         29.10    Welding grounds and returns should be securely attached to the work by cable lugs,\\\
      n                 by clamps in the case of stranded conductors, or by bolts for strip conductors. The\\n \
      \                 ground cable will not be attached to equipment or existing installations or apparatus.\\\
      n\\n\\n         29.11   Use a low voltage open circuit relay device  if welding with alternating current in\\\
      n                     constricted or damp places.\\n\\n         29.12    Take precautions against the risk\
      \ of increased fume hazards when welding with\\n                chrome containing fluxed consumables or high\
      \ current metal  inert gas (MIG) or\\n                   tungsten inert gas (TIG) processes.\\n\\n       \
      \  29.13    Avoid being in contact with water or wet floors when welding. Use duckboards or\\n           \
      \        rubber protection.\\n\\n\\n         29.14     All electrical installations shall meet the IS: 5571:\
      \ 1997 and NFPA 70 for gas cylinder\\n                   storage area and other hazardous areas.\\n\\n\\n\
      \         29.15   The current for Electric arc welding shall not exceed 300 A on a hand welding\\n       \
      \             operation.\\n\\n\\n          30.0    Dangerous and harmful environment\\n\\n\\n            \
      \    As per BOCWR Rule 40,\\n\\n                                 i)   When internal combustion engines are\
      \ to be used into a confined space or\\n                         excavation or tunnel or any other workplace\
      \ where neither natural or artificial\\n                             ventilation system  is inadequate  to\
      \ keep carbon monoxide below 50ppm,\\n                       exposure of building workers shall be avoided\
      \ unless suitable measures are\\n                        taken and provided by the contractor.\\n\\n\\n  \

      \ or\\n                         excavation wherein there  is given  off any dust, fumes  / vapours or other\\\
      n                            impurities which is likely to be injurious or offensive, explosive or poisonous\
      \ or\\n                        noxious or gaseous material or other harmful articles unless steps are carried\\\
      n                          out by the contractor and certified by the responsible person to be safe.\\n\\\

      \      ],\n      \"block_number\": 3,\n      \"text\": \" \\n29.3 \\nAll gas cylinders shall be fixed with\
      \ pressure regulator and dial gauges  \\n \\n29.4 \\nNon-return valve and Flashback arrester shall be fixed\
      \ at both end of cylinder and \\ntorch. \\n \\n29.5  \\nDomestic LPG cylinders shall not be used for Gas welding\
      \ and Cutting purpose. \\n \\n29.6 \\nDCP or CO2 type Fire Extinguisher not less than 5 kg shall be fixed\
      \ at or near to \\nwelding process zone in an easily accessible location. Fire Extinguisher should \\nconfirm\
      \ to IS 2190: 1992. \\n \\n29.7 \\nUse firewatchers if there is a possibility of ignition unobserved by the\
      \ operator (e.g. on \\nthe other side of bulkheads). \\n \\n29.8 \\nOxygen cylinders and flammable gas cylinders\
      \ shall be stored separately, at least 6.6 \\nmeters (20 feet) apart or separated by a fire proof, 1.5 meters\
      \ (5 feet) high partition. \\nFlammable substances shall not be stored within 15 meters of cylinder storage\
      \ areas. \\n \\n29.9 \\nTransformer used for electrical arc welding shall be fixed with Ammeter and Voltmeter\
      \ \\nand also fixed with separate main power switch. \\n \\n29.10 \\nWelding grounds and returns should be\
      \ securely attached to the work by cable lugs, \\nby clamps in the case of stranded conductors, or by bolts\
      \ for strip conductors. The \\nground cable will not be attached to equipment or existing installations or\
      \ apparatus. \\n \\n29.11 \\nUse a low voltage open circuit relay device if welding with alternating current\
      \ in \\nconstricted or damp places. \\n29.12 \\nTake precautions against the risk of increased fume hazards\
      \ when welding with \\nchrome containing fluxed consumables or high current metal inert gas (MIG) or \\ntungsten\
      \ inert gas (TIG) processes. \\n29.13 \\nAvoid being in contact with water or wet floors when welding. Use\
      \ duckboards or \\nrubber protection. \\n \\n29.14 \\nAll electrical installations shall meet the IS: 5571:\
      \ 1997 and NFPA 70 for gas cylinder \\nstorage area and other hazardous areas. \\n \\n29.15 \\nThe current\
      \ for Electric arc welding shall not exceed 300 A on a hand welding \\noperation. \\n \\n30.0 \\nDangerous\
      \ and harmful environment \\n \\n\"\n    },\n    {\n      \"bbox\": [\n        85.56157684326172,\n      \
      \  602.099365234375,\n        515.888427734375,\n        790.3717651367188\n      ],\n      \"block_number\"\
      : 4,\n      \"text\": \"As per BOCWR Rule 40, \\ni) \\nWhen internal combustion engines are to be used into\
      \ a confined space or \\nexcavation or tunnel or any other workplace where neither natural or artificial \\\
      nventilation system is inadequate to keep carbon monoxide below 50ppm, \\nexposure of building workers shall\
      \ be avoided unless suitable measures are \\ntaken and provided by the contractor. \\n \\nii) \\nNo worker\
      \ shall be allowed into any confined space or tank or trench or \\nexcavation wherein there is given off any\
      \ dust, fumes / vapours or other \\nimpurities which is likely to be injurious or offensive, explosive or\

      \ the contractor and certified by the responsible person to be safe. \\n \\n \\n \\n\"\n    },\n    {\n  \

      \ strain to his workers.\\n\\n           x)    Stock should be clamped or otherwise secured firmly to prevent\
      \ it from moving.\\n\\n             xi)   Workers shall never stand on the top of the ladder to  drill holes\

      \ Number of the local fire brigade should be\\n          prominently displayed near each telephone on site.\\\

  text: Plugs, socket-outlets, and couplers at construction sites must be splash-proof with a minimum degree of
    Ingress Protection of IP44 under BS EN 60529, and weatherproof fittings must be colour-coded for 110V (Yellow),
    240V (Blue), and 415V (Red).

      \          itself.\\n\\n\\n          26.12.2   All non-current carrying metal parts of electrical equipment\

      \ kg shall be fixed at or near to\\n                   welding process zone  in an easily accessible  location.\
      \ Fire Extinguisher should\\n                    confirm to IS 2190: 1992.\\n\\n\\n          29.7    Use firewatchers\
      \ if there is a possibility of ignition unobserved by the operator (e.g. on\\n                    the other\

      \ (5 feet) high partition.\\n                 Flammable substances shall not be stored within 15 meters of\
      \ cylinder storage areas.\\n\\n\\n          29.9     Transformer used for electrical arc welding shall be\
      \ fixed with Ammeter and Voltmeter\\n                and also fixed with separate main power switch.\\n\\\
      n\\n         29.10    Welding grounds and returns should be securely attached to the work by cable lugs,\\\
      n                 by clamps in the case of stranded conductors, or by bolts for strip conductors. The\\n \
      \                 ground cable will not be attached to equipment or existing installations or apparatus.\\\
      n\\n\\n         29.11   Use a low voltage open circuit relay device  if welding with alternating current in\\\
      n                     constricted or damp places.\\n\\n         29.12    Take precautions against the risk\
      \ of increased fume hazards when welding with\\n                chrome containing fluxed consumables or high\
      \ current metal  inert gas (MIG) or\\n                   tungsten inert gas (TIG) processes.\\n\\n       \
      \  29.13    Avoid being in contact with water or wet floors when welding. Use duckboards or\\n           \
      \        rubber protection.\\n\\n\\n         29.14     All electrical installations shall meet the IS: 5571:\
      \ 1997 and NFPA 70 for gas cylinder\\n                   storage area and other hazardous areas.\\n\\n\\n\
      \         29.15   The current for Electric arc welding shall not exceed 300 A on a hand welding\\n       \
      \             operation.\\n\\n\\n          30.0    Dangerous and harmful environment\\n\\n\\n            \
      \    As per BOCWR Rule 40,\\n\\n                                 i)   When internal combustion engines are\
      \ to be used into a confined space or\\n                         excavation or tunnel or any other workplace\
      \ where neither natural or artificial\\n                             ventilation system  is inadequate  to\

      \ or\\n                         excavation wherein there  is given  off any dust, fumes  / vapours or other\\\
      n                            impurities which is likely to be injurious or offensive, explosive or poisonous\
      \ or\\n                        noxious or gaseous material or other harmful articles unless steps are carried\\\
      n                          out by the contractor and certified by the responsible person to be safe.\\n\\\
      n\\n\\n\\n\\n         Bangalore Metro Rail Corporation Ltd.              September 2026     Section Page 49\
      \ of 114\",\n  \"text_blocks\": [\n    {\n      \"bbox\": [\n        50.15998077392578,\n        15.768376350402832,\n\

      \  85.5599594116211,\n        809.042724609375,\n        511.7470703125,\n        830.5714111328125\n    \
      \  ],\n      \"block_number\": 2,\n      \"text\": \"Bangalore Metro Rail Corporation Ltd.               \

      \        85.55961608886719,\n        38.09945297241211,\n        515.8887939453125,\n        596.9318237304688\n\
      \      ],\n      \"block_number\": 3,\n      \"text\": \" \\n29.3 \\nAll gas cylinders shall be fixed with\
      \ pressure regulator and dial gauges  \\n \\n29.4 \\nNon-return valve and Flashback arrester shall be fixed\
      \ at both end of cylinder and \\ntorch. \\n \\n29.5  \\nDomestic LPG cylinders shall not be used for Gas welding\
      \ and Cutting purpose. \\n \\n29.6 \\nDCP or CO2 type Fire Extinguisher not less than 5 kg shall be fixed\
      \ at or near to \\nwelding process zone in an easily accessible location. Fire Extinguisher should \\nconfirm\
      \ to IS 2190: 1992. \\n \\n29.7 \\nUse firewatchers if there is a possibility of ignition unobserved by the\
      \ operator (e.g. on \\nthe other side of bulkheads). \\n \\n29.8 \\nOxygen cylinders and flammable gas cylinders\
      \ shall be stored separately, at least 6.6 \\nmeters (20 feet) apart or separated by a fire proof, 1.5 meters\
      \ (5 feet) high partition. \\nFlammable substances shall not be stored within 15 meters of cylinder storage\
      \ areas. \\n \\n29.9 \\nTransformer used for electrical arc welding shall be fixed with Ammeter and Voltmeter\
      \ \\nand also fixed with separate main power switch. \\n \\n29.10 \\nWelding grounds and returns should be\
      \ securely attached to the work by cable lugs, \\nby clamps in the case of stranded conductors, or by bolts\
      \ for strip conductors. The \\nground cable will not be attached to equipment or existing installations or\
      \ apparatus. \\n \\n29.11 \\nUse a low voltage open circuit relay device if welding with alternating current\
      \ in \\nconstricted or damp places. \\n29.12 \\nTake precautions against the risk of increased fume hazards\
      \ when welding with \\nchrome containing fluxed consumables or high current metal inert gas (MIG) or \\ntungsten\
      \ inert gas (TIG) processes. \\n29.13 \\nAvoid being in contact with water or wet floors when welding. Use\
      \ duckboards or \\nrubber protection. \\n \\n29.14 \\nAll electrical installations shall meet the IS: 5571:\
      \ 1997 and NFPA 70 for gas cylinder \\nstorage area and other hazardous areas. \\n \\n29.15 \\nThe current\
      \ for Electric arc welding shall not exceed 300 A on a hand welding \\noperation. \\n \\n30.0 \\nDangerous\
      \ and harmful environment \\n \\n\"\n    },\n    {\n      \"bbox\": [\n        85.56157684326172,\n      \
      \  602.099365234375,\n        515.888427734375,\n        790.3717651367188\n      ],\n      \"block_number\"\
      : 4,\n      \"text\": \"As per BOCWR Rule 40, \\ni) \\nWhen internal combustion engines are to be used into\
      \ a confined space or \\nexcavation or tunnel or any other workplace where neither natural or artificial \\\
      nventilation system is inadequate to keep carbon monoxide below 50ppm, \\nexposure of building workers shall\
      \ be avoided unless suitable measures are \\ntaken and provided by the contractor. \\n \\nii) \\nNo worker\
      \ shall be allowed into any confined space or tank or trench or \\nexcavation wherein there is given off any\
      \ dust, fumes / vapours or other \\nimpurities which is likely to be injurious or offensive, explosive or\
      \ poisonous or \\nnoxious or gaseous material or other harmful articles unless steps are carried \\nout by\
      \ the contractor and certified by the responsible person to be safe. \\n \\n \\n \\n\"\n    },\n    {\n  \

      pending_manual_review\",\n  \"rotation\": 0,\n  \"text\": \"Safety Health & Environment (SHE) Manual\\n  \
      \                                                        242\\n\\n36.7     Regulatory signs\\n\\n\\n36.7.1\
      \    Regulatory signs impose legal restriction on all traffic.  It is essential, therefore, that\\n      \
      \   they are used only after consulting the local police and traffic authorities.\\n\\n\\n36.8     Warning\
      \ signs\\n\\n\\n36.8.1   Warning signs in the traffic control zone shall be utilised to warn the drivers of\
      \ specific\\n         hazards that may be encountered.\\n\\n\\n36.8.2   The contractor shall place detour\
      \ signage at strategic locations and install appropriate\\n         warning signs.  In order to minimize disruption\
      \ of access to residences and business,\\n          the contractor shall maintain at least one entrance to\
      \ a property where multiple\\n         entrances exist.\\n\\n\\n36.8.3   A warning sign as given in general\
      \ instruction BMRC/SHE/CEO/012 shall be installed\\n        an at all secondary road which merges with the\
      \ primary road where the construction\\n         work is in progress at sufficient distance before it merges\
      \ with the primary road so as\\n           to alert the road users regarding the ‘Metro Work in Progress’.\\\
      n\\n\\n36.8.4    Materials hanging over / protruded from the chassis / body of any vehicle especially\\n \
      \         during material handling shall be indicated by red indicator (red light/flag) to indicate\\n   \
      \       the caution to the road users.\\n\\n\\n36.9      Delineators\\n\\n        The delineators are the\
      \ elements of a total system of traffic control and have two\\n            distinct purposes:\\n\\n      \
      \          i)    To delineate and guide the driver to and along a safe path\\n\\n                  ii)   As\
      \ a taper to move traffic from one lane to another.\\n\\n\\n36.9.1   These channelizing devices such as cones,\
      \ traffic cylinders, tapes and drums shall be\\n         placed in or adjacent to the roadway to control the\
      \ flow of  traffic. These should\\n          normally be retro-reflectors complying to IRC: 79 - Recommended\
      \ Practice for Road\\n          Delineators.\\n\\n\\n36.9.2    Traffic cones and cylinders\\n\\n\\n36.9.2.1\
      \  Traffic cones of 500mm, 750mm and 1000mm high and 300mm to 500mm in diameter\\n          or in square shape\
      \ at base and are often made of plastic or rubber and normally have\\n           retro-reflectorised red and\
      \ white band shall be used wherever required.\\n\\n36.9.3   Drums\\n\\n36.9.3.1  Drums about 800mm to 1000mm\
      \ high and 300mm in diameter can be used either as\\n          channelising or warning devices. These are\
      \ highly visible, give the appearance of\\n         being formidable objects and therefore command the respect\
      \ of drivers.\\n\\n\\n36.9.4    Barricades\\n\\n\\n36.9.4.1  Full height fence, barriers, barricades etc.\
      \ shall be erected around the site in order to\\n         prevent the working area from  the  risk  of  accidents\
      \ due  to speedy  vehicular\\n        movement. Same the way barricades protect the road users from the danger\
      \ due to\\n          construction equipment and other temporary structures.\\n\\n\\n36.9.4.2  The structure\
      \ dimension of the barricade, material and composition, its colour scheme,\\n      BMRC logo and other details\
      \ shall be in accordance with specifications laid down in\\n          tender document.\\n\\n\\n\\n\\nBangalore\
      \ Metro Rail Corporation Ltd.              September 2026     Section Page 54 of 114\",\n  \"text_blocks\"\
      : [\n    {\n      \"bbox\": [\n        47.039981842041016,\n        15.768376350402832,\n        561.0993041992188,\n\

      \ of the barricade, material and composition, its colour scheme, \\nBMRC logo and other details shall be in\

      pending_manual_review\",\n  \"rotation\": 0,\n  \"text\": \"Safety Health & Environment (SHE) Manual\\n  \
      \                                                        240\\n                i)    every compressed air\
      \ system in a tunnel is provided with emergency power\\n               supply for maintained continued supply\
      \ of compressed air as per Rule 155 of\\n         BOCWR\\n\\n                  ii)    watertight bulkhead\
      \ doors are installed at the entrance of a tunnel to prevent\\n                 flooding.\\n\\n          \
      \        iii)    reliable and effective means of communication such as telephone or walkie-\\n           \
      \        talkie are provided and maintained for arranging better effective communication\\n              \
      \   at an excavation or tunnelling work as per Rule 136 of BOCWR.\\n\\n             iv)     all portable electrical\
      \ hand tools and inspection lamp used in under ground and\\n               confined space at an excavation\
      \ or tunnelling work is operated at a voltage not\\n              exceeding 24V.\\n\\n           v)    only\
      \ flame proof equipment of appropriate type as per IS:5571:2000 and or\\n                other relevant national\
      \ standard is used inside the tunnel\\n\\n             vi)    petrol or LPG of any other flammable substances\
      \ are not used, stored inside the\\n                tunnel except with prior approval from Employer, and also\
      \ no oxy-acetylene gas\\n                    is used in a compressed air environment in excavation or tunnelling\\\
      n\\n              vii)   adequate number of water outlets provided for fire fighting purpose, an audible\\\
      n                     fire alarm and adequate number and types of fire extinguishers are provided\\n     \
      \        and maintained.\\n\\n               viii)  temperature in any working chamber in an excavation or\
      \ tunnelling work where\\n              workers employed does not exceed 29C as per Rule 165 of BOCWR.\\\
      n\\n             ix)     all working areas in a free air tunnel are provided with ventilation system as\\\
      n              approved by the Director General and the fresh air supplied in such tunnel is not\\n      \
      \          less than 6 m3/ min for each worker employed in tunnel as per Rule 153 of\\n          BOCWR.\\\
      n\\n\\n34.3     Warning signs and notices:\\n\\n\\n34.3.1   The contractor shall ensure that\\n\\n       \
      \         i)     suitable warning signs or notices, required for the safety of building workers\\n       \
      \         carrying out the work of an excavation or tunnelling, shall be displayed or\\n               erected\
      \ at conspicuous  places in Hindi and in a language understood by\\n                majority of such building\
      \ workers at such building such excavation or tunnelling\\n              work\\n\\n                  ii) \
      \   such warning signs and notices with regard to compressed air working shall\\n                include\\\
      n\\n                a)    the danger involved in such compressed air work\\n\\n                b)     fire\
      \ and explosion hazard\\n\\n                 c)    the emergency procedures for rescue from such danger or\
      \ hazards.\\n\\n\\n35.0    Work Permit system\\n\\n\\n35.1    The Contractor shall develop a Work Permit system,\
      \ which is a formal written system\\n        used to control certain types of work that are potentially hazardous.\
      \ A work permit is a\\n         document, which specifies the work to be done, and the precautions to be taken.\
      \ Work\\n         Permits form an essential part of safe systems of work for many construction activities.\\\
      n        They allow work to start only after safe procedures have been defined and they\\n          provide\
      \ a clear record that all foreseeable hazards have been considered. Permits to\\n        Work are usually\
      \ required in high-risk areas as identified by the Risk Assessments.\\n\\n\\n35.2    A permit  is needed when\
      \ construction work can only be carried out   if normal\\n         safeguards are dropped or when new hazards\
      \ are introduced by the work. Examples\\n           of high-risk activities include but are not limited to:\\\
      n\\n\\n                 i)     Entry into confined spaces\\n                  ii)   Work in close proximity\
      \ to overhead power lines and telecommunication cables.\\n                  iii)   Hot work.\\n          \
      \   iv)   To dig—where underground services may be located.\\n           v)   Work with heavy moving machinery.\\\
      n\\n\\nBangalore Metro Rail Corporation Ltd.              September 2026     Section Page 52 of 114\",\n \

      \      ],\n      \"block_number\": 3,\n      \"text\": \"i) \\nevery compressed air system in a tunnel is\
      \ provided with emergency power \\nsupply for maintained continued supply of compressed air as per Rule 155\
      \ of \\nBOCWR \\nii) \\nwatertight bulkhead doors are installed at the entrance of a tunnel to prevent \\\
      nflooding. \\niii) \\nreliable and effective means of communication such as telephone or walkie-\\ntalkie\
      \ are provided and maintained for arranging better effective communication \\nat an excavation or tunnelling\

      \ 24V. \\nv) \\nonly flame proof equipment of appropriate type as per IS:5571:2000 and or \\nother relevant\
      \ national standard is used inside the tunnel \\nvi) \\npetrol or LPG of any other flammable substances are\
      \ not used, stored inside the \\ntunnel except with prior approval from Employer, and also no oxy-acetylene\
      \ gas \\nis used in a compressed air environment in excavation or tunnelling \\nvii) \\nadequate number of\
      \ water outlets provided for fire fighting purpose, an audible \\nfire alarm and adequate number and types\
      \ of fire extinguishers are provided \\nand maintained. \\nviii) \\ntemperature in any working chamber in\
      \ an excavation or tunnelling work where \\nworkers employed does not exceed 29C as per Rule 165 of BOCWR.\
      \ \\nix) \\nall working areas in a free air tunnel are provided with ventilation system as \\napproved by\
      \ the Director General and the fresh air supplied in such tunnel is not \\nless than 6 m3/ min for each worker\
      \ employed in tunnel as per Rule 153 of \\nBOCWR. \\n \\n34.3 \\nWarning signs and notices: \\n \\n34.3.1\
      \ \\nThe contractor shall ensure that  \\ni) \\nsuitable warning signs or notices, required for the safety\

      \ \\nfire and explosion hazard \\nc) \\nthe emergency procedures for rescue from such danger or hazards. \\\
      n \\n35.0 \\nWork Permit system \\n \\n35.1 \\nThe Contractor shall develop a Work Permit system, which is\
      \ a formal written system \\nused to control certain types of work that are potentially hazardous. A work\
      \ permit is a \\ndocument, which specifies the work to be done, and the precautions to be taken. Work \\nPermits\
      \ form an essential part of safe systems of work for many construction activities. \\nThey allow work to start\
      \ only after safe procedures have been defined and they \\nprovide a clear record that all foreseeable hazards\
      \ have been considered. Permits to \\nWork are usually required in high-risk areas as identified by the Risk\
      \ Assessments. \\n \\n35.2  \\nA permit is needed when construction work can only be carried out if normal\

      \ services may be located. \\nv) \\nWork with heavy moving machinery. \\n\"\n    },\n    {\n      \"bbox\"\

      n                  ii)    Foot Protection (Safety footwear, Gumboot, etc)\\n                  iii)   Body\

      n         standard as prescribed by Bureau of Indian Standards  (BIS).  If materials\\n        conforming\

      pending_manual_review\",\n  \"rotation\": 0,\n  \"text\": \"Safety Health & Environment (SHE) Manual\\n241\\\
      n                          vi)   Working on electrical equipment\\n                             vii)  Work\
      \ with radioactive isotopes.\\n                               viii)  Heavy lifting operations and lifting\
      \ operations closer to live power line\\n\\n\\n          35.3    The permit-to-work system should be fully\
      \ documented, laying down:\\n\\n\\n                                 i)   How the system works;\\n        \
      \                            ii)   The jobs it is to be used for;\\n                                     iii)\
      \   The responsibilities and training of those involved; and\\n                          iv)  How to check\
      \ its operation;\\n\\n\\n          35.4    A Work Permit authorisation form shall be completed with the maximum\
      \ duration\\n                    period not exceeding 12 hours.\\n\\n\\n          35.5    A copy of each Permit\
      \ To Work shall be displayed, during its validity, in a conspicuous\\n                     location in close\
      \ proximity to the actual works location to which it applies.\\n\\n\\n          36.0      Traffic Management\\\
      n\\n\\n          36.1    The basic objective of the following guidelines  is to lay down procedures to be\\\
      n                  adopted by contractor to ensure the safe and efficient movement of traffic and also to\\\
      n                  ensure the safety of workmen at construction sites.\\n\\n\\n          36.2       All construction\
      \ workers should be provided with high visibility jackets with reflective\\n                   tapes as most\
      \ of viaduct /tunnelling/station and depot works or either above or under\\n                      right-of-way.\
      \ The conspicuity of workmen at  all times shall be increased so as to\\n                     protect from\
      \ speeding vehicular traffic.\\n\\n\\n          36.3    The guiding principles to be adopted for safety in\
      \ construction zone are to\\n\\n\\n                                 i)    Warn the road user clearly and sufficiently\
      \ in advance.\\n\\n                                    ii)    Provide safe and clearly marked lanes for guiding\
      \ road users.\\n\\n                                     iii)    Provide safe and clearly marked buffer and\
      \ work zones\\n\\n                          iv)   Provide adequate measures that control driver behaviour\
      \ through construction\\n                        zones.\\n\\n\\n          36.4     Legal permission\\n\\n\\\
      n          36.4.1    In  all cases, the contractor shall employ proper precautions. Wherever operations\\\
      n                  undertaken are likely to interfere with public traffic, specific traffic management plans\\\
      n                      shall be drawn up and implemented by the contractor in consultation with the approval\\\
      n                      of local police authorities and/or the concerned metropolitan/civil authorities as\
      \ the\\n                 case may be.\\n\\n\\n          36.4.2   Such  traffic management plans  shall  include\
      \  provision  for  traffic  diversion and\\n                     selection of alternative routes for transport\
      \ of equipment.  If necessary, the contractor\\n                      shall carry out road widening before\
      \ commencement of works to accommodate the\\n                    extra load\\n\\n\\n          36.5    The\
      \ primary traffic control devices used in work zones shall include signs, delineators,\\n                \
      \    barricades, cones, pylons, pavement markings and flashing lights.\\n\\n\\n          36.6    The road\
      \ construction and maintenance signs which fall into the same three major\\n                    categories\
      \ as do other traffic signs, that are Regulatory Signs, Warning Signs and\\n                     Direction\
      \ (or guidelines) Signs shall only be used. The IRC: 67 (Code of Practice for\\n               Road Signs)\
      \ provide a list of traffic signs. The size, colours and placement of sign\\n                      shall confirm\
      \ to IRC: 67.\\n\\n\\n\\n         Bangalore Metro Rail Corporation Ltd.              September 2026     Section\

      pending_manual_review\",\n  \"rotation\": 0,\n  \"text\": \"Safety Health & Environment (SHE) Manual\\n243\\\
      n          36.9.4.3  All barricades shall be erected as per the design requirements of the Employer,\\n  \
      \               numbered, painted and maintained in good condition and also Barricade in-charge\\n       \
      \            maintains a barricade register in site.\\n\\n\\n          36.9.4.4  All barricades shall be conspicuously\
      \ seen in the dark/night time by the road\\n                 users so that no vehicle hits the barricade.\
      \ Conspicuity. shall be ensured by\\n                     affixing retro reflective stripes of required size\
      \ and shape at appropriate angle at\\n                  the bottom and middle portion of the barricade at\
      \ a minimum gap of 1000mm. In\\n                   addition minimum one red light or red light blinker should\
      \ be placed at the top\\n                   of each barricade.\\n\\n\\n          36.9.5   The contractor shall\
      \ ensure that all his construction vehicles plying on public roads\\n                         (like dump trucks,\
      \ trailers, etc.) have proper license to ply on public roads from the\\n                    State Transport\
      \ Authority. Drivers holding proper valid license as per the requirements\\n                      of Motor\
      \ Vehicles Act shall drive these vehicles\\n\\n\\n          36.9.6   The contractor shall not undertake loading\
      \ and unloading at carriageways obstructing\\n                    the free flow of vehicular traffic and encroachment\
      \ of existing roads by the contractor\\n                    applying the excuse of work execution.\\n\\n\\\
      n          36.9.7   Tow away vehicle\\n\\n\\n          36.9.7.1  The contractor shall make arrangements keeping\
      \ tow away van / manpower to\\n                tow away any breakdown vehicle in the traffic flow without\
      \ loosing any time at\\n                   his cost.\\n\\n          36.9.8   Cleaning of roads\\n\\n\\n  \
      \        36.9.8.1  The contractor shall ensure the cleanliness of roads and footpaths by deploying\\n    \
      \             proper manpower for the same. The contractor shall have to ensure proper\\n                \
      \ brooming, cleaning washing of roads and footpaths on all the time throughout\\n                  the entire\
      \ stretch till the currency of the contract including disposal of seepage.\\n\\n          37.0    Work to\
      \ adjacent railways\\n\\n          37.1     Whenever work is to be conducted in close proximity to the live\
      \ railways then the\\n                     following measures shall need to be addressed:\\n\\n          \
      \            (a)  The rules provided for in the Railway’s manual should be followed.\\n\\n               \
      \       (b)  No persons are allowed to encroach onto the railway unless the owner has\\n                 \
      \        given specific authority.\\n\\n                       (c)   Adequate protection in accordance with\
      \ the railway owner’s requirements shall\\n                     be followed. (Provision of Block Inspectors,\
      \ Flagmen and Lookouts)\\n\\n                      (d)    All persons shall wear high visibility clothing\
      \ at all times.\\n\\n                      (e)  Any induction training requirements of the railways shall\
      \ be strictly observed\\n\\n\\n          38.0     Batching Plant and Casting Yard layout\\n\\n\\n        \
      \                         i)    The batching plant / casting yard shall be effectively planned for smooth\
      \ flow of\\n                         unloading and stacking the aggregates reinforcements and cement, batching\\\
      n                             plant, transport of concrete, casting the segment, stacking the segment and\\\
      n                          loading the segments to the trucks. As far as possible the conflicts should be\\\
      n                         avoided.\\n\\n                                    ii)   The batching plant / casting\
      \ yard shall be barricaded and made as a compulsory\\n                  PPE zone\\n\\n                   \
      \                  iii)      If in case of material unloading area is not maintainable as PPE zone, the same\\\
      n                             shall be segregated properly and made as a non-PPE zone with appropriate\\n\
      \                            barrications.\\n\\n                          iv)    Electrical system  shall\
      \ also be suitably planned so that location  of diesel\\n                          generator,  if any, location\
      \ of DBs, routing of cables and positioning of area\\n                              lighting poles/masts does\
      \ not infringe on any other utility and pose danger.\\n\\n\\n\\n\\n\\n         Bangalore Metro Rail Corporation\

      36.9.4.3 All barricades shall be erected as per the design requirements of the Employer, \\nnumbered, painted\
      \ and maintained in good condition and also Barricade in-charge \\nmaintains a barricade register in site.\
      \  \\n \\n36.9.4.4 All barricades shall be conspicuously seen in the dark/night time by the road \\nusers\

      \ of required size and shape at appropriate angle at \\nthe bottom and middle portion of the barricade at\

      \ top \\nof each barricade. \\n \\n36.9.5  \\nThe contractor shall ensure that all his construction vehicles\
      \ plying on public roads \\n(like dump trucks, trailers, etc.) have proper license to ply on public roads\

      \ roads by the contractor \\napplying the excuse of work execution.   \\n \\n36.9.7 \\nTow away vehicle \\\
      n \\n36.9.7.1 The contractor shall make arrangements keeping tow away van / manpower to \\ntow away any breakdown\
      \ vehicle in the traffic flow without loosing any time at \\nhis cost. \\n36.9.8 \\nCleaning of roads \\n\
      \ \\n36.9.8.1 The contractor shall ensure the cleanliness of roads and footpaths by deploying \\nproper manpower\
      \ for the same. The contractor shall have to ensure proper \\nbrooming, cleaning washing of roads and footpaths\
      \ on all the time throughout \\nthe entire stretch till the currency of the contract including disposal of\
      \ seepage. \\n37.0 \\nWork to adjacent railways \\n37.1 \\nWhenever work is to be conducted in close proximity\
      \ to the live railways then the \\nfollowing measures shall need to be addressed: \\n(a) \\nThe rules provided\
      \ for in the Railway’s manual should be followed. \\n(b) \\nNo persons are allowed to encroach onto the railway\
      \ unless the owner has \\ngiven specific authority. \\n(c) \\nAdequate protection in accordance with the railway\
      \ owner’s requirements shall \\nbe followed. (Provision of Block Inspectors, Flagmen and Lookouts) \\n(d)\
      \ \\nAll persons shall wear high visibility clothing at all times. \\n(e) \\nAny induction training requirements\
      \ of the railways shall be strictly observed \\n \\n38.0 \\nBatching Plant and Casting Yard layout \\n \\\
      n\"\n    },\n    {\n      \"bbox\": [\n        130.55909729003906,\n        616.1395263671875,\n        515.8872680664062,\n\
      \        772.4920043945312\n      ],\n      \"block_number\": 4,\n      \"text\": \"i) \\nThe batching plant\
      \ / casting yard shall be effectively planned for smooth flow of \\nunloading and stacking the aggregates\
      \ reinforcements and cement, batching \\nplant, transport of concrete, casting the segment, stacking the segment\
      \ and \\nloading the segments to the trucks. As far as possible the conflicts should be \\navoided. \\nii)\
      \ \\nThe batching plant / casting yard shall be barricaded and made as a compulsory \\nPPE zone \\niii) \\\
      nIf in case of material unloading area is not maintainable as PPE zone, the same \\nshall be segregated properly\
      \ and made as a non-PPE zone with appropriate \\nbarrications. \\niv) \\nElectrical system shall also be suitably\
      \ planned so that location of diesel \\ngenerator, if any, location of DBs, routing of cables and positioning\
      \ of area \\nlighting poles/masts does not infringe on any other utility and pose danger. \\n\"\n    },\n\

      n                          iv)   examine the walls of all structures adjacent to the structure to be demolished\
      \ to\\n                        determine thickness, method of support to such adjacent structures\\n\\n  \
      \                    v)   no demolishing work be performed if the adjacent structure seems to be unsafe\\\
      n                         unless and until remedial measures life sheet piling, shoring, bracing or similar\\\
      n                    means be ensured for safety and stability for adjacent structure from collapsing.\\n\\\
      n                          vi)    debris / bricks and other materials or articles shall be removed by means\
      \ of\\n                           a)      chutes\\n                           b)     buckets or hoists\\n\
      \                            c)      through openings through floors or\\n                           d)  \
      \   any other safe means\\n\\n                             vii)   no person other than  building workers \
      \ or other persons  essential  to the\\n                         operation of demolition work shall be permitted\
      \ to enter a zone of demolition and\\n                          the area be provided with substantial barricades.\\\
      n\\n\\n          34.0     Excavation and Tunnelling:\\n\\n\\n          34.1     Excavation\\n\\n\\n      \
      \    34.1.1   The contractor shall ensure\\n\\n\\n                                 i)    where any construction\
      \ building worker engaged in excavation is exposed to\\n                       hazard of falling or sliding\
      \ material or article from any bank or side of such\\n                         excavation which is more than\
      \ one 1.5 m above his footing, such worker is\\n                          protected by adequate piling and\
      \ bracing against such bank or side.\\n\\n\\n                                    ii)    where banks of an\
      \ excavation are undercut, adequate shoring is provided to\\n                         support the material\
      \ or article overhanging such bank.\\n\\n\\n                                     iii)   excavated material\
      \ is not stored at least 0.65 m from the edge of an open\\n                         excavation or trench and\
      \ banks of such excavation or trench are stripped of\\n                         loose rocks and the banks\
      \ of such excavation or trench are stripped of loose\\n                         rocks and other materials\
      \ which may slide,  roll or  fall upon a construction\\n                           building worker working\
      \ below such bank\\n\\n\\n                          iv)   metal ladders and staircases or ramps are provided,\
      \ as the case may be, for\\n                         safe access to and egress from excavation where, the\
      \ depth of such excavation\\n                      exceeds 1.5 m and such ladders, staircases or ramps comply\
      \ with the IS 3696\\n                          Part 1&2 and other relevant national standards.\\n\\n\\n  \
      \                    v)    trench and excavation  is protected against  falling of a person by suitable\\\
      n                     measures  if the depth of such trench or excavation exceeds 1.5 m and such\\n      \
      \                     protection is an improved protection in accordance with the design and drawing\\n  \
      \                          of a professional engineer, where such depth exceeds 4m.\\n\\n\\n          34.2\
      \      Tunnelling\\n\\n\\n          34.2.1   The contractor shall inform in writing to the Director General\
      \ within 30 days, prior to\\n                    the commencement of any tunnelling work.\\n\\n\\n       \
      \   34.2.2   The contractor shall appoint a responsible person for safe operation for tunnelling\\n      \
      \           work as per Rule 121 & 125 of BOCWR.\\n\\n\\n          34.2.3   The contractor shall ensure\\\

    personnel with substantial barricades.

- kind: parameter
  text: Excavation safety mandates piling and bracing for banks exceeding 1.5 meters, shoring for undercut banks,
    storing excavated material at least 0.65 meters from trench edges, and providing metal ladders, staircases,
    or ramps compliant with IS 3696.

- kind: parameter
  text: Tunnelling safety requirements include written notification to the Director General 30 days prior to commencement,
    appointment of a responsible person under BOCWR Rules 121 and 125, emergency power supply for compressed air
    systems, watertight bulkhead doors, and maximum working chamber temperatures of 29 degrees Celsius.
