### Jebd4d2e3f8dc5d1d

[[OKF_bundle/Technical/Vol3/vol3_part2#Clause 18.0 — Working at Height|Clause 18.0 — Working at Height]]

> {
>   "pdf_page": 35,
>   "text": "18.10.3  The contractor shall ensure that no material or object is thrown or tipped from\n                    height in circumstances where it is liable to cause injury to any person.\n\n\n          18.10.4  Every employer shall ensure that materials and objects are stored in such a way\n                 as  to prevent  risk  to any person  arising from the  collapse, overturning or\n                  unintended movement of such materials or objects.\n\n\n         18.11    Danger areas\n\n\n          18.11.1  Without prejudice to the preceding requirements of these Regulations, every\n                     contractor shall ensure that\n\n                     a)   where a workplace contains an area in which, owing to the nature of the\n                         work, there is a risk of any person at work\n\n                                           i)      falling a distance; or\n\n                                              ii)    being struck by a falling object,\n\n                       which  is liable to cause personal  injury, the workplace  is so far as  is\n                        reasonably  practicable equipped  with devices  preventing unauthorised\n                       persons from entering such area; and\n\n                     b)   such area is clearly indicated.\n\n\n         18.12    Inspection of work equipment\n\n\n          18.12.1  The contractor shall ensure that, where the safety of work equipment depends on\n               how it is installed or assembled, it is not used after installation or assembly in any\n                     position unless it has been inspected in that position.\n\n\n          18.12.2  The contractor shall ensure that work equipment exposed to conditions causing\n                     deterioration which is liable to result in dangerous situations is inspected\n\n                     a)    at suitable intervals; and\n\n                     b)   each time that exceptional circumstances which are liable to jeopardise the\n                          safety of the work equipment have occurred,\n\n                      to ensure  that  health and  safety  conditions  are maintained and  that any\n                     deterioration can be detected and remedied in good time.\n\n\n          18.12.3  Without prejudice to paragraph 18.12.1, the contractor shall ensure that a working\n                    platform\n\n                     a)   used for construction work; and\n\n                     b)    from which a person could fall 2 metres or more,\n\n                         is not used in any position unless it has been inspected in that position or, in the\n                 case of a mobile working platform, inspected on the site, within the previous 7\n                   days.\n\n\n          18.12.4  The contractor  shall ensure  that the reports  of  all inspections are properly\n                   maintained and shown to the Employer as and when required.\n\n\n          18.12.5   In this clause \"inspection\",\n\n                     a)   means such visual or more rigorous inspection by a competent person as is\n                          appropriate for safety purposes;\n\n                     b)    includes any testing appropriate for those purposes,\n\n\n         18.13    Inspection of places of work at height\n\n\n          18.13.1  The contractor shall so far as is reasonably practicable ensure that the surface\n                and every parapet, permanent rail or other such fall protection measure of every\n                   place of work at height are checked on each occasion before the place is used."
> }

### Jd60de5aba5750378

[[OKF_bundle/Technical/Vol3/vol3_part2#Clause 18.0 — Working at Height|Clause 18.0 — Working at Height]]

> {
>   "pdf_page": 36,
>   "text": "18.14    Duties of persons at work\n\n\n18.14.1  Any workmen employed by the contractor shall report to the supervisor about any\n          defect relating to work at height which he knows is likely to endanger the safety of\n          himself or another person.\n\n\n18.14.2  Every workmen shall use any work equipment or safety device provided to him for\n         work at height by the contractor, in accordance with\n\n\n          a)   any training in the use of the work equipment or device concerned which\n             have been received by him; and\n\n          b)    the instructions respecting that use which have been provided to him by the\n                contractor as per the requirements of the Employer\n\n\n18.15    Requirements for existing places of work and means of access or egress at height\n         Every existing place of work or means of access or egress at height shall\n\n\n          a)   be stable and of sufficient strength and rigidity for the purpose for which it is\n               intended to be or is being used;\n\n          b)   where applicable, rest on a stable, sufficiently strong surface;\n\n           c)   be of sufficient dimensions to permit the safe passage of persons and the\n               safe use of any plant or materials required to be used and to provide a safe\n               working area having regard to the work to be carried out there;\n\n          d)   possess suitable and sufficient means for preventing a fall;\n\n          e)   possess a surface which has no gap\n\n                          i)    through which a person could fall;\n\n                            ii)    through which any material or object could fall and injure a person; or\n\n                             iii)    giving rise to other risk of injury to any person, unless measures have\n                  been taken to protect persons against such risk;\n\n               f)    be so constructed and used, and maintained  in such condition, as to\n                prevent, so far as is reasonably practicable -\n\n                          i)     the risk of slipping or tripping; or\n\n                            ii)    any person being caught between it and any adjacent structure;\n\n          g)   where   it has moving parts, be prevented by appropriate devices from\n             moving inadvertently during work at height.\n\n\n18.16    Requirements for guardrails, toe-boards, barriers and similar collective means of\n          protection\n\n\n                i)    Unless the context otherwise requires, any reference in this section to\n            means of protection is to a guardrail, toe-board, barrier or similar collective\n            means of protection.\n\n                  ii)   Means of protection shall\n\n                a)   be of sufficient dimensions, of sufficient strength and rigidity for the\n                   purposes for which they are being used, and otherwise suitable;\n\n                b)   be so placed, secured and used as to ensure, so far as is reasonably\n                       practicable, that they do not become accidentally displaced; and\n\n                 c)   be so placed as to prevent, so far as is practicable, the fall of any\n                     person, or of any material or object, from any place of work.\n\n                  iii)    In relation to work at height involved in construction work\n\n                a)    the top guard-rail or other similar means of protection shall be at least\n                  950 millimetres above the edge from which any person is liable to fall;\n\n                b)    toe-boards shall be suitable and sufficient to prevent the fall of any\n                     person, or any material or object, from any place of work; and"
> }

### J459842af1f243bdb

[[OKF_bundle/Technical/Vol3/vol3_part2#Clause 18.0 — Working at Height|Clause 18.0 — Working at Height]]

> {
>   "pdf_page": 37,
>   "text": "c)   any intermediate guardrail or similar means of protection shall be\n                                positioned so that any gap between  it and other means of protection\n                           does not exceed 470 millimetres.\n\n                          iv)   Any structure or part of a structure which supports means of protection or to\n                       which means of protection are attached shall be of sufficient strength and\n                           suitable for the purpose of such support or attachment.\n\n\n         18.17    Requirements for all Working Platforms\n\n\n                                 i)    Every working platforms requires a supporting structure for holding it\n\n                                    ii)   Any surface upon which any supporting structure rests shall be stable, of\n                              sufficient  strength and  of  suitable  composition  safely  to  support  the\n                         supporting structure, the working platform and any loading intended to be\n                        placed on the working platform.\n\n                                    iii).    Stability of supporting structure\n\n                    Any supporting structure shall\n\n                           a)   be suitable and of sufficient strength and rigidity for the purpose for\n                            which it is being used;\n\n                           b)     in the case of a wheeled structure, be prevented by appropriate\n                              devices from moving inadvertently during work at height;\n\n                            c)     in other cases, be prevented from slipping by secure attachment to\n                               the bearing surface or to another structure, provision of an effective\n                                      anti-slip device or by other means of equivalent effectiveness;\n\n                           d)   be stable while being erected, used and dismantled; and\n\n                           e)   when altered or modified, be so altered or modified as to ensure that it\n                             remains stable.\n\n                                      f)    Have suitable base plates and properly footed thereby.\n\n\n                            iv).    Stability of working platforms\n\n                  A working platform shall\n\n                           a)   be suitable and of sufficient strength and rigidity for the purpose or\n                            purposes for which it is intended to be used or is being used;\n\n                           b)   be so erected and used as to ensure that  its components do not\n                        become accidentally displaced so as to endanger any person;\n\n                            c)   when altered or modified, be so altered or modified as to ensure that it\n                             remains stable; and\n\n                           d)   be dismantled in such a way as to prevent accidental displacement.\n\n\n                      v)    Safety on working platforms\n\n                  A working platform shall\n\n                           a)   be of sufficient dimensions to permit the safe passage of persons and\n                               the safe use of any plant or materials required to be used and to\n                               provide a safe working area having regard to the work being carried\n                               out there;\n\n                           b)   possess a suitable surface and, in particular, be so constructed that\n                               the surface of the working platform has no gap\n\n                                                     i)      through which a person could fall;\n\n                                                         ii)      through which any material or object could fall and injure a\n                                      person; or\n\n                                                          iii)      giving  rise  to other  risk  of  injury  to any person, unless\n                                 measures have been taken to protect persons against such\n                                                 risk; and\n\n                            c)   be so erected and used, and maintained in such condition, as to\n                                prevent, so far as is reasonably practicable\n\n                                                     i)       the risk of slipping or tripping; or\n\n                                                         ii)     any person being caught between the working platform and\n                                  any adjacent structure."

### J3340c21e9aa1985b

[[OKF_bundle/Technical/Vol3/vol3_part2#Clause 18.0 — Working at Height|Clause 18.0 — Working at Height]]

> {
>   "pdf_page": 38,
>   "text": "vi)   Loading\n\n           A working platform and any supporting structure shall not be loaded so as to\n                give rise to a risk of collapse or to any deformation, which could affect its\n               safe use.\n\n\n              vii)   Additional requirements for scaffolding\n\n               Strength and stability calculations for scaffolding shall be carried out unless\n\n                a)   a note  of the  calculations, covering the  structural arrangements\n                     contemplated, is available; or\n\n                b)       it is assembled in conformity with a generally recognised standard\n                       configuration.\n\n\n               viii)  Depending on the complexity of the scaffolding selected, a competent\n              person shall draw up an assembly, use and dismantling plan. This may be\n                   in the form of a standard plan, supplemented by items relating to specific\n                  details of the scaffolding in question.\n\n\n             ix)  A copy of the plan, including any instructions  it may contain, shall be kept\n                available  for  the use  of  persons  concerned  in  the  assembly,  use,\n                dismantling or alteration of scaffolding until it has been dismantled.\n\n\n           x)   The dimensions form and layout of scaffolding decks shall be appropriate to\n                the nature of the work to be performed and suitable for the loads to be\n                 carried and permit work and passage in safety.\n\n\n             xi)   While a scaffold  is not available for use, including during  its assembly,\n                dismantling or alteration,  it shall be marked with general warning signs in\n              accordance with and be suitably delineated by physical means preventing\n              access to the danger zone.\n\n\n              xii)   Scaffolding may be assembled, dismantled or  significantly altered only\n              under the supervision of a competent person and by persons who have\n               received appropriate and specific training in the operations envisaged which\n              addresses specific risks which the operations may entail and precautions to\n             be taken, and more particularly in\n\n                a)    understanding of the plan for the assembly, dismantling or alteration\n                        of the scaffolding concerned;\n\n                b)    safety during the assembly, dismantling or alteration of the scaffolding\n                    concerned;\n\n                 c)   measures to prevent the risk of persons, materials or objects falling;\n\n                d)    safety measures in the event of changing weather conditions which\n                     could adversely affect the safety of the scaffolding concerned;\n\n                e)    permissible loadings;\n\n                       f)    any other risks which the assembly, dismantling or alteration of the\n                       scaffolding may entail.\n\n\n18.18    Requirements for collective safeguards for arresting falls\n\n\n                i)     Collective safeguard are a safety net, airbag or other collective safeguard\n                  for arresting falls\n\n\n                  ii)   A safeguard shall be used only if\n\n                a)   a risk assessment has demonstrated that the work activity can so far\n                   as is reasonably practicable be performed safely while using  it and\n                      without affecting its effectiveness;"

                     a)     in the case of a safeguard which  is designed to be attached, be\n                               securely attached to all the required anchors, and the anchors and the\n   b)   where necessary, fit the user;\n\n                            c)   be correctly fitted;\n\n                           d)   be designed to minimise injury to the user and, where necessary, be\n ### J5ff58b37257f71d1

[[OKF_bundle/Technical/Vol3/vol3_part2#Clause 19.0 — Overhead protection|Clause 19.0 — Overhead protection]]

> {
>   "clause_id": "19.0",
>   "fragments": [
>     {
>       "pdf_page": 40,
>       "text": "19.0    Overhead protection\n\n\n            All contractors shall provide overhead protections as per Rule 41 of BOCWR\n\n                i)    Overhead protection should be erected along the periphery of every building\n              which is under construction and the building height shall be 15m or above\n                  after construction.\n\n                  ii)    Overhead protection shall be minimum 2m wide and the outer edge shall be\n           150mm higher than the inner edge and an angle not more than 200 to its\n                 horizontal sloping into the building.\n\n                  iii)   Overhead protection shall not be erected more than a height of 5m from the\n             base of the building.\n\n             iv)   Areas of inadvertent hazard of  falling of material  shall be guarded or\n               barricaded or roped-off thereby by the contractor."
>     }
>   ],

### J885c7e78c6927b04

[[OKF_bundle/Technical/Vol3/vol3_part2#Clause 22.0 — Launching Operation|Clause 22.0 — Launching Operation]]

> {
>   "clause_id": "22.0",
>   "fragments": [
>     {
>       "pdf_page": 44,
>       "text": "22.0     Launching Operation\n\n22.1    As launching operation  is one of the  riskiest job, the contractor shall take utmost\n          precaution  at  all stages  like; planning, establishing casing yard, casting segments,\n          transporting segments,  fabrication and  erection  of launching  girders, launching  of\n         segments, pre-stressing, auto launching of girders and dismantling of launching girders.\n\n\n22.2    The contractor shall prepare a comprehensive Method Statement  for the launching\n          operation, adhering to the SHE conditions laid down in conditions of contract on SHE and\n          project SHE manual. Particular reference shall be made to the provisions on working at\n           height. As the entire process of launching has to be undertaken at an elevated level, the\n          safety of workers and the girder is paramount important. The following general guidelines\n           shall be adhered throughout the launching operation.\n\n\n                i)    Necessary ‘working platforms’ and fall protection anchorage arrangement shall be\n               provided in the launching girder itself.\n\n                  ii)    Provisions for mounting light fittings shall also be made available in the launching\n                  girder.\n\n                  iii)   The casting yard shall be established ensuring the provision given in clause 38.0\n\n             iv)   The workmen engaged in fabrication of reinforcement, concreting the segment\n                  shall be provided with necessary PPEs including compulsory hand protection\n                gloves.\n\n           v)    Casting and curing of segment shall be undertaken under the direct supervision of\n                the responsible engineer of the contractor.\n\n             vi)   Trucks  with  valid  registration,  licence, safe worthiness  certificate, Employer’s\n               approval certificate, and pollution under check certificate shall only be used for\n                transport of segments\n\n              vii)   Drivers engaged for driving these trucks, shall be trained once in 6 months at\n                specified locations as directed by the employer on defensive driving.\n\n               viii)   Drivers shall also have undergone proper medical examination as per relevant\n               clause mentioned under ‘Medical Facilities’.\n\n             ix)   The segments shall rigidly secured to the truck with necessary wooden wedges\n             and necessary red indicators/safety tapes provided so that the vehicle is clearly\n             seen by other road users both in day / night time.\n\n           x)    Every launching girder shall have a responsible engineer on duty all the time.\n\n             xi)    All the time from erection to dismantling the area between the two piers\n              wherein launching is in progress shall always be barricaded.\n\n              xii)   Unloading  of  segments  from  trucks,  lifting  of  segments,  shifting  of\n              segments, gluing shall be done under the direct supervision of the approved\n               engineer of the contractor.\n\n               xiii)  Auto launching shall be done only after approval from the Employer. After\n               every auto launching the stability of launching girder shall be ensured.\n\n            xiv)  The vertical deflection of launching girder shall be monitored at all critical\n               stages like with/without loads and after every auto launching.\n\n          xv)  A  register containing  all important operational  details from erection  to\n                dismantling of launching girders shall be maintained and made available to\n              Employer whenever called for.\n\n            xvi)  Test  certificate  for  all  lifting  gears  including  Macalloy  bars  shall be\n               maintained at a location closer to the launching girder itself so that it can be\n                referred during all inspections.\n\n             xvii)  Adequate lighting at all time shall be ensured in the entire area of operation."
>     },
>     {
>       "pdf_page": 45,
>       "text": "xviii) Access to drinking water & toilet shall be ensured to all workmen engaged\n                              for launching process.\n\n                       xix)  Proper access ladders/stairways shall be maintained for safe ascending  /\n                       descending of workmen / engineers.\n\n\n          22.3     Non-adherence to any of the clauses mentioned above shall be viewed\n                   seriously by the Employer and penalty levied as per relevant clause."
>     }
>   ],

### Jbff97c59f82a7339

[[OKF_bundle/Technical/Vol3/vol3_part2#Clause 21.0 — Lifting Appliances and Gear|Clause 21.0 — Lifting Appliances and Gear]]

> {
>   "pdf_page": 42,
>   "text": "21.6    The contractor shall also maintain a register containing a system of identification\n           of all tools and tackles, its date of purchase, safe working load, competent person\n         date of examination etc.\n\n\n21.7     Test and periodical examination of lifting appliances and gears\n\n\n21.7.1     All  lifting appliances including  all parts and gears  thereof, whether  fixed or\n        movable shall be thoroughly tested and examined by a competent person once at\n           least in every six months or after it has undergone any alterations or repairs liable\n           to affect its strength or stability. Within the validity,  if the lifting appliances are\n           shifted to a new site, re-examination by the same competent person for ensuring\n              its safety shall also be done.\n\n21.7.2    Contractors can  utilise the services of any competent person as defined  in\n          Factories Act, 1948 and approved by Chief Inspector  of Factories with the\n         permission of the Employer.\n\n\n21.7.3     All alarms and signals  like automatic safe load indicators (SLI), boom angle\n           indicators, boom extension indicators, over lift boom alarm, swing alarm, hydraulic\n          safety valves, mechanical radius indicators, load moment indicators etc. shall be\n           periodically examined and maintained always in working condition\n\n\n21.8     Automatic safe load indicators\n\n\n21.8.1   As stipulated in Rule 78 of BOCWKR 2006, no lifting appliances gear or any\n         other material handling appliance is used, if:\n\n                i)     the  Inspector  having  jurisdiction  is  not  satisfied  with  reference  to a\n                   certification of test or examination or to an authenticated record maintain as\n               provided under these rules; and\n\n                  ii)     in the view of such Inspector, the lifting appliance, lifting gear or any other\n                material  handling  appliance  is  not  safe  for use  in  building  or  other\n                construction work; and\n\n                  iii)   no pulley block is used in building or other construction work unless the safe\n               working load and its identification are clearly marked on such block.\n\n\n21.9      Qualification of operator of lifting appliances and of signaller etc\n\n\n21.9.1   The contractor shall not employ any person to drive or operate a lifting machine\n            like crane, hydra etc whether driven by mechanical power or otherwise or to give\n          signals to work as a operator of a rigger or derricks unless he\n\n                i)      is above twenty-one years of age and possesses a valid heavy transport\n                vehicle driving licence as per Motor Vehicle Act and Rules.\n\n                  ii)     is absolutely competent and reliable\n\n                  iii)   possesses the knowledge of the inherent risks involved in the operation of\n                      lifting appliances by undergoing a formal  training  at any  institution  of\n                national importance acceptable to Employer\n\n             iv)     is medically examined periodically as specified in schedule VII of BOCW\n               Rules.\n\n\n21.10    General requirements of appliances\n\n\n21.10.1   Out-of level\n\n\n21.10.1.1 One of the most severe effects of being out-of fit level is that side loads develop in\n          the boom. Because of side loads all mobile cranes lose capacity rapidly as the\n         degree of out-of-level increases and therefore"
> }

### Jda21eec19c54839f

[[OKF_bundle/Technical/Vol3/vol3_part2#Clause 21.0 — Lifting Appliances and Gear|Clause 21.0 — Lifting Appliances and Gear]]

> {
>   "pdf_page": 41,
>   "text": "21.0      Lifting Appliances and Gear\n\n\n          21.1       Lifting appliances means a crane, hoist machinery, derrick, winch, gin pole, sheer\n                      legs, jack, hoist drum, slewing machinery, slewing bearing fasteners,  loffing\n                  machinery sheaves, pulley blocks, hooks or other equipment used  for  lifting\n                     materials, objects or building workers and lifting gears means ropes, chain slings,\n                    shackles, hooks, lifting lugs, wire ropes, lifting eyebolts and eyenuts and other\n                   accessories of a lifting appliance.\n\n\n          21.2    No machine shall be selected to do any lifting on a specific job until its size and\n                     characteristics are considered against:\n\n\n                                 i)     the weights, dimensions and lift radii of the heaviest and largest loads\n\n                                    ii)    the maximum lift height, the maximum lift radius and the weight of the loads\n                            that must be handled at each\n\n                                     iii)    the number and frequency of lifts to be made\n\n                          iv)   how long the crane will be required on site\n\n                      v)    the type of lifting to be done (for example, is precision placement of loads\n                          important?)\n\n                          vi)    the type of carrier required (this depends on ground conditions and machine\n                          capacity In its operating quadrants) capacity is normally greatest over the\n                             rear, less over the side, and non-existent over the front\n\n                             vii)   whether loads will have to be walked or carried\n\n                               viii)  whether loads will have to be suspended for lengthy periods\n\n                          ix)    the site conditions, including the ground where the machine will be set up,\n                       access roads and ramps it must travel, space for erection and any obstacles\n                            that might impede access or operation\n\n\n          21.3    The contractor shall ensure that a valid certificate of fitness issued as per clause\n                   21.5  is available for all lifting appliances including synchronised mobile jacks, pre-\n                    stressing hydraulic jacks, jacks fitted with launching girders etc. and Employers\n                   approval before inducting to the site. Only after obtaining the approval from the\n                Employer any lifting appliances and gear shall be used.\n\n\n          21.4    The laminated photocopies  of  fitness  certificate issued by competent\n                  person, the Employers’ approval letter, the operators’ photo, manufacturer’s\n                  load chart and competency certificate shall always be either kept in the\n                  operator cabin or pasted on the visible surface of the lifting appliances.\n\n\n          21.5      All lifting appliances and loose gears shall be clearly marked for its safe\n                 working load and identification by stamping or other suitable means."

### J026fff02246527c2

[[OKF_bundle/Technical/Vol3/vol3_part2#Clause 26.0 — Site Electricity|Clause 26.0 — Site Electricity]]

> {
>   "pdf_page": 48,
>   "text": "26.7      Electrical protection circuits\n\n26.7.1    Precautions shall be taken, either by earthing or by other suitable means, to prevent\n         danger arising when any conductor (other than a  circuit conductor) which may\n         reasonably foreseeable become charged as a result of either the use of a system, or a\n            fault in a system, becomes so charged. A conductor shall be regarded as earthed\n        when conductors of sufficient strength and current-carrying capability to discharge\n           electrical energy to earth connect it to the general mass of earth.\n\n                If a circuit conductor is connected to earth or to any other reference point, nothing\n         which might reasonably be expected to give rise to danger by breaking the electrical\n           continuity or introducing high impedance shall be placed in that conductor unless\n          suitable precautions are taken to prevent that danger.\n\n\n26.7.2    Appropriate electrical protection shall be provided for all circuits, against over load,\n          short circuit and earth fault current.\n\n\n26.7.3   The contractor shall provide sufficient ELCBs (maintain sensitivity 30 mA) / RCCBs for\n              all the equipments (including Potable equipments), electrical switchboards, distribution\n         panels etc. to prevent electrical shocks to the workers.\n\n\n26.7.4     All protection devices shall be capable of interrupting the circuit without damage to any\n         equipments and circuits in case of any fault may occur.\n\n\n26.7.5    Rating of fuses and circuit breakers used for the protection of circuits should be\n          coordinate with equipment power ratings.\n\n\n26.7.6    Protection against lightning shall be ensured to all equipment kept in open at sites.\n\n\n26.8     Cables:\n\n\n26.8.1   Cables shall be selected after full consideration of the condition to which they shall be\n        exposed and the duties for which they are required. Supply cable up to 3.3 kV shall be\n            in accordance with BS 6346.\n\n\n26.8.2   For supplies to mobile or transportable equipment where operating of the equipment\n          subjects the cable to flexing, the cable shall conform to any of these codes BS 6007 /\n       BS 6500 / BS 7375.\n\n\n26.8.3    Flexible cords with a conductor cross sectional area smaller than 1.5 mm2 shall not be\n        used and insulated flexible cable shall conform to BS 6500 and BS 7375.\n\n\n26.8.4   Where low voltage cables are to be used, reference shall be made to BS 7375. The\n          following standards shall also be referred to particularly for under ground cables BS\n        6346 and BS 6708\n\n\n26.8.5   Cables buried directly in the ground shall be of a type incorporating armour or metal\n         sheath or both. Such cables shall be marked by cable covers or a suitable marking\n         tape and be buried at a  sufficient depth to avoid  their being damaged by any\n          disturbance of the ground. Cable routes shall be marked on the plans kept in the site\n           electrical register.\n\n26.8.6    Cabling passing under the walk way and across way  for transport and mobile\n         equipment shall be laid in ducts at a minimum depth of 0.6 meters.\n\n26.8.7   Cables that need to cross open areas, or where span of 3m or more are involved, a\n         catenary wire on poles or other supports shall be provided for convenient means of\n         suspension. Minimum height shall be 6 m above ground.\n\n\n26.8.8   Cables carrying a voltage to earth in excess of 65V other than supply for welding\n         process shall have metal armour or sheath, which has been effectively earthed and\n         monitored by the contractor. In case of flexible and trailing cables such earthed metal"

### J85cb8851adc8cf4a

[[OKF_bundle/Technical/Vol3/vol3_part2#Clause 23.0 — Construction machinery|Clause 23.0 — Construction machinery]]

> {
>   "clause_id": "23.0",
>   "fragments": [
>     {
>       "pdf_page": 45,
>       "text": "23.0     Construction machinery\n\n\n          23.1     Construction machineries may include dumpers and dump trucks,  lift trucks and\n                     telescopic handlers piling rigs, vibro hammers, rail welding equipments, mobile\n                    elevating work platforms, cranes, tipper lorries, lorry loaders, skip wagons, 360°\n                    excavators, 180° backhoe loaders, crawler tractors, scrapers, graders, loading\n                    shovels,  trenchers,  side  booms,  pavers,  planers,  chippers,  road  rollers,\n                    locomotives, tankers and bowsers, trailers, hydraulic and mechanical breakers\n                       etc.\n\n\n          23.2     Safe worthiness certificate\n\n\n          23.2.1   Every construction equipment shall be in sound mechanical working condition and\n                       certified by  either competent person under Factories Act  or manufacturers’\n                   warranty in case of brand new equipments or authorized persons / firms approved\n                 by Employer before induction to any site.\n\n\n          23.2.2   Every such  certificate  shall have  the  date  of  purchase, main  overhauling\n                  undertaken in the past, any accident to the equipment, visual examination details,\n                          critical components safety check, list of safety devises and its working condition,\n                   manufacturer’s maintenance checklist, past projects wherein the equipments were\n                 used etc as its minimum content.\n\n\n          23.3     Reverse Horns\n\n\n          23.3.1    All Vehicles shall be fitted with audible reverse alarms and maintained in\n               good working condition. Reversing  shall be done only when there  is\n                 adequate rear view visibility or under the directions of a banksman\n\n\n          23.4     General operating procedures\n\n\n                                 i)     Drivers entering site shall be instructed to follow the safe system of work adopted on\n                                site. These shall be verbal instructions or, preferably, written instructions showing\n                          the relevant site rules, the site layout, delivery areas, speed limits, etc.\n\n                                    ii)   No passengers shall be carried, unless specific seating has been provided  in\n                       accordance with the manufacturers’ recommendations.\n\n                                     iii)   Working on gradients beyond any equipments capability shall not be allowed.\n\n                          iv)   Prevention of dumper and dump truck accidents should be managed by providing\n                       wheel stops at a sufficient distance from the edges of excavations, spoil heaps, pits,\n                             etc.\n\n                      v)   The manufacturer’s recommended bucket size must not be exceeded in excavators.\n\n                          vi)      If excavators operating on a gradient which cannot be avoided, it must be ensured\n                            that the working cycle is slowed down, that the bucket is not extended too far in the\n                          downhill direction, and that travel  is undertaken with extreme caution. A large\n                         excavator must never be permitted to travel in a confined area, or around people,\n                          without a banksman to guide the driver, who should have the excavator attachment\n                         close in to the machine, with the bucket just clear of the ground. On wheeled\n                         excavators, it is essential that the tyres are in good condition and correctly inflated.\n                                           If stabilizing devices are  fitted, they should be employed when the machine  is\n                          excavating."
>     },
>     {
>       "pdf_page": 46,
>       "text": "vii)  When the front shovel of the 1800 backhoe loaders is being employed, the backhoe\n               attachment shall be in its “travel” position, with the safety locking device in place.\n\n               viii)  When operating the backhoe in poor ground conditions, the stabilisers tend to sink\n                  into the surface of the ground, reducing stability. Therefore frequent checks shall be\n           made for the stability of the machine. The loading shovel should always be lowered\n                 to the ground to stabilise the machine when the backhoe is employed.\n\n             ix)   The netting operation of the skip wagons should be carried out prior to lifting the\n                skip to reduce the risks of working on the rear platform\n\n           x)       If a tractor dozer is employed on clearing scrub or felling trees, it shall be provided\n                with adequate driver protection.\n\n             xi)   When two or more scrapers are working on the same job, a minimum distance of at\n                 least 25m shall be kept between them.\n\n              xii)   Incase of hydraulic breakers, hydraulic rams and hoses shall be in good working\n                condition\n\n\n23.5       All wood working machines shall be fitted with suitable guards and devices such as top\n          guard, riving knife, push stick, guards for drive belts and chains, and emergency stop\n          switch easily accessible by the operator.\n\n\n23.6     Penalty\n\n\n23.6.1      If any of the above clauses are not adhered, penalty shall be imposed as per\n         relevant clause depending upon the gravity of the unsafe act and or condition."
>     }

>       "source_line_number": 40,
>       "text": ""
>     },
>     {
>       "pdf_page": 45,
>       "source_line_number": 41,
>       "text": ""
>     },
>     {
>       "pdf_page": 45,
>       "source_line_number": 42,
>       "text": "          23.3     Reverse Horns"
>     },
>     {
>       "pdf_page": 45,
>       "source_line_number": 43,
>       "text": ""
>     },
>     {
>       "pdf_page": 45,
>       "source_line_number": 44,
>       "text": ""
>     },
>     {
>       "pdf_page": 45,
>       "source_line_number": 45,
>       "text": "          23.3.1    All Vehicles shall be fitted with audible reverse alarms and maintained in"
>     },
>     {
>       "pdf_page": 45,
>       "source_line_number": 46,
>       "text": "               good working condition. Reversing  shall be done only when there  is"
>     },
>     {
>       "pdf_page": 45,
>       "source_line_number": 47,
>       "text": "                 adequate rear view visibility or under the directions of a banksman"
>     },
>     {
>       "pdf_page": 45,
>       "source_line_number": 48,
>       "text": ""
>     },
>     {
>       "pdf_page": 45,
>       "source_line_number": 49,
>       "text": ""
>     },
>     {
>       "pdf_page": 45,
>       "source_line_number": 50,
>       "text": "          23.4     General operating procedures"
>     },
>     {
>       "pdf_page": 45,
>       "source_line_number": 51,
>       "text": ""
>     },
>     {
>       "pdf_page": 45,
>       "source_line_number": 52,
>       "text": ""
>     },
>     {
>       "pdf_page": 45,
>       "source_line_number": 53,
>       "text": "                                 i)     Drivers entering site shall be instructed to follow the safe system of work adopted on"
>     },
>     {
>       "pdf_page": 45,
>       "source_line_number": 54,
>       "text": "                                site. These shall be verbal instructions or, preferably, written instructions showing"
>     },
>     {
>       "pdf_page": 45,
>       "source_line_number": 55,
>       "text": "                          the relevant site rules, the site layout, delivery areas, speed limits, etc."
>     },
>     {
>       "pdf_page": 45,
>       "source_line_number": 56,
>       "text": ""
>     },
>     {
>       "pdf_page": 45,
>       "source_line_number": 57,
>       "text": "                                    ii)   No passengers shall be carried, unless specific seating has been provided  in"
>     },
>     {
>       "pdf_page": 45,
>       "source_line_number": 58,
>       "text": "                       accordance with the manufacturers’ recommendations."
>     },
>     {
>       "pdf_page": 45,
>       "source_line_number": 59,
>       "text": ""
>     },
>     {
>       "pdf_page": 45,
>       "source_line_number": 60,
>       "text": "                                     iii)   Working on gradients beyond any equipments capability shall not be allowed."
>     },
>     {
>       "pdf_page": 45,
>       "source_line_number": 61,
>       "text": ""
>     },
>     {
>       "pdf_page": 45,
>       "source_line_number": 62,
>       "text": "                          iv)   Prevention of dumper and dump truck accidents should be managed by providing"
>     },
>     {
>       "pdf_page": 45,
>       "source_line_number": 63,
>       "text": "                       wheel stops at a sufficient distance from the edges of excavations, spoil heaps, pits,"
>     },
>     {
>       "pdf_page": 45,
>       "source_line_number": 64,
>       "text": "                             etc."
>     },
>     {
>       "pdf_page": 45,
>       "source_line_number": 65,
>       "text": ""
>     },
>     {
>       "pdf_page": 45,
>       "source_line_number": 66,
>       "text": "                      v)   The manufacturer’s recommended bucket size must not be exceeded in excavators."
>     },
>     {
>       "pdf_page": 45,
>       "source_line_number": 67,
>       "text": ""
>     },
>     {
>       "pdf_page": 45,
>       "source_line_number": 68,
>       "text": "                          vi)      If excavators operating on a gradient which cannot be avoided, it must be ensured"
>     },
>     {
>       "pdf_page": 45,
>       "source_line_number": 69,
>       "text": "                            that the working cycle is slowed down, that the bucket is not extended too far in the"
>     },
>     {
>       "pdf_page": 45,
>       "source_line_number": 70,
>       "text": "                          downhill direction, and that travel  is undertaken with extreme caution. A large"
>     },
>     {
>       "pdf_page": 45,
>       "source_line_number": 71,
>       "text": "                         excavator must never be permitted to travel in a confined area, or around people,"
>     },
>     {
>       "pdf_page": 45,
>       "source_line_number": 72,
>       "text": "                          without a banksman to guide the driver, who should have the excavator attachment"
>     },
>     {
>       "pdf_page": 45,
>       "source_line_number": 73,
>       "text": "                         close in to the machine, with the bucket just clear of the ground. On wheeled"
>     },
>     {
>       "pdf_page": 45,
>       "source_line_number": 74,
>       "text": "                         excavators, it is essential that the tyres are in good condition and correctly inflated."
>     },
>     {
>       "pdf_page": 45,
>       "source_line_number": 75,
>       "text": "                                           If stabilizing devices are  fitted, they should be employed when the machine  is"
>     },
>     {
>       "pdf_page": 45,
>       "source_line_number": 76,
>       "text": "                          excavating."
>     },
>     {
>       "pdf_page": 45,
>       "source_line_number": 77,
>       "text": ""
>     },
>     {
>       "pdf_page": 45,
>       "source_line_number": 78,
>       "text": ""
>     },
>     {
>       "pdf_page": 45,
>       "source_line_number": 79,
>       "text": ""
>     },
>     {
>       "pdf_page": 45,
>       "source_line_number": 80,
>       "text": ""
>     },
>     {
>       "pdf_page": 46,
>       "source_line_number": 3,
>       "text": "              vii)  When the front shovel of the 1800 backhoe loaders is being employed, the backhoe"
>     },
>     {
>       "pdf_page": 46,
>       "source_line_number": 4,
>       "text": "               attachment shall be in its “travel” position, with the safety locking device in place."
>     },
>     {
>       "pdf_page": 46,
>       "source_line_number": 5,
>       "text": ""
>     },
>     {
>       "pdf_page": 46,
>       "source_line_number": 6,
>       "text": "               viii)  When operating the backhoe in poor ground conditions, the stabilisers tend to sink"
>     },
>     {
>       "pdf_page": 46,
>       "source_line_number": 7,
>       "text": "                  into the surface of the ground, reducing stability. Therefore frequent checks shall be"
>     },
>     {
>       "pdf_page": 46,
>       "source_line_number": 8,
>       "text": "           made for the stability of the machine. The loading shovel should always be lowered"
>     },
>     {
>       "pdf_page": 46,
>       "source_line_number": 9,
>       "text": "                 to the ground to stabilise the machine when the backhoe is employed."
>     },
>     {
>       "pdf_page": 46,
>       "source_line_number": 10,
>       "text": ""
>     },
>     {
>       "pdf_page": 46,
>       "source_line_number": 11,
>       "text": "             ix)   The netting operation of the skip wagons should be carried out prior to lifting the"
>     },
>     {
>       "pdf_page": 46,
>       "source_line_number": 12,
>       "text": "                skip to reduce the risks of working on the rear platform"
>     },
>     {
>       "pdf_page": 46,
>       "source_line_number": 13,
>       "text": ""
>     },
>     {
>       "pdf_page": 46,
>       "source_line_number": 14,
>       "text": "           x)       If a tractor dozer is employed on clearing scrub or felling trees, it shall be provided"
>     },
>     {
>       "pdf_page": 46,
>       "source_line_number": 15,
>       "text": "                with adequate driver protection."
>     },
>     {
>       "pdf_page": 46,
>       "source_line_number": 16,
>       "text": ""
>     },
>     {
>       "pdf_page": 46,
>       "source_line_number": 17,
>       "text": "             xi)   When two or more scrapers are working on the same job, a minimum distance of at"
>     },
>     {
>       "pdf_page": 46,
>       "source_line_number": 18,
>       "text": "                 least 25m shall be kept between them."
>     },
>     {
>       "pdf_page": 46,
>       "source_line_number": 19,
>       "text": ""
>     },
>     {
>       "pdf_page": 46,
>       "source_line_number": 20,
>       "text": "              xii)   Incase of hydraulic breakers, hydraulic rams and hoses shall be in good working"
>     },
>     {
>       "pdf_page": 46,
>       "source_line_number": 21,
>       "text": "                condition"
>     },
>     {
>       "pdf_page": 46,
>       "source_line_number": 22,
>       "text": ""
>     },
>     {
>       "pdf_page": 46,
>       "source_line_number": 23,
>       "text": ""
>     },
>     {
>       "pdf_page": 46,
>       "source_line_number": 24,
>       "text": "23.5       All wood working machines shall be fitted with suitable guards and devices such as top"
>     },
>     {
>       "pdf_page": 46,
>       "source_line_number": 25,
>       "text": "          guard, riving knife, push stick, guards for drive belts and chains, and emergency stop"
>     },
>     {
>       "pdf_page": 46,
>       "source_line_number": 26,
>       "text": "          switch easily accessible by the operator."
>     },
>     {
>       "pdf_page": 46,
>       "source_line_number": 27,
>       "text": ""
>     },
>     {
>       "pdf_page": 46,
>       "source_line_number": 28,
>       "text": ""
>     },
>     {
>       "pdf_page": 46,
>       "source_line_number": 29,
>       "text": "23.6     Penalty"
>     },
>     {
>       "pdf_page": 46,
>       "source_line_number": 30,
>       "text": ""
>     },
>     {
>       "pdf_page": 46,
>       "source_line_number": 31,
>       "text": ""
>     },
>     {
>       "pdf_page": 46,
>       "source_line_number": 32,
>       "text": "23.6.1      If any of the above clauses are not adhered, penalty shall be imposed as per"
>     },
>     {
>       "pdf_page": 46,
>       "source_line_number": 33,
>       "text": "         relevant clause depending upon the gravity of the unsafe act and or condition."
>     },
>     {
>       "pdf_page": 46,
>       "source_line_number": 34,
>       "text": ""
>     },
>     {
>       "pdf_page": 46,
>       "source_line_number": 35,
>       "text": ""
>     }
>   ],

>   "text": "26.0      Site Electricity\n\n26.1     Competency of Electrical personnel:\n\n26.1.1   The contractor shall employ qualified and competent electrical personnel as\n         specified in general instruction BMRC/SHE/CEO/001.\n\n\n26.2     Assessment of power"

>       "text": "27.0     Lighting:\n\n\n27.1    The contractor shall provide sufficient site lighting, of the right type and at the right\n         place for it to be properly effective. Lighting ought not to introduce the risk of electric\n         shock. Therefore, 230V supplies should be used for those fittings, which are robustly\n           installed, and well out of reach e.g. flood lighting or high-pressure discharge lamps.\n\n27.2      Selection of Luminaries:\n\n        The contractor shall select the luminaries as per the area requirement indicated below:\n\n            Sl.   Type of         Area of Requirement             Luminaries\n         No.  Lighting\n\n             1.   Area Lighting    Workmen and vehicles       i)  Shovel type: non-symmetrical\n                                      to move about in safely.     ii)  Symmetrical or non-\n                                                             symmetrical tungsten halogen\n\n             2.  Beam flood      Concentrated light over      i)  Portable flood light (Conical\n                    lighting         an area from a            beam)\n                                        relatively great                     ii)  Wide angle flood (fan shaped\n                                    distance.                 beam)\n\n                                                                                                               iii)  Medium or narrow angle flood\n                                                                (Conical beam)\n\n             3.   Dispersive        Lighting for indoor               i)  Dispersive (Mercury florescent)\n                    lighting                                                                  ii)  Cargo cluster\n\n                                                                                                               iii)  Florescent trough\n\n             4.   Walkway lighting  Lighting for stairways,         i)  Well glass unit\n                                  ladder ways, corridors,       ii)  Bulkhead unit (tungsten filament)\n                                     scaffold access routs, etc\n                                                                                                               iii)  Bulk head unit (Florescent)\n\n             5.   Local lighting     Lighting on sites and fittin   i) PAR (Parabolic Aluminised\n                                 are generally accessible t     Reflector) lamp cluster\n                                  operatives                            ii)  Festoons (with or without shades)\n\n                                                                                                               iii)  Adjustable florescent work lamp\n\n                                                                               iv)  Portable flood lamp (mounted on\n                                                own cable drum)\n\n\n27.3    The contractor shall ensure that luminaries should always be placed so that no person\n             is required to work in their own shadow and so that the local light for one person is not"
>     },
>     {
>       "pdf_page": 51,
>       "text": "a source of glare for the others. Strongly made clamps should be available  for\n                    attaching luminaries to poles and other convenient supports.\n\n\n          27.4     Luminaries should be robust, resistant to corrosion and rain proof especially at the\n                     point of the cable entry.\n\n\n          27.5    The correct type of lamp for each luminaries should always be used and when lamps\n                need to be replaced if shall be in accordance with the supply voltage.\n\n\n          27.6    Lamp holders not fitted with a lamp should be capped off.\n\n\n          27.7    The contractor shall take every effort to illuminate the work site as per the Employer’s\n                   requirement illustrated in general instruction BMRC/SHE/CEO/0011."
>     }

### Jacfcf580da82fece

[[OKF_bundle/Technical/Vol3/vol3_part2#Clause 26.0 — Site Electricity|Clause 26.0 — Site Electricity]]

> {
>   "pdf_page": 49,
>   "text": "sheath and/or armour should be in addition to the earth core in the cable and shall not\n                be used as the protective conductor.\n\n\n          26.8.9   Armoured cables having an over-sheath of polyvinyl chloride (PVC) or an  oil\n                      resisting and flame retardant compound shall be used whenever there is a risk of\n                  mechanical damage occurring\n\n\n          26.9     Plugs, socket-outlets and couplers:\n\n\n          26.9.1   The contractor shall ensure plugs, socket-outlets, and couplers available in\n                  the construction  site as “splash proof” type. The minimum degree of\n                  Ingress Protection should be of IP44 in accordance with BS EN 60529.\n\n\n          26.9.2   Only plugs and fittings of the weatherproof type shall be used and they should be colour\n                 coded in accordance with the Internationally recognised standards for example as detailed\n                 as follows:\n\n                      (a)   110 volts : Yellow.\n\n                      (b)   240 volts : Blue.\n\n                       (c)   415 volts : Red.\n\n         26.10    Connections\n\n          26.10.1  Every joint and connection in a system shall be mechanically and electrically\n                   suitable  for  use  to  prevent  danger.  Proper  cable  connectors  as  per\n                    national/international standards shall only be used to connect cables.\n\n          26.10.2  No loose connections or tapped joints shall be allowed any where in the work\n                       site, office area, stores and other areas. Penalty as per relevant clause shall be\n                  put in case of observation of any tapped joints.\n\n\n         26.11    Portable and hand-held equipments:\n\n\n          26.11.1  The contractor shall ensure the use of double insulated or all-insulated portable\n                       electrical hand equipment may be used without earthing (i.e. two core cables), but\n                   they shall still be used only on 110V because of the risk of damage to trailing leads.\n\n\n         26.12    Other equipments:\n\n\n          26.12.1   All equipment shall have the provision for major switch/cut-off switch in the equipment\n                           itself.\n\n\n          26.12.2   All non-current carrying metal parts of electrical equipment shall be earthed through\n                    insulated cable\n\n\n          26.12.3   Isolate exposed high-voltage (over 415 Volts) equipment, such as transformer banks,\n                open switches, and similar equipment with exposed energized parts and prevent\n                   unauthorised access.\n\n\n          26.12.4  Approved perimeter markings shall be used to isolate restricted areas from designated\n                 work areas and entryways and shall be erected before work begins and maintained for\n                      entire duration of work. Approved perimeter marking shall be installed  with either red\n                      barrier tape printed with the words \"DANGER—HIGH VOLTAGE\" or a barrier of yellow\n                     or orange synthetic rope, approximately 1 to 1.5 meter above the floor or work\n                    surface.\n\n\n         26.13   Work on or near live conductors"

### Jb43d24671a70324c

[[OKF_bundle/Technical/Vol3/vol3_part2#Clause 26.0 — Site Electricity|Clause 26.0 — Site Electricity]]

> {
>   "pdf_page": 47,
>   "text": "26.2.1   The contractor shall assess the size and location of the electrical loads and the\n                manner in which they vary with time during the currency of the contract.\n\n\n          26.2.2   The contractor shall elaborate as to how the total supply is to be obtained  /\n                   generated. The  details  of  the  source  of  electricity,  earthing  requirement,\n                    substation  / panel boards, distribution system shall be prepared and necessary\n                   approval from Employer obtained before proceeding of the execution of the job.\n\n\n          26.2.3   The main contractor shall take consideration, the requirements of the sub /\n                   petty contractors’ electric power supply and arrive at the capacity of main\n                 source of power supply from diesel generators.\n\n\n          26.2.4   As the sub / petty contractors’ small capacity generators create more noise\n               and safety hazard, no small capacity diesel generators shall be allowed for\n                 whatsoever the type of job to be executed under this contract.\n\n\n          26.2.5      If any unsafe noise making small capacity diesel generators are found used\n                by sub / petty contractors the main contractor shall only be penalised.\n\n\n          26.3    Work on site\n\n\n          26.3.1   The contractor shall also submit electrical single line diagram, schematic\n                diagram and the  details of the equipment  for  all temporary  electrical\n                     installation and these diagrams together with the temporary  electrical\n                equipment shall be submitted to the Employer’s for necessary approval.\n                   Failure to do so shall invite penalty as per relevant clause.\n\n\n          26.4     Strength and capability of electrical equipment\n\n\n          26.4.1   No electrical equipment shall be put into use where its strength and capability may\n                be exceeded in such a way as may give rise to danger.\n\n\n          26.5     Adverse or hazardous environments\n\n          26.5.1    Electrical equipment, which may reasonably foreseably be exposed to-\n\n                      (a)   mechanical damage;\n                      (b)   the effects of the weather, natural hazards, temperature or pressure;\n                       (c)   the effects of wet, dirty, dusty or corrosive conditions; or\n                      (d)   any flammable or explosive substance, including dusts, vapours or gases,\n                             shall be of such construction or as necessary protected as to prevent, so far\n                      as is reasonably practicable, danger arising from such exposure.\n\n\n\n          26.6      Distribution system:\n\n\n          26.6.1   The contractor shall provide distribution system for control and distribution of\n                        electricity from a main AC supply of 50Hz for typical appliances,\n\n\n                                 i)    Fixed plant – 400V 3 phase\n\n                                    ii)    Movable plant fed via trailing cable over 3.75 kW – 400 3 phase\n\n                                     iii)    Installation in site buildings – 230V single phase\n\n                          iv)   Fixed flood lighting – 230V single phase\n\n                      v)    Portable and hand tools – 115V single phase\n\n                          vi)    Site lighting  - 115V single phase\n\n                             vii)   Portable hand lamps – 115V single phase"
> }

### Jc37b230c86ee4459

[[OKF_bundle/Technical/Vol3/vol3_part2#Clause 26.0 — Site Electricity|Clause 26.0 — Site Electricity]]

> {
>   "pdf_page": 50,
>   "text": "26.13.1  No person shall be engaged in any work activity on or so near any live conductor\n          (other than one suitably covered with insulating material so as to prevent danger) that\n         danger may arise unless-\n\n          a)       it is unreasonable in all the circumstances for it to be dead; and\n          b)       it is reasonable in all the circumstances for him to be at work on or near it while\n                             it is live; and\n           c)    suitable  precautions  (including where necessary  the  provision  of  suitable\n                 protective equipment) are taken to prevent injury.\n\n\n26.14    Inspection and Maintenance\n\n\n26.14.1   All electrical equipment should be permanently numbered and a record kept of the\n         date of issue, date of last inspection and recommended inspection period.\n\n\n26.14.2  Fixed installations shall be inspected at least at three monthly intervals; routine\n         maintenance  being  carried  out  in  accordance  with  equipment  manufactures\n         recommendations."
> }

        used by his employees and that of his sub-contractors.\n\n\n          28.1.2   Use of short / damaged hand tools shall be avoided and the contractor shall ensure all\n                      his hand tools used at his worksite are safe to work with or stored and shall also train\n                      his employees (including his sub-contractors) for proper use thereby.\n\n\n          28.1.3     All hand tools and power tools shall be duly inspected before use for safe operation.\n\n\n          28.1.4     All hand tools and power tools shall have sufficient grip and the design specification\n                on par with national/international standards on anthropometrics.\n\n\n          28.2    Hand tools\n\n\n          28.2.1   Hand tools shall include saws, chisels, axes and hatches, hammers, hand planes,\n                 screw drivers, crow bars, nail pullers.\n\n\n          28.2.2   The contractor shall ensure that,\n\n\n                                 i)    For crosscutting of hardwood, saws with larger teeth points (no. of points per\n                           inch) shall be preferred to avoid the saw jumping out of the job.\n\n                                    ii)   Mushroom headed  chisels  shall  not be used  in  the  worksite where  the\n                        fragments of the head may cause injury.\n\n                                     iii)   Unless hatchet has a striking face, it shall be used as a hammer.\n\n                          iv)   Only knives of retractable blades shall be used in the worksite.\n\n                      v)   No screwdrivers shall be used for scraping, chiselling or punching holes.\n\n                          vi)   A pilot hole shall always be driven before driving a screw.\n\n                             vii)   Wherever necessary, usage of proper PPEs shall be used by his employees.\n\n\n          28.3     Power tools\n\n\n          28.3.1   Power tools include drills, planes, routers, saws, jackhammers, grinders, sprayers,\n                    chipping hammers, air nozzles and drills.\n\n\n          28.3.2   The contractor shall ensure that\n\n                                 i)     Electric tools are properly grounded or / and double insulated."

The same shall also apply to working with equipments, which\n                gives out more noise as mentioned in clause 43.0 of this contract document.\n\n           v)    Tool is held firmly and the material is properly secured before turning on the\n                   tool.\n\n             vi)    All  drills shall have suitable attachments respective of the operations and\n               powerful for ease of operation.\n\n              vii)  When any work  / operation need to be performed repeatedly or continuously,\n                 tools specifically designed for that work shall be used. The same is applicable to\n               detachable tool bit also.\n\n               viii)   Size of the drill shall be determined by the maximum opening of the chuck n\n              case of drill bit.\n\n             ix)   Attachments such as speed reducing screwdrivers and buffers shall be provided\n                 to prevent fatigue and undue muscle strain to his workers.\n\n           x)    Stock should be clamped or otherwise secured firmly to prevent it from moving.\n\n             xi)   Workers shall never stand on the top of the ladder to  drill holes in walls  /\n                  ceilings, which can be hazardous, instead standing on the fourth or fifth rung\n                  shall be recommended.\n\n              xii)    Electric plane shall not be operated with loose clothing or long scarf or open\n                 jacket.\n\n               xiii)   Safety guards used on right angle head or vertical portable grinders must cover\n             a minimum of 1800 of the wheel and the spindle / wheel specifications shall be\n              checked.\n\n            xiv)   All power tools / hand tools shall have guards at their nip points.\n\n          xv)  Low profile safety chain shall be used in case of wood working machines and\n                the saw shall run at high rpm when cutting and also correct chain tension shall\n             be ensured to avoid “kickback”.\n\n            xvi)  Leather aprons and gloves shall be used as an additional personal protection\n                  auxiliary to withstand kickback.\n\n             xvii)  Push sticks shall be provided and properly used to hold the job down on the\n                 table while the heels moves the stock forward and thus preventing kickbacks.\n\n              xviii)  Air pressure is set at a suitable level for air actuated tool or equipment being\n               used. Before changing or adjusting pneumatic tools, air pressure shall be turned\n                     off.\n\n            xix)  Only trained employees shall use explosive actuated tools and the tool shall\n                also be unloaded when not in use.\n\n          xx)  Usage of such explosive actuated tools shall be avoided in case of places\n             where explosive/flammable vapours or gases may be present.\n\n            xxi)  Explosive actuated tools and their explosives shall be stored separately and be\n               taken out and loaded only before the time of immediate use.\n\n             xxii)  Misfired cartridges of explosive actuated tools must be placed in a container of\n               water and be removed safely from the project.\n\n              xxiii) No worker shall point any power operated  / hand tool to any other person\n                especially during loading / unloading."

[[OKF_bundle/Technical/Vol3/vol3_part2#Clause 29.0 — Welding, Gouging and Cutting|Clause 29.0 — Welding, Gouging and Cutting]]

> {
>   "clause_id": "29.0",
>   "fragments": [
>     {
>       "pdf_page": 52,
>       "text": "29.0     Welding, Gouging and Cutting\n\n\n29.1    Gas cylinders in use shall be kept upright on a custom-built stand or trolley fitted\n          with a bracket to accommodate the hoses and equipment or otherwise secured.\n        The metal cap shall be kept in place to protect the valve when the cylinder is not\n         connected for use.\n\n\n29.2    Hose clamp or clip shall be used to connect hoses firmly in both sides of cylinders\n        and torches."
>     },
>     {
>       "pdf_page": 53,
>       "text": "29.3       All gas cylinders shall be fixed with pressure regulator and dial gauges\n\n\n          29.4     Non-return valve and Flashback arrester shall be fixed at both end of cylinder and\n                      torch.\n\n\n          29.5     Domestic LPG cylinders shall not be used for Gas welding and Cutting purpose.\n\n\n          29.6    DCP or CO2 type Fire Extinguisher not less than 5 kg shall be fixed at or near to\n                   welding process zone  in an easily accessible  location. Fire Extinguisher should\n                    confirm to IS 2190: 1992.\n\n\n          29.7    Use firewatchers if there is a possibility of ignition unobserved by the operator (e.g. on\n                    the other side of bulkheads).\n\n\n          29.8    Oxygen cylinders and flammable gas cylinders shall be stored separately, at least 6.6\n                  meters (20 feet) apart or separated by a fire proof, 1.5 meters (5 feet) high partition.\n                 Flammable substances shall not be stored within 15 meters of cylinder storage areas.\n\n\n          29.9     Transformer used for electrical arc welding shall be fixed with Ammeter and Voltmeter\n                and also fixed with separate main power switch.\n\n\n         29.10    Welding grounds and returns should be securely attached to the work by cable lugs,\n                 by clamps in the case of stranded conductors, or by bolts for strip conductors. The\n                  ground cable will not be attached to equipment or existing installations or apparatus.\n\n\n         29.11   Use a low voltage open circuit relay device  if welding with alternating current in\n                     constricted or damp places.\n\n         29.12    Take precautions against the risk of increased fume hazards when welding with\n                chrome containing fluxed consumables or high current metal  inert gas (MIG) or\n                   tungsten inert gas (TIG) processes.\n\n         29.13    Avoid being in contact with water or wet floors when welding. Use duckboards or\n                   rubber protection.\n\n\n         29.14     All electrical installations shall meet the IS: 5571: 1997 and NFPA 70 for gas cylinder\n                   storage area and other hazardous areas.\n\n\n         29.15   The current for Electric arc welding shall not exceed 300 A on a hand welding\n                    operation."
>     }

### J13cc94d8a9f49968

[[OKF_bundle/Technical/Vol3/vol3_part2#Clause 30.0 — Dangerous and harmful environment|Clause 30.0 — Dangerous and harmful environment]]

> {
>   "clause_id": "30.0",
>   "fragments": [
>     {
>       "pdf_page": 53,
>       "text": "30.0    Dangerous and harmful environment\n\n\n                As per BOCWR Rule 40,\n\n                                 i)   When internal combustion engines are to be used into a confined space or\n                         excavation or tunnel or any other workplace where neither natural or artificial\n                             ventilation system  is inadequate  to keep carbon monoxide below 50ppm,\n                       exposure of building workers shall be avoided unless suitable measures are\n                        taken and provided by the contractor.\n\n\n                                    ii)   No worker shall be allowed into any confined space or tank or trench or\n                         excavation wherein there  is given  off any dust, fumes  / vapours or other\n                            impurities which is likely to be injurious or offensive, explosive or poisonous or\n                        noxious or gaseous material or other harmful articles unless steps are carried\n                          out by the contractor and certified by the responsible person to be safe."
>     }
>   ],

### Jfe3645300d8a3364

[[OKF_bundle/Technical/Vol3/vol3_part2#Clause 31.0 — Fire prevention, protection and fighting system|Clause 31.0 — Fire prevention, protection and fighting system]]

> {
>   "clause_id": "31.0",
>   "fragments": [
>     {
>       "pdf_page": 54,
>       "text": "31.0      Fire prevention, protection and fighting system\n\n\n31.1    The  contractor  shall ensure  that  construction  site  is provided  with  fire\n         extinguishing  equipment  sufficient  to  extinguish  any  probable   fire  at\n         construction site. An adequate water supply is provided at ample pressure as\n         per national standard.\n\n\n31.2     Recharging of fire extinguishers and their proper maintenance should be ensured and\n         as a minimum should meet Indian National Standards\n\n\n31.3       All drivers  of vehicles, foreman, supervisors and managers  shall be trained on\n          operating the fire extinguishers and fire fighting equipment.\n\n31.4    The contractor shall also give consideration to the provision of adequate fire fighting\n         arrangements within the underground and tunnelling operations including the provision\n           of Fire Service compatible hose connections and emergency lighting\n\n\n31.5    As per the BOCWK Rules 2006, Rule 79(a)(vii), all lifting appliances’ driver cabin\n         should be provided with a suitable portable fire extinguisher.\n\n\n31.6     Combustible scrap and other construction debris should be disposed off site on a\n          regular basis. If scrap is to be burnt on site, the burning site should be specified and\n          located at a distance no less than 12 metres from any construction work or any other\n         combustible material.\n\n\n31.7     Every fire, including those extinguished by contractor personnel, shall be reported to\n          the Employer representatives.\n\n\n31.8     Emergency plans and Fire Evacuation plans shall be prepared and issued. Mock drills\n         should be held on a regular basis to ensure the effectiveness of the arrangements and\n         as a part of the programme, the Telephone Number of the local fire brigade should be\n          prominently displayed near each telephone on site."
>     }

### J65f1a57f515d8a85

[[OKF_bundle/Technical/Vol3/vol3_part2#Clause 35.0 — Work Permit system|Clause 35.0 — Work Permit system]]

> {
>   "clause_id": "35.0",
>   "fragments": [
>     {
>       "pdf_page": 56,
>       "text": "35.0    Work Permit system\n\n\n35.1    The Contractor shall develop a Work Permit system, which is a formal written system\n        used to control certain types of work that are potentially hazardous. A work permit is a\n         document, which specifies the work to be done, and the precautions to be taken. Work\n         Permits form an essential part of safe systems of work for many construction activities.\n        They allow work to start only after safe procedures have been defined and they\n          provide a clear record that all foreseeable hazards have been considered. Permits to\n        Work are usually required in high-risk areas as identified by the Risk Assessments.\n\n\n35.2    A permit  is needed when construction work can only be carried out   if normal\n         safeguards are dropped or when new hazards are introduced by the work. Examples\n           of high-risk activities include but are not limited to:\n\n\n                 i)     Entry into confined spaces\n                  ii)   Work in close proximity to overhead power lines and telecommunication cables.\n                  iii)   Hot work.\n             iv)   To dig—where underground services may be located.\n           v)   Work with heavy moving machinery."
>     },
>     {
>       "pdf_page": 57,
>       "text": "vi)   Working on electrical equipment\n                             vii)  Work with radioactive isotopes.\n                               viii)  Heavy lifting operations and lifting operations closer to live power line\n\n\n          35.3    The permit-to-work system should be fully documented, laying down:\n\n\n                                 i)   How the system works;\n                                    ii)   The jobs it is to be used for;\n                                     iii)   The responsibilities and training of those involved; and\n                          iv)  How to check its operation;\n\n\n          35.4    A Work Permit authorisation form shall be completed with the maximum duration\n                    period not exceeding 12 hours.\n\n\n          35.5    A copy of each Permit To Work shall be displayed, during its validity, in a conspicuous\n                     location in close proximity to the actual works location to which it applies."
>     }
