### J8e418199fb2f83a4

[[OKF_bundle/Technical/Vol3/vol3_part2#Clause 34.0 — Excavation and Tunnelling:|Clause 34.0 — Excavation and Tunnelling:]]

> {
>   "clause_id": "34.0",
>   "fragments": [
>     {
>       "pdf_page": 55,
>       "text": "34.0     Excavation and Tunnelling:\n\n\n          34.1     Excavation\n\n\n          34.1.1   The contractor shall ensure\n\n\n                                 i)    where any construction building worker engaged in excavation is exposed to\n                       hazard of falling or sliding material or article from any bank or side of such\n                         excavation which is more than one 1.5 m above his footing, such worker is\n                          protected by adequate piling and bracing against such bank or side.\n\n\n                                    ii)    where banks of an excavation are undercut, adequate shoring is provided to\n                         support the material or article overhanging such bank.\n\n\n                                     iii)   excavated material is not stored at least 0.65 m from the edge of an open\n                         excavation or trench and banks of such excavation or trench are stripped of\n                         loose rocks and the banks of such excavation or trench are stripped of loose\n                         rocks and other materials which may slide,  roll or  fall upon a construction\n                           building worker working below such bank\n\n\n                          iv)   metal ladders and staircases or ramps are provided, as the case may be, for\n                         safe access to and egress from excavation where, the depth of such excavation\n                      exceeds 1.5 m and such ladders, staircases or ramps comply with the IS 3696\n                          Part 1&2 and other relevant national standards.\n\n\n                      v)    trench and excavation  is protected against  falling of a person by suitable\n                     measures  if the depth of such trench or excavation exceeds 1.5 m and such\n                           protection is an improved protection in accordance with the design and drawing\n                            of a professional engineer, where such depth exceeds 4m.\n\n\n          34.2      Tunnelling\n\n\n          34.2.1   The contractor shall inform in writing to the Director General within 30 days, prior to\n                    the commencement of any tunnelling work.\n\n\n          34.2.2   The contractor shall appoint a responsible person for safe operation for tunnelling\n                 work as per Rule 121 & 125 of BOCWR.\n\n\n          34.2.3   The contractor shall ensure"
>     },
>     {
>       "pdf_page": 56,
>       "text": "i)    every compressed air system in a tunnel is provided with emergency power\n               supply for maintained continued supply of compressed air as per Rule 155 of\n         BOCWR\n\n                  ii)    watertight bulkhead doors are installed at the entrance of a tunnel to prevent\n                 flooding.\n\n                  iii)    reliable and effective means of communication such as telephone or walkie-\n                   talkie are provided and maintained for arranging better effective communication\n                 at an excavation or tunnelling work as per Rule 136 of BOCWR.\n\n             iv)     all portable electrical hand tools and inspection lamp used in under ground and\n               confined space at an excavation or tunnelling work is operated at a voltage not\n              exceeding 24V.\n\n           v)    only flame proof equipment of appropriate type as per IS:5571:2000 and or\n                other relevant national standard is used inside the tunnel\n\n             vi)    petrol or LPG of any other flammable substances are not used, stored inside the\n                tunnel except with prior approval from Employer, and also no oxy-acetylene gas\n                    is used in a compressed air environment in excavation or tunnelling\n\n              vii)   adequate number of water outlets provided for fire fighting purpose, an audible\n                     fire alarm and adequate number and types of fire extinguishers are provided\n             and maintained.\n\n               viii)  temperature in any working chamber in an excavation or tunnelling work where\n              workers employed does not exceed 29C as per Rule 165 of BOCWR.\n\n             ix)     all working areas in a free air tunnel are provided with ventilation system as\n              approved by the Director General and the fresh air supplied in such tunnel is not\n                less than 6 m3/ min for each worker employed in tunnel as per Rule 153 of\n          BOCWR.\n\n\n34.3     Warning signs and notices:\n\n\n34.3.1   The contractor shall ensure that\n\n                i)     suitable warning signs or notices, required for the safety of building workers\n                carrying out the work of an excavation or tunnelling, shall be displayed or\n               erected at conspicuous  places in Hindi and in a language understood by\n                majority of such building workers at such building such excavation or tunnelling\n              work\n\n                  ii)    such warning signs and notices with regard to compressed air working shall\n                include\n\n                a)    the danger involved in such compressed air work\n\n                b)     fire and explosion hazard\n\n                 c)    the emergency procedures for rescue from such danger or hazards."
>     }

[[OKF_bundle/Technical/Vol3/vol3_part2#Clause 33.0 — Demolition|Clause 33.0 — Demolition]]

> {
>   "clause_id": "33.0",
>   "fragments": [
>     {
>       "pdf_page": 54,
>       "text": "33.0     Demolition\n\n33.1    The Contractor shall ensure that\n\n                i)       all  demolition  works be  carried  out  in a  controlled manner  under  the\n            management of experienced and competent supervision.\n\n                  ii)    the concerned department of the Government or local authority be informed and\n               permission obtained wherever required. Media shall also be informed regarding\n                   this concern.\n\n\n                  iii)     all glass or similar materials or articles in exterior openings are removed\n              before commencing any demolition work and all water, steam, electric,\n             gas and other similar supply lines are put-off and such lines so located or\n            capped with substantial coverings so as to protect it from damage and to\n               afford safety to the building workers and public.."
>     },
>     {
>       "pdf_page": 55,
>       "text": "iv)   examine the walls of all structures adjacent to the structure to be demolished to\n                        determine thickness, method of support to such adjacent structures\n\n                      v)   no demolishing work be performed if the adjacent structure seems to be unsafe\n                         unless and until remedial measures life sheet piling, shoring, bracing or similar\n                    means be ensured for safety and stability for adjacent structure from collapsing.\n\n                          vi)    debris / bricks and other materials or articles shall be removed by means of\n                           a)      chutes\n                           b)     buckets or hoists\n                            c)      through openings through floors or\n                           d)     any other safe means\n\n                             vii)   no person other than  building workers  or other persons  essential  to the\n                         operation of demolition work shall be permitted to enter a zone of demolition and\n                          the area be provided with substantial barricades."
>     }
>   ],

### J96ecb6f98c77702f

[[OKF_bundle/Technical/Vol3/vol3_part2#Clause 38.0 — Batching Plant and Casting Yard layout|Clause 38.0 — Batching Plant and Casting Yard layout]]

> {
>   "clause_id": "38.0",
>   "fragments": [
>     {
>       "pdf_page": 59,
>       "text": "38.0     Batching Plant and Casting Yard layout\n\n\n                                 i)    The batching plant / casting yard shall be effectively planned for smooth flow of\n                         unloading and stacking the aggregates reinforcements and cement, batching\n                             plant, transport of concrete, casting the segment, stacking the segment and\n                          loading the segments to the trucks. As far as possible the conflicts should be\n                         avoided.\n\n                                    ii)   The batching plant / casting yard shall be barricaded and made as a compulsory\n                  PPE zone\n\n                                     iii)      If in case of material unloading area is not maintainable as PPE zone, the same\n                             shall be segregated properly and made as a non-PPE zone with appropriate\n                            barrications.\n\n                          iv)    Electrical system  shall also be suitably planned so that location  of diesel\n                          generator,  if any, location of DBs, routing of cables and positioning of area\n                              lighting poles/masts does not infringe on any other utility and pose danger."
>     },
>     {
>       "pdf_page": 60,
>       "text": "v)    Drainage shall be effectively provided and waste water shall be disposed after\n               proper treatment\n\n             vi)   Time office, canteen, drinking water,  toilet and rest place shall be suitably\n                located  for the easy access to workers.  All the  facilities shall be properly\n              cleaned and maintained during the entire period of operation.\n\n              vii)   Manual handling of cement shall be avoided to a larger extent. Whenever  it is\n                absolutely necessary the workmen shall be given  full body protection, hand\n                protection and respiratory protection as a basic measure of ensuring better\n                 health.\n\n               viii)  The PPEs provided to cement handling workmen shall conform to international\n               standards.\n\n             ix)   Access roads and internal circulation roads shall be well laid and maintained\n                properly at all time.\n\n           x)    Non-adherence to any of the above provision shall be penalised as per relevant\n                penalty clause."
>     }
>   ],

### Jab37b02fb3e0dd56

[[OKF_bundle/Technical/Vol3/vol3_part2#Clause 37.0 — Work to adjacent railways|Clause 37.0 — Work to adjacent railways]]

> {

>   "fragments": [
>     {
>       "pdf_page": 59,
>       "text": "37.0    Work to adjacent railways\n\n          37.1     Whenever work is to be conducted in close proximity to the live railways then the\n                     following measures shall need to be addressed:\n\n                      (a)  The rules provided for in the Railway’s manual should be followed.\n\n                      (b)  No persons are allowed to encroach onto the railway unless the owner has\n                         given specific authority.\n\n                       (c)   Adequate protection in accordance with the railway owner’s requirements shall\n                     be followed. (Provision of Block Inspectors, Flagmen and Lookouts)\n\n                      (d)    All persons shall wear high visibility clothing at all times.\n\n                      (e)  Any induction training requirements of the railways shall be strictly observed"
>     }

### Jbc37df6ba968168a

[[OKF_bundle/Technical/Vol3/vol3_part2#Clause 36.0 — Traffic Management|Clause 36.0 — Traffic Management]]

> {
>   "clause_id": "36.0",
>   "fragments": [
>     {
>       "pdf_page": 57,
>       "text": "36.0      Traffic Management\n\n\n          36.1    The basic objective of the following guidelines  is to lay down procedures to be\n                  adopted by contractor to ensure the safe and efficient movement of traffic and also to\n                  ensure the safety of workmen at construction sites.\n\n\n          36.2       All construction workers should be provided with high visibility jackets with reflective\n                   tapes as most of viaduct /tunnelling/station and depot works or either above or under\n                      right-of-way. The conspicuity of workmen at  all times shall be increased so as to\n                     protect from speeding vehicular traffic.\n\n\n          36.3    The guiding principles to be adopted for safety in construction zone are to\n\n\n                                 i)    Warn the road user clearly and sufficiently in advance.\n\n                                    ii)    Provide safe and clearly marked lanes for guiding road users.\n\n                                     iii)    Provide safe and clearly marked buffer and work zones\n\n                          iv)   Provide adequate measures that control driver behaviour through construction\n                        zones.\n\n\n          36.4     Legal permission\n\n\n          36.4.1    In  all cases, the contractor shall employ proper precautions. Wherever operations\n                  undertaken are likely to interfere with public traffic, specific traffic management plans\n                      shall be drawn up and implemented by the contractor in consultation with the approval\n                      of local police authorities and/or the concerned metropolitan/civil authorities as the\n                 case may be.\n\n\n          36.4.2   Such  traffic management plans  shall  include  provision  for  traffic  diversion and\n                     selection of alternative routes for transport of equipment.  If necessary, the contractor\n                      shall carry out road widening before commencement of works to accommodate the\n                    extra load\n\n\n          36.5    The primary traffic control devices used in work zones shall include signs, delineators,\n                    barricades, cones, pylons, pavement markings and flashing lights.\n\n\n          36.6    The road construction and maintenance signs which fall into the same three major\n                    categories as do other traffic signs, that are Regulatory Signs, Warning Signs and\n                     Direction (or guidelines) Signs shall only be used. The IRC: 67 (Code of Practice for\n               Road Signs) provide a list of traffic signs. The size, colours and placement of sign\n                      shall confirm to IRC: 67."
>     },
>     {
>       "pdf_page": 58,
>       "text": "36.7     Regulatory signs\n\n\n36.7.1    Regulatory signs impose legal restriction on all traffic.  It is essential, therefore, that\n         they are used only after consulting the local police and traffic authorities.\n\n\n36.8     Warning signs\n\n\n36.8.1   Warning signs in the traffic control zone shall be utilised to warn the drivers of specific\n         hazards that may be encountered.\n\n\n36.8.2   The contractor shall place detour signage at strategic locations and install appropriate\n         warning signs.  In order to minimize disruption of access to residences and business,\n          the contractor shall maintain at least one entrance to a property where multiple\n         entrances exist.\n\n\n36.8.3   A warning sign as given in general instruction BMRC/SHE/CEO/012 shall be installed\n        an at all secondary road which merges with the primary road where the construction\n         work is in progress at sufficient distance before it merges with the primary road so as\n           to alert the road users regarding the ‘Metro Work in Progress’.\n\n\n36.8.4    Materials hanging over / protruded from the chassis / body of any vehicle especially\n          during material handling shall be indicated by red indicator (red light/flag) to indicate\n          the caution to the road users.\n\n\n36.9      Delineators\n\n        The delineators are the elements of a total system of traffic control and have two\n            distinct purposes:\n\n                i)    To delineate and guide the driver to and along a safe path\n\n                  ii)   As a taper to move traffic from one lane to another.\n\n\n36.9.1   These channelizing devices such as cones, traffic cylinders, tapes and drums shall be\n         placed in or adjacent to the roadway to control the flow of  traffic. These should\n          normally be retro-reflectors complying to IRC: 79 - Recommended Practice for Road\n          Delineators.\n\n\n36.9.2    Traffic cones and cylinders\n\n\n36.9.2.1  Traffic cones of 500mm, 750mm and 1000mm high and 300mm to 500mm in diameter\n          or in square shape at base and are often made of plastic or rubber and normally have\n           retro-reflectorised red and white band shall be used wherever required.\n\n36.9.3   Drums\n\n36.9.3.1  Drums about 800mm to 1000mm high and 300mm in diameter can be used either as\n          channelising or warning devices. These are highly visible, give the appearance of\n         being formidable objects and therefore command the respect of drivers.\n\n\n36.9.4    Barricades\n\n\n36.9.4.1  Full height fence, barriers, barricades etc. shall be erected around the site in order to\n         prevent the working area from  the  risk  of  accidents due  to speedy  vehicular\n        movement. Same the way barricades protect the road users from the danger due to\n          construction equipment and other temporary structures.\n\n\n36.9.4.2  The structure dimension of the barricade, material and composition, its colour scheme,\n      BMRC logo and other details shall be in accordance with specifications laid down in\n          tender document."
>     },
>     {
>       "pdf_page": 59,
>       "text": "36.9.4.3  All barricades shall be erected as per the design requirements of the Employer,\n                 numbered, painted and maintained in good condition and also Barricade in-charge\n                   maintains a barricade register in site.\n\n\n          36.9.4.4  All barricades shall be conspicuously seen in the dark/night time by the road\n                 users so that no vehicle hits the barricade. Conspicuity. shall be ensured by\n                     affixing retro reflective stripes of required size and shape at appropriate angle at\n                  the bottom and middle portion of the barricade at a minimum gap of 1000mm. In\n                   addition minimum one red light or red light blinker should be placed at the top\n                   of each barricade.\n\n\n          36.9.5   The contractor shall ensure that all his construction vehicles plying on public roads\n                         (like dump trucks, trailers, etc.) have proper license to ply on public roads from the\n                    State Transport Authority. Drivers holding proper valid license as per the requirements\n                      of Motor Vehicles Act shall drive these vehicles\n\n\n          36.9.6   The contractor shall not undertake loading and unloading at carriageways obstructing\n                    the free flow of vehicular traffic and encroachment of existing roads by the contractor\n                    applying the excuse of work execution.\n\n\n          36.9.7   Tow away vehicle\n\n\n          36.9.7.1  The contractor shall make arrangements keeping tow away van / manpower to\n                tow away any breakdown vehicle in the traffic flow without loosing any time at\n                   his cost.\n\n          36.9.8   Cleaning of roads\n\n\n          36.9.8.1  The contractor shall ensure the cleanliness of roads and footpaths by deploying\n                 proper manpower for the same. The contractor shall have to ensure proper\n                 brooming, cleaning washing of roads and footpaths on all the time throughout\n                  the entire stretch till the currency of the contract including disposal of seepage."
>     }
>   ],

>     },
>     {
>       "pdf_page": 57,
>       "source_line_number": 42,
>       "text": "                                 i)    Warn the road user clearly and sufficiently in advance."
>     },
>     {
>       "pdf_page": 57,
>       "source_line_number": 43,
>       "text": ""
>     },
>     {
>       "pdf_page": 57,
>       "source_line_number": 44,
>       "text": "                                    ii)    Provide safe and clearly marked lanes for guiding road users."
>     },
>     {
>       "pdf_page": 57,
>       "source_line_number": 45,
>       "text": ""
>     },
>     {
>       "pdf_page": 57,
>       "source_line_number": 46,
>       "text": "                                     iii)    Provide safe and clearly marked buffer and work zones"
>     },
>     {
>       "pdf_page": 57,
>       "source_line_number": 47,
>       "text": ""
>     },
>     {
>       "pdf_page": 57,
>       "source_line_number": 48,
>       "text": "                          iv)   Provide adequate measures that control driver behaviour through construction"
>     },
>     {
>       "pdf_page": 57,
>       "source_line_number": 49,
>       "text": "                        zones."
>     },
>     {
>       "pdf_page": 57,

>       "text": ""
>     },
>     {
>       "pdf_page": 57,
>       "source_line_number": 52,
>       "text": "          36.4     Legal permission"
>     },
>     {
>       "pdf_page": 57,
>       "source_line_number": 53,
>       "text": ""
>     },
>     {

>       "text": ""
>     },
>     {
>       "pdf_page": 57,
>       "source_line_number": 55,
>       "text": "          36.4.1    In  all cases, the contractor shall employ proper precautions. Wherever operations"
>     },
>     {
>       "pdf_page": 57,
>       "source_line_number": 56,
>       "text": "                  undertaken are likely to interfere with public traffic, specific traffic management plans"
>     },
>     {
>       "pdf_page": 57,
>       "source_line_number": 57,
>       "text": "                      shall be drawn up and implemented by the contractor in consultation with the approval"
>     },
>     {
>       "pdf_page": 57,
>       "source_line_number": 58,
>       "text": "                      of local police authorities and/or the concerned metropolitan/civil authorities as the"
>     },
>     {
>       "pdf_page": 57,
>       "source_line_number": 59,
>       "text": "                 case may be."

>     {
>       "pdf_page": 57,
>       "source_line_number": 60,
>       "text": ""
>     },
>     {
>       "pdf_page": 57,
>       "source_line_number": 61,
>       "text": ""
>     },
>     {
>       "pdf_page": 57,
>       "source_line_number": 62,
>       "text": "          36.4.2   Such  traffic management plans  shall  include  provision  for  traffic  diversion and"
>     },
>     {
>       "pdf_page": 57,
>       "source_line_number": 63,
>       "text": "                     selection of alternative routes for transport of equipment.  If necessary, the contractor"
>     },
>     {
>       "pdf_page": 57,
>       "source_line_number": 64,
>       "text": "                      shall carry out road widening before commencement of works to accommodate the"
>     },
>     {
>       "pdf_page": 57,
>       "source_line_number": 65,
>       "text": "                    extra load"
>     },
>     {
>       "pdf_page": 57,
>       "source_line_number": 66,
>       "text": ""
>     },
>     {
>       "pdf_page": 57,
>       "source_line_number": 67,
>       "text": ""
>     },
>     {
>       "pdf_page": 57,
>       "source_line_number": 68,
>       "text": "          36.5    The primary traffic control devices used in work zones shall include signs, delineators,"
>     },
>     {
>       "pdf_page": 57,
>       "source_line_number": 69,
>       "text": "                    barricades, cones, pylons, pavement markings and flashing lights."

>       "source_line_number": 70,
>       "text": ""
>     },

>       "pdf_page": 57,
>       "source_line_number": 71,
>       "text": ""
>     },
>     {
>       "pdf_page": 57,
>       "source_line_number": 72,
>       "text": "          36.6    The road construction and maintenance signs which fall into the same three major"
>     },
>     {
>       "pdf_page": 57,
>       "source_line_number": 73,
>       "text": "                    categories as do other traffic signs, that are Regulatory Signs, Warning Signs and"
>     },
>     {
>       "pdf_page": 57,
>       "source_line_number": 74,
>       "text": "                     Direction (or guidelines) Signs shall only be used. The IRC: 67 (Code of Practice for"
>     },
>     {
>       "pdf_page": 57,
>       "source_line_number": 75,
>       "text": "               Road Signs) provide a list of traffic signs. The size, colours and placement of sign"
>     },
>     {
>       "pdf_page": 57,
>       "source_line_number": 76,
>       "text": "                      shall confirm to IRC: 67."
>     },
>     {
>       "pdf_page": 57,
>       "source_line_number": 77,
>       "text": ""
>     },
>     {
>       "pdf_page": 57,
>       "source_line_number": 78,
>       "text": ""
>     },
>     {
>       "pdf_page": 57,
>       "source_line_number": 79,
>       "text": ""
>     },
>     {
>       "pdf_page": 58,
>       "source_line_number": 3,
>       "text": ""
>     },
>     {
>       "pdf_page": 58,
>       "source_line_number": 4,
>       "text": "36.7     Regulatory signs"
>     },
>     {
>       "pdf_page": 58,
>       "source_line_number": 5,
>       "text": ""
>     },
>     {
>       "pdf_page": 58,
>       "source_line_number": 6,
>       "text": ""
>     },
>     {
>       "pdf_page": 58,
>       "source_line_number": 7,
>       "text": "36.7.1    Regulatory signs impose legal restriction on all traffic.  It is essential, therefore, that"
>     },
>     {
>       "pdf_page": 58,
>       "source_line_number": 8,
>       "text": "         they are used only after consulting the local police and traffic authorities."
>     },
>     {
>       "pdf_page": 58,
>       "source_line_number": 9,
>       "text": ""
>     },
>     {
>       "pdf_page": 58,
>       "source_line_number": 10,
>       "text": ""
>     },
>     {
>       "pdf_page": 58,
>       "source_line_number": 11,
>       "text": "36.8     Warning signs"
>     },
>     {
>       "pdf_page": 58,
>       "source_line_number": 12,
>       "text": ""
>     },
>     {
>       "pdf_page": 58,
>       "source_line_number": 13,
>       "text": ""
>     },
>     {
>       "pdf_page": 58,
>       "source_line_number": 14,
>       "text": "36.8.1   Warning signs in the traffic control zone shall be utilised to warn the drivers of specific"
>     },
>     {
>       "pdf_page": 58,
>       "source_line_number": 15,
>       "text": "         hazards that may be encountered."
>     },
>     {
>       "pdf_page": 58,
>       "source_line_number": 16,
>       "text": ""
>     },
>     {
>       "pdf_page": 58,
>       "source_line_number": 17,
>       "text": ""
>     },
>     {
>       "pdf_page": 58,
>       "source_line_number": 18,
>       "text": "36.8.2   The contractor shall place detour signage at strategic locations and install appropriate"
>     },
>     {
>       "pdf_page": 58,
>       "source_line_number": 19,
>       "text": "         warning signs.  In order to minimize disruption of access to residences and business,"
>     },
>     {
>       "pdf_page": 58,
>       "source_line_number": 20,
>       "text": "          the contractor shall maintain at least one entrance to a property where multiple"
>     },
>     {
>       "pdf_page": 58,
>       "source_line_number": 21,
>       "text": "         entrances exist."
>     },
>     {
>       "pdf_page": 58,
>       "source_line_number": 22,
>       "text": ""
>     },
>     {
>       "pdf_page": 58,
>       "source_line_number": 23,
>       "text": ""
>     },
>     {
>       "pdf_page": 58,
>       "source_line_number": 24,
>       "text": "36.8.3   A warning sign as given in general instruction BMRC/SHE/CEO/012 shall be installed"
>     },
>     {
>       "pdf_page": 58,
>       "source_line_number": 25,
>       "text": "        an at all secondary road which merges with the primary road where the construction"

>     {
>       "pdf_page": 58,
>       "source_line_number": 26,
>       "text": "         work is in progress at sufficient distance before it merges with the primary road so as"
>     },
>     {
>       "pdf_page": 58,
>       "source_line_number": 27,
>       "text": "           to alert the road users regarding the ‘Metro Work in Progress’."
>     },
>     {
>       "pdf_page": 58,
>       "source_line_number": 28,
>       "text": ""
>     },
>     {
>       "pdf_page": 58,
>       "source_line_number": 29,
>       "text": ""
>     },
>     {
>       "pdf_page": 58,
>       "source_line_number": 30,
>       "text": "36.8.4    Materials hanging over / protruded from the chassis / body of any vehicle especially"
>     },
>     {
>       "pdf_page": 58,
>       "source_line_number": 31,
>       "text": "          during material handling shall be indicated by red indicator (red light/flag) to indicate"
>     },
>     {
>       "pdf_page": 58,
>       "source_line_number": 32,
>       "text": "          the caution to the road users."
>     },
>     {
>       "pdf_page": 58,
>       "source_line_number": 33,
>       "text": ""
>     },
>     {
>       "pdf_page": 58,
>       "source_line_number": 34,
>       "text": ""
>     },
>     {
>       "pdf_page": 58,
>       "source_line_number": 35,
>       "text": "36.9      Delineators"
>     },
>     {
>       "pdf_page": 58,
>       "source_line_number": 36,
>       "text": ""
>     },
>     {
>       "pdf_page": 58,
>       "source_line_number": 37,
>       "text": "        The delineators are the elements of a total system of traffic control and have two"
>     },
>     {
>       "pdf_page": 58,
>       "source_line_number": 38,
>       "text": "            distinct purposes:"

>     {
>       "pdf_page": 58,
>       "source_line_number": 39,
>       "text": ""
>     },
>     {
>       "pdf_page": 58,
>       "source_line_number": 40,
>       "text": "                i)    To delineate and guide the driver to and along a safe path"
>     },
>     {
>       "pdf_page": 58,
>       "source_line_number": 41,
>       "text": ""
>     },
>     {
>       "pdf_page": 58,
>       "source_line_number": 42,
>       "text": "                  ii)   As a taper to move traffic from one lane to another."
>     },
>     {
>       "pdf_page": 58,
>       "source_line_number": 43,
>       "text": ""
>     },
>     {
>       "pdf_page": 58,
>       "source_line_number": 44,
>       "text": ""
>     },
>     {
>       "pdf_page": 58,
>       "source_line_number": 45,
>       "text": "36.9.1   These channelizing devices such as cones, traffic cylinders, tapes and drums shall be"
>     },
>     {
>       "pdf_page": 58,
>       "source_line_number": 46,
>       "text": "         placed in or adjacent to the roadway to control the flow of  traffic. These should"
>     },
>     {
>       "pdf_page": 58,
>       "source_line_number": 47,
>       "text": "          normally be retro-reflectors complying to IRC: 79 - Recommended Practice for Road"
>     },
>     {
>       "pdf_page": 58,
>       "source_line_number": 48,
>       "text": "          Delineators."
>     },
>     {
>       "pdf_page": 58,
>       "source_line_number": 49,
>       "text": ""
>     },
>     {
>       "pdf_page": 58,
>       "source_line_number": 50,
>       "text": ""
>     },
>     {
>       "pdf_page": 58,
>       "source_line_number": 51,
>       "text": "36.9.2    Traffic cones and cylinders"
>     },
>     {
>       "pdf_page": 58,
>       "source_line_number": 52,
>       "text": ""
>     },
>     {
>       "pdf_page": 58,
>       "source_line_number": 53,
>       "text": ""
>     },
>     {
>       "pdf_page": 58,
>       "source_line_number": 54,
>       "text": "36.9.2.1  Traffic cones of 500mm, 750mm and 1000mm high and 300mm to 500mm in diameter"
>     },
>     {
>       "pdf_page": 58,
>       "source_line_number": 55,
>       "text": "          or in square shape at base and are often made of plastic or rubber and normally have"
>     },
>     {
>       "pdf_page": 58,
>       "source_line_number": 56,
>       "text": "           retro-reflectorised red and white band shall be used wherever required."
>     },
>     {
>       "pdf_page": 58,
>       "source_line_number": 57,
>       "text": ""
>     },
>     {
>       "pdf_page": 58,
>       "source_line_number": 58,
>       "text": "36.9.3   Drums"
>     },
>     {
>       "pdf_page": 58,
>       "source_line_number": 59,
>       "text": ""
>     },
>     {
>       "pdf_page": 58,
>       "source_line_number": 60,
>       "text": "36.9.3.1  Drums about 800mm to 1000mm high and 300mm in diameter can be used either as"
>     },
>     {
>       "pdf_page": 58,
>       "source_line_number": 61,
>       "text": "          channelising or warning devices. These are highly visible, give the appearance of"
>     },
>     {
>       "pdf_page": 58,
>       "source_line_number": 62,
>       "text": "         being formidable objects and therefore command the respect of drivers."
>     },
>     {
>       "pdf_page": 58,
>       "source_line_number": 63,
>       "text": ""
>     },
>     {
>       "pdf_page": 58,
>       "source_line_number": 64,
>       "text": ""
>     },
>     {
>       "pdf_page": 58,
>       "source_line_number": 65,
>       "text": "36.9.4    Barricades"

>       "source_line_number": 66,
>       "text": ""
>     },
>     {
>       "pdf_page": 58,
>       "source_line_number": 67,
>       "text": ""
>     },
>     {
>       "pdf_page": 58,
>       "source_line_number": 68,
>       "text": "36.9.4.1  Full height fence, barriers, barricades etc. shall be erected around the site in order to"
>     },
>     {
>       "pdf_page": 58,
>       "source_line_number": 69,
>       "text": "         prevent the working area from  the  risk  of  accidents due  to speedy  vehicular"
>     },
>     {
>       "pdf_page": 58,
>       "source_line_number": 70,
>       "text": "        movement. Same the way barricades protect the road users from the danger due to"
>     },
>     {
>       "pdf_page": 58,
>       "source_line_number": 71,
>       "text": "          construction equipment and other temporary structures."
>     },
>     {
>       "pdf_page": 58,
>       "source_line_number": 72,
>       "text": ""
>     },
>     {
>       "pdf_page": 58,
>       "source_line_number": 73,
>       "text": ""
>     },
>     {
>       "pdf_page": 58,
>       "source_line_number": 74,
>       "text": "36.9.4.2  The structure dimension of the barricade, material and composition, its colour scheme,"
>     },
>     {
>       "pdf_page": 58,
>       "source_line_number": 75,
>       "text": "      BMRC logo and other details shall be in accordance with specifications laid down in"
>     },
>     {
>       "pdf_page": 58,
>       "source_line_number": 76,
>       "text": "          tender document."
>     },
>     {
>       "pdf_page": 58,
>       "source_line_number": 77,
>       "text": ""
>     },
>     {
>       "pdf_page": 58,
>       "source_line_number": 78,
>       "text": ""
>     },
>     {
>       "pdf_page": 58,
>       "source_line_number": 79,
>       "text": ""
>     },
>     {
>       "pdf_page": 58,
>       "source_line_number": 80,
>       "text": ""
>     },
>     {
>       "pdf_page": 59,
>       "source_line_number": 3,
>       "text": "          36.9.4.3  All barricades shall be erected as per the design requirements of the Employer,"
>     },
>     {
>       "pdf_page": 59,
>       "source_line_number": 4,
>       "text": "                 numbered, painted and maintained in good condition and also Barricade in-charge"
>     },
>     {
>       "pdf_page": 59,
>       "source_line_number": 5,
>       "text": "                   maintains a barricade register in site."
>     },
>     {
>       "pdf_page": 59,
>       "source_line_number": 6,
>       "text": ""
>     },
>     {
>       "pdf_page": 59,
>       "source_line_number": 7,
>       "text": ""
>     },
>     {
>       "pdf_page": 59,
>       "source_line_number": 8,
>       "text": "          36.9.4.4  All barricades shall be conspicuously seen in the dark/night time by the road"
>     },
>     {
>       "pdf_page": 59,
>       "source_line_number": 9,
>       "text": "                 users so that no vehicle hits the barricade. Conspicuity. shall be ensured by"
>     },
>     {
>       "pdf_page": 59,
>       "source_line_number": 10,
>       "text": "                     affixing retro reflective stripes of required size and shape at appropriate angle at"
>     },
>     {
>       "pdf_page": 59,
>       "source_line_number": 11,
>       "text": "                  the bottom and middle portion of the barricade at a minimum gap of 1000mm. In"
>     },
>     {
>       "pdf_page": 59,
>       "source_line_number": 12,
>       "text": "                   addition minimum one red light or red light blinker should be placed at the top"
>     },
>     {
>       "pdf_page": 59,
>       "source_line_number": 13,
>       "text": "                   of each barricade."
>     },
>     {
>       "pdf_page": 59,
>       "source_line_number": 14,
>       "text": ""
>     },
>     {
>       "pdf_page": 59,
>       "source_line_number": 15,
>       "text": ""
>     },
>     {
>       "pdf_page": 59,
>       "source_line_number": 16,
>       "text": "          36.9.5   The contractor shall ensure that all his construction vehicles plying on public roads"
>     },
>     {
>       "pdf_page": 59,
>       "source_line_number": 17,
>       "text": "                         (like dump trucks, trailers, etc.) have proper license to ply on public roads from the"
>     },
>     {
>       "pdf_page": 59,
>       "source_line_number": 18,
>       "text": "                    State Transport Authority. Drivers holding proper valid license as per the requirements"
>     },
>     {
>       "pdf_page": 59,
>       "source_line_number": 19,
>       "text": "                      of Motor Vehicles Act shall drive these vehicles"
>     },
>     {
>       "pdf_page": 59,
>       "source_line_number": 20,
>       "text": ""
>     },
>     {
>       "pdf_page": 59,
>       "source_line_number": 21,
>       "text": ""
>     },
>     {
>       "pdf_page": 59,
>       "source_line_number": 22,
>       "text": "          36.9.6   The contractor shall not undertake loading and unloading at carriageways obstructing"
>     },
>     {
>       "pdf_page": 59,
>       "source_line_number": 23,
>       "text": "                    the free flow of vehicular traffic and encroachment of existing roads by the contractor"
>     },
>     {
>       "pdf_page": 59,
>       "source_line_number": 24,
>       "text": "                    applying the excuse of work execution."
>     },
>     {
>       "pdf_page": 59,
>       "source_line_number": 25,
>       "text": ""
>     },
>     {
>       "pdf_page": 59,
>       "source_line_number": 26,
>       "text": ""
>     },
>     {
>       "pdf_page": 59,
>       "source_line_number": 27,
>       "text": "          36.9.7   Tow away vehicle"
>     },
>     {
>       "pdf_page": 59,
>       "source_line_number": 28,
>       "text": ""
>     },
>     {
>       "pdf_page": 59,
>       "source_line_number": 29,
>       "text": ""
>     },
>     {
>       "pdf_page": 59,
>       "source_line_number": 30,
>       "text": "          36.9.7.1  The contractor shall make arrangements keeping tow away van / manpower to"
>     },

>       "text": ""

>       "text": ""

>     {

>       "text": "39.0     Personal Protective Equipments (PPEs)\n\n\n39.1    The contractor shall provide required PPEs to workmen to protect against safety and /\n          or health hazards. Primarily PPEs are required for the following protection\n\n\n                i)    Head Protection (Safety helmets)\n                  ii)    Foot Protection (Safety footwear, Gumboot, etc)\n                  iii)   Body Protection (High visibility clothing (waistcoat/jacket), Apron, etc)\n             iv)   Personal fall protection (Full body harness, Rope-grap fall arrester, etc)\n           v)   Eye Protection (Goggles, Welders glasses, etc)\n             vi)   Hand Protection (Gloves, Finger coats, etc)\n              vii)   Respiratory Protection. (Nose mask, SCBAs, etc)\n               viii)  Hearing Protection (Ear plugs, Ear muffs, etc)\n\n\n39.2    The PPEs and safety appliances provided by the contractor shall be of the\n         standard as prescribed by Bureau of Indian Standards  (BIS).  If materials\n        conforming to BIS standards are not available, the contractor as approved by\n         the Employer shall procure PPE and safety appliances.\n\n\n39.3      All construction workers should be provided with high visibility jackets with\n          reflective tapes confirming to the requirement specified under BS EN 471: 1994\n        as most of viaduct /tunnelling/station and depot works are executed either\n        above or under right-of-way. The conspicuity of workmen at all times shall be\n         increased so as to protect them from speeding vehicular traffic.\n\n39.4    The contractor shall provide safety helmet, safety shoe and high visibility clothing\n            for all employees including workmen, traffic marshal and other employees who are\n        engaged for any work under this contract as per the following requirement."

Failing  to do so  shall  invite appropriate penalty as per the\n          provisions of the contract.\n\n\n 39.8         It is always the duty of the contractor to provide required PPEs for all visitors. [[OKF_bundle/Technical/Vol3/vol3_part2#Clause 40.0 — Visitors to site|Clause 40.0 — Visitors to site]]

>       "pdf_page": 62,
>       "text": "40.0      Visitors to site\n\n\n 40.1    No visitor is allowed to enter the site without the permission of the Employer. All\n          authorised visitors should report at the site office. Contractor shall provide visitor’s\n          helmet (White helmet with visitor sticker) and other PPEs like Safety Shoe, reflective\n            jacket, respiratory protection etc. as per requirement of the site.\n\n\n 40.2       All Visitors shall be accompanied at all times by a responsible member of the site\n          personnel.\n\n\n 40.3    The contractor shall be fully responsible for all visitors’ safety and health within the\n             site.\n\n\n 40.4    As indicated earlier in this Manual, the Engineer shall undertake regular audits at\n           quarterly intervals, of the Contractor’s onsite practices and procedures as a means of\n          assessing the ongoing performance of the Contractor.\n\n 40.5    The criteria against which the audits will be undertaken shall be derived from the\n          clauses within the Environment Protection Requirements (Appendix III herein above),\n           contract-specific Site Environmental Plan and previous site inspection results.\n\n 40.6      In addition to the quarterly audits by the Engineer, site inspection shall be undertaken\n         by the Contractor’s staff to inspect the construction activities in order to ensure that\n           appropriate environmental protection and pollution control measures are properly\n           followed and implemented.\n\n 40.7    The frequency of site inspection shall be at least once a week.\n\n 40.8    The Contractor shall prepare an ‘Environmental Inspection and Action Reporting\n          System’ and submit to the Engineer for approval and make amendments as\n          suggested.  It shall contain a contract specific comprehensive Environment Inspection\n           checklist as requirement of Site Environmental Plan.\n 40.9    The area of inspection shall not be limited to environmental compliance within the site\n           but areas outside the site which are likely to be affected, directly or indirectly by\n             activities at site.\n\n 40.10     Results of inspection shall be discussed with Engineer and his recommendations on\n           better environmental protection shall be notified to the Contractor for taking immediate\n           action and rapid resolution of identified non-compliance.\n40.11       If significant environmental problems are identified or if there is an environmental\n          complaint or as a part of investigation work, then the Engineer shall also carry out Ad\n         hoc site inspection which shall be attended by Contractor’s Representative.\n\n 40.12   REPORTING SYSTEM\n\n 40.12.1   reporting under  the Environmental Management System  will  contain  results  of"
>     },
>     {
>       "pdf_page": 63,
>       "text": "monitoring and inspection programs.\n\n          40.12.2   In  Site  Environmental  Plan,  the  Contractor  shall  prepare and submit monthly\n                   Environmental Quality Management Reports in accordance with Requirements as per\n                    Contract.\n\n          40.12.3  The monthly report shall include (but not limited to) the following:\n                       Executive Summary\n\n                       Brief mention of construction activities\n\n                       Monitoring results under AMCP, and NMCP\n\n                       Interpretation of monitoring results, significance and influencing factors\n\n                       Graphical representation of monitored results over past four reporting periods.\n\n                      Measures to control spill under SPCP.\n\n                       Action taken on recommendations under site inspection programme or specific\n                          directions.\n\n                      Summary of complaints, results of investigations and follow-up action\n\n                       Future key issues.\n\n         40.13   COMPLAINT RESPONSE PROCESS\n          40.13.1   Inquiries, complaints and requests for information can be expected from a wide range\n                      of  individuals and organizations both private and government.  The majority of\n                   complaints is likely to be received by BMRCL, although the site offices are also likely\n                      to be contacted.\n\n          40.13.2  The objective of complaint process is to ensure that public and agency complaints are\n                  addressed and resolved consistently and expeditiously.\n\n          40.13.3  The Contractor’s Site Manager will be notified immediately on receipt of complaint that\n              may relate to environmental impacts. The Site Manager will immediately inform the\n                  Engineer and through him the BMRCL.\n\n          40.13.4   Field investigation should determine whether the complaint has merit, and if so action\n                   should be taken to address the impact.\n          40.13.5  The outcome of the investigation and the action taken shall be documented on a\n                   complaint Performa prepared by the Contractor and approved by the Engineer in\n                 advance of the works.\n\n          40.13.6  Where possible, a formal response to each complaint received shall be prepared by\n                    the Contractor within seven days in order to notify the concerned person(s) that action\n                 has been taken.\n\n         40.14   COMPLETION OF THE EQM PROGRAMME\n          40.14.1  The construction of Bangalore Metro  will be undertaken as a series of individual\n                    construction contracts with necessarily different construction program and completion\n                    dates.\n\n          40.14.2  The Engineer shall maintain an overview of the ‘impact causing potential’ of each site\n                     or contract and monitoring parameter with a view to maintaining the most cost\n                      effective use of the environmental resources dedicated to the Project.\n\n          40.14.3 Termination of EQM should focus on the percentage contract completion status and on\n                  the basis of a history of environmental impact arising from the site over a representative\n                 period of monitoring.\n\n         40.13.5    Justifiable application for termination of EQM shall be put forward by the\n                    Contractor  to the Engineer, as necessary throughout the  construction\n                       period."
>     }

>   "text": "Safety Health & Environment (SHE) Manual\n215\n                                PART – II : SAFETY\n\n          17.0     Housekeeping\n\n\n          17.1     Housekeeping is the act of keeping the working environment cleared of all unnecessary\n                   waste, thereby providing a first-line of defence against accidents and injuries.\n\n\n          17.2      Contractor shall understand and accept that improper housekeeping is the primary\n                  hazard in any construction site and ensure that a high degree of housekeeping is\n                  always maintained. Indeed “Cleanliness is indeed next to Godliness”\n\n\n          17.3     Housekeeping  is  the  responsibility  of  all  site  personnel, and  line management\n                 commitment shall be demonstrated by the continued efforts of supervising staff towards\n                        this activity.\n\n\n          17.4     General Housekeeping shall be carried out by the contractor and ensured at all times at\n                Work Site, Construction Depot, Batching Plant, Labour Camp, Stores, Offices and\n                        toilets/urinals. Towards  this  the  Contractor  shall  constitute a  special  group  of\n                  housekeeping personnel as per General Instruction BMRC/SHE/CEO/001. This group\n                      shall ensure daily cleaning at work sites and surrounding areas and maintain a register\n                 as per the approved format by the Employer.\n\n\n          17.5     Adequate time shall be assigned to ensure that good housekeeping is maintained.\n              Team of housekeeping squad shall carry out this.\n\n\n          17.6    The contractor shall be responsible to provide segregated containers for disposal of\n                    debris at required places and regular cleaning of the same.\n\n\n          17.7      Full height fence, barriers, barricades etc. shall be erected around the site in order to\n                   prevent the surrounding area from excavated  soil, rubbish etc, which may cause\n                   inconvenience to and endanger the public. The barricade especially those exposed to\n                     public shall be aesthetically maintained by regular cleaning and painting as directed by\n                    the Employer. These shall be maintained in one line and level.\n\n\n          17.8    The structure dimension of the barricade, material and composition, its colour scheme,\n            BMRC logo and other details shall be in accordance with specifications laid down in\n                   tender document.\n\n\n          17.9       All stairways, passageways and gangways shall be maintained without any blockages\n                     or obstructions. All emergency exits passageways, exits fire doors, break-glass alarm\n                      points, firefighting equipment, first aid stations, and other emergency stations shall be\n                   kept clean, unobstructed and in good working order.\n\n\n         17.10    Lumber with protruding nails shall be bent or removed and properly stacked.\n\n\n         17.11     All surplus earth and debris are removed/disposed  off from the working areas to\n                          officially designated dumpsites. Trucks  carrying sand,  earth and any  pulverized\n                    materials etc. in order to avoid dust or odour impact shall be covered while moving.\n\n               The tyres of the trucks leaving the site shall be cleaned with water, wherever the\n                    possibility of spillage on carriageways meant for regular road traffic exists.\n\n\n         17.12  No parking of trucks/trolleys, cranes and trailers etc. shall be allowed on roads, which\n              may obstruct the traffic movement.\n\n\n         17.13   Roads shall be kept clear and materials like: pipes, steel, sand boulders, concrete,\n                   chips and brick etc. shall not be allowed on the roads to obstruct free movement of\n                 road traffic.\n\n\n\n\n\n         Bangalore Metro Rail Corporation Ltd.              September 2026     Section Page 27 of 114",

>   "text": "Safety Health & Environment (SHE) Manual\n                                                          216\n17.14   Water logging or bentonite spillage on roads shall not be allowed.  If bentonite\n          spillage is observed on road endangering the safety of road users, the contractor\n          shall be penalised as per relevant clause.\n\n\n17.15   Proper and safe stacking of material are of paramount importance at yards, stores\n       and such locations where material would be unloaded for future use. The storage\n        area shall be well laid out with easy access and material stored  / stacked in an\n         orderly and safe manner.\n\n\n17.16   Flammable chemicals / compressed gas cylinders shall be safely stored.\n\n\n17.17   Unused/surplus cables, steel items and steel scrap lying scattered at different\n        places within the working areas shall be removed to identified locations(s).\n\n\n17.18    All wooden scrap, empty wooden cable drums and other combustible packing\n         materials, shall be removed from work place to identified location(s).\n\n\n17.19   Empty cement bags and other packaging material shall be properly stacked and\n        removed.\n\n\n17.20   The  Contractor  shall  ensure  that  all  his  sub-contractors  maintain  the  site\n        reasonably clean through provisions related to house keeping\n\n\n18.0    Working at Height\n\n\n18.1     Definitions\n\n\n18.1.1   “access” and “egress” include ascent and descent.\n\n\n18.1.2   “fragile surface” means a surface, which would be able to fail  if any reasonably\n         foreseeable loading were to be applied to it.\n\n\n18.1.3   “line” includes rope, chain or webbing\n\n\n18.1.4   “personal fall protection” means -\n\n          a)   a  fall prevention, work  restraint, work positioning,  fall arrest or rescue\n               system,   other than a system in which the only safeguards are collective\n               safeguards; or\n          b)    rope access and positioning techniques;\n\n\n18.1.5    \"work at height\" means -\n           a)   work in any place, including a place at or below ground level;\n           b)    obtaining access to or egress from such place while at work, except by a\n                staircase in a permanent workplace,\n              where,  if protective measures were not taken, a person could fall a distance\n                   liable to cause personal injury;\n\n\n18.1.6    \"work equipment\" means any machinery, appliance, apparatus, tool or installation for\n        use at work (whether exclusively or not) and includes\n          a)   a guard-rail, toe-board, barrier or similar collective means of protection\n          b)   a working platform\n           c)   a net, airbag or other collective safe guard for arresting falls.\n          d)    personal fall protection system\n          e)    ladders\n\n18.1.7    “working platform”\n          a)   means any platform used as a place of work or as a means of access to or\n              egress from a place of work;\n\n\n\nBangalore Metro Rail Corporation Ltd. >   "text": "Safety Health & Environment (SHE) Manual\n217\n                     b)    includes any scaffold, suspended scaffold, cradle, mobile platforms,  trestle,\n                      gangway, gantry and stairway which is so used.\n\n\n          18.2     Organisation and planning\n\n                The contractor shall ensure that work at height is\n\n                                 i)     properly planned for any emergencies and rescue\n\n                                    ii)    appropriately supervised; and\n\n                                     iii)    carried out in a manner, which is reasonably practicable safe.\n\n\n          18.3    The contractor shall ensure that work at height is carried out only when the weather\n                    conditions do not jeopardise the health or safety of persons involved in the work.\n\n\n          18.4     Competence\n\n                The  contractor  shall ensure  that no person engages  in any  activity,  including\n                     organization, planning and supervision, in relation to work at height or work equipment\n                       for use in such work unless he is competent to do so or,  if being trained, is being\n                   supervised by a competent person.\n\n\n          18.5     Avoidance of risks from work at height\n\n                The contractor shall ensure that work is not carried out at height where it is reasonably\n                     practicable to carry out the work safely otherwise than at height.\n\n\n          18.6    Where work is carried out at height, the contractor shall take suitable and sufficient\n                 measures as given below to prevent, so far as is reasonably practicable, any person\n                      falling a distance liable to cause personal injury.\n\n\n                     a)    his ensuring that the work is carried out\n\n                                           i)    from an existing place of work; or\n\n                                              ii)     (in the case of obtaining access or egress) using an existing means,\n                             complying to the requirements as given in clause 18.15 .\n\n                      where  it is reasonably practicable to carry  it out safely and under appropriate\n                       ergonomic conditions; and\n\n\n                     b)   where  it is not reasonably practicable for the work to be carried out in\n                       accordance with sub-paragraph (a), his providing sufficient work equipment\n                              for preventing, so far as is reasonably practicable, a fall occurring.\n\n\n          18.7    Where the measures taken under clause 18.6 do not eliminate the risk of a fall\n                     occurring, every contractor shall\n\n                     a)   so far as is reasonably practicable, provide sufficient work equipment to\n                        minimise -\n\n                                           i)     the distance and consequences; or\n\n                                              ii)    where  it is not reasonably practicable to minimise the distance, the\n                            consequences, of a fall; and\n\n                     b)    Without prejudice to the generality of clause 18.4 provide such additional\n                             training and  instruction or take other  additional suitable and  sufficient\n                     measures to prevent, so far as is reasonably practicable, any person falling\n                     a distance liable to cause personal injury.\n\n\n          18.8      Selection of ‘work equipment’ for work at height\n\n\n                     1)    the contractor, in selecting work equipment for use in work at height, shall\n\n                           a)    give collective protection measures priority over personal protection\n                            measures; and\n\n                           b)    take account of\n\n\n\n\n\n         Bangalore Metro Rail Corporation Ltd. >       "text": "b)  \nwhere it is not reasonably practicable for the work to be carried out in \naccordance with sub-paragraph (a), his providing sufficient work equipment \nfor preventing, so far as is reasonably practicable, a fall occurring. \n \n18.7  \nWhere the measures taken under clause 18.6 do not eliminate the risk of a fall \noccurring, every contractor shall \na) \nso far as is reasonably practicable, provide sufficient work equipment to \nminimise -  \ni) \nthe distance and consequences; or \nii) \nwhere it is not reasonably practicable to minimise the distance, the \nconsequences, of a fall; and \nb) \nWithout prejudice to the generality of clause 18.4 provide such additional \ntraining and instruction or take other additional suitable and sufficient \nmeasures to prevent, so far as is reasonably practicable, any person falling \na distance liable to cause personal injury.  \n \n18.8  \nSelection of ‘work equipment’ for work at height \n \n"

### J35783b23984f7765

[[OKF_bundle/Technical/Vol3/vol3_part2#Safety, Health and Environment Manual – Part II: Safety|Safety, Health and Environment Manual – Part II: Safety]]

>   "text": "Safety Health & Environment (SHE) Manual\n219\n\n          18.10.3  The contractor shall ensure that no material or object is thrown or tipped from\n                    height in circumstances where it is liable to cause injury to any person.\n\n\n          18.10.4  Every employer shall ensure that materials and objects are stored in such a way\n                 as  to prevent  risk  to any person  arising from the  collapse, overturning or\n                  unintended movement of such materials or objects.\n\n\n         18.11    Danger areas\n\n\n          18.11.1  Without prejudice to the preceding requirements of these Regulations, every\n                     contractor shall ensure that\n\n                     a)   where a workplace contains an area in which, owing to the nature of the\n                         work, there is a risk of any person at work\n\n                                           i)      falling a distance; or\n\n                                              ii)    being struck by a falling object,\n\n                       which  is liable to cause personal  injury, the workplace  is so far as  is\n                        reasonably  practicable equipped  with devices  preventing unauthorised\n                       persons from entering such area; and\n\n                     b)   such area is clearly indicated.\n\n\n         18.12    Inspection of work equipment\n\n\n          18.12.1  The contractor shall ensure that, where the safety of work equipment depends on\n               how it is installed or assembled, it is not used after installation or assembly in any\n                     position unless it has been inspected in that position.\n\n\n          18.12.2  The contractor shall ensure that work equipment exposed to conditions causing\n                     deterioration which is liable to result in dangerous situations is inspected\n\n                     a)    at suitable intervals; and\n\n                     b)   each time that exceptional circumstances which are liable to jeopardise the\n                          safety of the work equipment have occurred,\n\n                      to ensure  that  health and  safety  conditions  are maintained and  that any\n                     deterioration can be detected and remedied in good time.\n\n\n          18.12.3  Without prejudice to paragraph 18.12.1, the contractor shall ensure that a working\n                    platform\n\n                     a)   used for construction work; and\n\n                     b)    from which a person could fall 2 metres or more,\n\n                         is not used in any position unless it has been inspected in that position or, in the\n                 case of a mobile working platform, inspected on the site, within the previous 7\n                   days.\n\n\n          18.12.4  The contractor  shall ensure  that the reports  of  all inspections are properly\n                   maintained and shown to the Employer as and when required.\n\n\n          18.12.5   In this clause \"inspection\",\n\n                     a)   means such visual or more rigorous inspection by a competent person as is\n                          appropriate for safety purposes;\n\n                     b)    includes any testing appropriate for those purposes,\n\n\n         18.13    Inspection of places of work at height\n\n\n          18.13.1  The contractor shall so far as is reasonably practicable ensure that the surface\n                and every parapet, permanent rail or other such fall protection measure of every\n                   place of work at height are checked on each occasion before the place is used.\n\n\n\n         Bangalore Metro Rail Corporation Ltd.              September 2026     Section Page 31 of 114",

>       "text": " \n18.10.3 \nThe contractor shall ensure that no material or object is thrown or tipped from \nheight in circumstances where it is liable to cause injury to any person. \n \n18.10.4 \nEvery employer shall ensure that materials and objects are stored in such a way \nas to prevent risk to any person arising from the collapse, overturning or \nunintended movement of such materials or objects. \n \n18.11 \nDanger areas \n \n18.11.1 \nWithout prejudice to the preceding requirements of these Regulations, every \ncontractor shall ensure that \na) \nwhere a workplace contains an area in which, owing to the nature of the \nwork, there is a risk of any person at work \ni) \nfalling a distance; or \nii) \nbeing struck by a falling object, \nwhich is liable to cause personal injury, the workplace is so far as is \nreasonably practicable equipped with devices preventing unauthorised \npersons from entering such area; and \nb) \nsuch area is clearly indicated. \n \n18.12 \nInspection of work equipment \n \n18.12.1 \nThe contractor shall ensure that, where the safety of work equipment depends on \nhow it is installed or assembled, it is not used after installation or assembly in any \nposition unless it has been inspected in that position. \n \n18.12.2 \nThe contractor shall ensure that work equipment exposed to conditions causing \ndeterioration which is liable to result in dangerous situations is inspected \na) \nat suitable intervals; and \nb) \neach time that exceptional circumstances which are liable to jeopardise the \nsafety of the work equipment have occurred, \nto ensure that health and safety conditions are maintained and that any \ndeterioration can be detected and remedied in good time. \n \n18.12.3 \nWithout prejudice to paragraph 18.12.1, the contractor shall ensure that a working \nplatform \na) \nused for construction work; and \nb) \nfrom which a person could fall 2 metres or more, \nis not used in any position unless it has been inspected in that position or, in the \ncase of a mobile working platform, inspected on the site, within the previous 7 \ndays. \n \n18.12.4 \nThe contractor shall ensure that the reports of all inspections are properly \nmaintained and shown to the Employer as and when required. \n \n18.12.5 \nIn this clause \"inspection\",  \na) \nmeans such visual or more rigorous inspection by a competent person as is \nappropriate for safety purposes; >   "text": "Safety Health & Environment (SHE) Manual\n                                                          220\n\n18.14    Duties of persons at work\n\n\n18.14.1  Any workmen employed by the contractor shall report to the supervisor about any\n          defect relating to work at height which he knows is likely to endanger the safety of\n          himself or another person.\n\n\n18.14.2  Every workmen shall use any work equipment or safety device provided to him for\n         work at height by the contractor, in accordance with\n\n\n          a)   any training in the use of the work equipment or device concerned which\n             have been received by him; and\n\n          b)    the instructions respecting that use which have been provided to him by the\n                contractor as per the requirements of the Employer\n\n\n18.15    Requirements for existing places of work and means of access or egress at height\n         Every existing place of work or means of access or egress at height shall\n\n\n          a)   be stable and of sufficient strength and rigidity for the purpose for which it is\n               intended to be or is being used;\n\n          b)   where applicable, rest on a stable, sufficiently strong surface;\n\n           c)   be of sufficient dimensions to permit the safe passage of persons and the\n               safe use of any plant or materials required to be used and to provide a safe\n               working area having regard to the work to be carried out there;\n\n          d)   possess suitable and sufficient means for preventing a fall;\n\n          e)   possess a surface which has no gap\n\n                          i)    through which a person could fall;\n\n                            ii)    through which any material or object could fall and injure a person; or\n\n                             iii)    giving rise to other risk of injury to any person, unless measures have\n                  been taken to protect persons against such risk;\n\n               f)    be so constructed and used, and maintained  in such condition, as to\n                prevent, so far as is reasonably practicable -\n\n                          i)     the risk of slipping or tripping; or\n\n                            ii)    any person being caught between it and any adjacent structure;\n\n          g)   where   it has moving parts, be prevented by appropriate devices from\n             moving inadvertently during work at height.\n\n\n18.16    Requirements for guardrails, toe-boards, barriers and similar collective means of\n          protection\n\n\n                i)    Unless the context otherwise requires, any reference in this section to\n            means of protection is to a guardrail, toe-board, barrier or similar collective\n            means of protection.\n\n                  ii)   Means of protection shall\n\n                a)   be of sufficient dimensions, of sufficient strength and rigidity for the\n                   purposes for which they are being used, and otherwise suitable;\n\n                b)   be so placed, secured and used as to ensure, so far as is reasonably\n                       practicable, that they do not become accidentally displaced; and\n\n                 c)   be so placed as to prevent, so far as is practicable, the fall of any\n                     person, or of any material or object, from any place of work.\n\n                  iii)    In relation to work at height involved in construction work\n\n                a)    the top guard-rail or other similar means of protection shall be at least\n                  950 millimetres above the edge from which any person is liable to fall;\n\n                b)    toe-boards shall be suitable and sufficient to prevent the fall of any\n                     person, or any material or object, from any place of work; and\n\n\n\n\n\nBangalore Metro Rail Corporation Ltd.              September 2026     Section Page 32 of 114",

>   "text": "Safety Health & Environment (SHE) Manual\n                                                          218\n                                    i)     the working conditions and the risks to the safety of persons at\n                           the place where the work equipment is to be used;\n\n                                       ii)     in the case of work equipment for access and egress, the\n                           distance to be negotiated;\n\n                                        iii)    the distance and consequences of a potential fall;\n\n                             iv)    the duration and frequency of use;\n\n                        v)    the need  for easy and timely evacuation and rescue in an\n                        emergency; and\n\n                             vi)   any additional risk posed by the use, installation or removal of\n                              that work equipment or by evacuation and rescue from it;\n\n\n          2)   The contractor shall select work equipment for work at height which:\n\n\n                a)   has characteristics including dimensions which:\n\n                                    i)    are appropriate to the nature of the work to be performed and\n                           the foreseeable loadings; and\n\n                                       ii)    allow passage without risk; and\n\n                b)     is in other respects the most suitable work equipment, having regard\n                          in particular to the purposes specified in 18.5 and 18.6 .\n\n\n18.9      Fragile surfaces\n\n\n18.9.1   The contractor shall ensure that no person at work passes across or near, or\n         working on, from or near, a fragile surface where  it is reasonably practicable to\n          carry out work safely and under appropriate ergonomic conditions without his\n         doing so.\n\n\n18.9.2   Where   it  is not reasonably practicable  to carry out work  safely and under\n          appropriate ergonomic conditions without passing across or near, or working on,\n         from or near, a fragile surface, every contractor shall,\n\n\n          a)    ensure, so far as  is reasonably practicable, that suitable and sufficient\n                platforms, coverings, guard rails or similar means of support or protection\n               are provided and used so that any foreseeable loading is supported by such\n               supports or borne by such protection;\n\n\n          b)   where a risk of a person at work falling remains despite the measures taken\n              under the preceding provisions of this regulation, take suitable and sufficient\n             measures to minimise the distances and consequences of his fall.\n\n\n18.9.3   Where any person at work may pass across or near, or work on, from or near, a\n            fragile surface, every contractor shall ensure that\n\n          a)    prominent warning notices are so far as is reasonably practicable affixed at\n                the approach to the place where the fragile surface is situated; or\n\n          b)   where that is not reasonably practicable, such persons are made aware of it\n              by other means.\n\n\n18.10     Falling objects\n\n\n18.10.1  The contractor  shall, where necessary to prevent injury to any person, take\n          suitable and sufficient steps to prevent, so far as is reasonably practicable, the fall\n           of any material or object.\n\n\n18.10.2  Where  it is not reasonably practicable to comply with the requirements of 18.9,\n         every contractor shall take suitable and sufficient steps to prevent any person\n         being struck by any falling material or object which is liable to cause personal\n            injury.\n\n\n\nBangalore Metro Rail Corporation Ltd.              September 2026     Section Page 30 of 114",

### J08371c421ef4c610
